jobs.title: Information Systems & Data Management Officer
jobs.description:
**Summary:**

The Information Systems & Data Management Officer is responsible for strengthening the organisation’s programme data systems and digital data management capabilities. The role leads the configuration and maintenance of DHIS2 and digital data collection platforms, supports database management and GIS analysis, develops dashboards and data visualizations, and promotes data quality, integrity, security and use. Working closely with programme and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) teams, the Officer helps ensure that reliable, timely and accessible data informs programme planning, monitoring, reporting and decision-making. General ICT support is not a core function and, where required, is limited to a maximum of 10% of the role and to issues directly affecting programme data systems.

**Working Relationships:**

The Officer works closely with programme teams, MEAL colleagues, field staff and relevant regional or global technical colleagues. The role coordinates with designated ICT personnel or service providers for general ICT infrastructure and support outside the limited scope defined in this job description.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**A. Data Systems Management and Development**

- Design, configure, maintain and improve databases and systems used to store, manage and analyse programme data.
- Develop and maintain digital data collection forms, workflows and applications using platforms such as KoboToolbox, CommCare and DHIS2 Mobile, as relevant to programme needs.
- Manage DHIS2 configuration and maintenance, including metadata, organisation units, data elements, indicators, datasets, validation rules, user roles and dashboards.
- Work with programme and MEAL teams to translate reporting and monitoring requirements into practical data system solutions.
- Support appropriate integration and interoperability between DHIS2, digital data collection platforms, GIS tools and other approved programme systems.
- Maintain clear documentation of system configurations, data definitions, workflows, changes and technical procedures.

**B. Data Quality, Governance and Protection**

- Develop and implement data collection standards, protocols, validation rules and quality assurance procedures.
- Conduct routine data quality checks, identify gaps or anomalies, coordinate corrective action with relevant teams and document recurring issues.
- Promote completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness and appropriate use of programme data across implementation areas.
- Support data cleaning, consolidation and preparation for analysis and reporting, maintaining traceability and appropriate version control.
- Apply organisational policies and applicable requirements for data privacy, confidentiality, access control, retention and secure handling of information.
- Maintain appropriate data backup and recovery arrangements for systems under the role’s responsibility, in coordination with designated ICT or system administrators where necessary.

**C. Data Analysis, Visualization and Reporting**

- Develop and maintain automated dashboards, visualizations and routine reports using Power BI, Tableau or comparable tools.
- Analyse programme data to identify trends, performance gaps, outliers and findings relevant to programme implementation and management decisions.
- Support teams to define and interpret indicators and ensure that calculations and reporting outputs are consistent and clearly documented.
- Produce accurate, user-friendly data summaries and visual products for programme reviews, planning, monitoring and reporting.
- Work with programme and MEAL colleagues to improve the accessibility and practical use of data by technical and non-technical users.

**D. Geographic Information Systems (GIS)**

- Develop and maintain GIS datasets and spatial databases relevant to programme implementation and monitoring.
- Conduct spatial analysis and prepare thematic maps to support programme planning, resource allocation, coverage analysis and monitoring.
- Integrate geographic information with DHIS2 and other approved programme data systems where appropriate.
- Apply consistent standards for geographic data management, documentation, accuracy and presentation.

**E. Capacity Building and User Support**

- Train and coach programme, MEAL and field staff in the use of DHIS2, digital data collection platforms, dashboards and GIS outputs.
- Develop user guides, standard operating procedures and training materials for data systems and reporting processes.
- Provide technical guidance to users on data entry, validation, analysis and interpretation, adapting explanations to different levels of technical ability.
- Support field teams to resolve issues with mobile data collection devices and applications when these directly affect programme data collection or submission.
- Gather user feedback and identify opportunities to improve system usability, adoption and data workflows.

**F. System Improvement and Innovation**

- Identify opportunities to simplify data workflows, automate routine processes and reduce duplication or manual handling.
- Assess and recommend improvements to data systems and tools based on programme needs, data protection considerations, usability and sustainability.
- Monitor relevant developments in data management, DHIS2, GIS and data visualization, recommending practical improvements where beneficial.
- Maintain an inventory of programme data platforms, relevant subscriptions and system dependencies within the role’s remit, coordinating procurement or licensing matters with the responsible team.

**G. Limited ICT Support (Maximum 10% of Role)**

- Provide limited troubleshooting for devices, connectivity or software only where an issue directly prevents the use of programme data systems or digital data collection tools.
- Refer general hardware, network, server, email, account administration, cybersecurity infrastructure and helpdesk issues to the designated ICT team or service provider.
- Do not assume responsibility for organisation-wide network or server administration, general end-user IT support, email administration or overall ICT infrastructure management.

**Required Qualifications and Experience:**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Data Management, Computer Science, Information Technology, Statistics, GIS, Monitoring and Evaluation, or a closely related field.
- Specialized training or certification in DHIS2 and GIS is required, or equivalent demonstrable technical expertise supported by relevant training and practical experience.

**Experience**

- At least three years of relevant experience in data management, information systems, digital data collection, database administration or programme data systems.
- Demonstrated practical experience configuring or administering DHIS2, including metadata management, indicators, validation rules, user roles or dashboards.
- Experience with GIS software such as QGIS or ArcGIS and with spatial analysis and map production. Experience designing, maintaining or analyzing databases, with knowledge of SQL Server, MySQL or comparable database technologies.
- Experience using digital data collection platforms such as KoboToolbox, CommCare or DHIS2 Mobile.
- Demonstrated ability to develop dashboards and data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau or similar tools.
- Experience supporting and training non-technical users and working collaboratively with programme and MEAL teams.
- Experience in an NGO, humanitarian or development programme environment is an advantage.

**4. Technical Skills**

- Strong working knowledge of DHIS2 configuration, metadata management, data quality controls and reporting.
- Practical GIS skills, including spatial data management, analysis and thematic mapping. • Proficiency in data visualization and reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
- Knowledge of database design, data structures, data cleaning and SQL; Python or R is an advantage.
- Understanding of data protection, access control, confidentiality, secure data handling and backup principles.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills focused on data systems and programme information needs.

**5. Core Competencies and Personal Attributes**

- Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.
- Commitment to data accuracy, integrity, confidentiality and responsible data use.
- Ability to translate technical concepts into clear guidance for non-technical colleagues.
- Strong communication, facilitation and training skills.
- Collaborative approach and ability to work effectively with programme, MEAL and field teams.
- Proactive, organized and able to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
- Continuous improvement mindset, with an emphasis on practical and sustainable solutions.
- Commitment to the mission, vision and values of Feed the Children.

**Commitment to Equal Employment**

At **Feed the Children**, we believe in Equal Employment Opportunities. Therefore, we consider all applicants based on merit, regardless of race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are also committed to promoting a gender-responsive approach as a cross-cutting principle throughout our organization.

**Safeguarding Policy**

**Feed the Children** strives to provide an environment free from sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment in all locations where humanitarian assistance and development programs are implemented. Feed the Children has a zero-tolerance policy toward sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment. We expect all employees to uphold the highest ethical standards, protect the organization's integrity and reputation, and ensure that all work is conducted honestly and fairly, in accordance with Feed the Children's Safeguarding and related policies.

We are committed to keeping children safe. Therefore, our recruitment and selection process includes background checks, reflecting our commitment to child safeguarding.

Our primary commitment is to foster a culture that prioritizes the promotion of safe and protective environments for children participating in the various programs implemented by Feed the Children in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, ensuring zero tolerance for any form of harm, abuse, or mistreatment of children.

**Commitment to Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion**

Feed the Children is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, respectful, and safe work environment where everyone is treated fairly and with dignity and respect. Feed the Children expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or workplace bullying in any work environment. As part of our strategy, we aim to increase the representation and recruitment of women across our workforce, as well as individuals from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds.

jobs.title: Regional Ebola Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Starting Date**
January 2026 – 24 months, full-time

**Role Summary**
The Regional Ebola Coordinator is responsible for coordinating, supporting, and representing Medair's Ebola Treatment Centre activities in Mambasa, Biakato, and other Ebola response locations established beyond Medair's existing operational bases.

Based in Bunia, the role ensures that the operational needs, priorities, and challenges of these remote treatment centres are effectively represented within Medair's Ebola response structure and with external stakeholders.

The Regional Ebola Coordinator serves as the principal focal point for Mambasa and Biakato and any response in new locations, facilitating communication between the treatment centres and Bunia-based support functions while ensuring that logistics, finance, human resources, administration, security, and programme support are provided in a timely and effective manner.

Working closely with the Project Coordinator and Country Ebola Coordinator, the Regional Ebola Coordinator supports the implementation of Ebola response activities through practical coordination, stakeholder engagement, representation, problem-solving, and operational oversight. The role contributes to maintaining high-quality service delivery while ensuring that the specific needs of the remote treatment centres are adequately represented both internally and externally.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Coordination**
Act as the primary coordination focal point for Medair's Ebola Treatment Centres in Mambasa, Biakato and new locations to be identified

Monitor operational activities and support the effective implementation of programme objectives in each location.

Identify operational constraints, emerging risks, and resource gaps and facilitate timely solutions.

Support planning, prioritisation, and implementation of activities in coordination with field teams and management.

Assist in balancing priorities between activities in and around Bunia and those in the remote treatment centres.

**Internal Support Coordination**
Coordinate closely with logistics, finance, human resources, supply chain, administration, security, and other support functions to ensure timely support to the locations.

Follow up on operational requests and ensure support departments respond effectively to field requirements.

Facilitate communication and collaboration between field teams, Bunia-based management, and technical advisors.

Ensure support services remain aligned with operational priorities.

**Representation and Stakeholder Engagement**
Represent the needs, priorities, and operational challenges of the field locations within Medair and with local authorities, health officials, coordination structures, and response partners.

Develop and maintain effective relationships with relevant external stakeholders.

Attend meetings and coordination forums relating to Mambasa and Biakato and any new locations

Prepare updates and briefing notes for the Country Ebola Coordinator to support participation in wider strategic coordination forums.

Represent Medair professionally and confidently in challenging or high-pressure situations involving external stakeholders.

**Support to Leadership**
Support the Project Coordinator in the practical coordination of activities in Mambasa and Biakato. And new locations

Provide regular analysis and recommendations concerning operational priorities, risks, and support requirements.

Ensure that management is informed of significant developments affecting programme implementation.

Contribute to operational planning and response decision-making for the assigned region.

**Monitoring and Reporting**
Contribute to operational reporting, situation updates, planning documents, and performance reviews.

Monitor key operational indicators and identify areas requiring additional support or intervention.

Promote accountability, effective communication, and adherence to Medair policies and procedures.

**Reporting Line**
Line Manager: Country Ebola Coordinator

**Education and experience**
Relevant university degree, with postgraduate, security, and leadership training desirable. Training in Public Health an advantage but not essential,

At least 2 years’ experience in managing programmes in international public health work, with at least 1 year in humanitarian emergency context. Experience in Ebola/VHF or infectious disease outbreaks strongly preferred.

Strong project management skills with the ability to support, oversee and coordinate multiple projects

Fluent English and French (spoken and written).

Experience in the design, monitoring of implementation and evaluation of public health programmes.

Strong knowledge of humanitarian principles, Sphere and CHS Standards.

Good report and proposal writing skills. Experience of external representation.

**Behavioral Skills**
Strong servant leadership skills with a consultative management style.

Creative, open-minded, flexible, self-learner, with good understanding of cross-cultural issues.

Capacity to work under pressure and manage personal stress levels.

Able to oversee multiple tasks, prioritising and delegating as required.

Excellent communication and diplomacy skills. Ability to represent the organization confidently externally.

**‍Team Spiritual Life**
Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

jobs.title: Employment Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
- Participate in program meetings, trainings, and professional development activities; follow all IRC policies including safeguarding and confidentiality standards.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, workforce development, or related field strongly preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of case management, employment, job placement, or business experience in a social services setting.
- Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of U.S. job search process and ability to coach clients through securing employment.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking/presentation skills preferred.
- Proven ability to problem-solve, prioritize tasks, and meet goals independently or as part of a team.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** ($20.97/hour). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

At the IRC, we seek to build a welcoming, inclusive environment not only for our refugee clients, but for all of our employees. As an equal opportunity employer, we value the strength found in the diversity of voices, experiences, and backgrounds who join us in our work. Fostering an inclusive culture with equitable practices is everyone's responsibility, and we regularly offer trainings and opportunities to learn more and find ways to do better. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, socioeconomic status, or disability status. We are dedicated to ensuring that disabled individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. In your application, please feel free to indicate your preferred pronouns.

We recognize that few applicants may "check all the boxes," but that each person has their own unique strengths that they would bring to the table. In our commitment to building a diverse and authentic work culture, we invite you to apply anyway. You belong here.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Project Director
jobs.description:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a Project Director to join our team. The Project Director will lead the strategy and delivery of GRC’s worker-led monitoring and remedy programme in Cambodia’s garment sector and will be accountable for its quality and results. The role will shape and convene the programme’s multi-stakeholder platform, bringing together trade unions, civil society organisations, government, employers and international brands and make sure worker-generated evidence leads to remedy and to changes in sourcing practices. Alongside this, they will manage the in-country team, oversee partner relationships, budget and donor reporting and make sure the project is delivered safely for workers, partners and staff.

**Full / Part-time:** Full-time

**Location:** Remote (with regular travel to Cambodia)

**The Role**

- Develop and lead the strategy for the programme against its workplan and budget, adapting the approach as required.
- Represent GRC with government actors, including the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, as well as suppliers, international brands and buyers, multi-stakeholder initiatives, donors and embassies.
- Lead cross-cutting work on responsible sourcing and labour rights, linking Cambodian evidence to brand due diligence and relevant regulation.
- Develop and facilitate workshops, multi-stakeholder events and training courses.
- Lead advocacy activities in-country, including launch events, roundtables and briefings.
- Set priorities for the team and make sure deliverables are completed on time and to a high standard.
- Oversee how documented cases are turned into remedy, whether through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, or advocacy.
- Ensure the program complies with donor and GRC financial rules, working with GRC’s finance team.
- Lead the preparation of narrative reports, workplans and other donor deliverables.
- Build a robust understanding of the training needs, strategic plans and priorities of workers and workers' organisations.
- Lead the rollout of a bilingual documentation and monitoring tool in Cambodia with trade unions, CSOs and paralegals, including training, data quality and secure data handling.
- Provide leadership and support to the worker centres and worker monitors.
- Manage relationships with trade union and CSO partners, including any sub-grant or partnership agreements, capacity support and oversight.
- Mentor consultants and team members to help them perform to their full potential.
- Hold in-country responsibility for safeguarding, do-no-harm and security, including informed consent, protecting the identity of workers and union members, and reporting concerns under GRC policy.
- Monitor the political and civic space context, including retaliation risks to workers and unions, and maintain a project risk register and security plan.
- Make sure gender, including gender-based violence and harassment at work, is reflected in programme design and delivery.
- Identify opportunities for future work, collaboration, and funding in Cambodia and the region, consistent with GRC's strategic priorities.

**Your Background**

- 8+ years of experience in labour rights, business and human rights, or related legal practice.
- Qualified with a law degree, LLM or other postgraduate qualification in human rights, labour or international law, or equivalent is desirable.
- Practical experience addressing labour rights abuses in Cambodia, ideally in the garment and apparel sector.
- Knowledge of international labour standards and business and human rights frameworks and how they apply to the garment and apparel sector.
- Experience designing or convening multi-stakeholder processes involving unions, business and government, ideally in garment supply chains
- Practical experience working with trade unions, civil society organisations, businesses and government institutions on labour rights or corporate accountability.
- Experience engaging international brands and suppliers on labour rights, remediation and human rights due diligence.
- Experience developing programme or organisational strategy, including partnerships and funding models.
- A clear understanding of the risks facing workers and union representatives in Cambodia, and experience working safely and confidentially in a sensitive environment.
- Experience leading teams and managing donor-funded programs, including budget management.
- Experience designing and delivering training and workshops.
- Experience applying gender-responsive approaches, including on gender-based violence and harassment at work.
- Strategic and diplomatic, being able to hold the confidence of unions, brands and governments while keeping worker interests centred.
- Proactive and practical, anticipates problems, proposes solutions and can break a strategy down into workable steps.
- Flexible and willing to support deliverables beyond the core remit when needed.
- Well organised and able to manage competing urgent demands.
- Fluent in written and spoken English.
- Experience with worker-led monitoring, documentation or investigations, including handling sensitive data, is desirable.
- Experience coordinating multi-partner programmes, including indicator tracking and sub-grant management, is desirable.
- Experience engaging with international garment brands, suppliers and other business actors on labour rights violations, remediation and human rights due diligence is desirable.

jobs.title: Logistics Assistant (Local Nationals only)
jobs.description:
**Organizational Profile**

Founded in 1991, Secours Islamique France (SIF) is a national and international solidarity NGO that has worked in France and around the world for over 30 years. SIF acts wherever there are humanitarian and social needs, delivering emergency relief, development programs and advocacy campaigns without proselytism or discrimination.

The SIF Kenya & Somalia Mission was registered in 2012 and currently implements humanitarian and development programs in Education and Child Welfare, Food Security and Livelihoods, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) across Kenya and Somalia.

**Job Summary**

SIF is seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Logistics Assistant to manage overall logistics operations in Nairobi, supporting SIF programs and staff. Reporting directly to the Head of Mission, the successful candidate will ensure logistics activities comply with Kenyan regulations, SIF procedures and donor guidelines.

The successful candidate will be responsible for:

- Procurement: Collect supplier quotations, prepare purchase documents and follow up deliveries in line with SIF and donor procedures, including supplier screening and record keeping.
- Fleet Management: Prepare movement plans, keep vehicle and fuel logs, and coordinate servicing, insurance and licensing of vehicles and generators.
- Stock Management: Receive and check goods against purchase orders, keep stock and asset records up to date, and support stock counts.
- Office Support: Keep office utilities, equipment and logistics files in good working order.
- Reporting and Compliance: Contribute to monthly logistics reports, support audits and report any security or compliance concerns promptly.

The successful candidate should be qualified in:

- Degree or diploma in purchasing and procurement, supply chain management, business administration or a related field
- Relevant experience of three to four years in logistics, procurement or supply chain management with an NGO
- Good knowledge of logistics principles, including inventory, fleet and asset management
- Basic knowledge of electricity, engines and vehicle mechanics; a valid driving licence is an advantage
- Very good skills in Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook
- Well organised, able to prioritise under pressure, with strong attention to detail
- A team player with integrity, accountability and a commitment to safeguarding.

**Do No Harm Principle**

Secours Islamique France considers diversity a strength. We therefore review all applications, provided they demonstrate the skills required for the position to be filled. As a humanitarian NGO, SIF is committed to respecting the humanitarian principle of “Do No Harm” and ensures that the safety of our beneficiaries (including children), employees, volunteers, partners, and service providers is a primary consideration in all its activities. SIF maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of fraud, corruption, psychological/sexual harassment, abuse or violence of any kind, and, more broadly, any breach of legislation, regulations, the Child Safeguarding Policy (CSP), or the internal code of conduct, both at headquarters and in the field. In line with these principles, this position is subject to a criminal record check as well as professional reference checks. Our charter is a genuine commitment: we mobilize all of our staff to promote, share, and uphold the principles set out. Together, let’s rise to the challenge for solidarity that transcends differences.

jobs.title: Technical Field Manager - Team Leader
jobs.description:
**Technical Field Manager Team Leader, Syria**

**The starting salary package for this position is £78,436 GBP including all allowances.**

**Expanding Our Syria Programme – We’re Recruiting for two Permanent Positions.**

**Location: These two positions will be based in the northwest and northeast of the country, operating from Hama and Raqqa, respectively, with regular travel between team locations within their assigned areas.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

Our Technical Field Manager Team Leader leads, oversees and safely manages mine/ERW clearance, EOD and IEDD operations within the project area, in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and consistent with MAG's policies and mandate.

The role manages Technical Field Managers (TFMs) and other technical staff, overseeing their work either as direct line manager or roaming technical specialist, and performing a quality assurance role across their output.

The Technical Field Manager – Team Leader supports the TOM in developing project strategy, plans, proposals and budgets for technical training and operations, and represents MAG within the project area.

**About the Syria programme:**

MAG has been responding to the Syria crisis since 2013, working to support development by finding and destroying the explosive remnants of war so that communities can raise their families and pursue their livelihoods in a safe and secure environment, free from fear of death or injury. In addition to our current programme in the North East, we are expanding our life-saving initiatives further throughout Syria. You will join our growing team to support across all of Syria, based on where and how opportunities arise in the future.

**Responsibilities:**

**Operations**

• Plan, prioritise and coordinate clearance operations within the identified project area to achieve project outputs.

• Supervise and conduct MAG field operations, including manual, and or integrated mechanical clearance assets, Battle Area Clearance (BAC), EOD and IED clearance, as relevant to the programme.

• Implement all aspects of mine, EOD and IED clearance operations and related tasks within the project, in line with SOPs and as directed by the TOM.

• Ensure full knowledge and implementation of all SOPs, drills and other work practices.

• Assist the STM to Review, develop and revise SOPs, as appropriate, for the TOM's approval.

• Conduct ongoing risk assessment to maximise the safety of operations.

• Monitor and evaluate operational tasks to ensure effectiveness.

• Conduct reconnaissance and survey of EO-contaminated areas, as appropriate.

• Maintain in-depth, up-to-date knowledge of explosive ordnance and technical equipment in the theatre of operations.

• Coordinate with Community Liaison Manager - TL and IM on the planning and delivery of technical operations, where appropriate.

• Ensure the maintenance and safe storage of project materials and equipment (including explosives and accessories).

• Perform a quality assurance role across the work of TFMs and field teams within the project, escalating non-conformities to the TOM.

• Advise and assist the TOM on new systems and procedures to improve productivity and safety.

• Conduct assessments and technical missions on behalf of MAG in-country and worldwide, as required by the TOM.

• Deputise for the TOM when required, including assuming operational management responsibility.

**Capacity Building**

• Assist the TOM and the Standards & Training Manager (STM) with the design, development, delivery and evaluation of appropriate training programmes for technical personnel.

• Oversee the day-to-day training and development of TFMs and national staff in mine and EOD clearance activities, in line with MAG SOPs.

• Build and maintain good working relationships with all staff to support capacity-building objectives.

• Assist the CD/TOM with the recruitment of national technical staff.

• Motivate and develop the technical team to perform to a high standard.

**Management and HR**

• Manage, motivate and develop TFMs and the technical team within the project to a high standard, including international staff where applicable.

• Ensure 1-1’s take place, objectives are set and appraisals take place annually to identify and address development and training needs.

• Ensure HR policies and procedures are implemented in consultation with the TOM and MAG HQ.

• Participate in the recruitment of project staff, in line with MAG's policies and procedures.

• Hold regular Ops team meetings to keep staff informed of project activities.

**Communication and Reporting**

• With the TOM, liaise with and represent MAG to donors, implementing partners, local officials and other agencies, to further MAG's aims and support operational efficiency.

• Keep the TOM fully briefed on technical and operational issues and any difficulties arising.

• Assist the TOM with relevant and useful information and case studies on MAG's activities.

• Submit accurate operational reports as directed by the TOM, and produce other technical reports and documents as required.

• Assist the TOM with the development and production of project proposals, reports and budgets.

• Keep staff informed of wider programme issues, developments and achievements within MAG.

• Ensure that thorough investigation reports on incidents/accidents are completed and provided to the TOM, with details of action taken, in line with MAG policies.

• Contribute to operational planning to improve project outputs.

**Health, Safety and Security**

• Monitor the security situation in your work location and areas of operations, keeping the TOM informed of risks and developments.

• Ensure MAG health and safety requirements are complied with in your area of operations and field accommodations (if applicable), including, ensuring duty of care to staff.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Essential Experience**

• Experience of working in HMA operations in developing countries that are contaminated by remnants of conflict including humanitarian IED clearance.

• Experience of managing manual mine clearance (MMC), Battle Area Clearance (BAC), EOD and IED clearance operations.

• Experience of managing integrated clearance assets within manual and mechanical clearance operations.

• Experience of managing field operations, including through other field managers or team leaders.

• Experience of leading, motivating and managing a diverse team of people.

• Experience of mentoring and coaching others.

• Experience of managing and conducting formal or informal training and the transfer of skills to others.

• Experience of working independently for extended periods of time in stand-alone environments with minimal supervision.

• Experience in managing teams conducting Improvised Explosive Device Disposal (IEDD).

• Experience in conducting IEDD render safe procedures in a humanitarian environment.

**Essential Skills and Knowledge**

• Highly authoritive technical knowledge of Explosive Ordnance and clearance techniques including IED clearance, including any new developments. At a minimum this is to be at the level of supervisor in line with IMAS 09.10/01/2023

• Ability to develop, review and comply with security and technical SOPs.

• Ability to contribute technical knowledge and clearance targets to proposals and reports.

• Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to plan and coordinate activities and projects.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• Good literacy, numeracy and IT skills.

**Essential Qualifications**

• Explosive Ordnance Qualification to IMAS Level 3+ in line with IMAS 09.10/01/2023 (Advanced Explosive Theory, Bulk Demolitions, Air Dropped Weapons, Guided Weapons, Chemical Ordnance (Basic), Armoured Fighting Vehicle Clearance) This should be from a relevant and recognised military, civilian or HMA NGO.

**Desirable Experience, Skills, Knowledge and Aptitude**

· Understanding of managing Information Management Systems (including Esri – ArcGIS, IMSMA)

· Experience in managing teams conducting mechanically assisted land release.

· Experience in managing teams conducting debris management and rubble clearance.

· Experience in managing teams conducting EOD and clearance in an urban environment.

· Knowledge of research and development of innovative HMA tools and procedures

· Knowledge and experience In Weapons and Ammunition management, including ammunition processing.

· Experience in manging Bulk Demolitions and advanced EOD techniques including render safe of Aerial Bombs, Guided Weapons and Chemical Ordnance.

· Advanced Knowledge of IT tools (Microsoft Office (advanced Excel), Outlook 365, SharePoint, Power BI)

· Knowledge and experience in foreign languages (Arabic).

**Desirable Qualifications**

· Improvised Explosive Device Disposal (IEDD) up to Level 3+ in line with IMAS 09.31/01/2019. This should be from a relevant and recognised military, civilian or HMA NGO.

· Explosive Ordnance Qualification to IMAS Level 3+ in line with IMAS 09.10/01/2023 (Advanced Explosive Theory, Bulk Demolitions, Air Dropped Weapons, Guided Weapons, Chemical Ordnance (Basic), Armoured Fighting Vehicle Clearance) This should be from a relevant and recognised military, civilian or HMA NGO.

· Ammunition Technical/Ammunition Technical Officer qualification or equivalent. This should be in line with the competencies outlined in Ammunition Technical Guidelines 1.90 up to level 6. This should be from a relevant and recognised military, civilian or HMA NGO.

· Formal Accident & Incident Investigation training. This should be from a relevant and recognised military, civilian or HMA NGO

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

Women are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Benefits:**

- **Renumeration Package**: **£78,436 per annum including basic salary and all allowances and this increases with service. (for IEDD up to Level 3+ in line with IMAS 09.31/01/2019 certified candidates a £6,200 allowance per annum will be added).**
- **Accommodation:** MAG will provide accommodation in-country.
- **Leave**: We recognize our staff work hard and need the appropriate time out to stay motivated. You'll have a minimum of eight weeks out of the programme per year.
- **Flights**: MAG provides four international flights home per year.
- **Insurance**: Internationally contracted, programme based staff are automatically covered by MAG's comprehensive insurance package including: Personal accident and medical expenses insurance; Death by natural causes insurance and access to 24-hour medical assistance.

jobs.title: Health Supply Chain Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**1. Job Overview**

The Health Supply Chain Specialist will provide integrated operational and technical leadership to strengthen supply chain performance across four critical health program areas, including but not limited to: Nutrition (with a focus on Ready-to-Use Food, or RUF), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH, covering Family Planning commodities and Postpartum Hemorrhage prevention and treatment supplies), Primary Healthcare (PHC, covering essential medicines and primary-level clinical supplies), and Infection and Disease Prevention and Control (IDPC). Focus will be on IRCs Impact at Scale ‘’go-big’’ designated country programs.

This is a project management and integration role embedded in Global Supply Chain (GSC), with a Management in Partnership (MIP) reporting line to Deputy Director, Health Unit (HU). The role translates health program priorities into optimized, scalable supply chain solutions, and directly advances the IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) objectives across all program areas.

Working in close collaboration with Country Programs, Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs), Global Procurement, Nutrition, SRH and IDPC Technical Leads, and external partners (including UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, other UN agencies and NGOs, and vendors), the Specialist will cover demand planning, forecasting, procurement coordination, and delivery across all four commodity areas, including essential medicines and IDPC commodities used in IRC health facilities and outbreak response. The role will also act as a key connector between field realities and global supply strategies — ensuring operational challenges are converted into actionable learning, system
improvements, and scalable solutions.

**2. Key Responsibilities**

**2.1 Integrated Demand Planning and Forecasting**

- Develop and maintain a consolidated global demand plan covering RUF (Nutrition), IDPC and key SRH commodities (FP and PPH) for Go-big countries.
- Lead responses to specific commodity shortages and urgent projects across all countries.
- Analyze consumption data across programs (procured and Contribution in Kind -CIK) to inform forecasting and procurement decisions.
- Implement forecasts and supply chain plans for FY27 and FY28 for all Go-Big countries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.
- Regularly analyze and report on demand, stock, pipeline, and spend data at global and country levels, incorporating stockout data and mitigation actions.
- Proactively monitor global supply outlook for RUF, SRH and IDPC commodities and escalate alerts within program, supply chain and leadership.

**2.2 SRH Supply Chain Strategy and UNFPA Engagement**

- Lead scoping and stakeholder engagement to design and implement a UNFPA relationship strengthening strategy, including pre-positioning, CIK strengthening at global/country level, service and delivery improvements etc.
- Classify IRC country programs into operational SRHR supply chain profiles (e.g., PPH-focused, LARC-driven (long‑acting reversible contraception), UNFPA-dependent, emergency-only) to support differentiated supply chain strategies and prioritization.
- In alignment with country scale plans, support short-, medium-, and long-term improvement activities anchored to each country's operational profile and risk level.
- Engage with vendors like DKT, MSI, and other partners to leverage their in-country distribution networks and broad FP/PPH product portfolios.

**2.3 RUF SOP Implementation and Fraud Risk Management**

- Coordinate with Ethics and Risk and Compliance (R&C), and country focal points to strengthen fraud risk monitoring, incident review, and mitigation actions.
- Track RUF SOP adoption, compliance gaps, and corrective actions to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including travel to at least one country program.

**2.4 IDPC-Specific Supply Chain Strengthening**

- Assess the availability of key designated IDPC commodities and supply chain readiness against WHO IDPC minimum requirements at health facility level, and support country teams in developing corrective action plans.
- Support country programs in forecasting and pre-positioning key designated IDPC and essential medicine stocks for outbreak and epidemic preparedness and response.

**2.5 Supply Chain Strengthening and Capacity Building**

- Build country capacity, with a focus on pharmacists, in forecasting and demand planning, stock monitoring and stockout mitigation, and supply and sourcing strategies.
- Provide targeted technical support to address bottlenecks and operational challenges in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH programs.

**2.6 Stakeholder Engagement and External Representation**

- Cultivate strong relationships with UNFPA, UNICEF supply chain teams, WHO, DKT, MSI, and other key SRH, nutrition, and IDPC stakeholders.
- Represent IRC in relevant external supply chain and humanitarian coordination platforms, including the Global Health Cluster and IDPC technical working groups.
- Act as the global focal point for CIK deliveries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.

**2.7 Reporting, Data, and Knowledge Management**

- Document best practices and lessons learned to inform future improvements across all commodity areas.
- Produce a data-driven summary report linking supply levels to FY27 and FY28 I@S targets for Nutrition, IDPC and SRH Go-Big countries.
- Maintain an evidence repository (data, reports, learnings) for handover to Nutrition, SRH, IDPC and GSC teams.
- Lead the integration of Impact at Scale (I@S) priorities and core indicators into the Global Pharma Indicator (GPI) Dashboard, in collaboration with relevant I@S Leads, the Health Unit/Pharma Specialist, and Global Supply Chain teams. Ensure the dashboard tracks key pharmaceutical and nutrition supply chain performance indicators aligned with I@S objectives, enabling progress monitoring, gap identification, and evidence-based decision-making.

**3. Key Working Relationships**

**Reporting Line**

Position Reports to: Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain, with a Management in Partnership (MIP) line to the Deputy Director, Health Unit, and with strong technical engagement with the Global Practice Leads for Nutrition, SRH, Primary Healthcare (PHC), and Infection and Disease Prevention and Control (IDPC).

**Internal Relationships**

- Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs)
- Nutrition Technical Advisors, SRH specialists, and Health / PHC and IDPC Technical Advisors —
- Senior Pharmacy Specialist & Deputy Director for Pharma QA
- Country program teams and CP pharmacists —
- Global Procurement and Senior Procurement Manager for Health
- Risk & Compliance (R&C) and ECU
- Research and Nutrition/SRH/IDPC leads

**External Relationships**

- UNFPA, UNICEF, Hulo/EUHAB/Airlink, Vendors, WHO, INGOs,

**4. Job Requirements**

**Essential Qualifications**

- Degree in supply chain management, pharmacy, business administration, public health, nutrition, or related field — or equivalent additional experience.
- Minimum 4 years' experience in commodity procurement or supply chain management in humanitarian or development settings.
- Proven experience managing health commodities across at least two of the following areas: nutrition (therapeutic foods, RUF), SRH (FP, PPH supplies), primary healthcare (essential medicines), or infection and disease prevention and control.
- Demonstrated understanding of donor procurement regulations — particularly U.S. Department of State (formerly USAID/BHA), ECHO, FCDO, and UNFPA/UNICEF frameworks.
- Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills in supply chain optimization, forecasting, and risk mitigation.
- Familiarity with Nutrition supply chain challenges (RUTF/RUF, therapeutic food systems), SRH supply chain dynamics (FP method mix, PPH commodity management), primary healthcare essential medicines management, and IDPC commodity requirements.
- Experience with MEAL, ERPs, or Logistics Management Information Systems (LMIS); experience with Power BI or similar data visualization tools is an asset.
- Understanding of international freight (Incoterms), warehousing, transportation logistics, and last-mile delivery in humanitarian contexts.
- Knowledge of pharmaceutical management — vendor prequalification, quality assurance, cold chain, distribution, and pharmacovigilance — is an advantage.
- Exceptional interpersonal and stakeholder management skills; ability to engage credibly with country program staff, global leads, and external partners.
- Familiarity with UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, and NGO supply chain partnership modalities.
- Proactive, results-oriented, service-focused.
- Fluency in English required; French proficiency is a strong advantage.

**Key Competencies**

- Strategic thinking and systems-level supply chain leadership, including the ability to integrate multiple health program supply chains (Nutrition, SRH, PHC, and IDPC) into a unified, efficient approach.
- Ability to synthesize complex multi-country data into clear, actionable recommendations.
- Collaboration and effectiveness in multicultural, matrixed environments.
- Commitment to ethical standards and to the IRC Way values of Integrity, Service, Equality, and Accountability.
- Attention to detail; proactive risk identification and response.

**5. Additional Information**

**Working Environment**

- Remote work / standard office environment (location dependent).
- Travel upto 20%

IRC-UK is committed to equality of opportunity and to non-discrimination for all job applicants and employees, and we seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce regardless of gender, race, religious beliefs, nationality, ethnic/national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.

**Compensation (UK):** ***(GBP 41,767- GBP 49,599 - annually)***. Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.
