jobs.title: Development of Integrated M&E Data Management and Visualization System
jobs.description:
**Wildlife Conservation Society**

Term of Reference

Development of Integrated M&E Data Management and Visualization System

**Background**

The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a US non-profit established in 1895 that saves wildlife and wild places around the world. WCS runs four zoos and an aquarium in New York and has global conservation programs in more than 50 countries. WCS uses science to discover and understand the natural world. This knowledge helps us engage and inspire decision-makers, communities, and millions of supporters to take action with us to protect the wildlife and wild places we all care about.

In Africa, WCS operates in 13 counties and 15 protected or conserved areas. WCS Global Conservation Programs generate thus a large volume of heterogeneous data, including financial and human resources records, law enforcement and wildlife protection data, wildlife survey and ecological monitoring data, socio-economic surveys data, and spatial datasets.

WCS Africa Hub requires a robust, centralized, and automated system to manage its data for Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) purposes. Current processes rely on fragmented data sources, necessitating a unified platform that can translate raw data into actionable insights for performance and impact tracking.

**Objective of the consultancy**

The primary objective of this consultancy is to design, develop, and deploy across WCS landscapes in Africa an integrated data management and visualization system. This system will streamline the lifecycle of data—from ingestion and validation to spatial and statistical visualization.

**Scope of Work**

In strict collaboration with the Regional Technical Directors and other technical leads, the consultant will be responsible for the following key functional areas:

***A. Data Collation & Integration***

- **Multi-Source Ingestion:** Build connectors for spreadsheet-based data (Excel, CSV, Google Sheets), including developing application programming interfaces (API) depending on data source locations.
- **Geospatial Integration:** Ensure the system can ingest and process GIS files (Esri Shapefile, GeoJSON, GPX, GeoTIFF, etc.) to map impact, including processes for automated updated versions of key datasets as they are released (e.g.forest loss form Global Forest Watch).
- **Centralized Repository:** Establish a structured database to house historical and real-time MEL indicators and associated information. To maintain data integrity and institutional memory, the system must be governed by a rigorous data governance framework that incorporates standardized metadata (defining data lineage and ownership), a comprehensive indicator dictionary (providing clear definitions, calculation formulas, and units of measure), and robust version control to track all modifications to datasets and system configurations over time.
- **Offline Functionality:** The system must include features for offline data entry and local caching to ensure full functionality in low-bandwidth areas or sites with no internet connectivity, with automated synchronization once a connection is re-established.

***B. Validation & Processing***

- **Automated Quality Checks:** Implement scripts for data cleaning, identifying outliers, and ensuring consistency across reporting periods.
- **Transformation Logic:** Create workflows to process raw inputs into standardized performance and impact indicators, including geospatial processing.

***C. Dynamic Visualization & Dashboarding***

- **Interactive Dashboards:** Develop a user-friendly interface featuring charts, heatmaps, and trend lines.
- **Custom Aggregation:** Users must be able to filter and aggregate data dynamically by:
- **Variables:** Region, sector, demographic, project identity/ type, etc. Disaggregation variables are defined for each indicator.
- **Timeframes:** Monthly, quarterly, annual, or custom ranges.
- **Spatial Visualization:** Integrated maps that overlay MEL data onto geographic layers.

**Phased approach**

The work will be structured around a phased approach. The first phase will focus on developing and implementing the system architecture and processes required for site-specific M&E, with the aim of directly supporting adaptive management at the site level. The second phase will integrate thematic indicators across relevant programmatic areas, while the third phase will incorporate high-level, regional and Africa-wide indicators to enable regional aggregation, performance monitoring, and strategic decision-making.

**Technical Requirements**

The proposed system must adhere to the following:

- **Scalability:** Ability to handle increasing data volumes and new sites over time.
- **Interoperability:** Compatible with existing organizational software and databases.
- **Security:** Role-based access control to protect sensitive MEL data.
- **User Autonomy:** The system should allow non-technical staff to generate basic reports without coding.
- **Accountability and transparency:** The system must maintain a clear and navigable traceability chain (audit trail) that allows users to drill down from high-level dashboard indicators directly to the specific raw datasets and the document folders containing the original means of verification (MoV; e.g., reports, photos, participant lists, etc.).

**Deliverables**

- **Inception Phase:**
- Deliverable: Technical Design Document
- Description: System architecture, data flow diagrams (including offline sync logic), and UI/UX wireframes.
- **Development Phase:**
- Deliverable: Beta Version (Prototype)
- Description: Functional system with core data ingestion capabilities and basic dashboarding.
- **Testing Phase:**
- Deliverable: Validation Report detailing
- Description: Results of UAT (User Acceptance Testing), including connectivity stress tests and bug fixes.
- **Deployment Phase:**
- Deliverable: Final System & Manuals
- Description: Full rollout, including source code, admin manuals, and user guides.
- **Training Phase:**
- Deliverable: Capacity building
- Description: Training sessions for MEL staff and system administrators

**Consultant Qualifications and Experience**

The consultant should meet the following minimum requirements:

- Advanced degree in Information Systems, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field.
- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in data architecture and systems design.
- Proven track record in developing M&E systems specifically for international development or conservation organizations with impact tracking.
- Demonstrated experience in GIS integration and advanced data modeling from flat files (Excel/CSV).
- Evidence of ability to create dynamic, interactive dashboards with multi-variable filtering and time-series analyses for business intelligence.
- Strong communication skills and ability to translate technical concepts into practical guidance.

**Application and Selection Criteria**

Interested candidates are requested to submit:

- A technical proposal outlining understanding of the assignment and proposed approach, including relevant examples of similar assignments (80%)
- A financial proposal (20%)
- Qualifications and CVs of key personnel (Lead Architect, GIS Specialist, and Data Analyst).

A detailed workplan, timeline, and deliverable schedule will be agreed at contract inception.

WCS reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal and is not bound to select the lowest-cost offer.

jobs.title: ETI (International Technical Expert) & HR Assistant
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

The ETI & HR Assistant is working under the HR Senior Officer and the overall supervision of the Head of Support Services.

She/He will support the HR and provide coordinated administrative, logistical, human-resources, and operational support to International Technical Experts (ETI).

The position requires a highly organized and detail-oriented professional who can manage travel, expert and interpreter coordination, recruitment administration, employee records, HR documentation, invoices, reimbursements, schedules, and confidential information.

**Job title**

International Technical Expert (ETI) & HR Assistant

**Reporting line**

Under the supervision of the HR Senior Officer

**Direct reports**

None

Main areas of responsibility

ETI & HR support and administration

**Main Responsibilities of the ETI & HR Assistant**

The role is structured around two complementary workstreams. The **ETI workstream** focuses on the support and administration of experts while the **HR workstream** covers recruitment, employee administration, HR records, insurance, training, and related staff support.

**1. ETI Support and Administration**

**Logistics and Financial Administration**

- Coordinate with Logistics department international and domestic travel for experts, including flights, train tickets, ground transportation, and hotel accommodation.
- Act as the primary administrative contact with Logistics and sometimes service providers, ensuring arrangements are accurate, timely, and aligned with approved requirements.
- Review and process invoices related to expert logistics and travel, including the preparation and submission of payment requests for approved services.
- Ensure compliance with applicable financial procedures, supporting-documentation requirements, and internal approval processes.

**Expert Onboarding, Security, and Presence Coordination**

- Support the onboarding of incoming experts by liaising with the Security Officer, Support Services, project managers, and relevant colleagues to ensure that administrative, logistical, and security arrangements are completed before and upon arrival.
- Maintain an accurate and up-to-date schedule of expert presence in-country, including planned and unplanned absences such as vacation, sick leave, and official missions.
- Facilitate effective coordination of expert presence information with HR, project teams, and headquarters.

**Legal and Immigration Administration**

- Coordinate and follow up on administrative procedures with the Head of Support Services, HQ and Country Director related to expert passports, visas, residency permits, and other required legal or immigration documentation.
- Maintain organized records, monitor deadlines, identify missing documents, and liaise with relevant authorities or service providers when required.

**Expert Reimbursements**

- Receive, review, and process expert reimbursement requests with the Finance department.
- Verify completeness, accuracy, and supporting documentation before submitting requests for financial approval.

## **Interpreter Coordination and Administration**

- When needed, liaise with procurement department on the administrative cycle of the Interpreter, including selection support, onboarding, assignment coordination, follow-up, and contract .
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records and documentation for Interpreter .
- Liaise with procurement department to assign Interpreterto experts according to operational needs, geographical area, workload, and availability, ensuring balanced and efficient allocation.
- Collect, review, and verify invoices, timesheets, and supporting documents submitted by Interpreterand prepare them for processing through EF workflow (Senior HR Officer, Procurement and Finance)

**Communication and Reporting Support**

- Act as the primary administrative link between Experts and the Communication Officer.
- Proactively collect relevant information, updates, achievements, and success stories from experts and provide timely content to support social-media and other external-communication activities.

**ETI Documentation Management**

- Maintain the central administrative repository for Expert-related documentation.
- Collect, verify, organize, and archive monthly reports, timesheets, travel documents, reimbursement records, legal and immigration documentation, contracts, and other deliverables required for coordination with HR and headquarters.

**2. HR Administration and Support**

**Recruitment Administration**

· Publish recruitment advertisements on specialized websites,

· Contact shortlisted candidates and organize interview appointments.

· Ensure logistics for technical tests (required equipment: PC, etc…) and interviews (room booking)

· Welcome new staff members and provide briefings on HR procedures.

**Employee Administration and HR Records**

- Prepare and maintain employee HR files and provide required hiring documentation to new employees.
- Monitor leave requests and ensure that related documentation is correctly filed and archived.
- Coordinate requests for administrative documents, including employment, salary, and leave certificates, with the payroll or relevant HR focal point.
- Support employee offboarding by preparing the required administrative documentation.
- Enter and maintain employee data in the HR database and other relevant HR tools.
- Update records following changes such as work accidents, maternity leave, absences, contract amendments, and other employment-related developments.

**Health Insurance and Employee Case Administration**

- Manage the health-insurance file in coordination with the designated insurance contact.
- Maintain accurate records, follow up on supporting documentation, and ensure requests are directed to the appropriate parties.
- Provide administrative follow-up on cases involving unfitness for work and disciplinary sanctions, while maintaining strict confidentiality and respecting applicable internal procedures and legal requirements.

**HR Reporting and Mandatory Requirements**

- Support the preparation of mandatory HR reports and statements, including HR dashboards, social reports, and other internal or external reporting requirements assigned by the HR Senior Officer. Training and Skills Administration
- Support the collection of training and skills-development needs from employees and teams.
- Liaise with the Procurement team to obtain quotations from local training providers.
- Coordinate training logistics, including venue booking, participant communication, reminders, attendance follow-up, and documentation.

**Common Standards and Coordination Requirements**(Across both workstreams, the position is expected to):

- Maintain accurate, complete, and well-organized records.
- Protect confidential information relating to experts, interpreter, candidates, employees, contracts, remuneration, health insurance, disciplinary matters, and immigration documentation.
- Monitor deadlines proactively and communicate delays or missing information promptly.
- Apply internal administrative, financial, procurement, HR, security, and document-management procedures.
- Coordinate professionally with colleagues, candidates, experts, service providers, public authorities, and international partners.
- Provide clear updates and escalate sensitive, urgent, or unresolved matters to the HR Senior Officer or Head of Support Services.
- Demonstrate flexibility in managing simultaneous ETI and HR priorities in a fast-paced environment.

**Minimum Qualifications**

· Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Administration, Procurement, Supply Chain Management, or a closely related field.

· At least three years of experience in a similar HR, administration, operations, logistics, project-coordination, or support-services position.

· At least three years of experience with an international NGO, international organization, development agency, embassy, public-sector project, or similar institution is preferred or required according to organizational policy.

· Prior experience in logistics management, travel coordination, expert administration, language-assistant coordination, immigration administration, invoice processing, or reimbursement management is an asset.

· Experience supporting recruitment, employee files, leave administration, HR databases, onboarding, offboarding, insurance administration, training logistics, or HR reporting is required or strongly preferred.

· Good PC literacy and demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, with the ability to learn new administrative and HR systems.

· Fluency in written and spoken Arabic, and English. French would be a strong asset

Competencies

- Analytical Thinking
- Excellent organizational and time-management skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Strong ability to multi-task
- Teamwork skills

**French:**

**Présentation du poste**

L’assistant(e) ETI & RH travaille sous la responsabilité du/de la Chargé(e) RH senior et sous la supervision générale du Coordinateur fonctions transverses.

Il/Elle appuiera les RH et fournira un soutien administratif, logistique, en ressources humaines et opérationnel, de manière coordonnée, aux experts techniques internationaux (ETI).

Le poste exige un(e) professionnel(le) très organisé(e) et rigoureux(se), capable de gérer les déplacements, la coordination des experts et des interprètes, l’administration du recrutement, les dossiers du personnel, la documentation RH, les factures, les remboursements, les plannings et les informations confidentielles.

Intitulé du poste

Assistant(e) ETI et RH

Rattachement hiérarchique

Sous la supervision du/de la Chargé(e) RH senior

Subordonnés directs

Aucun

Principaux domaines de responsabilité

Appui et administration ETI & RH

**Principales responsabilités de l’assistant(e) ETI & RH**

Le poste s’articule autour de deux axes complémentaires. L’**axe ETI** porte sur l’appui et l’administration des experts, tandis que l’**axe RH** couvre le recrutement, l’administration du personnel, les dossiers RH, les assurances, la formation et le soutien associé aux employés.

**1. Appui et administration ETI**

**Logistique et administration financière**

- Coordonner avec le département Logistique les déplacements internationaux et nationaux des experts, y compris les vols, billets de train, transports terrestres et hébergements hôteliers.
- Servir de principal point de contact administratif avec la Logistique et, parfois, avec les prestataires de services, en veillant à ce que les dispositions prises soient exactes, ponctuelles et conformes aux exigences approuvées.
- Examiner et traiter les factures liées à la logistique et aux déplacements des experts, y compris la préparation et la soumission des demandes de paiement pour les services approuvés.
- Veiller au respect des procédures financières applicables, des exigences en matière de pièces justificatives et des processus internes d’approbation.

**Accueil des experts, sécurité et coordination de leur présence**

- Appuyer l’accueil des experts entrants en assurant la liaison avec le Responsable sécurité, les Services support, les chefs de projet et les collègues concernés, afin que les dispositions administratives, logistiques et de sécurité soient finalisées avant et à l’arrivée des experts.
- Tenir à jour un planning précis de la présence des experts dans le pays, y compris les absences prévues et imprévues telles que congés, congés maladie et missions officielles.
- Faciliter la coordination efficace des informations relatives à la présence des experts avec les RH, les équipes projet et le siège.

**Administration juridique et migratoire**

- Coordonner et assurer le suivi des démarches administratives avec le Coordinateur fonctions transverses, le siège et le Directeur pays concernant les passeports, visas, titres de séjour des experts et autres documents juridiques ou migratoires requis.
- Tenir des dossiers organisés, surveiller les échéances, identifier les documents manquants et assurer la liaison avec les autorités ou les prestataires de services concernés si nécessaire.

**Remboursements des experts**

- Recevoir, examiner et traiter les demandes de remboursement des experts avec le département Finance.
- Vérifier l’exhaustivité, l’exactitude et les pièces justificatives avant de soumettre les demandes pour approbation financière.

## **Coordination et administration des interprètes**

- Si nécessaire, assurer la liaison avec le département Achats sur le cycle administratif de l’interprète, y compris l’appui à la sélection, l’intégration, la coordination des missions, le suivi et le contrat.
- Tenir à jour des dossiers et une documentation exacts concernant l’interprète.
- Assurer la liaison avec le département Achats pour affecter l’interprèteaux experts selon les besoins opérationnels, la zone géographique, la charge de travail et la disponibilité, en garantissant une répartition équilibrée et efficace.
- Collecter, examiner et vérifier les factures, feuilles de temps et pièces justificatives soumises par l’interprèteet les préparer pour traitement via le circuit de validation d’EF (Chargé(e) RH senior, Achats et Finance)

**Appui en communication et reporting**

- Servir de principal relais administratif entre les experts et le/la Chargé(e) de communication.
- Collecter de manière proactive les informations, actualités, réalisations et témoignages de réussite des experts et fournir en temps utile des contenus pour appuyer les réseaux sociaux et les autres activités de communication externe.

**Gestion de la documentation ETI**

- Tenir le référentiel administratif central de la documentation relative aux experts.
- Collecter, vérifier, organiser et archiver les rapports mensuels, feuilles de temps, documents de voyage, justificatifs de remboursement, documents juridiques et migratoires, contrats et autres livrables nécessaires à la coordination avec les RH et le siège.

**2. Administration et appui RH**

**Administration du recrutement**

· Publier les offres d’emploi sur des sites spécialisés,

· Contacter les candidats présélectionnés et organiser les rendez-vous d’entretien.

· Assurer la logistique des tests techniques (équipement requis : PC, etc.) et des entretiens (réservation de salle)

· Accueillir les nouveaux collaborateurs et leur présenter les procédures RH.

**Administration du personnel et dossiers RH**

- Préparer et tenir à jour les dossiers RH des employés et remettre aux nouvelles recrues les documents d’embauche requis.
- Suivre les demandes de congé et veiller à ce que les documents correspondants soient correctement classés et archivés.
- Coordonner, avec le référent paie ou RH compétent, les demandes de documents administratifs, notamment les attestations d’emploi, de salaire et de congés.
- Appuyer le départ des employés en préparant les documents administratifs requis.
- Saisir et tenir à jour les données des employés dans la base de données RH et les autres outils RH pertinents.
- Mettre à jour les dossiers à la suite de changements tels que accidents du travail, congés maternité, absences, avenants aux contrats et autres évolutions liées à l’emploi.

**Assurance santé et suivi des dossiers individuels**

- Gérer le dossier d’assurance santé en coordination avec l’interlocuteur désigné de l’assureur.
- Tenir des dossiers exacts, assurer le suivi des pièces justificatives et veiller à ce que les demandes soient transmises aux bons interlocuteurs.
- Assurer le suivi administratif des dossiers d’inaptitude au travail et de sanctions disciplinaires, dans le strict respect de la confidentialité, des procédures internes applicables et des exigences légales.

**Reporting RH et obligations réglementaires**

- Appuyer la préparation des rapports et états RH obligatoires, y compris les tableaux de bord RH, les bilans sociaux et les autres exigences de reporting internes ou externes confiées par le/la Chargé(e) RH senior. Formation et développement des compétences
- Appuyer le recueil des besoins en formation et en développement des compétences des employés et des équipes.
- Assurer la liaison avec l’équipe Achats pour obtenir des devis auprès de prestataires de formation locaux.
- Coordonner la logistique des formations, notamment la réservation des lieux, la communication avec les participants, les rappels, le suivi des présences et la documentation.

**Normes communes et exigences de coordination** (Pour les deux axes, il est attendu du titulaire du poste de :

- Tenir des dossiers exacts, complets et bien organisés.
- Protéger les informations confidentielles relatives aux experts, interprètes, candidats, employés, contrats, rémunérations, assurance santé, questions disciplinaires et documents migratoires.
- Surveiller proactivement les échéances et signaler rapidement les retards ou informations manquantes.
- Appliquer les procédures internes administratives, financières, d’achats, RH, de sécurité et de gestion documentaire.
- Coordonner de manière professionnelle avec les collègues, candidats, experts, prestataires de services, autorités publiques et partenaires internationaux.
- Fournir des points d’information clairs et remonter les sujets sensibles, urgents ou non résolus au/à la Chargé(e) RH senior ou au Coordinateur fonctions transverses.
- Faire preuve de flexibilité pour gérer simultanément les priorités ETI et RH dans un environnement dynamique.

**Qualifications minimales**

· Licence (Bachelor) en gestion des ressources humaines, administration des affaires, administration, achats, gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ou domaine étroitement apparenté.

· Au moins trois ans d’expérience dans un poste similaire en RH, administration, opérations, logistique, coordination de projet ou services support.

· Au moins trois ans d’expérience au sein d’une ONG internationale, d’une organisation internationale, d’une agence de développement, d’une ambassade, d’un projet du secteur public ou d’une institution similaire, préférée ou exigée selon la politique de l’organisation.

jobs.title: Finance Officer
jobs.company: International Association for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
## **About ONSUR:**

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

**Location:** **Damascus**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The position holder will work under the technical supervision of the Finance Coordinator at the Head Office, and in coordination with Project Coordinators, to prepare periodic financial reports, monitor daily financial operations, and provide the necessary financial and administrative support to ensure the smooth implementation of project and office activities.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**Key Responsibilities**

- Verify implementing partners’ financial documentation as required.
- Review financial support agreements and supporting documentation to ensure accuracy, consistency, reasonableness, and compliance with organizational standards.
- Review and provide advice on budget modification requests and no-cost extension requests.
- Review financial audit reports to ensure compliance with the signed agreement and project budget.
- Maintain a complete, accurate, detailed, and up-to-date record of payments made to implementing partners.
- Conduct regular follow-up with implementing partners to obtain financial reports.
- Review interim and final financial reports and confirm amounts for additional payments.
- Initiate payment verification processes as required and follow up on any recoveries or reimbursements.
- Conduct spot financial checks in accordance with operational procedures.
- Support the Grants Manager in the preparation of unit cost plans.
- Train partners on grant regulations, rules, and requirements.
- • Ensure timely submission of financial reports in accordance with donor requirements.
- • Follow up on documentation, reports, and guidance related to program matters.
- • Monitor the posting and recording of transactions in the accounting system.
- • Electronically archive financial documents and ensure completeness of records in accordance with donor requirements.
- • Record accounting entries in the cash journal.
- • Prepare financial files for payment processing after receiving and reviewing them from the relevant support departments.
- • Perform monthly and annual project reconciliations.
- **Comply with the organizational Code of Conduct, Safeguarding Policy, and Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) Policy, and report any safeguarding or misconduct concerns.**

**Note:** The key responsibilities listed above are illustrative only. The employee may be assigned additional responsibilities in the future depending on the organizational structure of the department.

## **Required Qualifications & Experience**

**Education:**

- Bachelor's degree or institute diploma in Finance or Accounting.

**Experience:**

- 03 years of experience in an administrative finance/accounting position with a non-governmental organization (NGO).

**Technical Skills**

- Very good proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel.

**Core Competencies**

- Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to think and work strategically.
- Excellent attention to detail and outstanding data entry skills.
- Experience in budget preparation and financial reporting.
- Commitment to upholding the highest standards of **safeguarding, accountability**, technical integrity, impartiality, and professional ethics

**Languages:**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

**Child Protection Policy**

ONSUR maintains a strict **zero-tolerance policy** toward all forms of child abuse and exploitation. The organization is fully committed to creating and maintaining a **child-safe environment** across all areas of its work. All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

**Anti-Discrimination, Harassment, and Abuse Policy**

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. Discrimination, harassment, or abuse of any kind — whether based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, or military status — is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.

All staff are expected to **promote a culture of respect** and integrity. Participation in any form of abuse, harassment (verbal, physical, or sexual), intimidation, or exploitation — whether inside or outside the workplace — is a violation of ONSUR’s core values and policies.

**Diversity & Inclusion**

ONSUR is strongly committed to gender equality and **encourages qualified female candidates** to apply for this position.

jobs.title: Head of Support Services
jobs.description:
**Overall purpose of the role**: The HoSS ensures effective, efficient Finance, Administration, HR, IT and Supply Chain services across Syria, complying with DRC procedures and guidelines. As a Senior Management Team (SMT) member, the HoSS oversees programme support and timely achievement of annual support-function performance indicators, develops and implements country strategies, and improves operational systems, processes and policies supporting DRC’s mission. The role helps assess and implement global and regional organizational development and financial accountability initiatives. The HoSS ensures timely, appropriate communication with the Head of Program and support departments on finance, administration, supply chain and HR matters, proactively resolving differences and prioritizing time-sensitive tasks.

**Responsibilities**:

The key responsibilities outlined below are not exhaustive; additional duties, including ad hoc tasks, may be assigned to support the effective fulfillment of the role’s overall purpose.

## **Management**

- Lead and manage the Support service teams Managers and technically manage area support services teams (including people planning, performance, well-being and staff development).
- Manage, deliver and report on current operations programme support in geographic scope.
- Establish high performing support teams ensuring high-quality approaches are maintained.
- Develop and improve operational approaches, compliance, and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations.
- Ensure support for annual planning and review processes.

## **Operational Management**

- Oversee the operational support units for the country by providing strategic leadership and technical support to the areas under his/her supervision.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and transport systems.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation through frequent in-service training sessions and mentoring support.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives.
- Decentralization of support services functions and empowering area support teams to enhance the efficiency of support functions in country and area offices.

## **Workforce Planning and Operational Transitions**

- Lead workforce planning with Programme, HR, Finance and Area teams, forecasting staffing needs and costs against humanitarian priorities, funding scenarios and operational requirements.
- Develop and update country and field office organigrams, ensuring clear reporting lines, appropriate staffing structures and alignment with approved budgets.
- Coordinate support services readiness for operational scale-up and scale-down, including recruitment, redeployment and responsible staffing transitions, in line with DRC policies and applicable labour requirements.
- Lead coordinated support planning for new office setups, relocations and closures, covering staffing, budgets, premises, logistics, IT and administrative requirements to maintain operational continuity.

## **Strengthening Localization**

- Coordinate support services due diligence for new local implementing partners, assessing financial management, procurement, HR and internal control systems, and ensuring identified risks and capacity gaps are addressed before partnership approval.
- Oversee the timely review and verification of local implementing partners’ financial and support services reports, monitoring expenditure, supporting documentation and compliance with partnership agreements and donor requirements, and ensuring follow-up on discrepancies and corrective actions.
- Lead support services capacity building for local implementing partners through joint capacity assessments, tailored development plans, training and mentoring, strengthening systems, internal controls and reporting quality.
- Promote and develop a phased nationalization plan for the Syria operation with the Country Director, HR and relevant technical leads, incorporating succession planning, staff development, knowledge transfer and clear milestones while maintaining operational continuity and transparent, merit-based processes.

## **Policies and SOPs Development and Rollout**

- Lead the development, contextualization and regular review of support services policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs), ensuring alignment with DRC frameworks, donor requirements, applicable legislation and humanitarian operational needs.
- Coordinate updates with relevant technical leads, Programme and Area teams, securing required approvals and maintaining clear responsibilities, version control and accessible guidance.
- Oversee rollout across country and field offices through clear communication, staff briefings, training and practical tools to support consistent implementation.
- Monitor implementation and compliance, address gaps and incorporate staff feedback, audit findings and changes in the operating context into timely policy and SOP revisions.

## **Budget Management**

- Ensure that the Country Master Budget is updated on a regular basis and is used to adequately prepare project proposals or cost cutting measures.
- Ensure the timely completion of monthly budget follow-up meetings, financial reports and month-end closing processes, maintaining data accuracy and integrity.
- Develop country office support services budget including staff costs for all donor project proposals and track spending on regular basis to ensure budget is used according to plan.
- Implement Core cost project and other global initiatives related to Budgeting.

## **Risk Management**

- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team (SMT) in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit respectively.
- Supervise audits, controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area.
- Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Develop a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy. Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Participate in audit kick-off and exit meetings and ensure cooperation at all time during every audit field works. Lead on providing management response on each audit report.

## **DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff.
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance.
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities.

## **Experience and technical competencies:**

- At least 10 years' management experience in relevant field.
- At least 5 years’ experience in playing similar role, preferably in an international NGO.
- Previous experience as Country Senior Management is essential.
- Previous experience of working in the Middle East and/or a fast-paced conflict setting is preferred.
- Proven leadership skills and competence in people management
- Proven operational experience in one or more of the following thematic areas: financial, supply chain, human resources, and information management.
- Proven experience managing the scale-up and scale-down of humanitarian operations in response to changing needs and funding levels.
- Experience working in an ERP system, including supply chain, finance, and HR systems.

## **Education:**

Master’s degree in finance, HR, Economics, business administration or related field.

## **Languages:**

- Fluency in written and spoken English required.
- Arabic language skills would be an advantage.

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract Length**: 1 year (Renewable, based on performance and fund availability).
- **Salary Level**: Management – E level 1 (Based on DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Syria, Damascus.
- **Expected Start date**: January or February 2027

jobs.title: Head, English Translation Section (P.5)
jobs.location: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.description:
**Classification Grade:**

P.5

**Vacancy Announcement:**

V.N. 26-13 (Readvertisement)

**Contract Information**

Fixed-term for two years (first year is probationary) with the possibility of further extension, subject to satisfactory performance.

**Salary**

US$ 103,165 net per annum, plus post adjustment (currently US$ 78,818). Salary is free of income tax in the United Kingdom.

**Purpose of the Post**

Under the supervision of the Director, Conference Division, the successful candidate will be responsible for managing the work of the English Translation Section.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

1. Set the objectives for satisfactory and good performance, and develop work plans, for the English Translation Section (ETS), including establishing priorities, performance standards and delivery targets for the Section’s overall programme of work, in order to ensure the timely, efficient and high-quality provision of English translation, revision, editing and related language services in support of the Organization’s meetings, official documentation and publications.
2. Provide guidance and advice to ETS staff to help develop their skills and careers. Enhance staff morale and team spirit, carry out performance appraisals for ETS staff. and exercise full managerial responsibility for the supervision, performance management, development and effective utilization of the Section’s staff and other personnel assigned to the Section.
3. Assist with the identification and application of new computer-assisted translation (CAT) tools and technology, for the benefit of efficiency and quality assurance, and lead the assessment, introduction, implementation and monitoring of language technologies, workflow tools and quality-assurance systems relevant to the work of the Section.
4. Develop strong professional relationships with colleagues inside and outside ETS to exchange experience and methodological approaches and liaise as required with colleagues concerned for the production of documents and publications, including advising submitting officers and senior leadership on documentation priorities, scheduling, language quality, drafting requirements and related procedural matters.
5. Supervise and evaluate the work done by ETS in terms of quality and quantity with a view to ensuring that the resources available to ETS are put to the best possible use and ensure that the Section’s outputs meet the Organization’s required standards for accuracy, consistency, clarity, timeliness and cost-effectiveness.
6. Keep under constant review the need for changes in ETS and make recommendations for improvement as needed, including proposals relating to work methods, staffing structures, workflow planning, use of technology, quality assurance and service delivery arrangements.
7. Supervise administrative matters concerning outsourced translation, including quality assurance and timely delivery of the translation work, and ensure that ETS can rely on an adequate roster of contractual translators to reinforce its capacity when the volume of work requires, including the planning and oversight of contractual requirements, monitoring of performance, and recommendation of appropriate use of external capacity within available resources.
8. Tap into the translation market for optimal use of human and financial resources for outsourced translation, keep abreast with developments in the profession and the language-services market, and advise on the most effective and efficient use of internal and external capacity.
9. Recommend action on personnel, budgetary and procedural matters relating to the efficient operation of ETS, and advise the Director, Conference Division, on staffing, resource requirements, operational risks, succession planning, contractual arrangements and policy or procedural issues affecting the work of the Section.
10. Translate (from French and Spanish to English), revise and edit all sorts of IMO documents, particularly those containing complex, difficult, technical or sensitive texts and/or supervise work in this area, and promptly deal with urgent translation, revision or editing as required, with primary emphasis on overseeing, quality-assuring and directing such work within the Section. Coordinate document quality control updates across the language sections (English, French and Spanish) and personally undertake the most complex, sensitive, urgent or precedent-setting assignments as necessary.
11. Organize and coordinate the teams serving the committee and sub-committee meetings (including night shifts), supervise their work and coordinate with the submitting officers and documentation section in order to ensure the smooth and orderly arrival of the documents and the availability of the relevant documents on the last day of the meetings, and ensure the effective management of the Section’s contribution to major meetings and conferences serviced by the Organization.
12. Keep the IMO Style Guide under review and take authoritative decisions for IMO regarding English terminology, style and usage, thereby ensuring organization-wide consistency and serving as the principal authority within the Secretariat on English editorial standards and usage.
13. Keep the IMO Guidance on preparing documents under review through consultation with colleagues in other divisions and provide authoritative advice across the Secretariat on the preparation, drafting and presentation of documentation in English.
14. Manage and evaluate the use of the proofreading tool PerfectIt by colleagues in all divisions and update the IMO-specific style sheet on a regular basis, including promoting and providing training on the effective application of editorial and quality-assurance tools across the Organization and assessing their impact on consistency, efficiency and quality.
15. Advise and provide training for Secretariat staff on drafting in English, including the development and delivery of guidance, training and outreach aimed at improving the quality of drafting documents submitted for word processing and translation in the working languages.
16. Work with the Terminology Specialist on English entries in the United Nations terminology database, UNTERM, and assure the quality of term records relating to IMO, ensuring the integrity, consistency and authoritative status of IMO terminology in English.
17. Make proper arrangements in ETS to assist, where possible, if conference interpretation is required from its staff translators under exceptional circumstances.
18. Answer queries from, and provide assistance to, other UN organizations, IMO Member States and relevant institutions in the profession, as required, and represent IMO, as appropriate, in inter-agency, professional and technical exchanges on matters relating to translation, editing, terminology, language policy and relevant technologies.
19. Provide support to IMO Member States in respect of the English versions of IMO instruments and documents, including on complex or sensitive linguistic and editorial matters requiring authoritative clarification.
20. Provide advice, as requested, to drafting committees that might be established in the course of the diplomatic conferences convened by the Organization, including authoritative guidance on English drafting, style, terminology and consistency in negotiated texts.
21. Provide opportunities for training in translation and editing for junior translators and students.
22. Provide guidance and advice to staff members in the Section to help develop their skills and career and enhance staff morale and team spirit in the Section.
23. Host interns, school students and professionals seeking work experience at IMO in translation and editing. Give them feedback on their work and give them guidance on careers in the United Nations system.
24. Interact with other United Nations organizations to keep abreast of new technological developments and work methods in the United Nations system and promote the adoption of best practices and innovation relevant to the modernization and strategic development of the Section’s work.

**Required Competencies**

1. Strong leadership, managerial and coordination skills, with a demonstrated ability to work independently under general guidance and effectively manage and develop people and teams, set priorities, allocate resources, take decisions on operational and policy matters within delegated authority, and ensure delivery of services in a high-volume, time-sensitive environment.
2. Proven interpersonal skills and ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with internal and external stakeholders, at all levels including in an international, multicultural context, and to represent the Section and provide authoritative advice to senior managers, submitting offices, Member States and external counterparts on language, documentation and editorial matters.
3. Proven organizational and time management skills and a high degree of initiative together with the ability to work under pressure and manage conflicting priorities and high volumes of work, while maintaining oversight of section-wide outputs, service standards, staffing requirements and operational risks.
4. Effective oral and written communication skills and ability to draft effectively, provide guidance and explain positions to a variety of audiences, including on complex linguistic, editorial, policy and procedural matters.
5. Take ownership of all responsibilities and deliver high quality outputs within prescribed time and costs., , while ensuring the effective use of staff, contractual and budgetary resources and promoting continuous improvement in service delivery.
6. Consistently demonstrate integrity, tact, discretion and professionalism.

**Professional Experience**

Minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience in translation and revision, preferably within the framework of the United Nations Common System, of which at least 5 years as a Senior Translator/Reviser is essential. Minimum 5 years in a management role responsible for performance and development of staff is essential, including responsibility for planning, organizing and supervising the work of translators, managing competing priorities and deadlines, and overseeing the use of contractual resources and quality assurance arrangements.

**Education**

Advanced university degree (masters level)\* or equivalent in translation/languages.

\*A first-level university degree with four additional years of experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English to mother tongue standard and proficiency in French and Spanish. Knowledge of other official UN languages would be an asset.

**Other Skills**

Proficiency in MS Office applications is essential. Experience with computer assisted translation (CAT) tools is essential. Good working knowledge of computer-assisted translation (CAT) tools, such as eLuna, is essential. Experience in identification and managing the introduction and use of language technologies, quality-assurance tools and workflow improvements in a translation environment is highly desirable.

Responsible for assisting the Head of Project in planning, organizing, implementing and monitoring all cash transfer programming in all our areas of operation. ## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Assist the Head of Project in planning and implementation of the activities in the project.**

- Assist the Head of Project in the planning, coordination and execution of the Food Security and Livelihood (FSL) activities such as cash transfer programming

The post-holder is responsible for implementing emergency hygiene promotion activities, distributing WASH kits, ensuring the distribution of water supplies, promoting appropriate community involvement, and delivering essential WASH services. They also provide positive acceptance of Action Against Hunger in the intervention area.

## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Programming**

- Take the lead in the conduct of water supply, sanitation (WASH), and shelter technical engineering assessments at the field level, including analyzing, presenting, and reporting the results and recommendations to the Technical Team
- Participate in joint sector assessments, surveys, and evaluations to focus on water supply, sanitation (WASH), and shelter, and their contribution and impact on the other sectors.
- Apply and ensure Build Back Safer and Do No Harm principles and environmental protection in the design, planning, and implementation of construction activities.
- Prepare and Submit a Technical Dossier:
1. Technical Assessment Report
2. Interactive Map
3. Technical Design/ Plan
4. Bill of Quantity
5. Terms of Reference
6. Technical Clearance
- Facilitate and plan construction-related activities in the assigned sites, making sure that beneficiaries and vulnerable groups such as women, girls, the elderly, and people with special needs are consulted and involved in the process of the construction phases, such as protection concerns during nighttime use of sanitation facilities, provision of access aids for the elderly, and others.
- Implement and monitor day-to-day activities according to the Bill of Quantity and drawings/schematic diagrams in collaboration with skilled and unskilled labor. Submit the Constriction Monitoring Report once it reaches 20%, 50%, 80% and 100%
- Conduct regular water quality testing and monitoring of water facilities before and after the repair/construction works, and at the household level, and provide feedback to the community and LGU.
- Guarantees that activities don’t contribute to or impact the environment and the community, such as construction waste, contamination of sanitation facilities to surface water and water points, and others.
- Monitor and secure functionality of WASH and shelter, if needed, replace parts or repair WASH and shelter to ensure continuous use.
- Ensure good respect for working conditions while in the field, especially the respect for Action Against Hunger’s Code of Conduct and standard operating procedures for the area of operation and safety rules on the construction site.
- Conduct Capacity building for the WASH Committee/BAWASA for the sustainability of built WASH facilities.
- Represent Action Against Hunger with different community stakeholders at the field level.
- Maintain good communication with beneficiaries and partner organizations in the field.

**Objective 2: Reporting, Monitoring, Accountability**

- Monitor and report implementation of water supply, sanitation (WASH), and shelter.
- Archiving project technical documents systematically to facilitate organizational-level learning, memory, and reporting.
- Consolidate annual technical reports of Action Against Hunger project teams and of partners.
- Prepare regular reports on the detailed progress of construction for the assigned sites.
- Ensure the quality and quantity of material at the field as per BOQs and according to waybills.
- Ensure safety procedures and rules are respected in the field by all workers.
- Support the conduct of 3rd party monitoring of WASH and shelter before turnover to the community/LGU. Provide the necessary documents, such as the Bill of Quantity and Design, with the monitors. Findings on the technical results of the monitoring should be readily addressed.
- Collection and achievement of Sources of Verification based on the activities, indicators, and agreed format/tools, and submitted to the Head of Project
- Ensure proper Turnover of WASH infrastructures to LGUS and/or community-based committees such as BAWASA, WASH committee.
- Ensure completeness and quality of construction work based on the work plan and schedules.
- Ensure as-built designs are available, documented, and shared with relevant partners/LGUs.

**Objective 3: Finance and Admin responsibilities**

- Prepare the daily workers payment sheet and payment documents for workers/contractors as needed.
- Support to line manager for timely submitting daily payments sheets.
- Organize day-to-day logistics, administration, and personnel activities.
- Manage all related program equipment and materials in close consultation with the logistics/procurement officer. Maintain and ensure proper project asset register.

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- Education:
- University/college graduate of civil engineering, architecture, or other relevant degrees, and technical qualifications
- Licensed Engineer or Architect
- Technical Knowledge:
- Technical engineering knowledge of civil, structural, and/or emergency water supply, and sanitation (WASH).
- Familiarity with the water supply, sanitation (WASH), and shelter humanitarian standards, e.g., Sphere, Philippine Laws, and LGU ordinances
- Familiar with water systems, chlorination, water testing, plumbing, and carpentry workloads
- Significant proven work experience in engineering (designing, preparation of BOQ, and/or supervising) for water supply, sanitation, and shelter.
- Experience in implementing water supply, sanitation, and disaster risk reduction and livelihood infrastructures projects through the Cash for Work modality is an asset, including supervising CfW workers.
- Familiarity with the local culture, ability to develop respect from a wide range of people, and strong ability to communicate effectively in line with WASH and shelter.
- At least three 3 years’ experience in humanitarian organization, especially in the WASH and restoration
- With prior experience working in emergencies, recovery, and development works.
- Excellent English and Filipino. Speaking the local dialect is an advantage.
- IT systems:
- With good working knowledge on how to use Microsoft Office package e.g. Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Outlook, and TEAMS.
- Proficiency in the use of AutoCAD and SketchUp
- Valuable prior experience in issues related to the promotion of gender equality or personal commitment to gender equality.

jobs.title: TO PROVIDE PSYCHOSOCIAL SERVICES TO HUMANITY & INCLUSION (HI) STAFF IN KENYA
jobs.description:
**CONTEXT**
Handicap International Federation (HI), operating as Humanity & Inclusion, is an international organisation working alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations. In Kenya, HI operates from Nairobi and from field locations including Kakuma and Dadaab, where staff often work in demanding, remote and humanitarian settings that expose them to stress, critical incidents and workplace hazards.
HI Kenya recognises that the mental health and wellbeing of its staff are central to delivering quality programmes and to caring for its people. Staff working in humanitarian and field settings may be exposed to prolonged stress, burnout and distressing events, and need access to professional, confidential support.
To support this, HI is seeking a qualified service provider to offer psychosocial services for HI staff in Kenya

**DESCRIPTION OF THE EXPECTED SERVICE**
The contracted service provider is to provide the following services: -
**Specific objectives of the assignment**
• To provide confidential, professional and accessible psychosocial support services that promote the mental health and wellbeing of HI staff in Kenya.
• To provide timely psychological support to individuals and teams affected by critical incidents.
• To strengthen the capacity of managers and Human Resources staff to recognize distress and support staff wellbeing.
**Responsibilities and Tasks**
The service provider will carry out the following activities: -
a) Individual and Group Support
• Provide confidential individual counselling sessions, delivered in person or virtually, by qualified and licensed counsellors or psychologists, with the number of sessions per staff member to be agreed with HI.
• Facilitate group sessions and workshops on stress and burnout management, resilience, self-care and work-life balance.
• Refer staff requiring specialised psychiatric or medical care to appropriate providers, with
the staff member’s consent.
b) Critical Incident Response
• Provide psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing for individuals and teams following distressing events, such as accidents, security incidents or the loss of a colleague, within an agreed response time.
• Provide a mechanism for urgent support outside normal working hours, such as an on-call counsellor or helpline.
c) Manager and Human Resources Support • Orient managers and Human Resources staff on recognising signs of distress, supportive supervision and referral pathways.
• Advise HI on staff wellbeing initiatives based on anonymised trends.
d) Confidentiality and Inclusion
• Ensure strict confidentiality and safe handling of records in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and professional codes of ethics. HI will not have access to individual counselling content.
• Ensure services are inclusive and accessible, including for staff with disabilities, culturally sensitive, and available in English and Kiswahili.

**Scope and Target**
The assignment covers HI Kenya staff based in Nairobi and in the field locations of Kakuma and Dadaab. The estimated number of staff eligible for the service is 59
The scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
• Providing individual and group psychosocial support to HI staff throughout the contract period.
• Providing psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing when required.
• Providing urgent support outside normal working hours.
• Referring staff to specialised care where needed.
• Orienting managers and Human Resources staff on supporting staff wellbeing.
• Preparing and submitting the reports and deliverables listed in this TOR.

**Profile of the service provider**
The service provider will need to have the following capacities:
• Registered business entity in Kenya with a proven track record of providing psychosocial or counselling services to organisations. Experience with NGOs or humanitarian organisations is an added advantage.
• Counsellors and psychologists must be licensed by the Counsellors and Psychologists Board of Kenya, with experience in trauma, stress and burnout management and critical incident debriefing.
• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and protect client data in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019.
• Ability to deliver services in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab (in person or virtually), in English and Kiswahili.
• Experience in or commitment to disability inclusion is an added advantage.

Duration and Place of Performance of the Service
The contract will be for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of signing, renewable subject to satisfactory performance. Psychosocial services will be available throughout the contract period. The service shall be carried out in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab, with virtual counselling options where appropriate.
**Work Plan**
Based on the proposed assignment, the timeline shall be agreed upon by the service provider and HI. The service provider shall submit a service delivery plan within one (1) week of signing the contract.

**Report**
The service provider shall provide the following deliverables:-
• Psychosocial service delivery plan
• Quarterly psychosocial service report, with anonymised utilisation data, key themes and recommendations
• Summary report (without identifying details) for each critical incident response
• Final end-of-assignment report
All reports shall be submitted in both editable electronic format and PDF format. Reports shall not contain information that identifies individual staff members.
**Contact Person**
During the performance of the service, the service provider will be assisted by the Human Resources Officer – Kenya in coordinating schedules and logistics with the field offices.
**Appendices**
Willingness to adhere to Handicap International's Federation institutional policies (Prevention and fight against corruption, Child Protection, Protection of Beneficiaries against sexual abuse and harassment). Available on the website: [https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.](https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.)

**Evaluation**
Application documents submitted will be evaluated in three (stages);
**General Mandatory Evaluation Criteria**
**For firms or institutions**

-Certificate of Registration
-Trade license Certificate/ Business Permit
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate
-Personal Accident Insurance cover
-Valid practising licences of the proposed counsellors and psychologists (Counsellors and Psychologists Board)

**For Individuals**

-National ID
-Relevant certifications, professional licences and accreditations
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate
-Personal Accident insurance cover

**Technical Capacity Evaluation**
**(a) Profile and experience of the service provider:**

- The firm should have proven expertise and experience in providing psychosocial services. Attach three reference letters.
- Provide a list of assignments of similar scope of work undertaken within the last 2 years, along with names of clients (including contact person, email contacts, postal address and telephone numbers – this must include the three referees provided above)

**(b)Professional/technical capacity/ capability:**
- The proposed counsellors and psychologists should have relevant experience and professional qualifications in the relevant field.
- The proposal should describe the proposed approach to service delivery and the measures to ensure confidentiality and protection of staff data.

**Financial Evaluation**
\- At the Financial stage, the Lowest Competitive Evaluated bidder and within budget estimates will be considered for the award of the contract.

**NB: Your Financial proposal should Include flights, meals, accomodation,communication and any other contigency / miscelleneous costs for Kakuma ,Dadaab and Nairobi.**

jobs.title: Technical Advisor MHPSS Services
jobs.company: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.description:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 15 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors.

The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Technical Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting partner organizations to provide MHPSS services for specific target groups as well as for the scientific accompaniment of those services and the dissemination of the findings to promote the application of effective approaches. You will be working on these tasks in close collaboration with another colleague in a project team of overall 8 staff.

**Your tasks**

- Identifying and contracting suitable MHPSS-partner organizations that work with the project’s target groups
- Technically and administratively accompanying and supporting the partner organizations in their planning and implementation of these services; identifying and addressing capacity development needs of the partner organization, if any
- Technically and administratively accompanying and supporting the research teams who are documenting and systematically evaluating the MHPSS-services offered
- Ensuring the quality of the research papers/ research briefs prepared by the research teams and supporting the dissemination of the findings, e.g. through presentations
- Coordinating between different service offers and research teams
- Where suitable, bringing in expertise and ideas into the other work streams of the project (mentioned above), which will be mainly covered by your colleagues
- Supporting with team-internal tasks, including monitoring and evaluation, reporting, preparation of team workshops etc.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- A completed post-graduate degree in mental health, clinical or general psychology, psychological counselling, psychiatry or a related field
- At least 4 years of professional experience in MHPSS in the humanitarian or development sector, preferably in the Middle East, particularly in/ for Syria
- Proven experience with and openness for non-traditional MHPSS-interventions, for example arts-based or sports-based interventions
- Proven experience with scientific work and methods combined with strong analytical thinking
- Experience with project and process management
- A good overview of the MHPSS-actor landscape in Syria (particularly civil society)
- Strong team work and communication skills
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- High degree of initiative
- Structured and meticulous working methods – even under time pressure
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is a strong asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Technical Advisor, you will be responsible for training actors from other sectors on how to work in an MHPSS-informed way and advising them on integrating MHPSS-considerations into their policies, standard operating procedures and training efforts. You will moreover be contributing to developing and revising practice-oriented curricula in the field of MHPSS and to establishing them in local training institutions. You will be working on these tasks in close collaboration with two other colleagues in a project team of overall 8 staff.

**Your tasks**

- Coordinating and technically leading the development and adaptation of trainings on working in an MHPSS-informed way for governmental and non-governmental actors from other sectors such as peacebuilding, transitional justice, education and disaster management, based on existing training modules
- Organizing and giving trainings on working in an MHPSS-informed way to actors from other sectors such as the ones mentioned above
- Advising and supporting governmental institutions and non-governmental organizations in integrating MHPSS-considerations into their policies, training efforts and standard operating procedures
- Supporting with the revision of GIZ’s existing curriculum for a long-term training of clinical supervisors and its establishment at a local training institution
- Supporting with the development and/ or revision of two practice-oriented curricula in the field of MHPSS in cooperation with local training institutions and with their establishment in the training institutions’ range of studies.
- Where suitable, bringing in expertise and ideas into the other work streams of the project (mentioned above), which will be mainly covered by your colleagues
- Supporting with team-internal tasks, including monitoring and evaluation, reporting, preparation of team workshops etc.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- A completed post-graduate degree in mental health, clinical or general psychology, psychological counselling, psychiatry, social work or a related field
- At least 5 years of professional experience in MHPSS, preferably in the Middle East, particularly in/ for Syria
- Experience with developing and giving trainings on how to work in an MHPSS-informed way to actors without an MHPSS-background
- A high degree of understanding of the cross-sectoral nature of MHPSS, its interactions and relevance for other sectors such as peacebuilding, transitional justice, education and disaster management and how to work in an MHPSS-informed way
- Experience in working on the development or revision of academic curricula and/ or experience with giving trainings in the field of MHPSS in a practice-oriented way
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria, particularly in its cross-sectoral nature
- Strong perspective-taking
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- Experience with clinical supervision is an asset
- An existing network of actors in Syria particularly in the fields of peacebuilding, transitional justice, education or disaster management is an asset
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is an asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Implementation Manager, you will have both managerial and technical tasks and will be overall responsible for the project’s implementation and its work packages as mentioned above. In addition, you will be supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and standards for MHPSS-services in tandem with two other colleagues. You will be reporting to the head of project who is at the same time leading another GIZ project in the health sector.

**Your tasks**

- Overseeing and coordinating the project’s implementation across all abovementioned work packages
- Managing the MHPSS project team consisting of 5 national and 1 international MHPSS technical advisors.
- Technically supporting staff in their work regarding the abovementioned work packages
- Functioning as liaison person with governmental entities in Syria, particularly the Directorate for Mental Health within the Ministry of Health, the Council for Mental Health and Addiction, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management and the National Commission for Missing Persons
- Supporting governmental entities in strengthening MHPSS-systems and structures, including through the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and quality standards on MHPSS. This comprises for example providing continuous technical and process-oriented advisory services, capacity development measures, facilitating the coordination between different institutions, giving technical inputs etc.

- At least 3 years of experience in managing a team
