- Experience in interacting with government stakeholders, particularly regarding the development of MHPSS strategies and standards
- Experience with strengthening national or sub-national MHPSS-systems and structures
- A high degree of understanding of the Syrian MHPSS system (governmental, civil society, and academic)
- Knowledge in the areas of peacebuilding, social cohesion, transitional justice and their interactions with the field of MHPSS
- A high ability to maintain an overview of encompassing projects and coordinate them, also under pressure, as well as good judgement and decision-making
- Strong teamwork skills
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- High intercultural competence and diplomatic skills
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- Resilience and frustration tolerance

- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is an asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

jobs.title: Resource Development and Strategic Partnerships Director
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Resource Development and Strategic Partnerships Director**, you will provide strategic leadership and directly drive income growth and diversification for World Vision International Lao PDR. You will build a strong funding pipeline, strengthen acquisition and grants management systems, develop donor and partner relationships, and advance organisational positioning and technical brand. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will work across functions and with Support and Regional Offices to turn strategy and evidence into funding, influence and results for vulnerable children, while developing team capabilities and a positive, healthy work culture.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Drive Resource Growth and Funding Acquisition**

You will develop and continuously improve the WVI Laos Resource Development Strategy, lead annual funding plans and pipeline management, and identify and forecast donor opportunities. You will establish effective acquisition systems, lead proposal development and bid teams, guide Go/No-Go decisions, and develop fundable programme concepts that address the needs of vulnerable children. You will also coordinate donor feedback, negotiations, award mobilisation and emergency funding efforts, while applying lessons from successful and unsuccessful bids to improve future performance.

**Strategic Positioning and Partnerships**

You will build and maintain strategic relationships with institutional donors, Support and Regional Offices, UN agencies, government, civil society, private-sector partners and other development actors. You will position WVI Laos for funding opportunities, represent the organisation in relevant external forums, serve as the main focal point for Support and Regional Offices on funding and programme design, and monitor donor priorities, market developments and emerging opportunities.

**Acquisition and Grants Systems, Performance, and Accountability**

You will establish and embed effective end-to-end acquisition and grants management systems, with clear roles, workflows, quality standards and accountabilities. You will provide leadership with timely analysis of pipeline performance, funding trends and risks; maintain accurate records and reporting in Horizon and other required systems; and ensure safeguarding, integrity, risk management, donor compliance and organisational standards are applied throughout all activities. You will also monitor acquisition costs and budgets to maximise results.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration and Grants Management**

You will coordinate with Programme Quality, Operations, Finance, Support Services, People and Culture, Communications, Advocacy and field teams throughout the grant lifecycle. You will ensure effective handovers from acquisition to implementation, provide strategic oversight of grants management, support the resolution of compliance and donor issues, and improve systems based on audits, feedback and lessons learned. You will also strengthen resource development and grants management capabilities across the organisation.

**Team Leadership, Development, and Delivery**

You will lead, coach and manage the Resource Development and Grants Management team, setting clear priorities and performance expectations. You will strengthen staff capabilities through coaching, cross-training, delegation and development plans, while addressing succession and critical skills gaps. You will foster a positive, inclusive and accountable team culture built on trust, wellbeing, collaboration and learning. You will remain directly involved in priority funding opportunities, proposal writing, donor engagement, strategic communications and critical deliverables, while mobilising additional expertise when needed and modelling WVI values, integrity and sound judgement.

**Requirements include:**

- Significant senior-level experience in resource development, institutional fundraising, strategic partnerships, or business development within international development or humanitarian contexts.
- Demonstrated success securing and diversifying funding from bilateral, multilateral, UN, foundation, private-sector, or other institutional partners, including leading complex, high-value proposals and negotiations.
- Strong understanding of the full grants lifecycle, with experience establishing and embedding effective acquisition and grants management systems, accountabilities, quality standards, and organisational capacity.
- Proven ability to translate organisational strategy, programme evidence, and technical priorities into a focused funding pipeline, compelling programme concepts, and credible external positioning.
- Experience building and managing senior donor, partner, Support Office, and cross-organisational relationships, with strong influencing, negotiation, and representation skills.
- Demonstrated leadership of a small, multidisciplinary team, including coaching, performance management, talent development, succession planning, and building bench strength while remaining directly engaged in delivery.
- Proven ability to lead across functions and mobilise colleagues without relying solely on formal authority, creating shared ownership and delivering results in complex, cross-cultural environments.
- Experience providing strategic oversight and quality assurance for communications, external positioning, technical branding, or thought leadership.
- Excellent strategic judgement, analytical ability, written communication, and proposal development skills, with a record of delivering high-quality results under pressure.
- Master’s degree in international development, business, public policy, communications, a relevant technical discipline, or a related field; or equivalent senior-level professional experience.
- Strong working knowledge of institutional donor requirements and funding approaches, including major bilateral, multilateral, and UN donors.
- Experience working in Lao PDR, Southeast Asia, or a comparable development and humanitarian context.
- Established networks with relevant donors, development partners, Support Offices, or private-sector actors.
- Experience integrating safeguarding, gender equality, disability and social inclusion, climate resilience, and environmental sustainability into programme design and funding proposals.
- Experience mobilising resources and managing donor requirements in humanitarian emergencies.
- Working knowledge of Lao or another relevant regional language.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Travel and/or Work Environment:**

The position is based in Vientiane with up to 20% travel within the country and annual overseas travel to attend Global/Regional training and events.

**Encouragement:**

World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

World Vision offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package. We offer a challenging work environment, opportunities to lead, and a commitment to growing your skills in a fulfilling and international working environment.

**Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable du Service Contrôle de Gestion, votre mission sera d'assurer la gestion budgétaire, le suivi des couts du siège et garantir le respect du cadre de gestion sur son périmètre. Accompagner les managers dans le suivi budgétaire de leur l'activité.

Réaliser l'analyse financière des projets stratégiques

Vous avez développer des compétences en gestion de subventions bailleurs.
Une bonne maitrise de la Business Intelligence est un plus.
Vous avez un niveau Excel avancé.

Travaillant dans un environnement international, vous maîtrisez l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDD à compter de janvier 2027 - Temps plein

Rémunération : De 41K à 50Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience

Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)

Il a été défini pour ce poste une présence obligatoire au siège de 3 jours par an.
Temps de présentiels collectifs imposés / également obligatoires par l'employeur : pour les réunions et événements collectifs (jusqu'à 3 jours par mois) et 2 jours de présence obligatoire lors de votre intégration dans l'équipe
Indemnités de télétravail
Formation: Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft

jobs.title: 23740 Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) (P)
jobs.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) plays a leading role in supporting governments and communities to build health systems that are responsive to the needs of these populations and address public health concerns along the mobility continuum. IOM uses targeted interventions such as direct health service provision, establishment of referral networks for specialized care, and health promotion for migration-affected people and host communities.

In Afghanistan, IOM provides and supports access to good-quality primary and secondary healthcare services, with a focus on returnees, migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), and underserved host communities in border regions, as well as other vulnerable populations across the country. IOM employs a direct implementation modality of healthcare services through its Mobile Health Teams (MHTs), Community-Based Vaccination Centres (CBVC), Vaccination Outreach Teams (VOT), and Basic Health Centres (BHC), which ensures greater responsiveness to community needs. The primary health care services provided include reproductive health, maternal, neonatal and child health services, trauma care, basic nutrition and community-based Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). IOM also provides technical support as well as procurement, warehousing, and transportation of medical commodities for external partner health facilities.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes and Operations, with direct supervision from the Programme Coordinator (Migration Health), the Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) will provide management support, expert technical guidance and advice to the Migration Health Programme Coordinator towards successful implementation of the multi-programme Health Assistance to Crisis Affected Populations (H3) activities/emergency health portfolio, including implementation of the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005), and vaccination and polio interventions. The Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) is expected to carry out the duties in accordance with the strictest ethical standards and with due respect for gender and socio-cultural sensitivities.

**Responsibilities**

1. Substantively support the operationalization of the Country Office’s (CO) public health and emergency health preparedness, response, and recovery strategy.
2. Provide technical leadership for vaccination and polio interventions by ensuring high‑quality micro‑planning, cold chain continuity, vaccine accountability, and evidence‑based outbreak response across mobility‑affected and disaster‑impacted locations.
3. Manage and coordinate project activation, implementation, reporting, and evaluation of emergency health programs in coordination with the Migration Health Officer.
4. Develop and/or support the development of proposals in coordination with the Program Support Unit, and ensure regular reporting requirements are met, including on achievements, projects, problems encountered, pertinent developments, and strategic needs.
5. Strengthen national disease surveillance capacity in coordination with relevant stakeholders, alert and response capacity of border level/PoE staffing, and support the development of early warning systems (including event-based and indicator-based surveillance).
6. Regularly coordinate with IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Unit to ensure utilization of mobility data for health programme planning and response, and coordinate with other units, including the Program Support Unit, Cross-Border Post Arrival Humanitarian Assistance (CB-PAHA) and other units as necessary.
7. Prioritize and ensure information sharing between internal units, cluster partners, and IOM and other emergency response actors to facilitate effective and efficient coordination;
8. Provide expert technical support and advice for vulnerability assessments, risk mapping, and development of preparedness/contingency planning at the provincial level.
9. Monitor and ensure that national health staff and partners are familiar with internationally recognized tools and standards and lead organizing trainings/capacity building on an ad-hoc/as needed basis on migration health.
10. Lead organizing meetings, workshops, orientations, and training for different stakeholders on implementation of the International Health Regulations and disease surveillance.
11. Represent IOM at Health Cluster meetings and other relevant cluster meetings and liaise and coordinate with national and international health and humanitarian assistance authorities, agencies, and organizations regarding the planning and implementation of health-related activities. Key counterparts include the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH), World Health Organization (WHO), Health Cluster partner agencies, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Working Group and other stakeholders.
12. Undertake travel duties, as required and in line with prevailing security restrictions, related to project implementation and oversight, staff training, and liaison with partners, including regular travel duties to the borders with Afghanistan, Pakistan and Iran, and the Sub-Offices, to coordinate, develop and/or support programme implementation.
13. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Nursing, Medicine, Health Sciences, Community or Public Health, Epidemiology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.
- An additional qualification in clinical medicine, tropical medicine, maternal and child health, or public health is an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Minimum three years of relevant working experience in the design and implementation of International Health Regulations/public health in conflict settings and response at national and international levels;
- Experience in vaccination programmes, polio eradication, or Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)- focused public health interventions.
- Experience in proposal development and reporting required;
- Demonstrated experience with the UN, IOM, or International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) preferred;
- Demonstrated cluster experience is an advantage;
- Experience working in hardship duty stations and emergency settings with complex operating environments preferred;
- Demonstrated computer background, including experience with databases, Microsoft applications, spreadsheets, word processing, and SPSS/STATA;
- Demonstrated clinical experience is an advantage; and,
- Demonstrated operational and field experience in migration, refugee and displaced persons related programming is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent analytical, communication, presentation and writing skills;
- Proven capacity to develop and implement programmes in the area of migration and health.
- Ability to work effectively in high-pressure, rapidly changing environments; and,
- Demonstrated good people skills, and demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders and partners.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23572 Deputy Chief of Mission (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and in close coordination with relevant Departments in Headquarters (HQ), the Deputy Chief of Mission (DCoM) will be responsible and accountable for providing support to the CoM in their responsibility to ensure coherence between the Programmes and Support Services of the Country Office (CO), including Programme Development for the CO. The DCoM will ensure that implementation of IOM programmes is done in an effective and efficient manner consistent with CO’s Strategy and in line with the expectations of the IOM’s donors and beneficiaries, while collaborating with the national and regional authorities.

**Responsibilities**

1. In coordination with the CoM, represent the CO by promoting IOM activities with the national authorities, diplomatic corps, governmental and private donors, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), government authorities/ or de facto government authorities, and other partners in the Country and Region.
2. Oversee the formulation of Country Strategies, policies and approaches across IOM’s operational portfolio, and identify and develop new programmes to address emerging needs while ensuring systematic implementation capacity, in close coordination with the Programme Support Unit (PSU).
3. Contribute to ensuring the highest efficiency in CO’s Risk Management and Compliance functions, to ensure strengthening internal controls and compliance with contractual rules and regulations through effective management and the provision of accurate, researched, and documented risk and compliance information, effective delivery of services, transparent utilization, and management of programme resources.
4. Ensure the continuous, effective, and efficient planning, coordination, and integration between the CoM and DCoM Offices and the Sub-Offices.
5. Work closely with the CoM/ Special Envoy, Heads of Sub-Offices, and Heads of Units to enhance inter-unit collaboration and coordination, to maximize efficiencies and efficacy within the CO programming to ensure that all CO’s Units work towards common goals and a consistent and coherent strategy.
6. Make strategic recommendations and provide advice to the CoM and Senior Management to improve overall performance of the CO and support the CoM’s Office with development of strategy/policies/guidance notes, organize regular Senior Management Meetings (SMT), set up meetings with external partners (UN/ de facto authorities), prepare speeches/talking points, and support/facilitate consultation process with defector authorities/UN/international community on CO’s strategies.
7. In close coordination with the Resources Management Unit (RMU), Programme Support Unit and respective Programme Managers, ensure compliance of all projects with IOM and donor regulations, policies and obligations as indicated in the funding agreements, project documents, work plans and budgets.
8. Oversee field operations to ensure implementation of the humanitarian, development and peace building nexus to ensure timely, effective and efficient programming delivery, ensuring through sound leadership, supervision and monitoring that all blockages, disruptions and delays are avoided in order to achieve program results and that these results are measurable.
9. Lead the development of strong donor contacts and relations, monitoring, updating programme funding priorities across the migration management spectrum and provide expert support to the CoM in fundraising activities. Participate in all strategic inter-sector coordination and performance management mechanisms.
10. Ensure IOM participation in appropriate policy and operational United Nations Country Team (UNCT) inter-agency mechanisms; engage with UN agencies in the development and implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), and coordinate with UNCT and partners on the implementation and review processes of the migration-relevant Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Global Compact for Migration and the UN Network on Migration related activities as these processes move forward.
11. Formally deputize for CoM on an ongoing basis and exercising mission, staff, and financial management responsibility in CO, including chairing the Senior Management Team and/or Senior Operational Team meetings in the absence of the CoM.
12. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, Law, International Relations, Business Administration, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with twelve years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Excellent understanding of and proven experience in inter-agency coordination and strategic engagement, UN structures and systems, and experience in both crisis contexts and development settings;
- Extensive experience formulating and delivering internal displacement and solutions policy, strategy, and programming;
- Experience at international level on managing programmes, covering emergency, stabilization, and development areas;
- Previous experience as a Head of Office, Chief of Mission and/or Senior Programme Manager with a Government or UN agency, or a regional or international organization;
- Extensive experience in external relations or strategic engagement, as well as liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities and institutions;
- Experience in managing IOM Offices and liaising with governmental authorities, other national/international institutions; and,
- Work experience in the Region.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated knowledge of programme development, management and capacity-building methodologies;
- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Good knowledge of financial and administrative management;
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming; and,
- Knowledge of programme management in emergency context.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23770 MHPSS Response Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations and overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD), and the guidance of the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides advice and supports the implementation of institutional policy from HQ in Country Offices (COs) across the Region. Specifically, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides oversight, quality control, and thematic expertise to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming. Together with other Regional Thematic Units (RTUs), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) contributes to thought leadership on saving lives and protecting individuals on the move, driving solutions to displacement, and facilitating regular pathways for migration. The RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit also identifies regional opportunities and risks, fosters knowledge sharing, encourages policy and research development, and supports cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners in the region, the Regional Thematic Specialist Humanitarian Response and Recovery is the go-to source for humanitarian response and recovery expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. Strategic Direction: Lead and manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the Strategic Plan.

2\. Advocacy and Representation: Assist and provide strategic advice to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's Strategic Plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on HQ and Global Offices' (GOs) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. Technical Assistance: Lead the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on preparedness, protection in emergencies and AAP, life-saving actions, displacement tracking, peace, recovery and solutions.

4\. Training and Capacity Development: In coordination with HQ functional homes and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. Strategic Partnerships: Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. Resource Mobilization: In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnership and Advocacy, COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. Project Development and Reporting: In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook and thematic guidance from DHRR HQ.

8\. Monitoring and Evaluation: In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, hold regular bilateral discussions with CO thematic focal points to assess

challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff and guide COs' adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback. 9. Risk Management: In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

10\. Cash-Based Interventions: In coordination with the global CBI Officer, promote the use of cash-based modalities, where feasible, in line with IOM's global strategies, standards and commitments, and provide guidance and support to COs in designing, implementing and coordinating CBI.

**Knowledge Management, Policy, and Research:**

11\. Knowledge Management and Innovation: In coordination with the RPDO, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate innovative and best practices related to DHRR.

12\. Policy: In coordination with the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer, provide thematic support and recommendations on regional and country-level policies and frameworks to COs, donors, and key partners.

13\. Data, Research, and Foresight: In coordination with HQ and the Regional Data Hub, analyse and disseminate thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

14\. Thematic Community of Practice: Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

15\. Coordination: Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTSs, Global Thematic Specialists, and CO focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

16\. Mainstream: In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities and modalities (i.e., Cash-Based Interventions) in all areas of DHRR’s work in the region. The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is responsible for mainstreaming protection-centered approaches in all areas of IOM's work.

17\. Custodianship: The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is the regional custodian of IOM’s Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion in humanitarian settings, AAP, and Cash-Based Initiatives. Custodianship entails support to other RTUs, as requested, with technical knowledge and capacity on protection mainstreaming as outlined under the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery Terms of Reference and the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit Terms of Reference.

**DHRR Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

18\. Manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the Unit’s Terms of Reference.

**Education**

- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

jobs.title: Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert – CDR
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: Readvertisement UNDP/LBN/VA26/220**
- **Position Title**: Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert – CDR
- **Duty Station:** work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 9 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 10 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 17 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1I4CjphA3f10d4Xemt4XjIPPy2AeOVK9z/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1I4CjphA3f10d4Xemt4XjIPPy2AeOVK9z/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

Workplace integrity and employee protection arrangements are particularly relevant to the implementation of CDR's broader institutional reform programme. As organizational structures, responsibilities, processes, and management arrangements evolve, CDR requires clear institutional policies and mechanisms governing workplace conduct, employee protection, reporting of concerns, and equal treatment. Such arrangements need to be embedded within CDR's regular management and human resource practices rather than treated solely as requirements associated with individual donor-funded projects. They should also be supported by practical reporting, awareness, monitoring, and accountability mechanisms that can operate within CDR's existing institutional framework.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert to support CDR in developing the institutional instruments and operational arrangements required under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will prepare the policies and mechanisms governing whistleblowing and protection from retaliation, workplace conduct, discrimination, harassment, and gender equality in a form that can be adopted by the Board of Directors within the existing legal framework. The assignment will also establish a practical gender-mainstreaming framework, with defined entry points across workforce management, recruitment and promotion, staff development, workplace policies, reporting, and monitoring.

The assignment will further support the establishment of a confidential reporting channel and the awareness and communication arrangements required to ensure that staff understand their rights, responsibilities, reporting options, and available protections. Through these measures, the assignment will contribute to strengthening workplace integrity and employee protection at CDR and to embedding gender mainstreaming within the institution's management and human resource practices as an integral component of the broader reform programme.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1: Whistleblower Protection and Workplace Integrity**

- Identify the provisions of Lebanese law applicable to whistleblower protection, equality and non-discrimination, sexual harassment and other relevant workplace protections that bind CDR, citing the instrument, article and date for each, and determine what those provisions already require of the institution and what they leave to internal policy.
- Review the safeguarding and reporting arrangements that already operate within donor-funded project frameworks at CDR and determine which staff categories they cover and which they leave unprotected, including staff on all employment categories, contractors embedded within CDR and project implementation unit personnel. Identify relevant gender-related provisions, including measures addressing gender-based violence, sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment.
- Draft the Whistleblower Policy, covering a designated confidential reporting channel separate from line management and accessible to all staff and embedded personnel; a non-retaliation commitment enforceable by the Board that prohibits adverse employment action against a person making a good-faith report and defines the disciplinary consequences of retaliation; an investigation protocol owned by the Audit Committee that specifies handling, confidentiality and escalation, including referral to the internal audit function and, where appropriate, to the competent legal or regulatory authority; and a requirement that all staff are reminded annually of the policy, the channel and the protections in place.
- Draft the Workplace Conduct Policy covering discrimination, harassment and sexual harassment, setting out the prohibited conduct, the reporting routes, the investigation and decision procedure, the sanctions available, and the protection of complainants and witnesses.
- Draft the employee protection provisions that accompany both policies, including confidentiality of records, protection against secondary retaliation and the treatment of reports made in bad faith, in coordination with the human resource provisions on employee protection prepared by the Human Resources Expert.
- Specify the confidential reporting channel in operational terms, covering intake, case registration and numbering, confidentiality safeguards, conflict-of-interest handling, response timelines and record retention, and prepare the case-handling forms and the case register.
- Prepare the submission pack for the Board decision adopting the instruments, and brief the Audit Committee on its responsibilities as policy owner and oversight body.
- Deliver an awareness session for staff, and prepare the annual communication calendar and the awareness materials through which the policies are recalled to staff and embedded personnel.

**Workstream 2: Gender Mainstreaming**

- Assess the existing CDR institutional and human-resource arrangements from a gender-mainstreaming perspective, including women’s representation and participation across grades and decision-making levels taking into account the current workforce profile, recruitment and promotion arrangements, career development, performance management and staff development, and identify key gaps and opportunities for strengthening gender equality within CDR.
- Identify priority gender-mainstreaming entry points across CDR's human-resource and institutional management processes, including workforce planning, recruitment and selection, promotion and career development, performance management, staff development, workplace conduct, internal communication and staff engagement, as well as, where relevant, institutional planning, programmes/projects and decision-making processes.
- Review the existing workplace and employee-protection arrangements from a gender perspective and identify measures required to strengthen prevention of gender-based discrimination, harassment and sexual harassment, as well as gender-sensitive reporting and protection arrangements.
- Define the institutional framework for gender mainstreaming, including the roles, responsibilities and accountability of relevant CDR functions, priority areas for action, and appropriate arrangements for monitoring and periodic review of progress, including the use of sex-disaggregated data across relevant HR and institutional indicators where relevant and feasible.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 9 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 9 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Gender Studies, Gender and Development, Law, Human Resources, Management, Public Administration, Public Policy, Social Sciences, Organizational Development, International Development, or a related field. Specialized focus on gender equality, workplace integrity, employment law, anti-discrimination, safeguarding, sexual harassment, or institutional development is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) developing and implementing institutional policies and mechanisms relating to workplace integrity, whistleblower protection, discrimination, harassment, employee protection, safeguarding, or related areas; and (ii) designing and implementing gender-mainstreaming frameworks within organizations, including gender-responsive human-resource policies, institutional assessments, staff engagement, and monitoring arrangements.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZDyEggt_NrfJ8MVq6j5xAxy16FfFYT8K/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZDyEggt_NrfJ8MVq6j5xAxy16FfFYT8K/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon stands at a pivotal juncture in its governance and reform trajectory. Despite years of overlapping crises, the country has made landmark progress in building an integrity and anti-corruption framework, including the adoption and (partial) implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (2020–2025), the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and major legislative reforms on access to information, illicit enrichment, whistleblower protection, asset declaration, and public procurement. These milestones have laid the groundwork for the most coherent accountability architecture in Lebanon’s recent history.

However, these achievements remain fragile amid deep economic collapse, weakened institutions, and eroded public trust. While the strategic and legal frameworks are largely in place, implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped, and coordination among oversight institutions is still limited. The evaluation of the NACS highlighted the urgent need to consolidate progress by operationalizing national mechanisms, strengthening institutional capacities, and embedding corruption-risk management practices across public institutions.

In this context, the Integrity in ACTion Project is founded with the objective of improving the implementation of an institutionalised and targeted approach to prevent and combat corruption through improved coordination, operationalized oversight, enhanced preventive and enforcement mechanisms, and institutionalized integrity and risk-management practices, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and public trust. The Project is designed to achieve this objective by working on three outputs:

Output 1: Institutional capacities to coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the National Anti-Corruption Strategy strengthened and operationalized through participatory and inclusive mechanisms

Output 2: Legal frameworks and oversight institutions for preventing and combating corruption strengthened and effectively operationalized.

Output 3: Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.

The Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) plays a central role in advancing public sector reform and supporting national efforts to strengthen transparency, integrity, and accountability across public institutions. In this context, OMSAR is leading and coordinating the development of the new National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2027-2032, in close collaboration with relevant national stakeholders and with technical support from UNDP. In parallel, OMSAR launched the Reinventing Government 2030 program, which aims to reshape Lebanon’s public administration, enhance institutional effectiveness, and restore citizen trust by redefining public administration around the principles of efficiency, inclusiveness, accountability, and citizen-centered service delivery.

UNDP has been providing technical and advisory support to OMSAR to strengthen its institutional and operational capacity to coordinate and follow up on the implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2020-2025, support the development of the new strategy, and contribute to broader government reform efforts, including the Reinventing Government 2030 program. This support includes facilitating consultations and coordination with public institutions and partners; providing technical, policy, and legal inputs; supporting research, documentation, monitoring, reporting, CSOs engagement, and stakeholder outreach; and contributing to the overall management and follow-up of reform-related activities.

Based on OMSAR’s needs and priorities, UNDP is seeking to contract a Technical Assistant to provide technical support to OMSAR’s websites and digital platforms and to strengthen the transparency of information, through three complementary workstreams; the technical development and maintenance of the Matchmaking portal, the technical support, maintenance, and updating of the OMSAR website, and the mapping of public services to make information clear, complete, and openly available. The assignment will contribute to the implementation of Lebanon’s National Anti-Corruption Strategy, particularly their objectives related to transparency in public service delivery and citizen engagement.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP IACT Manager, and in close coordination with OMSAR, the Technical Assistant will provide technical support for the development, maintenance, and regular updating of the Matchmaking portal and the OMSAR website, building on the platforms already developed by OMSAR, and will map public services.

The Technical Assistant will undertake the following tasks:

**Task 1: Matchmaking portal technical development and maintenance**

- Provide ongoing technical support and maintenance for the Matchmaking portal, including bug fixing, security updates, performance optimization, backups, and monitoring of availability.
- Develop new features and enhancements in response to OMSAR’s needs, such as tools for publishing reform challenges and opportunities and showing their status and outcomes, improved registration and user profiles, and administration tools for managing content and users.
- Update portal content in Arabic and English, including challenges, opportunities, community and FAQ sections, and ensure correct bilingual display (including Arabic right-to-left).
- Ensure that new features and content remain compliant with web accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA), and test them for usability across browsers and devices.
- Provide technical support for events and outreach using the portal, such as university open houses and open-innovation challenges, and track and report on portal usage.

**Task 2: OMSAR website technical support and updates**

- Provide day-to-day technical support for the OMSAR website, including troubleshooting, bug fixing, security patches, software and plugin updates, backups, and coordination with hosting and IT service providers.
- Regularly update website content in Arabic and English, including news, announcements, publications, reports, events, and pages on OMSAR’s programmes and reform initiatives, in coordination with OMSAR teams.
- Review the structure, navigation, and performance of the website, and implement technical improvements to its usability, search, loading speed, mobile responsiveness, and accessibility.
- Develop new pages, sections, or features as required by OMSAR.
- Set up and monitor website analytics, and prepare periodic reports on website use and on the technical issues addressed.

**Task 3: Public-service mapping and transparency of service information**

- Identify and compile the public services delivered by relevant public institutions using official sources, including institutional websites, official publications, using automated data extraction (e.g., web scraping) where appropriate.
- Develop a structured database of mapped services covering, for each service, the responsible institution, legal basis, beneficiaries, required documents, official fees, processing time, steps and approvals, delivery channels, and complaint mechanisms.
- Verify the collected information with the concerned institutions, and identify gaps such as missing or inconsistent information, unclear fees or timeframes, and steps involving discretion or direct interaction.
- Develop standardized service information sheets for priority services, for publication on the OMSAR website.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 4 months (Total of 18 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under day-to-day management the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 4 months (Total of 18 working days per month).

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed within 4 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The Technical Assistant will be based in Beirut in the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform, STARCO, Block A, 5th floor.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science , software Engineering, Information Technology, Data Science, Information Management, Digital Transformation, or other related fields is required.
- **Experiences:** A minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience in software and web development, website maintenance and support, digital platforms and e-services, or data collection and analysis.
- **Language:** Fluency in English and Arabic.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

**POSITION INFORMATION**

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E5QcXhTsxjA_h7Oq3bXoa-NwMIwAdEQW/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E5QcXhTsxjA_h7Oq3bXoa-NwMIwAdEQW/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Public understanding of the Internal Security Forces’ (ISF) mandate and responsibilities remains limited, often contributing to unrealistic expectations, misconceptions, and negative perceptions of the institution. These challenges have been further compounded by the conflict, Lebanon’s protracted multidimensional crises, and evolving displacement and return dynamics, which have placed additional demands on security institutions and heightened communities’ need for clear, reliable information and accessible public services.

To address these challenges, UNDP is supporting the ISF in strengthening public communication, community engagement, and institutional coordination, particularly in conflict-affected areas. This includes targeted awareness campaigns and capacity-building activities at the governorate level, engaging ISF stations and substations in coordination with the ISF Public Relations Department. These efforts aim to improve public understanding of the ISF’s mandate, clarify its roles and responsibilities in both routine and crisis contexts, and strengthen linkages with Disaster Risk Management (DRM) structures at national and sub-national levels. At the same time, they seek to reinforce ISF personnel’s understanding of their responsibilities in responding to evolving community needs, particularly in areas affected by displacement and return.

As part of these efforts, UNDP will support the Internal Security Forces (ISF) in developing a digital awareness campaign to inform the public about the ISF’s mandate, services, and available support mechanisms. The campaign will provide clear, accessible, and practical information on relevant procedures, official reporting channels, and sources of assistance. It will translate institutional information into engaging, audience-centered content that addresses communities’ information needs, clarifies common misconceptions, and facilitates access to reliable official information. The campaign will comprise three short, animated videos using a photocollage format, each addressing a specific thematic area related to the ISF’s mandate and community needs.

To this end, UNDP seeks to recruit a Creative Director to lead the creative conceptualization, development, and production of the three videos, ensuring a coherent visual identity, compelling storytelling, and clear, accessible messaging tailored to the target audiences and aligned with the campaign’s overall objectives.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

The Creative Director will work under the supervision of the CTA and in close coordination with the UNDP and ISF teams throughout the assignment. The responsibilities will include:

**a) Creative Direction and Campaign Development**

- Develop the overall creative concept and communication approach, including the creative rationale, narrative direction, key messages, visual identity, and storytelling approach.
- Establish a consistent creative framework across the three videos while addressing the specific objectives of each.

**b) Content Development and Scriptwriting**

- Develop scripts for the three videos, translating approved institutional information and procedures into clear, concise, and actionable messages tailored to the target audience.
- Use an audience-centered storytelling approach, with relatable situations and clear narrative structures appropriate to the required video duration.
- All scripts will use gender-sensitive language.
- Videos will feature Arabic voice-over and English subtitles.
- The Creative Director will coordinate with UNDP and ISF to ensure the accuracy of messages and their alignment with validated institutional procedures.

**c) Graphic Design, Visual Content Development and Animation**

- Develop animated photo-collage assets, including graphic layouts, motion graphics, and transitions, in line with the approved creative concept, narrative, and key messages.
- Coordinate with UNDP and ISF to source required visual materials, ensuring appropriate usage rights and compliance with UNDP requirements.
- Ensure consistency in visual identity, typography, and animation, with outputs optimized for the intended digital platforms.

**d) Audiovisual Production and Post-Production**

- Produce three videos, each 40–60 seconds long, incorporating professional Arabic voice-over and suitable background music, as appropriate to the approved creative approach.
- Ensure that all music and third-party assets are appropriately licensed for the intended use and dissemination.

**e) Digital Platform Adaptation and Final Delivery**

- Prepare the final videos for dissemination through relevant ISF digital and social media channels, providing vertical, square, and horizontal versions, as applicable to the intended platforms.
- Deliver separate English subtitle files, editable source/project files, pictures and applicable third-party assets and licensing documentation.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities noting that the total duration should not exceed 1.5 months (total of 26 working days without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the day-to-day management by the CTA or designated mandated representative(s).
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 1.5 months (total of 26 working days).

The mission is expected to commence upon contract signature and be completed within 1.5 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will be based in Beirut; with services to be completed from home.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** A Bachelor’s degree in communications, advertising, marketing, film and audiovisual production, or another relevant field.
- **Experiences:** At least 8 years of experience in creative direction, developing and implementing public awareness campaigns, or institutional communication campaigns.
- **Language:** Fluency in Arabic and English.

jobs.title: HEAD OF FINANCE DEPARTMENT - YEMEN
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Country Director, your mission will be to lead and ensure effective, transparent and compliant financial management of the organization, safeguarding financial sustainability, ensuring full compliance with donor regulations, Yemeni laws and organizational policies, and providing strategic financial guidance to senior management to support the delivery of humanitarian programs in a complex operating environment.
The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:
Contribute to the definition of mission strategy
Ensure high quality financial accounting for the mission
Ensure high quality cash management for the mission
Provide leadership in financial and budget management
Promote and ensure financial collaboration and coordination with ACF's partners
Mitigate risks of financial fraud and corruption
Manage Finance team in coordination level and provide technical/support leadership for Finance Managers in the base offices.

Profile :

You hold a Master degree or equivalent in finance, accounting, business administration, or other relevant subject or a field.
You have at least 5 years of experience in finance department leadership at country level in one or more challenging context.
You have strong accounting skills and experience, including management of the general ledger, journal entries, payroll, payables and balance sheet, as well as skills in budget preparation and analysis, financial reporting preparation and presentation.
You are familiar with major international donor rules and non-profit accounting.
You have an advanced computer skills in MS Office programs, particularly Excel.
You are able to develop, implement and monitor financial management policies and procedures in challenging environments.
You have excellent managerial skills with proven ability to lead, motivate and develop a team.
You are able to adjust to constantly changing situations while maintaining focus on delivery and follow-through.

Conditions d'emploi

Monthly gross salary from 2597euros to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month

Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)
