- **Place: Kabul – Afghanistan**
- **Starting date: 01st January 2027**
- **Duration of contract: 12 month**

**Humanity & Inclusion (HI)**

is an independent and impartial aid organization working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organization works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At HI, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organization. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

## **JOB CONTEXT:**

The HI Afghanistan operating framework is outlined in the operational strategy (“Stratop”) developed at the beginning of 2026 to 2029. The pillars are Rehabilatation/Health, Resilience & Inclusion / Armed Violence Reduction, and Atlas Logistic.

HI is currently involved in different sectors of activities:

– Physical and functional rehabilitation (both on service provision and training – tech assistance), in development and chronic crisis settings

– Mental Health and Psycho-Social Support (MHPSS)

– Disability & Inclusion

– Economic Inclusion & Basic needs

– Mine Risk Education

– Humanitarian access logistic

HI has 4 offices located in the different provinces of intervention : in Herat (West), Kunduz (North), Kandahar (south) and Kabul,

HI Afghanistan employs 450 national and 9 international staff and has a budget of 7 millions euros. Most fundraising efforts and donor relationships are held at the Kabul level. HI is also part of different fora/coordination bodies (ACBAR, INSO, HAG, etc.) and a member of several clusters, including health, and Co-Chairs the Accountability andDisability Inclusion Working Group (ADIWG).

## Details relating to security risks, isolation, travel, and living conditions

The security and access situation in the country has improved significantly since the conflict ended; however, security measures remain in place as the context remains unpredictable.

International staff share the guesthouses in Kabul. They are spacious, well-equipped, secure, and comfortable, providing adequate living conditions and well-being to the global team, considering the limitations of moving around the city. The guesthouses have sports facilities and common areas for recreational activities. HI in Afghanistan provides a cleaner for the Guesthouses during working days.

## GENERAL MISSION:

Reporting to the Country Director and working in close collaboration with the Operations Manager and Technical Unit Manager, the postholder leads **three key components of the program:**

· **Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support to the Grants Team**

· **Business Development and Fundraising Strategy**

**· Relationship and Partnership Management (qith INGOs and national NGOs)**

**Mission 1: Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support to the Grants Team 40%**

Strengthen the technical and organizational capacities of the Grants team (1 senior Grant officer Manager, 2 Grant Officers)

Under the new organizational structure, the Grants team, previously managed by the Business Development Manager, will now report to the Operations Manager. During the first seven months, the Biz Dev Specialist will prioritize **capacity strengthening and coaching of the Grants team, particularly the Senior Grants Officer**, to increase their technical capacities and autonomy.

*1.1. Capacity assessment and tailored support*

*1.2. Donor reporting coordination and quality assurance*

*1.3. Grants compliance and coordination with other department*

**Mission 2: Business development management 50%**

*2.1 Strategic positioning and planning*

*2.2. Proposal Development and Coordination*

**Mission 3: Relationship and Partnership management 10%**

*3.1. Strategic Relationships and Representation*

*3.2. Partnership Strategy and Management*

REQUIREMENTS

## **Languages**:

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

**Skills:**

- Proposal development, donor reporting and technical writing.
- Experience working in humanitarian, conflict-affected or fragile contexts is essential; experience in Afghanistan or similar contexts is a strong asset.

**Soft skills:**

- Ability to work effectively under pressure in complex and rapidly changing environments.
- Strong organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines.
- High level of integrity, professionalism and respect for humanitarian principles and HI values.

BENEFITS

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

- 12 months International contract
- Starting January 2027 based in Kabul
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI
- Salary from 2757 € gross/month upon experience
- Perdiem: 599 € net/month – paid in the field
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year
- R&R: 5 days every 8 weeks
- Position: Unaccompanied
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI
- If you are resident in the country: local package

jobs.title: Grants Manager - Sudan - M/F
jobs.description:
**ALIMA PRESENTATION**

ALIMA ETHOS: ALIMA’s purpose is to save lives and provide care for the most vulnerable populations, without any discrimination based on identity, religion or politics. Its action is based on the alliance of organizations and individuals, working as close as possible to patients, to provide them with innovative, highquality medical care. We act with humanity and impartiality in accordance with universal medical ethics. To reach patients, we are committed to act in a neutral and independent manner.

Our CHARTER defines the VALUES and PRINCIPLES of our action:

1. Putting the patient First
2. Revolutionizing humanitarian medicine
3. Responsibility and freedom
4. Improve the quality of our actions
5. Showing trust
6. Collective intelligence
7. Environmental responsibility

ALIMA promotes and defends the principles of fundamental human rights. ALIMA has a zero-tolerance approach towards people guilty of acts of gender-based and sexual violence as well as towards inaction in the face of alleged or proven acts of violence. The protection of those benefiting from and impacted by our intervention is our top priority in everything we do. Anyone collaborating with ALIMA agrees to:

- Respect the charter, the code of conduct, the institutional policies including the policy of protection against abuse of power and sexist and sexual violence, the policy of prevention of corruption and fraud;
- Report any violation of the policies, framework documents and procedures to a superior, a referent or to the address provided for this purpose.

CARING - INNOVATING - TOGETHER:

Since its inception in 2009, ALIMA has treated more than 10 million patients and is now operating in 13 countries in Africa. In 2024, we have led 59 humanitarian medical response projects to meet the needs of populations affected by conflict, epidemics and extreme poverty. All of these projects support national health authorities through existing health facilities (including hospitals and health centers). We work in partnership, particularly with local NGOs, whenever possible to ensure that our patients benefit from expertise wherever it is available, whether in their country or in the rest of the world. In addition, to improve the humanitarian response, we conduct operational and clinical research projects, particularly in the areas of malnutrition and viral hemorrhagic fevers.

THE WORK WE DO: Primary and Secondary Health Care, with a main focus on children and women - including treatment and prevention of Acute Malnutrition, Maternal Health, Pediatric Care, Mental Health, response to Epidemics (Ebola, Cholera, Measles, Dengue, Lassa Fever), Surgery, Displaced Populations, and Gender-Based Violence

COUNTRIES WHERE WE WORK: Mali, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Democratic Republic of Congo, Cameroon, South Sudan, Mauritania, Senegal, Sudan, Ethiopia.

**ALIMA IN SUDAN**

ALIMA has been present in Sudan since 2021 with projects in South Kordofan and Khartoum states responding to urgent health and nutrition needs of populations affected by conflict and the COVID-19 pandemic.

ALIMA is currently operating in North and West Darfur. Its intervention aims to reduce mortality and morbidity among internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities affected by conflict through integrated health, nutrition and emergency response activities across North and West Darfur. In North Darfur, following the closure of El Fasher operations in July 2025 due to heightened insecurity, activities were concentrated in Tawila, where ALIMA supports six outpatient facilities and one inpatient facility, manages two cholera treatment facilities (CTU and CTC), supports state-level cholera preparedness, implements Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC), and provides medical services to humanitarian staff. Since August 2026, activities have expanded to Marta, Kergnoi, Katur and Gerni El Fasher, with plans to deploy two mobile clinics in IDP camps. In West Darfur, ALIMA supports five PHCCs in Kulbus, six PHCs in Jebel Moon and one hospital, providing health and nutrition services in collaboration with health authorities and partners including UNICEF, ECHO and EDESIA. Additional activities include a SMART nutrition survey and planned SQLNS distributions.

**MISSION LOCATION** : Sudan (El Geneina) with field visits.

PROTECTION OF BENEFICIARIES AND MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY

Level 3 : As part of his or her duties, the incumbent will be required to visit projects and be in contact with children and/or vulnerable adults. Therefore, a criminal record check or presentation of a certificate of good character will be required. In situations where it is not possible to provide a criminal record or a certificate of good morals and morals, a sworn statement will be requested.

FUNCTIONAL AND HIERARCHICAL LINKS

- Hierarchical Manager : Sudan Head of Mission
- Functional Manager : Grants Advisor ‐ HQ Desk 3

**MISSION AND OBJECTIVE**

Under the supervision of the Head of Mission, the Grants Manager is responsible for implementing the funding strategy in line with ALIMA's countries action plan.

More specifically, they are responsible for mobilizing funding to sustain the implementation of projects. They maintain regular relations with donors, and conduct an active search for funding. They are the guarantor of the drafting of project proposals and reports to donors. They support the technical team in monitoring contractual donor indicators, in collaboration with the Project Coordinators and the Medical Coordinator.

**TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Definition and Monitoring of the Country Financing Strategy

The Grants Manager carries out an analysis of donor strategy and the availability of funding for the country concerned, in order to maintain key information and up-to-date understanding of the priorities. They identify funding needs for the mission in collaboration with the coordination team and propose a relevant funding strategy for the mission. They assess the issues and propose the adaptation of the strategy according to the operational action plan of the country. During their assignment, the Grants Manager monitors the financing strategy and adapts it according to changing needs. In conjunction with the Head of Mission and the Grants Advisor at headquarters, they support the design and implementation of a strategy for acquiring grants and mobilizing resources.

- Maintenance of the relationship with donors

In conjunction with the Head of Mission, they ensure representation with donors and negotiate funding for ALIMA projects. They maintain relations with the national representations of donors who finance the projects through regular quality communication and in-person meetings. They coordinate the visit of donors to projects when the security situation allows it, with the support of the Head of Mission.

- Grants Prospection

The Grants Manager, in support of the Head of Mission, proactively identifies funding opportunities and prospects for new donors, while strengthening their understanding of ALIMA, its mission, and the projects implemented by its teams. They actively monitor the thematic priorities of donors and funding mechanisms in the countries. They carry out donor mapping and intelligence gathering, and regularly inform the country Coordination team on this subject. They develop external presentations and brochures to ensure institutional communication throughout the year.

- Support to operational planning in line with donor and funding priorities

The Grants Manager supports the Project Coordinators and the Coordination team in designing and planning interventions that are aligned with donor strategies. They ensure that proposed interventions are consistent with donors’ thematic and operational priorities, and that all submissions comply with donors’ specific requirements, guidelines and prescribed formats.

They also support the coordination teams in maintaining effective relationships with national and international partner organisations, ensuring regular coordination and follow-up on contractual matters. This includes monitoring partners’ compliance with contractual obligations, donor requirements and reporting deadlines, and facilitating the timely exchange of information and documentation between ALIMA and its partners to ensure proper implementation of partnership agreements.

- Coordination of concept notes and project proposals

The Grants Manager coordinates the development and timely submission of concept notes and project proposals in line with donor deadlines, requirements and funding priorities. They oversee the preparation of project documents in response to funding opportunities, ensuring that all submissions follow ALIMA’s internal processes, meet quality standards and comply with donors’ guidelines and expectations.

- Dissemination of key information on donor procedures and support in monitoring contractual requirements

The Grants Manager ensures that the Coordination team and Project Coordinators are regularly informed of donor guidelines, procedures and compliance requirements. They monitor changes in donor procedures and communicate relevant updates to the teams. They also support Project Coordinators in monitoring contractual obligations and tracking operational developments, including budgetary aspects, in order to identify potential deviations and propose contractual amendments when necessary.

- Data tracking to meet reporting requirements

The Grants Manager develops and maintains effective monitoring and follow-up mechanisms within project monitoring tools to ensure compliance with donor reporting requirements. In collaboration with Data Managers, Medical Coordinators and Medical Referents, they contribute to the collection, verification and compilation of operational data. They ensure that data monitoring tools linked to funding agreements are regularly updated and anticipate reporting deadlines to guarantee data completeness, consistency and quality analysis.

- Production of accurate and analytical narrative reports within the defined deadlines

The Grants Manager coordinates and prepares interim and final narrative reports in accordance with donors’ reporting requirements, guidelines and prescribed formats. They oversee the drafting process, ensuring that reports are based on accurate, comprehensive and up-to-date quantitative and qualitative information collected throughout the project implementation period. They maintain regular communication with Project Coordinators and Medical Referents to gather the necessary information and ensure consistency between commitments made to donors and actual project implementation. They ensure that project achievements, challenges and outcomes are accurately documented and that all reports are submitted within the required deadlines, meeting ALIMA’s quality and compliance standards.

- Contract management

The Grants Manager monitors and oversees donor funding agreements throughout their implementation. They act as the focal point for contractual management matters, maintaining regular communication with donors’ country representatives and relevant internal teams. They maintain and regularly update a shared contract management tool to ensure effective monitoring of contractual obligations, key deadlines, reporting requirements and compliance commitments.

- Ensuring the application of standards in the prevention of abuse

The Grants Manager participates in training and awareness-raising sessions on the prevention of abuse and ensures that ALIMA’s protection standards are applied across all assigned responsibilities. They contribute to integrating protection-related requirements into project proposals, donor reports and contractual documents, including relevant clauses on the prevention of abuse. They actively contribute to creating and maintaining a safe, respectful and protective working environment for beneficiaries, communities and colleagues.

## Experiences and Skills

- Higher education diploma (Master's level or equivalent) related to the position (humanitarian and development, public health, international relations, project management, etc.)
- Excellent level of spoken and written English
- Good command of project management tools (project cycle, logical framework, project proposal, reporting, etc.)
- Professional experience in reporting, project design and/or project management of at least three years, including field experience.
- Excellent analytical, synthesis and writing skills
- Autonomy, capacity for initiative, ability to work in a team and to communicate effectively
- Rigor, motivation, attention to details and willingness to achieve project support objectives
- Understanding and adherence to ALIMA's values and mission

## Conditions

- Contract Term : CDD under French law
- Contract length : 6 months (renewable subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability)
- Salary : According to ALIMA salary scale (level 10) + valuation of experience + Perdiem
- ALIMA covers :
- Travel costs between the expatriate’s country of origin and the mission location accommodation costs.
- Medical cover from the first day of the contract to a month after the date of departure from the mission country for the employee and his/her family. Medical evacuation of the employee.
- Break policy (R&R) : 7 days after three months in country

jobs.title: Protection from Violence Manager Ethiopia North Afar
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you passionate about advancing protection and making a tangible difference in the lives of people affected by violence and displacement?

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a **Protection from Violence (PfV) Project Manager** to lead its project portfolio in the North Area Office. This is an opportunity to provide strategic and operational leadership, drive high-quality protection programming, strengthen accountability and ensure effective project delivery in line with NRC standards, strategies and donor requirements.

As NRC continues to strengthen and expand its PfV programming across Ethiopia, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering integrated protection interventions across Amhara, Afar and Wolkait Tegede Setit Humera, while contributing to the wider programme's ambitions across the country.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Female candidates are encouraged to apply.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your specific responsibilities:

- Train, mentor and coach staff delivering specialised protection services, including protection case management and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), in line with NRC modalities, tools and guidance.
- Promote consistency and alignment of specialised protection activities across field teams and support the development or adaptation of common guidelines, tools and standard operating procedures (SOPs) where required.
- Ensure that tools and SOPs align with NRC approaches to specialised protection services and that appropriate transition or capacity-development plans are in place where needed.
- Lead or coordinate area-based, conflict-sensitive analysis and monitoring of protection risks to inform programme design, implementation and adaptation.
- Ensure that an appropriate case-management tracking system is maintained or established, with due attention to confidentiality, informed consent and data protection.
- Monitor trends in protection risks emerging from specialised protection services and engage with NRC teams and other protection actors to address risks at community level.
- Coordinate with the Monitoring and Evaluation team to ensure appropriate monitoring approaches and tools and promote safe monitoring of specialised protection activities.
- Capture and share lessons learned on project methodology and implementation, and use findings to improve programme quality.
- Provide technical and managerial support for implementation of specialised protection work plans.
- Contribute to regional donor reporting, including narrative and financial inputs.
- Lead the development and design of Civilian Self-Protection (CSP) activities, ensuring that interventions are contextually appropriate and informed by protection analysis.
- Ensure that learning from CSP implementation is documented and incorporated into programme adaptation and staff development.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBZxn6Fs8NTRYp9ytigCMdvAWezj2k686m80DaIw4drkbo?e=zUcUnn) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum five years of experience in a senior project implementation or management position in a humanitarian or recovery context.
- Experience working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Technical expertise in Protection programming.
- Demonstrated results relevant to the responsibilities of the position.
- Knowledge of own leadership skills and profile.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Technical expertise and field experience in general protection case management in operation area.
- Field experience conducting case management and referrals in low-resource settings.
- Strong interpersonal skills and knowledge of the North Area operational context.
- Knowledge of local language
- Experience managing teams and working with IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Afar, Asyita.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Programme Officer
jobs.description:
**Based:** We welcome applications from those with the right to work in Ireland. The role offers the option of hybrid working.

**Contract:** Permanent Contract

**Salary range** €38,000 to €45,000 *per annum,depending on experience*

**Work hours** Monday-Friday, 37.5 hours per week

**Benefits Flexible and hybrid working** arrangements and flexi-time;

\- **25 days** per annum annual leave, increasing by 1 day every two years to a **maximum of 28**

\- Option of joining **PRSA** contributory pension after 1 year

## **Job Overview**

CBM Ireland is seeking an experienced Programme Officer to support the oversight of it’s disability inclusion work in Africa and Asia. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to improving maternal and child health and support innovative newborn eye screening.

**About the Role**

Based in Ireland, you will be a member of a four-person Programme team, managed by the Programme Manager, and work alongside the Grants Manager and Programme Support Officer. You will play a critical role in ensuring CBM Ireland’s disability inclusion portfolio meets all donor compliance and reporting requirements. The portfolio is funded by a range of donors including Irish Aid, the EU, Electric Aid and The Ireland Funds.

## **Responsibilities and Duties**

**What will you do:**

- Facilitate project kick-off, review (including mid-term) and close-out meetings, documenting key decisions, risks and action points, and tracking follow-up actions, owners and timelines.
- Coordinate grant amendments (e.g., no-cost extensions, budget revisions, reprogramming requests and contract addenda), including internal clearances, donor correspondence drafts, and ensuring timely submission, with accurate filing and system updates i.e. Global Online.
- Conduct field monitoring visits to verify programme implementation against plans, strengthen oversight and accountability, validate reported results and documentation, and identify risks or compliance issues requiring follow-up.
- Review partner reports and submissions to ensure accuracy, consistency and completeness, including verification of indicator data against supporting evidence.
- Coordinate the drafting, compilation and timely submission of high-quality donor reports (narrative and financial), ensuring alignment with approved proposals, budgets and grant frameworks, and effective input from relevant teams.
- Monitor grant compliance requirements (e.g., visibility/branding, safeguarding, due diligence, data protection), proactively identify and track risks, and support the implementation of mitigation actions.
- Support preparedness for donor spot-checks, monitoring visits and audits, including coordinating documentation, briefing relevant teams and accompanying field visits as required.
- Support new business development by identifying and tracking funding opportunities, supporting engagement with prospective donors, and coordinating with country teams to develop high-quality, compliant proposals aligned with organisational strategy and programme priorities.
- Contribute to internal learning and continuous improvement by capturing lessons learned and good practice from audits, report reviews and close-outs, and supporting updates to tools and systems (templates, checklists, trackers and filing conventions).
- Participate in relevant coordination forums, working groups, and policy discussions to inform organisational learning and programme development.
- Develop programme-related communications content and products for donor visibility and CBM external communications.
- Undertake any other duties as may reasonably be required, contributing flexibly to programme delivery and organisational priorities as they evolve.

The description of responsibilities is not exhaustive, and additional tasks may be required as defined by the organisational requirements as they evolve.

## Person Specification

### CBM Ireland welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds and people with lived experience of disability.

### Essential Requirements:

- At least three years’ demonstrable experience with an INGO.
- Experience working on Irish Aid and EU funded projects and other institutional donors;
- Fluent in English, French at a standard to allow drafting of technical documents a benefit.
- Strong understanding of compliance, reporting, and financial oversight
- Experience of working on disability inclusion in projects, partnership and networks.
- Social media, creative content development skills are welcome;
- Willingness and aptitude to travel to programme locations internationally.

**Skills/competencies/personal qualities**

- Detail oriented and focussed;
- Highly organised with strong attention to detail
- Excellent communication and coordination skills
- Financial and analytical skills
- Ability to work effectively across teams
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- A good team player and positive contributor to wider office culture;

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor's Degree in Global Health, Development Studies, Business Administration, or a related field or experience of working on international development.

## Useful Information

CBM Ireland is a Christian organisation, being a member of a particular faith is not a requirement of this role - we encourage applications from all faiths and none. Respect for others’ faiths, however, including how they practice and giving them the space to do so, is essential. CBM Ireland is an equal opportunities employer. All applicants should have the legal right to live and work in Ireland before applying for this position.

At CBM Ireland, safeguarding is our top priority. We are fully committed to creating a safe and respectful environment for everyone, especially the most vulnerable. Inclusiveness is at the heart of everything we do, ensuring that people with disabilities are not only included but empowered to thrive. Our mission is to build a world where everyone is valued, protected, and has equal opportunities.

If you want to find out more about our accountability, please click on the following **link:** [Compliance — CBM Ireland](https://www.cbm.ie/compliance)

### Ready to dive into the incredible work happening at CBM Ireland?

### Find out more by clicking the following link: [CBM Ireland](https://www.cbm.ie/careers)

**Our Vision:** an inclusive world in which all people with disabilities enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.

**Our Mission:** fighting to end the cycle of poverty and disability.

**Our Values**:

- We champion **inclusion**
- We strive for **justice**
- We pursue **excellence**
- We embrace **partnership**
- We live with **integrity**

jobs.title: Legal Registration Project Manager
jobs.description:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Legal Registration Project Manager**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognising the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organisation from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa (MSF EA) is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Project Manager will be hired on a full-time basis (100% working time) to support MSF EA in:

1. Completing the legal registration of MSF EA in Rwanda;
2. Handling any legal matters arising from or related to the registration.

This position will be ***hierarchically***and ***functionally***accountable to the ***General Director***.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

The Project Manager will work closely with the Intersectional Legal Department (ILD) Units 4 and 5, and under the general coordination of MSF EA management team. The work will be structured in the following tasks:

- Review and update the **registration framework**, including timeline for execution and documentation requirement list;
- Coordinate between MSF EA teams and Rwandan local lawyers in the collection of required legal **documentation** for the registration;
- Supervise the **registration process in Rwanda** in order to achieve primary registration as quickly and securely as possible;
- Supervise the drafting of the legally required **framework MoU, Action Plan and all related documents**, which shall be part of the registration document package;
- Advise MSF EA management team and Board on local law requirements:
- regarding the finalisation of the Rwandan entity **statutes**;
- needing their approvals and delegation;
- regarding operational presence and **social mission activities** to be deployed in Rwanda;
- financial and budgetary aspects.
- Share **progress** with MSF EA on a weekly basis- highlighting any changes to the proposed timelines for execution and potential bottlenecks to the registration requiring institutional support.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Advanced university degree in law, international law, with relevant experience in international or comparative legal research.

**Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in project management, legal/regulatory affairs, NGO/INGO registration, compliance, or institutional development, ideally with an international NGO or humanitarian organisation.
- **Legal registration experience:** Demonstrated experience managing or supporting NGO/INGO legal registration processes, including primary registration and branch/subsidiary registration. Experience with Rwanda and/or Kenya registration frameworks is highly desirable.

**Knowledge**

- Strong knowledge of Rwandan NGO/INGO registration law and Kenyan INGO/NGO regulatory requirements, including statutes, MoUs, action plans, branch registration, and compliance obligations. Familiarity with MSF structures is desirable.

**Project management skills**

- Proven ability to develop workplans, timelines, documentation lists, risk tracking, and progress reports; coordinate multiple stakeholders; and deliver under tight deadlines.

**Legal drafting and advisory skills:**

- Excellent ability to draft/review legal documents, statutes, MoUs, action plans, registration packages, and briefs; ability to advise senior management, Board, and teams on legal, statutory, financial, and operational issues.

**Coordination and diplomacy:**

- Strong experience liaising with local lawyers, government authorities, MSF teams, management, and Board members. Excellent negotiation, intercultural, and communication skills.

**Language:**

- Fluency in English (spoken and written) is required. French, Kinyarwanda, and/or Swahili are an asset.

**Competencies**

- Ability to work autonomously, handle confidential matters, and commit to MSF principles and humanitarian values.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:***

- **Job Location**: Based in MSF EA office Kigali (Rwanda), in partnership with WEC Sourcing.
- **Contract**: 6 months renewable, full-time contract.
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.
- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 48,698 at HQ Grade 11** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
- **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
- **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
- **Employer Pension contribution**: 10% of basic salary:
- **International insurance** for both medical and disability**.**
- **Relocation support**; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
- **Work-life balance**: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- **School fees benefits**: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
- **Diverse team composition**; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
- **Career Development**: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
- **Mobility**: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
- **Annual home leave ticket**: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Psicólogo (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

Por favor verifique que cumpla con todos o la mayoría de los requisitos para aplicar.

***¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades***

El/La Psicólogo/a será responsable de contribuir a la implementación de acciones de Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial (SMAPS) dirigidas a personas, familias y comunidades afectadas por emergencias y desastres, incluyendo apoyo psicosocial comunitario y atención psicológica cuando corresponda.

Asimismo, contribuirá al fortalecimiento de las capacidades del voluntariado de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, a la integración de SMAPS dentro de las actividades del Hospital de Campaña de la Cruz Roja y de otros sectores de la respuesta, y al establecimiento de mecanismos seguros de identificación, apoyo, referencia y seguimiento.

**Funciones y responsabilidades**

- Participar en evaluaciones de necesidades de Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial (SMAPS), mediante metodologías individuales, grupales y comunitarias adaptadas al contexto, identificando necesidades, recursos, capacidades y grupos que puedan requerir apoyo adicional.
- Brindar apoyo psicosocial básico y aplicar habilidades de Primeros Auxilios Psicológicos (PAP) en situaciones de crisis.
- Realizar valoración y apoyo psicológico individual o grupal cuando esté indicado, de acuerdo con las necesidades identificadas, sus competencias profesionales y los protocolos establecidos.
- Identificar de manera segura a personas que puedan requerir apoyo adicional o atención especializada, facilitar las referencias correspondientes y contribuir al seguimiento cuando proceda, de acuerdo con los protocolos establecidos.
- Planificar y facilitar actividades comunitarias de apoyo psicosocial, incluyendo psicoeducación, actividades grupales y recreativas, fortalecimiento de redes de apoyo y otras intervenciones adaptadas a las necesidades y características de la población.
- Brindar acompañamiento técnico y supervisión de apoyo al voluntariado que desarrolla actividades SMAPS, promoviendo intervenciones seguras, pertinentes y acordes con sus competencias.
- Mantener registros de las actividades y atenciones realizadas y contribuir al monitoreo, análisis y elaboración de informes conforme a los protocolos establecidos.
- Garantizar la confidencialidad, la protección de datos, el consentimiento informado cuando corresponda y el respeto por la dignidad, seguridad y diversidad de las personas atendidas.
- Fortalecer las capacidades del voluntariado de la Cruz Roja Venezolana mediante formación, acompañamiento técnico y supervisión en PAP, apoyo psicosocial comunitario, psicoeducación, identificación segura de necesidades y mecanismos de referencia.
- Contribuir a acciones de bienestar y apoyo psicosocial dirigidas al personal y voluntariado involucrado en la respuesta, incluyendo apoyo en situaciones de malestar agudo y facilitando el acceso a atención adicional cuando sea necesario.
- Coordinar e integrar las acciones SMAPS con los equipos de Salud, Salud Comunitaria, PGI, CEA, RFL, WASH y otros componentes de la respuesta, según las necesidades identificadas.
- Contribuir a la adaptación y elaboración de materiales de información, psicoeducación y sensibilización, asegurando su pertinencia cultural y contextual.
- Promover y actuar de acuerdo con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja, el Marco y la Política SMAPS del Movimiento y las normas y procedimientos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
- Cumplir otras funciones relacionadas con el cargo asignadas por su supervisor/a directo/a.

**Lugar de trabajo**

Caracas, con disponibilidad para trasladarse a La Guaira.

**Requisitos**

- Título Universitario en Psicología.

- Dominio del idioma español; conocimientos de inglés serán valorados.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Alto sentido de ética profesional, confidencialidad y respeto por la dignidad humana.

jobs.title: Consultance - Évaluation Programme DGD quiquennal - SDSR
jobs.description:
[***Informations détaillées via ce lien***](https://jobpage.cvwarehouse.com/?companyGuid=14dacb70-fd86-419f-baa7-a286e0565aac&lang=fr-FR&job=405680&q=Consultance-Evaluation-Programme-DGD-quiquennal-SDSR&api=false)

## Contexte de la mission

***Mission et vision de Médecins du Monde***

Médecins du Monde Belgique (MdM-BE) est une association internationale de développement médical faisant partie d'un réseau international. Nous fournissons une assistance médicale aux groupes vulnérables, en Belgique, Europe du Sud-Est, Afrique du Nord, de l’Ouest et Centrale. Nous voulons une couverture universelle de santé où chaque personne a accès aux soins, sans obstacles (financiers, culturels, géographiques, etc.).

Nos projets se destinent à toutes les personnes qui n'ont pas ou plus d'accès aux soins de santé. En particulier, ils se structurent en cinq axes : les personnes en marge de la société (personnes sans-abri, sans papier, usagères de drogues, travailleuses du sexe, etc.) ; les enfants en situation de vulnérabilité ; les femmes (accompagnées dans leur combat pour l'égalité ou contre les violences sexuelles par exemple) ; les personnes migrantes ou déplacées et les victimes de crises ou de conflits.

Pour mener à bien notre mission, nous nous basons sur trois piliers :

- Soigner : donner un réel accès aux soins aux populations.
- Changer : plus qu'aider, nous voulons changer les choses à long terme.
- Témoigner : nous ne restons pas silencieux.

Grâce à notre expérience et notre présence sur le terrain, nous interpellons les pouvoirs (locaux, régionaux et (inter)nationaux) avec des faits, des chiffres et des réalités. Nos projets suivent une série de valeurs communes à toute notre organisation : Justice sociale, Empowerment, Indépendance, Engagement, Equilibre.

La présente évaluation s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme quinquennal (2022-2026), financé par la DGD à travers les outcomes SDSR intitulé « L’accès à des services de santé de qualité assure le droit et la capacité à la population d’exercer librement sa vie affective, sexuelle et reproductive dans le district sanitaire d'Agadez Commune, au Niger. » et SDM intitulé « La protection des personnes en situation de migration est renforcée par l’accès à des services de santé et d’appui psychosocial de qualité adaptés, dans la commune d’Agadez, au Niger ».

Cette évaluation finale porte en particulier sur les projets partie du programme liées aux deux outcomes, qui s’intègrent également dans les objectives spécifique du programme commun.

## Objectif de l'évaluation

**Objectifs général et spécifique(s)**

L'objectif de cette évaluation finale est de rendre compte des résultats obtenus des outcomes 4 & 5 «L’accès à des services de santé de qualité assure le droit et la capacité à la population d’exercer librement sa vie affective, sexuelle et reproductive dans le district sanitaire d'Agadez Commune, au Niger.», et «La protection des personnes en situati on de migration est renforcée par l’accès à des services de santé et d’appui psychosocial de qualité adaptés, dans la commune d’Agadez, au Niger. », et portera sur l’ensemble de ses résultats et activités mis en œuvre au Niger dans la commune d’Agadez. **Elle permet d’apprécier, à la fin du programme quinquennal l'efficacité, l’impact, et la durabilité, ainsi que l’intégration transversale du genre et de l’environnement, du plaidoyer et de la santé mentale.**

**Cette évaluation finale sera menée par un.e consultant.e/équipe de consultant.e.s. externe qui devra également identifier les bonnes pratiques et fournir des recommandations** pour des interventions similaires visant à renforcer la capacité des communautés et du système de santé. Les résultats de cette évaluation permettront de soutenir le plaidoyer en direction des autorités sanitaires afin de faire évoluer les approches et modèles de formation en santé sexuelle et reproduction, droits humains, équité, accès aux services ainsi qu’à la coordination et bonne gouvernance pour mieux adapter la stratégie. Ils seront autant d’arguments pour une mise à l’échelle sur d’autres districts sanitaires au niveau national ainsi que dans d’autres pays d’intervention.

Les résultats du projet étant généraux, l’équipe d’évaluation devra se référer aux principaux types d’indicateurs du cadre de résultats qui seront fournis dans la documentation du projet.

**L’évaluation devra analyser la théorie du changement du projet**.

**L’évaluation conjointe** de ces deux outcomes, mis en œuvre au Niger dans la commune d’Agadez, devra inclure **une analyse comparative du modèle** d’intervention conçu historiquement au niveau du siège de MdM et utilisé dans ces deux projets, **et son adaptabilité contextuelle**.

**L’évaluation finale du programme quinquennal** adoptera une approche intégrée et transversale permettant d’apprécier conjointement les changements générés par les outcomes SDSR et SDM, tout en tenant compte de leurs objectifs, de leurs cibles et de leurs contextes d’intervention spécifiques. Elle examinera la contribution à l’amélioration de l’accès équitable à des services de santé de qualité, au renforcement de la connaissance et de l’exercice des droits, à l’autonomisation des personnes et à la participation communautaires. Elle analysera également les effets du renforcement des capacités des prestataires et des acteurs institutionnels, de la coordination entre les parties prenantes et des actions de plaidoyer sur la qualité, l’accessibilité et la pérennité des services. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux changements observés auprès des femmes, des adolescentes, des personnes migrantes et des autres groupes vulnérables, ainsi qu’aux évolution des pratiques professionnelles, des normes sociales et des mécanismes de gouvernance. Cette démarche permettra d’identifier les résultats communs, les complémentarités entre les deux outcomes, les facteurs ayant favorisé ou limité les changements et les enseignements à tirer pour renforcer la durabilité des acquis et orienter les interventions futures de MdM- BE et des ses partenaires au Niger selon le contexte du pays.

**Cette évaluation finale vise les objectifs spécifiques suivants :**

1. **Evaluer la performance et les résultats du projet** :

- Évaluer la performance globale du projet au regard des critères d'évaluation définis:efficacité, l'impact et la durabilité, afin d’apprécier le niveau d’atteinte des objectifs et des résultats escomptés.
- Mesurer les changements et les effets observés auprès des ayants droit et des autres parties prenantes, et apprécier dans quelle mesure les interventions ont contribué à répondre aux besoins identifiés.

1. **Apprécier l’intégration des dimensions transversales**:

- Analyser dans quelle mesure les principes liés au genre, l’environnement, le plaidoyer, la participation des communautés hôtes, migrantes, et l’accès équitable de tous les groupes cibles aux activités du projet, surtout les plus vulnérables, ont été intégrés dans la conception et la mise en œuvre du projet.
- Apprécier les effets du projet sur les différents groupes bénéficiaires, en tenant compte notamment des éventuelles disparités liées au genre, à la santé mentale, au plaidoyer mené à la vulnérabilité ou à l’accès aux services.

1. **Identifier les bonnes pratiques et tirer les leçons apprises**:

- Identifier, documenter et analyser les bonnes pratiques, approches innovantes et facteurs de succès ayant contribué à l’atteinte des résultats du projet.
- Identifier les principales difficultés, contraintes et leçons apprises au cours de la mise en œuvre afin d’éclairer la conception et la mise en œuvre de futures interventions selon le contexte du pays.

1. **Formuler des recommandations pour les futures interventions :**

- Formuler les recommandations opérationnelles, réalistes et contextualisées fondées sur les résultats et les enseignements de l’évaluation, en vue de renforcer, l’efficacité, l’impact et la durabilité des interventions futures sur la SDSR et la SDM.
- Identifier les conditions nécessaires à la pérennisation et/ou à la réplication des approches ayant démontré leur pertinence et efficacité.

1. **Evaluer la redevabilité envers les populations**

- Apprécier dans quelle mesure les mécanismes de participation, d’information, des retours d’information et de gestion des plaintes ont permis de renforcer la redevabilité du projet envers les populations vulnérables.
- Evaluer la perception des populations, des autorités et des parties prenantes concernant la pertinence, la qualité et les résultats des interventions.
- Documenter les principaux résultats et enseignements de l’évaluation afin de favoriser une communication transparente et fondée sur les évidences auprès des différentes parties prenantes.

## **Profil recherché**

**Education**

- Diplôme universitaire de 2ème cycle (BAC + 5) en : statistique, sciences sociales, santé publique, gestion, protection ou autre discipline connexe
- Disposer d’un certificat valide en technique d’évaluation de projets humanitaires / de développement ou être membre ou affilié à une association d’experts en évaluation reconnue, est un atout

**Expérience**

- Expérience d’au moins 5 ans dans le travail d’évaluation de projets dans les secteurs de la santé et de la migration
- Expérience avec des méthodes d'évaluation innovantes (qualitatives) et des méthodes d'enquête sociale (collecte de données, saisie, analyse), des entretiens semi-structurés et des discussions de groupe.
- Expérience avérée dans l’utilisation de méthodes d’évaluation qualitatives, innovantes et participatives (entretiens semi-structurés, discussions de groupe, observation, ateliers, outils visuels et interactifs adaptés aux contextes de faible littératie), ainsi que dans la collecte, l’analyse qualitative et la triangulation des données.
- Expérience dans la collecte et l’analyse des données, et dans la consultation de groupes marginalisés (femmes, jeunes, personnes en situation de vulnérabilité).
- Expérience dans la mise en œuvre de démarches éthiques rigoureuses : consentement éclairé, confidentialité, principe « do no harm », sauvegarde et gestion des situations sensibles, y compris auprès de mineur·e·s et d’adolescent·e·s.
- Expérience dans le ou les pays d’intervention. Les équipes d’évaluation incluant des personnes résidant dans les pays ou régions du projet, ou associant des expert·e·s nationaux, sont appréciées.
- Expérience dans l’évaluation de projets financés par la DGD appréciée.

**Qualité et justification de la méthodologie**

- Proposition technique claire et adaptée basée sur la bonne compréhension des questions d’évaluation.
- Description générale et pertinence de la méthodologie.
- Présentation des outils proposés à chaque étape du processus d’évaluation.
- Calendrier de travail cohérent avec la méthodologie et les délais escomptés.
- Capacité démontrée de déployer les équipes d’évaluation dans les zones d’intervention, avec une composition d’équipe adaptée (genre, langues locales, connaissance du terrain).
- Présentation des outils proposés à chaque étape du processus d’évaluation, y compris les modalités de validation et de restitution aux parties prenantes.

**Autres atouts**

- Excellente maîtrise du français.
- La connaissance des langues locales est appréciée.
- Expérience de travail au sein ou avec une association internationale, en particulier dans le domaine de la Santé et de la Migration.
- Connaissance du contexte des pays d’intervention.

## Budget

Le budget devra inclure au minimum les éléments suivants :

- Les journées d’expertise des différents membres de l’équipe de consultance pour la réalisation de cette évaluation (Hébergement, frais de voyage, d’assurance et de séjour)
- Les frais occasionnés pour les déplacements (la logistique, l'hébergement, frais de voyage, d’assurance et de séjour) seront à la charge du consultant pour la phase terrain, et donc à prévoir dans le budget. L'équipe MdM-BE facilitera les démarches avec les autorités pour les mouvements sur le terrain au niveau de la commune d’Agadez.
- Les frais annexes nécessaires à la réalisation de l’évaluation et de sa restitution (reprographie,…)

**Le budget de cette consultance s’élève à maximum 32 500 euros pour les deux outcomes.**

jobs.title: Photography & Storytelling Trainers
jobs.description:
**PhotoVoice: Our Community, Our Stories**

Collateral Repair Project (CRP), in collaboration with the British Council in Amman, is inviting experienced photographers and storytellers to join our Photovoice: Our Community, Our Stories project as TOT trainers.

Photovoice is a community-based project that brings young people aged 18-25 from different backgrounds together to explore their communities, share their experiences, and tell their own stories through photography and storytelling.

We are looking for **two** passionate professionals who can share their knowledge, inspire creativity, and equip our project facilitators with practical skills to guide young people through this journey.

**Photography Trainer**

The selected trainer will deliver two days of training (4 hours per day), focusing on:

- Strengthening and building on community photographers’ existing photography skills and techniques.
- Photography as a tool for communication and storytelling.
- Practical photography exercises and creative activities.
- Different perspectives and ways of seeing the community.
- Ethical photography, consent, privacy, and respectful representation.

Key Responsibilities:

- Develop and prepare the training materials, presentations, and practical exercises for training days.
- Design an engaging and practical training plan.
- Deliver the two-day Training of Trainers (ToT).
- Provide facilitators with practical activities and guidance they can use when working with young people.
- Share relevant resources and recommendations with the project team.

**Storytelling Trainer**

The selected trainer will deliver two days of training (4 hours per day), focusing on:

- Storytelling and visual storytelling.
- Developing stories and messages behind photographs.
- Connecting personal experiences with community stories.
- Communication, listening, and public speaking.
- Inclusive and ethical storytelling.

Key Responsibilities:

- Develop and prepare the training materials, presentations, and storytelling exercises for training days.
- Design an engaging and practical training plan.
- Deliver the two-day Training of Trainers (ToT).
- Provide facilitators with practical storytelling activities and techniques they can use when working with young people.
- Share relevant resources and recommendations with the project team.

**Who Can Apply?**

We welcome applicants who:

- Have relevant experience in photography or storytelling.
- Have experience delivering workshops, training, or facilitating learning activities.
- Enjoy working with young people and people from diverse backgrounds.
- Are passionate about creative expression, community engagement, and giving people opportunities to share their voices.

**Assignment Details**

**Duration:** 2 days per trainer, 4 hours per day.

**Location:** CRP Downtown Community Center, Amman.

**Fee:** 160 JOD per trainer for the complete two-day assignment, including preparation of training materials.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Proyecto (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

Por favor verifique que cumpla con todos o la mayoría de los requisitos para aplicar.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Oficial de proyecto tendrá como responsabilidad principal garantizar la implementación integral del proyecto, mediante la coordinación técnica y administrativa de las actividades ejecutadas en las localidades correspondientes. Esto incluye la selección adecuada de comunidades beneficiarias, supervisión de actividades comunitarias y atenciones médicas, monitoreo y seguimiento de indicadores, aseguramiento de la correcta ejecución presupuestaria y recolección de fuentes de verificación. Además, el gerente de proyectos actuará como enlace entre la Cruz Roja Venezolana y las distintas organizaciones aliadas, siendo responsable de la elaboración de informes mensuales y contribuyendo a los reportes requeridos por el socio donante, así como de promover alianzas estratégicas y fortalecer las capacidades locales a través de capacitaciones y actividades educativas.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Supervisar la implementación del proyecto en los puntos de atención, asegurando que se cumplan los objetivos y plazos establecidos según los lineamientos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana y aliados.
- Coordinar la selección de comunidades beneficiarias asegurando el cumplimiento de los criterios establecidos en el proyecto.
- Coordinar y gestionar los recursos humanos, financieros y materiales necesarios para la ejecución del proyecto.
- Coordinar y trabajar en conjunto con los Coordinadores Locales y los equipos asignados al proyecto para asegurar la implementación efectiva de atenciones médicas, actividades comunitarias y generación de reportes.
- Implementar sistemas de monitoreo y evaluación para medir el progreso y el impacto del proyecto.
- Garantizar la coordinación, programación y supervisión de actividades comunitarias en las filiales participantes.
- Realizar visitas de campo regulares para supervisar las actividades del proyecto y asegurar la calidad de la implementación.
- Asegurar la correcta recolección, transcripción y análisis de información de las actividades realizadas.
- Llevar control activo de las fuentes de verificación de actividades, incluyendo el registro fotográfico y documental.
- Elaborar reportes detallados sobre las actividades del proyecto, incluyendo un informe mensual conforme a los formatos establecidos.
- Supervisar la gestión financiera del proyecto, incluyendo la elaboración de presupuestos, seguimiento de gastos y preparación de informes financieros.
- Asegurar el cumplimiento de las políticas y procedimientos financieros de la organización y gestionar las relaciones con los donantes previa autorización de la dirección de programas.
- Supervisar las obras y asegurar su alineación con los estándares técnicos y objetivos del proyecto.
- Respetar y hacer cumplir las normativas de visibilidad y difusión establecidas por la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
- Coordinar, junto con voluntarios y equipos locales, actividades de protección, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial, insumos no alimentarios entre otras.
- Asegurar la visibilidad del proyecto a través de la comunicación efectiva con las partes interesadas y la comunidad.
- Desarrollar y mantener relaciones con socios, autoridades locales y otras organizaciones relevantes.
- Asegurar que el proyecto cumpla con los estándares de calidad y las políticas de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
- Implementar medidas correctivas cuando sea necesario para mejorar la calidad del proyecto.
- Coordinar con otros departamentos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana y con socios del Movimiento de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Facilitar la colaboración y el intercambio de conocimientos entre los diferentes equipos y proyectos.
- Garantizar la confidencialidad de la información del proyecto, incluyendo datos presupuestarios.
- Realizar otras tareas relacionadas con el tipo de puesto y las asignadas por su superior inmediato, en función de las características y condiciones especiales del puesto, para brindar un servicio de calidad que cumpla con las metas y objetivos de la institución, de acuerdo con el Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo de la Sociedad Nacional.

*Reporte*

El/La Oficial de proyecto le reportará a la Dirección de Programas.

*Viajes*

Debe tener disponibilidad para viajar por el país.

*Equipos*

Es altamente deseable que cuente con equipos suficientes para el desempeño de su función de manera remota: laptop y/o computadora, buena conexión a Internet, entre otros.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas (Sede central de la Cruz Roja Venezolana).

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Grado universitario en un campo relevante al proyecto como: estudios internacionales, salud pública, ingeniería industrial, administración de empresas. Un grado universitario de primer nivel en combinación con cinco (5) años de experiencia laboral será aceptado como un grado universitario avanzado.
- Se requiere un mínimo de cinco (2) años de experiencia profesional en la implementación y coordinación de programas y proyectos humanitarios, preferiblemente con un enfoque en Migración y Protección.
- Fuertes habilidades de gestión de programas, incluyendo planificación, seguimiento de actividades, gestión financiera, monitoreo y evaluación.
- Antecedentes técnicos en una o más de las siguientes áreas: Salud, Protección, Migración, Finanzas y Logística es una ventaja.
- Experiencia en la gestión de proyectos financiados por donantes internacionales, es requerido.
- Fuertes habilidades analíticas y de redacción, capaces de fomentar y mantener alianzas.
- Experiencia en trabajo con organizaciones locales, para impulsar su fortalecimiento.
- Capacidad para capacitar y guiar al personal y voluntarios, para proporcionar apoyo técnico y fortalecimiento de capacidades.
- Experiencia en facilitar procesos de desarrollo organizacional es deseable.
- Experiencia trabajando con el Movimiento de la Cruz Roja / Media Luna Roja es deseable.
- Fluidez oral y escrita en español e inglés es un requisito.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, capacidad para construir relaciones a todos los niveles.
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y como miembro de un equipo.
- Capacidad y acuerdo para adherirse a los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Preferiblemente experiencia laboral en contextos de emergencia con gestión de voluntarios.
- Capacidad de mantener la confidencialidad.
