jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Oficial de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH) es responsable de coordinar y ejecutar las actividades del área ASH, contribuyendo al desarrollo de estrategias, la implementación técnica en terreno y el seguimiento de los proyectos, asegurando que se cumplan los estándares de calidad, eficiencia y sostenibilidad en comunidades afectadas por emergencias, desastres y otras situaciones de vulnerabilidad.

Será el/la encargado/a de:

- Coordinar y ejecutar proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene en comunidades priorizadas, asegurando el cumplimiento de estándares nacionales e internacionales. Las actividades pueden incluir:
- Respuesta a emergencias ASH
- Rehabilitación, instalación y mantenimiento de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y saneamiento, incluyendo componentes electromecánicos.
- Rehabilitación, instalación y mejoras en sistemas de energía, principalmente energías limpias
- Promoción de la higiene y uso eficiente del agua
- Contribuir a la elaboración de una propuesta estratégica ASH 2026–2030, en alineación con la estrategia general de la CRV.
- Identificar oportunidades de mejora e innovación en las intervenciones ASH, con base en las experiencias de campo.
- Brindar asistencia técnica a los equipos de las filiales para la correcta implementación de las intervenciones.
- Participar en estudios técnicos relacionados con la disponibilidad de recursos hídricos y análisis de calidad del agua, y aplicar sus resultados en el diseño de soluciones.
- Coordinar y facilitar procesos de capacitación técnica dirigidos a voluntarios y personal involucrado en proyectos ASH.
- Implementar metodologías participativas como PHAST, así como campañas comunitarias de educación y sensibilización en prácticas seguras de higiene y gestión del agua.
- Representar técnicamente al área ASH en espacios de coordinación con socios estratégicos, instituciones gubernamentales y actores humanitarios, previa autorización de la Dirección de Programas.
- Elaborar informes técnicos y de progreso de los proyectos, y generar reportes conforme a los requerimientos de la Dirección de Programas, donantes y organismos reguladores.
- Colaborar con otros sectores de la organización (como salud, gestión de riesgos, protección, entre otros) para asegurar la integración efectiva de las intervenciones.
- Gestionar y dar seguimiento al uso de insumos técnicos y materiales requeridos para la ejecución de los proyectos, incluyendo su solicitud, almacenamiento y distribución.
- Dar seguimiento al presupuesto asignado para las intervenciones, conforme a los procedimientos internos y garantizando la rendición de cuentas.
- Asegurar la aplicación de protocolos de seguridad y bioseguridad durante la ejecución de actividades en terreno.
- Cumplir y hacer cumplir las normativas internas de la CRV en materia de ética, protección, seguridad y estándares humanitarios, así como las leyes nacionales vigentes.
- Ejecutar otras tareas asignadas por su superior inmediato para contribuir al cumplimiento de los objetivos del área y de la organización.

*Reporte*

El/La Oficial de WASH le reportará a la Dirección de Programas.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas, con disponibilidad de viajes a nivel nacional.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Título universitario ingeniería civil, mecánica, industrial, eléctrica, o similares.
- Especialización o formación en Gestión de Recursos Hídricos, Saneamiento, Agua Potable y/o Higiene Comunitaria (deseable).
- Mínimo cinco (5) años de experiencia en diseño, ejecución y gestión de proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene en comunidades vulnerables.
- Experiencia comprobada en gestión de infraestructura WASH, mantenimiento de equipos y sistemas de potabilización de agua, así como tratamiento de agua a nivel domiciliario.
- Experiencia en capacitación de personal y comunidades en temas de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Experiencia en manejo de presupuestos, planificación y monitoreo de proyectos humanitarios.
- Conocimientos en metodologías de evaluación de necesidades WASH y respuesta en emergencias.
- Conocimiento en manejo de software de diseño como AutoCAD, EPANET, u otros softwares técnicos (deseable).
- Capacidad de liderazgo y gestión de equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Fuertes habilidades analíticas y de resolución de problemas en contextos humanitarios.
- Excelente capacidad de redacción de informes técnicos y propuestas de proyectos.
- Habilidad para la negociación y coordinación con actores institucionales y comunitarios.
- Fluidez en español (inglés deseable).
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y como miembro de un equipo.
- Capacidad de mantener la confidencialidad.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Gran sentido de la responsabilidad y ética profesional.

About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Responsable de Pôle Finance Opérationnelle, vous apporter une expertise financière et du support opérationnel aux équipes des finances régionales, coordonner les audits externes de la DAF et contribuer au recrutement et à la mobilité de la filière finance.
Plus précisément, vos missions seront de:
Soutenir les équipes des Finances Régionales

jobs.title: Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal
jobs.description:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal**

**Contracting organization**

arche nova (AN)

## 1. Introduction

arche nova (AN) ([www.arche-nova.org](http://www.arche-nova.org)), a German non-governmental organization, has since 2012, been supporting vulnerable communities in Kenya to strengthen resilience to climate change, water scarcity, food insecurity, environmental degradation, and recurrent humanitarian shocks. Working at the humanitarian-development-climate nexus, arche nova combines emergency response, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate adaptation, and sustainable development approaches to build long-term resilience and self-reliance. Together with our local partners working in Kibera; Human Needs Project (HNP) and Action for Social and Economic Progress (ASEP), we are preparing a project proposal for submission to the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The proposed intervention is envisaged for Kibera, Nairobi County, Kenya.

## 2. Background

The proposed project; “Strengthening urban resilience through a climate-smart, multifunctional satellite community hub in the Kibera slum, Nairobi, seeks to address interconnected water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), public-health, climate-resilience and community livelihood needs in Kibera. Objective: To strengthen urban resilience through WASH, income generation and social cohesion in the Kibera slum, Kenya. Target group: 20,000 people, including 55 per cent women, 35 per cent young people (18-25 years) and 10 per cent people with disability. The target groups are closely interconnected with overlapping co-benefits from the project hence a validation of the total beneficiaries reached by the project is necessary. The Junior Partner; HNP also directly benefit from the project through strengthened capacities from the senior partner ASEP.

The project components include construction of a climate-smart community hub for improved access to safe water and sanitation, livelihoods and social cohesion. Potential measures may include a solar-powered water supply, greywater treatment using nano-filtration for reuse e.g. for hydroponic farming, sanitation and bathing facilities, menstrual health and hygiene (MHM), and inclusive community engagement, a digital innovation training lab for green business, entrepreneurship, job placement, and conflict/legal advice. Building on HNP’s ‘Kibera Town Centre’, which successfully operates as a self-sustaining WASH, training and community centre. A senior-junior partnership model is being introduced: as an experienced stakeholder and AN partner, ASEP supports the smaller, locally-rooted organization HNP to facilitate better access to funding, technical support and innovation.

These are options for assessment and are not predetermined technical decisions. The project is structured around four results:

Result 1: Improved access to climate-resilient and inclusive WASH services for vulnerable residents in Kibera.

Result 2: Improved economic empowerment and green skills development for women and youth.

Result 3: Strengthened social cohesion and improved access to community justice services for underserved vulnerable community members.

Result 4: Strengthened institutional capacity and inclusive governance for sustainable service delivery.

A feasibility study is required to verify priority needs supporting the project idea to assess the suitability, affordability and sustainability of proposed measures as well as beneficiary, stakeholder and partner relationships and identify the key risks and recommend concrete adjustments to the project concept, the impact matrix and the planned measures. The study must be independent and sufficiently critical to recommend redesign, deferral or non-selection of any measure where evidence does not support it.

The study should consider applicable BMZ PT requirements and relevant OECD/DAC criteria: relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability. Cross-cutting considerations include gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights, environmental and climate safeguards, conflict sensitivity, accountability and Do No Harm.

## 3. Purpose and Scope of the Assignment

The purpose of the assignment is to provide AN and its partners with an independent, participatory and evidence-based basis for deciding on the proposed intervention and preparing a coherent, technically sound, costed and sustainable BMZ PT project proposal.

The feasibility study will:

- Validate priority needs, vulnerabilities, capacities and intended target groups in the proposed project area.
- Assess the technical, social, institutional, environmental, regulatory, operational and financial feasibility of proposed measures and compare viable alternatives.
- Analyze target groups and stakeholders, including their relationships, interests, influence, roles, coordination and potential risks of exclusion or conflict.
- Identify prerequisites, including land tenure and site access, asset ownership, water availability and rights, permits, environmental and social assessments, technical investigations, utility connections, and operation and maintenance arrangements.
- Recommend intervention logic, target groups, objectives, outputs, indicators, means of verification, assumptions and risks for the logical framework matrix; establish baseline values where feasible and propose evidence-based targets.
- Recommend sustainability, exit or transition, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) arrangements.

## 4. Methodology

The study should combine qualitative and quantitative methods and follow a participatory approach that reflects the needs and perspectives of intended beneficiaries and relevant stakeholders. The consultant shall propose a rigorous but proportionate methodology in the inception report, triangulating secondary evidence with field-based verification.

- The sampling approach must be justified, including selection of locations, respondent groups and sample size. A census or large-scale survey should not be assumed necessary unless justified by the study questions, available time and budget.
- Recent and relevant secondary data should be used wherever suitable. Sources, dates, geographic coverage and limitations must be stated; primary data collection should fill material evidence gaps rather than duplicate existing assessments.
- Data collection methods may include desk review, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, community consultations, site observations, structured facility assessments, quantitative data collection where justified, stakeholder and service mapping, risk analysis and preliminary costing.
- For every proposed outcome- and output-level indicator in the draft logical framework, assess measurability, data sources, disaggregation and feasibility of collection; establish a baseline value where evidence permits and recommend a realistic target.
- Assess the concept against the OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, explaining how each informs the feasibility judgement and recommendations.
- Data-collection tools must be shared with AN and partners for comment before fieldwork. Participation must be voluntary and informed. Personal data must be minimized, securely handled and reported in aggregated or anonymized form wherever possible.
- Validation with AN and partners should improve factual accuracy and usability but must not compromise the consultant’s independent judgement.

## 5. Tasks and Deliverables

### 5.1 Tasks

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks. The detailed methodology and sequencing will be agreed during inception.

#### Context and Initial Situation Analysis

- Review the concept note, available WASH and public-health data, relevant research, local plans and applicable national and county policies.
- Analyze Kibera’s socio-economic, public-health, environmental, climate, institutional and governance context relevant to the proposed intervention.
- Map existing and planned WASH, sanitation, MHM, livelihood and climate-resilience actors and interventions and identify synergies, referral pathways and duplication risks. Assess whether the established St. Juliet is complemented by the community service hub and or establish existing gaps.
- Verify the nature, scale and location of priority needs and identify population groups facing the greatest barriers or risks.
- Identify evidence gaps, stakeholder perceptions and assumptions requiring further investigation and prepare an evidence matrix.

1. **Stakeholder and Partner Analysis**

- Identify and engage key stakeholders, including young women, young men, parents, community and religious leaders, county and national government actors, and other civil society organisations.
- Assess the Partners regarding their roles, resources and competencies for
- project implementation.
- Evaluate the formal agreements and ownership structures between AN, ASEP, HNP
- Identify and analyse any gaps in collaboration and coordination.
- Identify synergies and confirm whether all official preconditions and authorizations for project implementation are in place

#### Needs, Target Groups and Beneficiary Analysis

- Consult residents and intended beneficiaries, including women and girls, youth, persons with disabilities, older people and other potentially marginalized groups, using safe and accessible methods.
- Suggest a beneficiary selection criterion, expected reach, affordability, barriers to access, protection concerns, participation and possible unintended consequences.

**Skills Training, Employment and Income-Generation Feasibility**
- Assess the gaps and needs among intended beneficiaries for the proposed skills training, including priority skills, participation barriers, existing competencies and the extent to which the proposed training responds to local needs and market demand.
- Analyse realistic employment, self-employment and income-generation opportunities linked to the proposed skills areas, including local labour-market conditions, viable value chains, market access, competition, start-up requirements. Technical and Operational Feasibility
- Assess proposed boreholes, toilets, showers and related facilities site suitability, accessibility, privacy, safety, gender responsiveness, MHM needs, cleaning, wastewater containment and disposal, desludging, drainage and recurrent costs.
- Assess whether proposed user fees are affordable and acceptable to intended beneficiaries and determine if the expected income can adequately cover recurrent operational and maintenance costs. Environmental, Social, Regulatory and Safeguarding Analysis
- Identify risks and mitigation needs related to groundwater abstraction, wastewater, sludge, solid waste, drainage, construction, energy use and treatment residuals.
- Identify the required environmental assessment and approval pathway, permits, land-access documentation, water-resource approvals and other statutory requirements; verify status where evidence is available.
- Assess gender, disability inclusion, child and adult safeguarding, protection, community safety, affordability and equitable access.
- Identify risks of exclusion, tension, elite capture, unequal benefits, displacement or disruption of existing services, and recommend practical mitigation measures.
- Recommend proportionate community consultation, complaints and feedback mechanisms, and ethical data-protection practices.

#### Project Concept Evaluation, Design and Recommendations

- Test the theory of change and causal links between needs, activities, outputs, outcomes and intended longer-term effects.
- Assess the coherence and manageability of combining WASH, livelihoods, access to justice and institutional strengthening in one hub, and recommend whether any component should be scaled down, phased or dropped.
- Map and assess the potential legal services gaps of intended beneficiaries,availability of qualified and legally authorized legal aid providers, community justice organizations, paralegals and relevant referral services operating in Kibera.
- Review and refine the draft logical framework, including indicators, potential baselines, proposed targets where evidence permits, sources of verification, assumptions and risks.
- Recommend MEAL responsibilities, data-collection frequency, disaggregation, community feedback and learning reviews.

### 5.2 Deliverables

The consultant shall submit the following deliverables in English. Due dates will be finalized at contracting and aligned with AN’s BMZ PT proposal-development schedule.

**Inception report:** Desk-review summary and evidence gaps; refined questions; justified sampling and respondent-selection approach; stakeholder plan; fieldwork locations and schedule; ethics, safeguarding and data-management arrangements; limitations; draft tools.

**Preliminary findings briefing**: Emerging findings, evidence gaps, options, key risks and decisions requiring partner input.

**Draft feasibility study**: Context and problem analysis; needs and target groups; stakeholder and partner analysis; options appraisal; technical and operational feasibility; safeguards; OECD/DAC assessment; risks and sustainability; indicator-by-indicator review with baseline values where feasible and proposed targets.

**Project-design annexes:** Draft logical framework matrix; intervention logic/theory of change; indicators and baseline information; implementation timetable; risk register; indicative activity-based budget

**Validation and final report:** Validation session with AN and partners; final report incorporating comments; stakeholder contact list, bibliography/source list and curated, captioned photographs where appropriate and consented.

- The final report should not exceed 30 pages excluding annexes and should open with an executive summary of no more than 3 pages.
- The report must give a clear, evidence-based recommendation for each proposed measure (proceed, proceed with modifications, defer or do not proceed), with the reasons and conditions attached.
- All reports and annexes must be submitted in PDF and editable formats (MS Word and Excel) and cleaned; anonymized datasets and data-collection tools shall be submitted as annexes

## 6. Supporting Documents

AN and its partners will provide relevant available documents to support the assignment, which may include:

- The latest project concept notes, draft proposal narrative, draft logical framework/results matrix and draft budget.
- Available site information, maps and previous project report relevant to Kibera and the proposed intervention.
- Relevant BMZ PT feasibility-study guidance, templates and proposal requirements.

## 7. Skills and Experience- consultant profile

AN invites application from Kenya-based independent consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms. Where a multidisciplinary team is proposed, one team member must act as team leader and take responsibility for the quality and timely delivery of all outputs. The team should collectively demonstrate:

- Postgraduate qualification in development studies, social sciences, public health, engineering, environmental studies, economics or another relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience conducting feasibility studies, assessments or project design for development programmes in Kenya, preferably in urban informal settlements or similarly complex settings
- Experience developing institutional-donor proposals, logical frameworks, results chains, implementation plans and activity-based budgets.
- Relevant WASH and public-health expertise. Specialist engineering or water-resource conclusions must be reviewed by appropriately qualified professionals.
- Experience with participatory and mixed-methods research, stakeholder analysis and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
- Competence in gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, environmental and social risk assessment, conflict sensitivity, social cohesion and accountability.
- Strong analytical, facilitation and report-writing skills; excellent written and spoken English; willingness to conduct fieldwork in Kibera.

## 8. Work Plan and Submission

The assignment is expected to be delivered within 21 consultant working days, completed within a period agreed with AN and aligned to the proposal-development schedule. The consultant should propose a realistic allocation of days. The following distribution is indicative:

- Inception and desk review: 2–3 days.
- Fieldwork and stakeholder consultations: 5–7 days.
- Analysis and options appraisal: 4–5 days.
- Draft report and design annexes: 3–4 days.
- Validation, revisions and finalization: 2–3 days.

Fieldwork dates and submission deadlines will be agreed during inception. AN’s review periods and partner feedback must be built into the detailed workplan. Deliverables are complete only after review and acceptance by AN.

## 9. Management, Coordination, Ethics and Data Management

- The consultant reports to the designated AN focal point, who coordinates comments and confirms acceptance of deliverables.
- AN and partners will provide available project documents, facilitate introductions to stakeholders and support agreed field logistics.
- The consultant is responsible for the quality and independence of the analysis, tools, fieldwork, analysis and timely delivery. Changes to scope, fieldwork, deliverables or timeline require written agreement by AN before additional work is undertaken.
- Obtain informed consent before interviews, discussions, photographs or collection of personal information; participation must be voluntary. Use safe, accessible and culturally appropriate methods and avoid creating expectations about project approval or benefits.
- Apply safeguarding and Do No Harm principles, including appropriate protections when engaging children or other groups requiring additional safeguards.
- Protect confidentiality and securely store notes, recordings and datasets in line with the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019, and applicable research-ethics requirements. The consultant must identify any research licence, ethical clearance or other authorization required and include the time and cost in the workplan and financial proposal.
- All reports, tools, datasets, photographs commissioned under the assignment and project-design annexes shall be provided to AN and handled in accordance with the consultancy contract. The consultant may not publish confidential project information or identifiable participant data without prior written authorization. Third-party sources must be acknowledged.

## 10. Application Requirements

Applications are invited from Kenya-based individual consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms, in line with Section 7. Applications must include:

- **Cover letter** (max. 2 pages) explaining interest and suitability for the assignment, and confirming availability for the proposed period.
- **Technical proposal** (max. 10 pages) setting out understanding of the assignment and the Kibera context; proposed methodology, sampling and options-appraisal approach; work plan with allocation of days per team member and per phase; team composition and roles; quality-assurance arrangements; and ethics, safeguarding and data-protection arrangements.
- **CVs** of all proposed team members (max. 2 pages each), including at least two references from recent, similar assignments.
- **Financial proposal** in Kenya Shillings (KES), with professional fees shown as daily rate × number of days for each team member, and separate lines for field costs (e.g. enumerators, transport, venues, consultation costs), research licence or ethical-clearance costs, and applicable taxes.
- **One sample** of a feasibility study, assessment or project-design report recently completed by the lead consultant or team (or a link to it).
- **Compliance documents:** copy of KRA PIN and valid tax compliance certificate; for firms, certificate of registration or incorporation.
- **Signed declaration** of no conflict of interest.

**Job Title:** Area Coordinator

**Reports to:** Programme Director

**Terms:** *12-month unaccompanied position based in Geneina, West Darfur*

**Salary:** GB6 - €46,821 - €52,024

**Requirements:** *El Genina, Darfur – Sudan - requiring travel to the field*

## **Responsibilities**

**Programme Cycle Management**

- Participate in the finalisation of programme proposal documents, taking a lead on Darfur
- activities, including the global proposal, logical frameworks, implementation plans, M&E plans and budget
- and participate in reviews and revisions as necessary during the life cycle of the programme.
- Oversee implementation of programme activities, recruitment, procurement planning and stock management that integrate all approved grants for Darfur.
- Ensure all programmes follow Project Cycle Management best practices, including kick-off/review/close-out meetings, adherence to M&E plan, learning sessions and evidence-based adaptations.
- Ensure mainstreaming of protection, equality, conflict-sensitivity and climate in programme design and implementation in Darfur
- Ensure all aspects of Concern’s activities in Darfur adhere to programme quality standards
- and policies.
- Collect and share information on humanitarian needs in Darfur to inform programme strategy.
- Identify needs for emergency response promptly and prioritise response where possible.

**Management of Darfur Field Offices (El Geneina, Kulbus and Seleia)**

- Ensure Concern’s and donors’ procedures and controls in relation to procurement, warehousing and fleet
- management are in place in each field office, understood and complied with by all relevant personnel,
- liaising with the systems team and Operations Director for support.
- Ensure all assets lists and inventories are properly recorded and maintained in all field locations.
- Conduct physical stock, asset and inventory counts when necessary.
- Ensure all monthly procurement, warehousing and transport reports from all field locations are accurate and
- completed in a timely manner and review these for any potential issues before forwarding to the logistics
- team, based in the coordination office (Port Sudan).

jobs.title: Reserve Director
jobs.description:
**About WCS**

Founded in 1895, the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a U.S.-based, tax-exempt nonprofit dedicated to saving wildlife and wild places through science and conservation action. Working in more than 60 countries, WCS has supported the establishment of over 150 protected areas, combining biological expertise, local knowledge, and long-term partnerships to conserve species, habitats, and ecosystems while supporting communities whose livelihoods depend on natural resources. Our mission is to save wildlife and wild places through science, conservation action, education, and inspiring people to value nature. Our vision is thriving wildlife in healthy lands and seas, valued by societies that embrace and benefit from life’s diversity and integrity. Our goal is to conserve the world’s largest wild places across 16 priority regions containing more than 50% of global biodiversity. Our values are Respect, Accountability and Transparency, Innovation, Diversity and Inclusion, Collaboration, and Integrity.

Since 2001, WCS has worked in Nigeria to protect threatened species, including Cross River gorillas and savannah and forest elephants, while supporting local livelihoods, conservation awareness, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. In Cross River State, WCS supports Cross River National Park, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, and the Mbe Mountains Community Forest; in Bauchi State, it provides technical expertise for the conservation and management of Yankari Game Reserve.

At Yankari Game Reserve, WCS supports ranger patrols and wildlife monitoring to strengthen the protection of wildlife and habitats. Through its community-based Elephant Guardian network, WCS also supports elephant monitoring, early warning, and conflict mitigation to help communities respond to human-elephant conflict. Building on this work, WCS plans to deepen its collaboration with the Bauchi State Government through a strengthened collaborative management partnership aimed at improving governance, conservation management, community participation, and sustainable financing for the Reserve.

The WCS Nigeria Program is seeking a Reserve Director for the Yankari Landscape.

**Job Summary**

The Reserve Director provides overall leadership and management of Yankari Game Reserve and the wider Yankari Landscape, leading protected area and wildlife and habitat management, community engagement, and institutional strengthening initiatives to ensure the long-term ecological and financial sustainability of the Reserve

The position reports to the WCS Nigeria Country Director and is accountable to the Yankari Game Reserve Steering Committee. The Director oversees all aspects of Reserve operations, leads multidisciplinary teams, and ensures delivery of agreed conservation and organisational objectives, including the landscape strategy.

As WCS's senior representative in Yankari, the Director serves as the principal liaison with government, communities, donors, conservation partners, and other stakeholders, fostering collaborative management, strategic partnerships, resource mobilisation, and stakeholder engagement in support of the Reserve's conservation and development goals.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Leadership, Management and Operations**

- Lead Yankari Game Reserve and the wider Yankari Landscape to deliver conservation and community engagement objectives.
- Lead implementation of the Reserve Management Plan and annual work plans, aligning budgets, performance targets, and operational priorities.
- Supervise and coordinate multidisciplinary teams in conservation law enforcement, wildlife management and monitoring, community conservation and safeguards, tourism, administration, and finance; foster accountability, staff development, and high organisational performance.
- Oversee financial, administrative, and operational systems to ensure compliance, efficiency, and effective resource use.

**Conservation, Protection and Community Engagement**

- Oversee wildlife protection, habitat management, biodiversity monitoring, and research to support evidence-based conservation and adaptive management.
- Work with the Conservation Law Enforcement Advisor and Wildlife Management Coordinator to strengthen law enforcement, improve the use of SMART, EarthRanger, and other management tools, and address poaching, encroachment, insecurity, and other threats.
- Support the Community Conservation Coordinator to strengthen community relations, advance participatory governance and collaborative management structures, reduce human-wildlife conflict, and promote conservation-linked livelihood and resilience initiatives.
- Partnerships and Reporting
- Represent WCS and Yankari Game Reserve with government agencies, donors, local communities, traditional institutions, conservation partners, and other stakeholders.
- Support fundraising, donor relations, proposal development, and strategic partnerships to strengthen the Reserve’s long-term sustainability.
- Monitor progress against conservation and operational targets and ensure timely, high-quality reports, proposals, and communications for WCS, donors, government partners, and the Steering Committee.
- Contribute to the WCS CWT strategy and the WCS Africa CWT strategy.

**Job Qualifications:**

- Master's degree or equivalent experience in conservation biology, ecology, environmental management, natural resource governance, protected area management, or a related field.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in conservation programs or protected area management, including leadership of complex, multi-component programs.
- Demonstrated experience in protected area management, conservation law enforcement coordination, biodiversity monitoring, and community engagement.
- Strong understanding of governance systems, collaborative management approaches, and stakeholder coordination in Nigeria or similar contexts.
- Proven track record of leading multidisciplinary teams and building effective institutional partnerships.
- Excellent leadership, team management, mentoring, and interpersonal skills.
- Strong strategic planning, organisational management, and problem-solving abilities.
- Effective communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Demonstrated ability to manage complex partnerships and multi-stakeholder processes.

**Additional Requirements:**

- Proficiency in conservation management and monitoring tools, including SMART, EarthRanger, GIS, KoboToolbox, and related platforms.
- Strong analytical skills and ability to apply data and evidence to management decisions.
- Ability to work effectively in challenging field environments with resilience, adaptability, and sound judgement.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of Hausa is highly desirable.
- Willingness to be based in Yankari Game Reserve with travel throughout the Yankari Landscape and nationally.
- Demonstrated commitment to biodiversity conservation and community-based conservation approaches.
- Ability to represent WCS effectively with government agencies, traditional institutions, donors, partners, and local communities.

**Why Join Us?**

- Leverage WSC’s conservation, protection, and law enforcement expertise to strategically guide the WSC's protection of wild places and wild species.
- Exceptional opportunity to make significant contributions to the protection of biodiversity conservation.
- Dynamic Team: Join a dynamic team and work in a collaborative and conducive environment where your ideas and everyone's input are valued.
- Growth Opportunities: We believe in providing an enabling environment to develop your career. We are committed to developing your skills and competencies and offer opportunities for career advancement.
- Supportive Environment: Work with a team that values respect, teamwork, and excellence

As a member of the Amman Hub, your duty will be to provide hands on support for the emergency nutrition and Food security components of these country programs with your high level technical expertise.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which you can find under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-expatriate-employees).

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

This is a core position in the Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan country office and is open for both Afghan National and International Candidates. The Head of Finance will provide strategic leadership and oversight of all financial functions for Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan across both its charitable and commercial activities. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the postholder will lead and develop the Finance team while positively contributing to the country strategy; organizational culture and values; equality; and cross-departmental collaboration.

The Head of Finance will work closely with the Country Director, in-country team, and key global team members to ensure strong financial management of the country office budget, effective stewardship of resources, and financial compliance. The role will oversee Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan’s country-level entities and ensure cohesive and collaborative financial management within and between entities. The successful candidate will cultivate strong working relationships with all heads of department and function leads to foster positive and unified financial and commercial operations within the country office.

The postholder will be responsible for overseeing a variety of financial management processes including, but not limited to, budgeting, accounting, cash flow, payroll, financial reporting, donor awards and sub-awards, audits, commercial finance, and internal controls. The role will also ensure compliance with organisational, donor, and government requirements, manage financial risks, and strengthen financial systems and processes. The successful candidate will develop strong working relationships with country and global teams and represent the organisation with authorities, donors, and partners.

The position will be based in Kabul, Afghanistan, and is expected to start 1 January 2027.

**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

**Management and Team Building**

- Oversee all finance functions of Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan, providing strategic direction and leadership to the Finance team across both charitable and commercial delivery streams.
- Be an active member of the Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan Senior Management Team and contribute positively to the strategic development of the country office and the implementation of its country strategy.
- Serve as a country office champion and leader for promoting and instilling Turquoise Mountain’s workplace environment, behaviour, and values.
- Actively promote and implement mechanisms that progress equality and inclusion in the workplace.
- Supervise and lead the Finance team. Facilitate one-on-one support, strategic guidance, and departmental meetings.
- Ensure and oversee the effective delegation of responsibility within the Finance team.
- In coordination and consultation with the Finance team, prepare departmental workplans and ensure the timely implementation of planned activities.
- Ensure effective collaboration with key country office functions including Programs, Operations, and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) across all field sites.
- Liaise and build strong working relationships with core global team functions, primarily Finance, Operations, Commercial, and Fundraising.

**Budgeting and Reporting**

*Country Budget*

- Work closely with budget holders to oversee the effective financial management of the country office operational budget, ensuring appropriate stewardship of resources.
- Work closely with the Country Director and Heads of Department to prepare accurate departmental budgeting and conduct routine expenditure and reforecast updates to the country budget over the course of the year, in line with organisational requirements and timelines.
- Oversee the accurate allocation of expenses in line with the approved country budget.
- Ensure effective coordination with the global team members including the Group Finance Director, Financial Controller, and Commercial Finance Manager on country and donor budget management and reporting.

*Award & Sub-Award Management*

- Work closely with the Country Director and Head of Programs to develop accurate and compliant donor budgets for new grant proposals and budget realignments for existing grants.
- Oversee the monthly Budget versus Actuals process and work closely with Finance and Programs teams to ensure the timely preparation and distribution of all grant reports to project teams; review, revision, reforecast, and finalisation process; and overall compliance with individual donor requirements.
- Serve as the focal point for sub-awardee budgeting and financial reporting processes, including consolidation and supporting strong sub-award financial management, ensuring compliance with internal and donor requirements.
- Ensure the timely submission of donor financial reports per contractual obligations.
- Ensure financial obligations in donor awards and sub-awards are met, including monitoring payment schedules and disbursements in line with compliance requirements.
- Serve as the country office focal point for donor, governmental, and organisational financial audits and oversee the completion of activities and submission of documentation for related processes.

*Commercial Management*

- Working closely with the Global Commercial Director, Group Finance Director, and Commercial Finance Manager, support the Business Development Finance Coordinator to ensure that Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan commercial finance obligations are met, including the timely disbursement of payments to suppliers, accounting of committed funds as required, and effective inter-entity accounting management.
- Facilitate strong working relationships between Turquoise Mountain’s country-level entities for a cohesive and integrated approach to organisational financial management.
- Apply a problem-solving approach to ensure that inter-entity transactions are accurate and processed in a timely way.
- Work closely with the Commercial Finance teams to create analytical and monitoring tools to allow the organisation to better understand financial performance.

**Accounting**

- Lead and oversee the country finance function, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant financial management and reporting.
- Ensure adherence to donor, statutory, regulatory, and organisational financial requirements.
- Oversee banking, treasury, cash management, and financial transfers, ensuring effective controls and adequate liquidity.
- Ensure robust cash flow forecasting and planning to support operational needs.
- Strengthen cross-departmental financial accountability, reporting, and reconciliation.
- Oversee financial management and compliance across all country entities.
- Ensure timely month-end closing, balance sheet reconciliations, and financial reporting in coordination with Global Finance.
- Monitor financial performance and proactively identify, manage, and escalate risks to the Country Director and Group Finance Director.
- Ensure effective payroll governance and controls in coordination with Human Resources.
- Maintain oversight of bank, cash, and third-party service provider reconciliations, ensuring timely review, approval, and resolution of discrepancies.

**Internal Controls**

- Ensure compliance with the country Finance Manual, including accurate utilisation and processing of internal templates, documentation, and financial records.
- Identify, propose, and roll out system and process improvement strategies.
- Deliver training and capacity building activities to the Finance team and Heads of Department to ensure comprehensive understanding and execution of internal control measures, policies, processes, and practices.
- Monitor budget execution and prepare and present the monthly management accounts to the Country Director and global finance team.
- Ensure that all financial activities and payments are in compliance with the entities’ and donors’ policies.
- Liaise with global finance colleagues on all aspects of documentation and control.
- Maintain strong cash controls and reconciliation processes.
- Work with global finance and operations colleagues, third party providers, to ensure timely inflow of cash to country office.

**Coordination, Representation, and External Liaison**

- Represent Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan and serve as an ambassador for the organisation in external engagements including with the Afghanistan authorities, donors, and partners.
- Work closely with internal teams to ensure the timely registration and reporting of projects with the organisation’s relevant line ministries.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of local financial requirements, including tax regulations, financial and legal regulations, and governmental processes.
- Actively cultivate and strengthen inter-entity and inter-departmental coordination.

**This list is not exhaustive, and other duties may be required as determined by the needs of the organisation.**

**Key working relationships / cross-working**

**Internal**: In-country Finance, Programs, and Operations departments, Global Finance, Operations, Commercial, and Fundraising departments

**External**: Donors, partners, Afghanistan authorities \[1\]

\[1\]: Delegation for in-person governmental representation may be accommodated dependent on the individual

**Person Profile**

**Professional approach:**

A strategic and genuinely collaborative finance leader with a proactive, solution-focused approach. The postholder should combine rigorous financial stewardship and attention to detail with sound judgement, adaptability, and a clear understanding of organizational priorities. Ability to synthesize different information and apply creativity and pragmatism to contribute to solutions. They will lead by example, coach and empower colleagues, delegate effectively, and promote accountability, equality, inclusion, and organizational values. Success requires strong relationship-building, clear communication, and constructive coordination across teams and entities, together with the confidence to represent the organization professionally with donors, partners, and authorities.

**Experience:**

- Significant senior financial leadership experience in a complex country office and multi-entity organisation.
- Experience managing operational, donor, and commercial budgets, including forecasting, reforecasting, and budget-versus-actual analysis.
- Strong accounting experience covering month-end processes, balance-sheet and bank reconciliations, trial balances, payroll, cash forecasting and financial reporting.
- Experience managing donor awards and sub-awards, including proposal budgets, reporting, compliance, disbursements, and audits.
- Experience in commercial finance, supplier payments, and inter-entity accounting.
- Experience developing and maintaining robust internal controls, financial policies, procedures, and documentation.
- Experience managing banking, cash transfers, and alternative payment mechanisms, ideally including third-party service providers.
- Experience leading, coaching, and developing finance teams and delegating responsibilities effectively.
- Experience designing and implementing financial systems, analytical tools, and process improvements.
- Experience working in international development, preferably in a complex operating environment.
- Experience with institutional and private donors, partners, auditors, authorities, and government ministries.
- Knowledge of applicable tax, financial, and legal requirements; Afghanistan experience would be advantageous.
- Experience delivering training and financial capacity building to finance and non-finance colleagues.

**Qualifications:**

ACCA/CGMA or equivalent

**Personal Attributes & Skills:**

- Collaborative approach with demonstrable experience of building strong and positive relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Strategic financial management and organisational planning.
- Budget preparation, monitoring, forecasting, and variance analysis.
- Financial accounting, management accounting, and cash-flow management.
- Donor budgeting, grant reporting, sub-award management, and compliance.
- Risk management, audit coordination, and internal-control oversight.
- Commercial financial analysis and performance monitoring.
- Team leadership, coaching, delegation, and capacity building.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
- Excellent planning, organisation, and management skills.
- Clear written and verbal communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.
- Strong stakeholder management, coordination, and external-representation skills.
- Ability to give and receive feedback in a constructive manner.
- Good listener and responsive to needs of wider team, a genuine business partner in approach.
- Ability to communicate vision and drive team forward.

**Digital skills and experience:**

Experienced in Microsoft Office: advanced Excel and strong proficiency in Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint.

Experience working with relevant Accountancy software.

Experience of working alongside dispersed (remote) teams would be an advantage.

**Language skills:**

Fluency in international standard spoken and written English (essential), Dari (desirable) and Pashto (desirable)

jobs.title: Référent.e Action Environnementale - ALIMA –Sénégal H/F
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :**

La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées surla proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

- Le patient et la patiente d’abord
- Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
- Responsabilité et liberté
- Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
- Faire confiance
- L’intelligence collective
- La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER - ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Éthiopie, Haïti, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Sénégal, Mauritanie et Soudan.

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**Niveau 1 :** le titulaire du poste n'aura pas de contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables ni accès à des données à caractère personnel les concernant dans le cadre de son travail. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs ne sera pas obligatoire pour ce poste, à moins que le contenu du poste ne change, auquel cas le niveau de protection des populations vulnérables devra être revu.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

**Supérieur hiérarchique** : Directeur Général Adjoint

**Il (elle) collabore avec** : Tous les départements de l’organisation, particulièrement le département logistique et les desks ainsi que les missions dans nos pays d’intervention. Il collabore étroitement avec le partenaire *Climate Action Accelerator*.

**CONTEXTE**

En 2021 ALIMA s’est engagé dans une démarche environnementale ambitieuse en intégrant le principe de Responsabilité environnementale dans sa charte associative, en effectuant son premier bilan carbone 2019-2020 et en produisant une feuille de route visant une adaptation radicale de son modèle d’ici 2030. Cette feuille de route environnementale définit les priorités d’action globale d’ALIMA en matière de prise en compte des enjeux du changement climatique dans sa mission, ses objectifs stratégiques en matière réduction de son empreinte, d’adaptation de son modèle, de recherche sur les liens entre santé et environnement, de plaidoyer et d'entraînement des acteurs de son écosystème. Lien vers la feuille de route environnementale ALIMA 2030 : [https://www.flipsnack.com/climateactionaccelerator/feuille-de-route-environnementale-alima_12-2021/full-view.html](https://www.flipsnack.com/climateactionaccelerator/feuille-de-route-environnementale-alima_12-2021/full-view.html)

Depuis 2022 l’action environnementale d’ALIMA s’est déclinée :

- En plusieurs projets de pilotes opérationnels pour tester et démontrer l’impact de certaines solutions : énergie solaire, gestion et recyclage des déchets humanitaires, l'adaptation des structures de santé au changement climatique (CRESH) etc…
- La duplication de certaines de ces solutions dans d’autres pays et d'autres projets
- La prise en compte des enjeux climatiques dans l'évaluation des besoins et le développement des projets médico-humanitaires
- La transition rapide vers l’énergie solaire pour nos projets et nos bases dans l’ensemble de nos pays d'intervention
- L’adaptation de nos politiques et en partie de nos pratiques en matière d’achat et d’approvisionnement, de fret, de déplacements en avion
- La formation des équipes pays à la planification et au suivi des solutions environnementales en sein de nos projets
- Le monitoring annuel de nos résultats
- L’entraînement de nos partenaires ONG nationales dans la prise en compte des enjeux climat et environnement dans leurs actions.
- Un plaidoyer actif et le partage d'expériences sur notre action au sein du secteur humanitaire et de la santé.

Afin d’accompagner concrètement ALIMA à tirer les meilleurs enseignements de cette première phase d’action, accélérer la mise en œuvre des solutions prioritaires, et développer le volet résilience des soins de santé et préparation des conséquences du changement climatique, ALIMA recherche son/sa nouveau/nouvelle **Référent.e Action Environnementale**

Mission : le/la RAE a pour mission d’animer, dynamiser, suivre et documenter la mise en œuvre les solutions prioritaires de la feuille de route environnementale d’ALIMA. Véritable “meneur de jeu” de l’opérationnalisation des solutions, il doit convaincre, conseiller et faire avancer les différentes parties prenantes au sein d’ALIMA (direction des opérations, référents techniques, équipes opérationnelles Siège, collègues sur les missions pays et sur les projets) afin d’atteindre les objectifs.

En partenariat étroit avec les équipes du Climate Action Accelerator, il est garant du rythme et de la qualité de la mise en œuvre des actions prioritaires de la feuille de route. Il identifie et propose les alliances et partenariats nécessaires à la pleine réussite de la feuille de route.

Lien hiérarchique : le/la RAE est rattaché.e directement à la direction générale et rend compte au Directeur général adjoint. Il travaille avec les référents techniques métiers, les responsables logistiques et la direction des opérations pour la pleine intégration des actions de la feuille de route dans les projets terrain ALIMA. A ce titre, il appuie les équipes dans le montage des activités environnement dans les propositions de projets, il se rend régulièrement dans les missions afin d’appuyer les équipes à planifier l’action et à opérationnaliser des solutions prioritaires, recueillir, monitorer les réalisations et les défis issus des projets.

Il/elle encadre et assure la bonne planification et la performance des activités du Référent Énergies/Bâtiments ALIMA

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

**Animation de l’action environnementale**

● Animer, en mode projet transversal, l’opérationnalisation de la feuille de route environnementale ALIMA ; A ce titre, planifie annuellement, suit et organise la transformation des objectifs en actions. Il organise le travail en interne avec les référents identifiés sur les différents volets d’action, et en externe avec les partenaires techniques (particulièrement le Climate Action Accelerator)

- Diffuser l’info et les connaissances concernant les différentes solutions portées par la feuille de route
- Monitorer et documenter les actions ; A ce titre, remonter les informations sur l’avancée des actions et proposer les adaptations nécessaires pour atteindre les objectifs. Il/elle rédige le rapport annuel d’action environnementale ALIMA, renseigne le tableau de bord des indicateurs, et contribue à mettre à jour la feuille de route et les priorités.
- Proposer et planifier, en collaboration avec les autres services, les formations nécessaires à l'acquisition et/ou au renforcement des compétences sur l’opérationnalisation des actions prioritaires ; A ce titre, identifie les prestataires externes les plus adaptés aux besoins.
- Coordonner avec les ressources internes et externes disponibles la réalisation des bilans carbones réguliers
- Être force de proposition, challenger la qualité de l’action environnementale d’ALIMA.

**Support à l’opérationnalisation de la feuille de route au niveau des missions**

- Appuyer les missions et les équipes projets dans les pays dans la planification des solutions climatiques ; apporter méthodologie et conseils sur la manière d’intégrer les solutions dans les activités projets (budgétisation, expertise technique nécessaires, procédures, outils)
- Accompagne les équipes pays dans la préparation et le suivi des plans annuels (volet action climatique)
- Assurer les missions d'appui technique nécessaires
- Animer, en étroite collaboration avec la direction des opérations, l’accélération de notre action en matière d'adaptation des actions ALIMA aux conséquences du dérèglement climatique (paquet de soins, préparation aux urgences, autonomie et résistance des structures de santé, mobilisation des soignants et des patients).

**Diffusion et promotion de l’action environnementale**

- Sensibiliser régulièrement l’ensemble des équipes aux différents aspects de la feuille de route et promouvoir la prise d’initiatives et les échanges sur l’action climatique ; diffuse la démarche environnementale et participe à l’influence des partenaires opérationnels d’ALIMA pour un effet domino (particulièrement les structures de santé et les ONG nationales partenaires)
- Partager l’expérience avec les acteurs de notre écosystème, et identifier les leçons apprises et les bonnes pratiques ; participer à construire les alliances et partenariats nécessaires.

**Soutien à la gestion des projets spécifiques "environnement/climat"**

- Participer activement à la bonne rédaction, planification et à la bonne gestion des projets et financements spécifiques dédiés à la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route environnementale (financements bailleurs et fondations …) ; articuler avec les équipes opérationnelles la gestion du projet, le suivi et le rapportage sur les projets "environnement"
- Participe, en appui aux services bailleurs et Développement, à la mobilisation de ressources et la sollicitation des partenaires financiers afin de disposer de tous les moyens nécessaires à l’atteinte des objectifs.

**COMPETENCES et EXPERIENCES**

**Niveau d’étude**

● Formation de niveau Bac + 4 en gestion de projets/action humanitaire, en ingénierie environnementale, action climatique, Écologie, Logistique. Ou tout autre domaine permettant de maîtriser la réalité des opérations médicales humanitaires

- Formations sur les aspects liés au changement climatique, à l’adaptation climatique, à la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre sont un atout majeur

**Expériences**

● solide expérience opérationnelle (au moins 5 ans) au sein d’une ONG (coordo projet, référent médical, référent logistique,) permettant de maîtriser les enjeux du management d’un projet d’action humanitaire, avec un appétit démontré pour l’action environnementale

Ou

- Au moins 5 années sur un poste sur les aspects Climat/environnement au sein d’une organisation nationale ou internationale

**Compétences techniques**

- Conduite du changement : capacité à convaincre et conduire du changement au sein d’une équipe, d’une organisation
- Solides Connaissances techniques sur la gestion de projets humanitaires et les dynamiques actuelles du secteur humanitaire en général
- Animation de projets impliquants plusieurs acteurs/partenaires
- Maîtrise des fondamentaux en suivi/évaluation

**Aptitudes professionnelles**

● Excellentes capacités de planification, d’organisation du travail pour atteindre des objectifs ambitieux dans des contextes complexes.

- Excellente capacité à analyser les avantages, les risques, la faisabilité et les coûts/bénéfices d’une action
- Appétit et ténacité à mettre en œuvre des solutions innovantes
- Excellentes qualités de pédagogie, d’explication, d’accompagnement des équipes, nécessaires pour mener des actions parfois à l’encontre des habitudes de l’organisation.

● excellente expression écrite et orale en français et en anglais

**CONDITIONS**

**Durée du contrat** : Contrat de droit sénégalais, CDD de 12 mois renouvelable, avec période d’essai de 3 mois renouvelable une fois.

**Prise de poste** : Dès que possible

**Salaire** : selon la grille de salaire en vigueur au Siège de Dakar.

Avantages extra contractuels :

- Cinq semaines de congés payés par an et système de jours de récupération pour les déplacements
- Couverture santé complémentaire et évacuation prises en charge par ALIMA pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.
