jobs.description:
**About the job**

The Grants Management Specialist assumes responsibility over the efficient management and maintenance of grants related information, documentation, reporting, and processes across DRC Syria, under the supervision of the Grants Management Manager (GMM). The Grants Management Specialist is responsible for the coordination, compilation, and review of donor narrative reports. This includes meeting external reporting deadlines; triggering and coordinating inputs; and compiling, reviewing, and finalizing narrative reports through to donor submission. Grants management responsibilities also include advising on donor regulations and compliance, reviewing of contractual terms, managing deadlines within and across grants, managing instalments, inputting and controlling of grants data in DRC’s Global Grants Management System (Dynamics) and SharePoint, and preparedness for audits. The Grants Management Specialist facilitates DRC grants management processes in terms of information management and administration tasks, including maintaining and circulating various trackers and grants management tools. The Grants Management Specialist plays a leading role in coordinating and facilitating monthly grant opening, review, and close-out meetings, including follow up on action points. The role requires significant liaison with counterparts in DRC Area Offices, Country Office, and HQ. The Grants Management Specialist will contribute to DRC Syria’s localisation commitments by strengthening equitable and compliant grant management practices with national partners, supporting transparent fund flows, and promoting capacity strengthening in donor compliance, reporting, and financial accountability across DRC and consortium partners.

In addition to the main roles and responsibilities outlined above, the Grants Management Specialist will support proposal development processes and other grants-related tasks upon delegation by the GMM and Head of Programme.

**Responsibilities**

**1. Grants Management**

- Facilitate the administration of grants management processes (reminders of deadlines; coordination of reports; submission via online portals; coordination of comments/revisions).
- Promote quality information management by maintaining an up-to-date filing system on SharePoint, including careful version control of proposals, grant amendments, top-ups, donor reports, etc.
- Ensure that DRC Dynamics is continually updated (reporting, instalments, start date, end date, total budget, and uploading of documents).
- Ensure the maintenance of an internal grants tracker, reporting schedule, grants review schedule, and proposal pipeline.
- Track and follow-up on installment requests, in close coordination with HQ and Finance counterparts.
- Support the Finance team with audit processes when grants-related documents are requested.
- Support the GMM for compliance checks in Donor Grant Agreements (compliance with codes, donor visibility requirements, etc.).
- Coordinate inputs and preparations for grant opening, review, and close-out meetings, including preparation of the Project Management Tool (PMT).
- Prepare internal guidance and updates on donor compliance, to be presented in grant meetings.
- Facilitate the meetings as delegated by the GMM, taking note of the action points, for circulation and follow-up post-meeting.
- Provide guidance to DRC staff on donor compliance, requirements and guidelines.

**2. Reporting**

- Take responsibility for donor reporting deadlines (setting internal deadlines, preparing templates providing clear guidance to relevant colleagues, and following up on inputs).
- Lead the coordination, compilation, review and finalization of donor narrative reports, including submission via online portals, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and DRC requirements.
- Support partners in improving report quality through structured feedback and mentoring on narrative and compliance standards.

**3. Partnerships**

- Support the Partnership Manager in conducting due diligence for new partnerships.
- Participate in local partner capacity assessments and the development of capacity building plans, where relevant.
- Support local partners with capacity building related to grants management.

**4. Proposal Development**

- As assigned by the GMM, support the development of project proposals, including coordination and follow up to ensure timely submission.
- Support quality assurance and submission including via online portals.

Other tasks delegated by the GMM, as required.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- Excellent written English communication skills; experience writing and copy editing complex and lengthy reports
- At least 3 years professional work experience in business development, reporting, or grants management in an NGO/INGO or similar
- Experience with grant management, and donor reporting
- Experience with inter-departmental coordination
- Understanding of localisation principles and equitable partnership frameworks in humanitarian programming.
- Cultural sensitivity and adaptability
- Ability to manage a high workload and manage stress
- Proven ability to manage stakeholders with strong communication, coordination, influencing and interpersonal skills.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and DRC values.
- Strong understanding of global protection sector standards, protection analysis, and Results-Based Protection
- Experience in project development (including proposal writing) an advantage
- Experience in DRC Core Sectors (Protection, SWI, Economic Recovery, HDP) an advantage

**Education:**

Bachelor of Arts or other relevant degree

**Languages:**

- English – fluent
- Arabic – fluent

*n this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract Length**: 6 months (Renewable, based on performance and fund availability).

jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

A home is the foundation on which we build our lives. When families have access to safe, affordable housing, they gain the stability to pursue opportunity, improve health and well-being, and build stronger futures. Yet every day, millions of people around the world face the challenges that come with inadequate housing. Celebrating our 50th year, we at Habitat for Humanity are working to change that by expanding access to housing solutions and opening doors to opportunity worldwide.

Reporting to the Chief Development Officer (based in the US), the newly-created Vice President, Global Fundraising & Partnerships will lead Habitat for Humanity International's philanthropic revenue generation across all regions outside the United States. This is a transformational leadership opportunity for a visionary fundraising executive who can inspire donors, partners, and teams to help advance a world where everyone has a decent place to live.

As a member of the Resource Development Management Group, you'll shape Habitat's international fundraising strategy and lead a global team responsible for generating more than $150 million annually. Through strategic philanthropy, you'll help mobilize the resources needed to expand housing access, strengthen communities, and accelerate lasting impact around the world.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Official Business Title**: Vice President, International Resource Development

**Scope:** All regions outside the U.S.

**Travel:** International travel of approximately 40-50%.

**Location**: This position may be based in a country where we are registered to do business, such as the UK, Slovakia, Kenya, Philippines, Costa Rica or the US. Importantly, this role must be generally available to support a variety of time zones, including the Asia/Pacific region.

**Why This Role Matters**

Habitat's work is grounded in a simple belief: housing matters. Safe, affordable homes create the foundation for stronger families, more resilient communities, and greater economic opportunity. As the Vice President, Global Fundraising & Partnerships, you will help build the partnerships and philanthropic investments that make this work possible at scale.

You will engage some of the world's leading corporations, foundations, institutions, and philanthropists to help open doors to housing solutions, mobilize resources for systemic change, and strengthen a global movement that has helped more than 65 million people access improved housing over the past 50 years.

**What You'll Do**

- Develop and lead an international fundraising strategy that integrates corporate, individual, and institutional giving to drive sustainable revenue growth across all regions outside the U.S.
- Cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors and partners, securing six-, seven-, and eight-figure commitments that advance Habitat's global mission.
- Lead, mentor, and support a global team of 5-6 direct and 30 indirect reports, fostering operational excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
- Build and strengthen high-level relationships with board members, international partners, government agencies, and senior leaders across the Habitat network.
- Partner across program, finance, communications, and advocacy teams to deliver a unified "One Habitat" donor experience and compelling cases for support.
- Serve as a strategic advisor to the Chief Development Officer and executive leadership on fundraising trends, opportunities, risks, and long-term revenue planning.

**What You'll Bring**

**Requirements**

- Commitment to Habitat's mission on a global scale and genuine passion for advancing a world where everyone has a decent place to live.
- Comfortable leading in an inclusive, Christian ministry.
- Bachelor's degree.
- 12+ years of progressive fundraising or business development leadership experience, including significant experience in complex international or multi-regional environments.
- Deep knowledge of international philanthropy, corporate social responsibility, bi- and multi-lateral institutional funding, and global development.
- Proven track record securing $1M-$10M+ gifts from corporations, foundations, and high-net-worth individuals.
- Demonstrated success leading high-performing fundraising teams with operational excellence and strong performance management.
- Experience navigating diverse cultures, geographies, and regulatory environments.
- Strong strategic planning, change management, negotiation, budgeting, and forecasting skills.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate a compelling global vision.
- Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across a federated or networked organization.

**Preferred**

- Master's degree.
- Fluency in one or more languages beyond English.
- Experience working in international development, humanitarian aid, or global nonprofit organizations.
- Experience with Blackbaud CRM or demonstrated ability to leverage systems to drive performance.
- Experience working within a multinational, federated organization.

**What We Offer**

- The opportunity to help lead one of the world's most recognized housing organizations during a pivotal period of global impact.
- A chance to build partnerships that open doors to safe, affordable housing for families around the world.
- A collaborative, mission-driven culture focused on innovation, accountability, and lasting change.
- The ability to contribute to a global movement dedicated to expanding housing access, affordability, and opportunity.

\#LI-BS1

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Research project management support consultant
jobs.description:
**About Truth Guardians:**

Truth Guardians is a non-profit organisation working in Syria and The Netherlands. The Organization is founded by White Helmets members aiming to provide aid to communities and persons recovering from conflicts and disasters; provide support to displaced people and hosting communities; support justice, accountability, rule of law, human rights efforts, and research activities.

Truth Guardians is an equal opportunities employer and applications are actively encouraged from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of sex, race, disability, age, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

**Introduction:**

Supporting the Syrian National Commission for Transitional Justice (NCTJ) through short-term, start-up project management support for the initial phase of the NCTJ Transitional Justice Research Support Project.

**1. Background**

The NCTJ is mandated to lead transitional justice processes in Syria, including through evidence-based research, legal analysis and advisory functions that underpin its work.

As part of the wider NCTJ-TG project, the NCTJ and Truth Guardians (TG) are developing the NCTJ Transitional Justice Research Support Project (the Research Support Project), which will begin with an initial phase of research activities to lay the foundations for a broader research and thought-leadership agenda in the future.

A consultant is therefore sought for a short, intensive assignment to provide start-up project management support for the Research Support Project. The consultant will be contracted by TG and report to the TG focal point, who will instruct the consultant based on guidance from the NCTJ, and will work closely with both the TG and NCTJ focal points.

**2. Purpose of the Assignment**

More specifically, the consultant will:

- Provide start-up project management and implementation support to the TG and NCTJ focal points, complementing the NCTJ focal points’ technical and academic expertise;
- Support the NCTJ to translate the research gaps and themes it has identified into an external call for small research studies;
- Support a transparent selection process, guided by the NCTJ's research priorities, and the contracting by TG and onboarding of the selected research studies;
- Help establish simple project management, monitoring and quality assurance tools for the research studies;
- Support the NCTJ focal point and relevant staff to lead management of the research activities by the end of the assignment.

Throughout the assignment, the consultant will apply conflict-sensitive and Do No Harm approaches, and ensure appropriate attention to confidentiality and institutional ownership by the Commission.

**3. Scope of Work**

**3.1** ***Call Design and Launch*** – the consultant will:

- Support the NCTJ to design and launch an external call for research, based on the research gaps and priorities identified by the Commission.

**3.2** ***Selection and Contracting*** – the consultant will

- Support a transparent selection process, guided by the NCTJ, for approximately six small research studies in the first call, and support the contracting by TG and onboarding of the selected research studies.

**3.3** ***Project Management, Early Implementation and Handover***

The consultant will:

- Help establish simple project management, monitoring and quality assurance tools for the research studies;
- Support the start of the selected research studies and early engagement between researchers and the NCTJ, and report on progress to the TG and NCTJ focal points;
- Support the TG and NCTJ focal points to take over day-to-day management of the research activities by the end of the assignment.

**3.4** ***Coordination and Facilitation***– the consultant will:

- Coordinate with relevant TG and NCTJ staff to ensure coherence with the wider NCTJ-TG project, and facilitate meetings or workshops.

The assignment is adaptive: this scope is an initial framework and may be refined during inception and implementation, in agreement with TG and the Commission.

**4. Deliverables - the consultant will produce:**

1. Inception note - workplan and timeline, coordination arrangements with the NCTJ focal point and TG, and quality assurance approach.
2. Call package - call for proposals, research questions, eligibility and selection criteria, application templates and timeline, validated by the NCTJ and approved by TG.
3. Selection and contracting procedures - review and selection process, panel arrangements, and templates for contracting and onboarding researchers.
4. Selection report - summary of the review process and the studies recommended for funding, submitted to TG for funding decisions based on NCTJ guidance.
5. Project management toolkit - project management plan, tracking and reporting tools, and quality assurance and peer review procedures for the research activities.
6. Periodic progress updates and coordination meeting notes - shared at agreed milestones with the NCTJ focal point and TG.
7. Handover note - status of the studies, outstanding actions, and recommendations for the TG and NCTJ focal points to manage the remaining implementation and future research rounds.

**5**. **Management and Reporting Arrangements**

TG is the contracting party for this assignment. The consultant reports to the TG focal point, who will instruct the consultant based on guidance from the NCTJ focal point; the TG and NCTJ focal points will work closely together. The NCTJ guides the research priorities and content of the Research Support Project.

**6. Quality Assurance**

All deliverables should demonstrate: :

- Evidence-based analysis and recommendations;
- Clear linkage to the research gaps and priorities identified by the Commission;
- Practical applicability and feasibility within the NCTJ's current institutional capacity and resources;
- Incorporation of perspectives from multiple NCTJ Directorates;
- Compliance with agreed confidentiality and conflict-sensitivity requirements;
- Clarity, accessibility and usability for decision-making by the Commission.

During the inception phase, the consultant shall propose a quality assurance framework, including deliverable review and validation processes, for approval by the Commission and Truth Guardians.

**7. Duration**

- Indicative initial duration: 3 months full-time (with possibility of extension)

**8. Required Expertise - the consultant should demonstrate experience in:**

We are looking for an experienced project manager with a background in research project start-up, able to work alongside the TG and NCTJ focal points during a short start-up phase. The consultant should demonstrate:

- Project management experience, ideally including research projects, grant programmes or calls for research proposals;
- Good knowledge of the Syrian context, including research, academic and civil society networks;
- Familiarity with transitional justice or human rights is an advantage.
- The consultant must be able to work in both Arabic and English.

The consultant should be able to be present in Syria for extended periods for in-person work with stakeholders.

**8. Confidentiality and Sensitivity**

Given the sensitive nature of the project, the consultant is expected to:

- Exercise discretion in all external communications
- Avoid public attribution of the work without prior agreement
- Adhere to agreed protocols regarding institutional representation and visibility
- The consultant may be required to sign relevant confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding, and ethical conduct commitments as part of the contracting process.

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY
Access to adequate and affordable housing remains a pressing challenge across Africa, particularly in the face of rapid urbanization and climate change. Compressed Earth Blocks (CEBs) present a sustainable, cost-effective, and locally sourced alternative to conventional building materials. The objective is to demonstrate viable market-led approaches to customer acquisition and demand generation that can be sustained and scaled by the partner beyond the period of support.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Background

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is anchored on a fundamental vision of a world where everyone has a decent place to live. This vision has been the driving force in all of Habitat’s actions and activities and has seen HFHI helping more than 29 million people around the world build or improve the place they call home. To further fulfil this vision, HFHI established the Terwilliger Centre for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) to Build and Expand Inclusive Housing Markets by supporting local firms to innovate and expand client-responsive services and products. TCIS understands that the role of local markets is critical in closing adequate housing gaps among the low-income and incremental market segment. TCIS strives to make markets work more effectively for low-income people in need of decent, affordable housing.

Context

Access to adequate and affordable housing remains a pressing challenge across Africa, particularly in the face of rapid urbanization and climate change. Compressed Earth Blocks (CEBs) present a sustainable, cost-effective, and locally sourced alternative to conventional building materials. To promote the adoption of this technology, HFHI, in partnership with a private sector actor, has been supporting efforts to stimulate the local housing market through innovation, demonstration activities, and awareness creation on the benefits of CEBs.

To catalyse greater market adoption of CEBs, HFHI seeks to support its private-sector partner to invest in and strengthen its market-development function through the engagement of a skilled below-the-line (BTL) experiential marketing agency. The agency will design and execute integrated consumer engagement and behaviour change campaigns that address information gaps and perception barriers, increase consumer awareness and confidence, and generate demand for CEB products. The objective is to demonstrate viable market-led approaches to customer acquisition and demand generation that can be sustained and scaled by the partner beyond the period of support.

Key objectives

- Design and implement integrated behaviour change communication (BCC) and BTL experiential marketing campaigns that addresses prevailing myths, misconceptions, promotes awareness, knowledge, demand and use of CEBs among identified households.
- Enhance the visibility and market presence of the private sector partner's CEB products and housing solutions among prospective customers, builders, artisans, developers, and other key market actors.
- Facilitate direct links between potential customers and the private sector partner for leads, product inquiries, referrals, and sales conversions.
- Monitor, document, and report on campaign performance and results, including reach, engagement, leads generation, converted leads, CEB adoption, partner sales and revenue changes and lessons learned.
- Develop a comprehensive Marketing Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) detailing marketing approaches, processes, collateral templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms, to strengthen the private sector partner’s capacity to independently implement future marketing and demand generation campaigns.

**Tasks and responsibilities**

- Conduct a review of secondary literature and existing project materials and market insights to inform campaign design and implementation.
- Develop a comprehensive BCC and BTL marketing approaches aligned with the project objectives and target audiences.
- Collaborate closely with the private sector partner and HFHI to ensure alignment of activities with project goals and business objectives.
- Design communication materials and promotional assets with clear, compelling, messaging that is tailored to the identified target audiences.
- Support in lead generation and customer referral database capturing consumer inquiries, leads, and referrals made to the private sector partner.
- Engage relevant local stakeholders, community representatives, housing sector actors, and influencers to support campaign implementation and message amplification
- Develop and implement a campaign reporting and monitoring framework to track performance against agreed indicators.
- Provide regular progress updates to the private sector partner and HFHI
- Develop a comprehensive Marketing SOP detailing marketing approaches, processes, collateral templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms for marketing and demand creation activities.

**Deliverables**

- BCC and BTL marketing campaign approach, including consumer engagement activities, key messages, promotional materials and designs.
- Detailed inception report detailing the campaign strategy, target audiences, key messages, implementation approach, activity schedule, and monitoring framework.
- Work plan detailing the campaign activities, milestones and timelines.
- Campaign monitoring reports providing updates on activities implemented, audience reach, engagement levels, lead generation, and emerging insights.
- Final campaign report summarizing activities, campaign performance against agreed indicators, key achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations for future demand creation efforts.
- A detailed Marketing SOP.

**Experience and qualification**

The selected agency should have the following qualification:

- Must be a legally registered firm with at least 5 years of proven experience in designing and implementing BTL marketing, consumer engagement, BCC, and demand creation campaigns.
- Strong regional presence
- Experience working with private sector companies especially Small, and Medium Enterprises to support market development.
- Experience in developing marketing SOPs to support continued implementation beyond the assignment period.
- Experience producing high-quality written technical reports
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
- Understanding of Market Systems approaches and experience working with housing sector is an added advantage.

Duration

The consultancy will be conducted in a duration of 6 months. This represents calendar period and not consultancy days.

Safeguarding and Data Protection

HFHI requires that all consultants take seriously their intended beneficiaries, their communities and all those with whom we work. The consultant shall support and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of all community members, especially children, and promotes implementation of HFHI’s code of conduct.

**Data Protection**

The contractor will be required to abide by HFHI’s data protection and security policy during the assignment period.

**Geographical scope:** The activities will focus on the Laikipia, Eastern and Western region

Submission

Interested agencies should submit the following:

- Technical Proposal providing a clear understanding of the assignment and proposed approach to achieve the objectives.
- A detailed financial proposal
- CVs of the team
- Case studies of similar work done

Application and Decision Process

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Submissions should be sent to by 25th Nov 2026, with subject line: **Below The Line Marketing Agency- Kenya.** The selected consultant may be required to show proof of professional indemnity cover

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Coordonnateur(trice) National(e) des Finances
jobs.description:
**Lieu d’affectation :** Bureau National, N’Djamena, avec des missions régulières dans les bases terrain (environ 20 % du temps)
**Rattachement hiérarchique :** Directeur National
**Date de prise de poste :** début janvier 2027
**Durée de l’engagement :** 1 an, renouvelable sous réserve de la disponibilité des financements et d’une performance satisfaisante

**À propos du JRS**

Le Service Jésuite des Réfugiés (JRS) est une organisation catholique internationale et une œuvre de la Compagnie de Jésus. Fondé en 1980, il accompagne, sert et défend les droits des réfugiés et des personnes déplacées de force dans plus de 50 pays.

Le JRS est présent au Tchad depuis 2006. Il y mène des programmes d’éducation, de protection de l’enfance, de cohésion sociale et de moyens de subsistance dans plusieurs régions qui accueillent des réfugiés.

**Objectif du poste**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) National(e) des Finances est responsable de la gestion budgétaire, financière, comptable et de trésorerie de JRS Tchad et de tous ses projets. Il/elle dirige le département Finances. Il/elle fait respecter les procédures internes et les exigences des bailleurs. Il/elle supervise l’Associé(e) Finances (Comptable) et l’Associé(e) Budget et Reporting.

**Relations de travail**

- *En interne :* le Directeur National ; l’équipe Finances du Bureau National et des bases ; les Directeurs et Chefs de projet ; les responsables Programmes, Logistique et RH.
- *En externe :* les bailleurs de fonds (UNHCR, UE, BPRM, etc.) ; l’administration fiscale, les banques et les institutions financières ; les auditeurs internes et externes ; les prestataires.

**Responsabilités principales**

*1. Pilotage stratégique, budget et management du département*

- Suivre et analyser la performance financière de JRS Tchad, et conseiller le Directeur National sur les choix stratégiques.
- Conduire la planification financière, préparer le budget annuel et répartir les ressources selon les exigences des subventions.
- Encadrer directement l’Associé(e) Finances et l’Associé(e) Budget et Reporting, et assurer le leadership technique de toute la filière Finances, y compris dans les bases.
- Renforcer le contrôle interne et suivre la mise en œuvre des recommandations d’audit.

*2. Comptabilité, trésorerie et conformité des subventions*

- Mettre en place des contrôles financiers internes solides et une méthode comptable rigoureuse, et respecter les délais de reporting.
- Gérer la trésorerie et suivre les soldes des projets pour éviter tout dépassement budgétaire.
- Veiller au respect permanent des exigences réglementaires, contractuelles, juridiques et financières des bailleurs.
- Garantir le bon paramétrage et la cohérence de la comptabilité dans le logiciel de gestion (Navision/ Business Central).

*3. Audits, reporting et coordination externe*

- Coordonner la préparation des audits annuels, internes et externes.
- Valider les rapports financiers internes et les rapports aux bailleurs.
- Préparer et réviser régulièrement les états financiers et les prévisions de recettes et de dépenses.
- Représenter le JRS dans les réunions sectorielles et inter-agences, et auprès des autorités financières.

**Profil recherché**

*Formation et expérience*

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+4/5 en comptabilité, finance, gestion ou administration des affaires. Une certification professionnelle (ACCA, CPA, DSCG ou équivalent) est un atout.
- Au moins 7 ans d’expérience en gestion financière dans le secteur humanitaire, dont au moins 3 ans à un poste de management dans l’humanitaire.

*Compétences techniques*

- Expertise en gestion financière, contrôle budgétaire et analyse financière en contexte humanitaire.
- Très bonne connaissance des procédures et exigences des bailleurs institutionnels (UNHCR, UE, BPRM, etc.).
- Maîtrise des logiciels comptables ERP (Navision/ Business Central, Sage) et d’Excel à un niveau avancé.
- Expérience confirmée en audit, contrôle interne et gestion des risques financiers.

*Langues*

- Maîtrise parfaite du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est fortement souhaitée.

*Qualités personnelles*

- Adhésion aux valeurs du JRS et au Code de conduite.
- Leadership, vision stratégique et sens des responsabilités.
- Intégrité irréprochable, sens de l’éthique et respect de la confidentialité.
- Capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et de négociation.
- Résilience et bonne résistance au stress.

**Ce que nous offrons**

Le poste s’accompagne d’un ensemble d’avantages adaptés à une mission en contexte humanitaire :

- **Indemnité mensuelle :** un montant attractif, au niveau des standards des ONG internationales au Tchad.
- **Logement :** une **aide mensuelle au logement d’environ 990 € (650 000 FCFA)**, versée en plus de l’indemnité mensuelle.
- **Couverture santé internationale :** une assurance médicale avec **évacuation et rapatriement sanitaires**, prise en charge par le JRS.
- **Voyages pris en charge :** billet aller-retour entre votre pays d’origine et N’Djamena, au début et à la fin de l’affectation. Les missions de terrain (visa, transport, repas, hébergement) sont aussi couvertes.
- **Repos et récupération (R&R) :** une semaine de R&R après **3 mois de service**.
- **Congés annuels :** **24 jours par an** (2 jours par mois de service effectif), plus des jours de voyage.
- **Autres congés :** 5 jours ouvrables de congé pour raisons familiales et jusqu’à 3 jours par an pour une retraite spirituelle.
- **Accompagnement :** soutien régulier de la Direction Nationale et du Bureau Régional, et formations internes.
- **Une mission qui a du sens :** vous rejoignez une organisation présente dans plus de 50 pays, au service direct des réfugiés au Tchad.

**Engagement du JRS**

Le JRS applique une politique de tolérance zéro envers toute forme d’exploitation, d’abus ou de harcèlement, notamment sexuels. Avant tout engagement, les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s feront l’objet de vérifications préalables : références professionnelles, identité, diplômes et antécédents. Ils/elles devront signer le Code de conduite et les politiques de safeguarding du JRS (PHEAS, protection de l’enfance). **Les candidatures féminines sont vivement encouragées.**

jobs.title: Finance Assistant
jobs.description:
## HAMAP-Humanitaire [https://hamap-humanitaire.org](https://hamap-humanitaire.org)

Halte aux Mines AntiPersonnel (HAMAP)-Humanitaire is a French NGO, established in 1999 in order to contribute to the struggle against mines and the risks it presents to civilian population. HAMAP-Humanitaire is active in 13 countries and pursues a mission of support to local partners from the need assessment, through project conception and to its sustainable implementation. HAMAP-Humanitaire diversified its field of activity, to encompass two sectors: Engineering (WASH, construction, energy) and Mine Action.

## Requirements and job status

Minimum education: Bachelor degree

Minimum experience: 2 years

Required travel: Within Syria

No of jobs: 1

Published date: 09/11/2026

Deadline date: 23/11/2026

**Start date: As soon as possible.** HAMAP-Humanitaire reserves the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a sufficient number of suitable applications has been received. Interested candidates are therefore encouraged to apply as early as possible.

## Description

HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking a qualified and detail-oriented Finance Assistant to support the financial management of its operations in Syria, contributing to the effective implementation of its humanitarian mine action programme.

The Finance Assistant will be responsible for supporting day-to-day financial operations, including accounting and bookkeeping, payment preparation, management of financial records, bank and cash reconciliations, and monthly financial reporting. The position will ensure that financial transactions are accurately recorded, properly documented, and processed in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s internal financial procedures, donor requirements, and applicable national regulations.

Under the direct supervision of the Country Coordinator in Syria, the Finance Assistant will work closely with programme and support teams to ensure timely financial processing, accurate reporting, and effective financial controls.

The position will also contribute to financial monitoring and reporting of local implementing partners, including reviewing supporting documentation, identifying discrepancies, and following up on financial reporting requirements in coordination with the Regional Finance Officer.

As HAMAP-Humanitaire establishes its operational presence in Syria, the Finance Assistant will support the implementation of financial systems, accounting tools, and documentation procedures, contributing to the accuracy, transparency, and accountability of financial operations.

**Hierarchical and organizational links:**

**Reports to:** Country Coordinator in Syria

**Technical reporting line:** Regional Finance Officer for Middle East

**Coordinates with**: Regional Support Functions Manager for Middle East, Admin and Logistics Assistant, programme and technical teams, HQ Finance Department, and local implementing partners.

**Objective 1: Day-to-Day Financial Management and Accounting**

To ensure accurate and timely processing of HAMAP-Humanitaire’s financial transactions in Syria, including bookkeeping, payment preparation, cash and bank management, and financial recordkeeping, in accordance with internal financial procedures, donor requirements, and applicable national regulations.

**Objective 2: Financial Reporting**

To support the preparation of monthly financial reports, reconciliations, and financial documentation required by regional management and HQ. Contribute to expenditure tracking and cash flow planning by maintaining accurate financial information and providing timely updates to the Regional Finance Officer.

**Objective 3: Partner Financial Reporting and Compliance**

To support the financial follow-up of local implementing partners through the review of supporting documentation, identification of discrepancies, and follow-up on required corrections. Contribute to ensuring compliance with partnership agreements, approved budgets, donor requirements, and HAMAP-Humanitaire’s financial procedures, under the technical guidance of the Regional Finance Officer.

## Main responsibilities

**Day-to-Day Financial Operations and Accounting**

- Record daily financial transactions in the relevant accounting sheets, ensuring accuracy and correct allocation of expenditures.
- Prepare payment documentation and verify that invoices, receipts, and supporting documents are complete and compliant with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s financial procedures.
- Verify that all required approvals are obtained before processing payments.
- Prepare and follow up on payments to suppliers, service providers, and staff, maintaining accurate records of outstanding payments and commitments.
- Maintain updated cashbooks and bankbooks, and prepare regular cash and bank reconciliations.
- Support the processing of monthly salaries, allowances, taxes, and social security contributions in coordination with the relevant support functions.
- Maintain accurate and organised financial records, ensuring proper physical and electronic filing of all supporting documentation.

**Financial Reporting and Compliance**

- Prepare and submit monthly financial reports, including cashbooks, bankbooks, reconciliations, and supporting documentation, in accordance with established reporting deadlines.
- Verify the completeness and accuracy of financial documentation, including procurement and HR-related supporting documents, before inclusion in financial reports.
- Assist in preparing financial information and documentation required for donor reporting and internal financial reviews.
- Support internal and external audits by organising financial records, providing requested documentation, and following up on identified documentation gaps.
- Identify and report financial discrepancies, missing documentation, or potential compliance issues to the Country Coordinator and Regional Finance Officer.

**Local Partner Financial Follow-Up**

- Follow up with local implementing partners to ensure the timely submission of financial reports and supporting documentation.
- Review partner financial reports, expenditure records, and supporting documents for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with approved budgets, partnership agreements, and donor requirements.
- Identify discrepancies, missing documents, or ineligible expenditures and communicate required corrections to partners, in coordination with the Regional Finance Officer.
- Maintain organised records of partner financial reports, supporting documentation, and follow-up actions.
- Provide practical guidance to partner finance staff on reporting templates, supporting documentation, and financial procedures, under the technical guidance of the Regional Finance Officer.

**Financial Coordination and Administrative Support**

- Coordinate with the Admin and Logistics Assistant to ensure that procurement-related financial documentation is complete and properly processed.
- Support cash management arrangements, including monitoring cash availability and preparing cash replenishment requests when required.
- Assist with administrative procedures related to bank account operations and financial transactions, in coordination with the Country Coordinator and Regional Finance Officer.
- Maintain regular communication with the Regional Finance Officer regarding financial reporting, pending payments, and operational challenges.
- Perform other finance-related duties reasonably assigned by the Country Coordinator, in coordination with the Regional Finance Officer\*\*.\*\*

## Risk Management and Authority

The Finance Assistant supports the implementation of financial controls and ensures that financial transactions, records, and supporting documentation comply with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s internal procedures, donor requirements, and applicable national regulations.

The position is responsible for identifying and reporting financial discrepancies, missing documentation, irregularities, or potential compliance risks to the Country Coordinator in Syria and the Regional Finance Officer for Middle East. Any corrective action requiring management approval must follow established procedures and delegations of authority.

## Limits of the Role

Unless specifically delegated and authorised, the Finance Assistant shall not:

- Approve expenditure, payments, procurement, or contractual commitments outside the established delegation of authority.
- Authorise payments or financial transactions without the required supporting documentation and approvals.
- Approve partner financial reports or validate questionable or unsupported expenditure independently.
- Make financial, contractual, or donor-related commitments on behalf of HAMAP-Humanitaire.
- Override established financial procedures, internal controls, or segregation of duties.

## Required competencies and qualifications

## Qualifications and Experience

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
- A relevant professional qualification or certification in accounting or finance would be an asset.

**Experience**

- Minimum of 2 years of relevant professional experience in finance, accounting, or financial administration within an NGO.
- Practical experience in bookkeeping, payment processing, cash and bank reconciliations, and financial reporting.
- Experience in reviewing financial documentation and ensuring compliance with internal financial procedures and donor requirements.
- Experience working with local implementing partners, including reviewing partner financial reports and supporting documentation, would be an asset.
- Previous experience in humanitarian mine action programmes would be an asset.

## Required Skills

**Behavioral**

- Demonstrates integrity, accountability and professionalism, taking responsibility for decisions and responding constructively to feedback.
- Plans and prioritises work effectively, anticipates risks and takes initiative to achieve high-quality results within established deadlines.
- Works collaboratively with colleagues, local partners and other stakeholders, contributing to a constructive and respectful working environment.
- Communicates clearly and effectively and builds positive working relationships across different functions, cultures and operational contexts.
- Promotes continuous learning, knowledge sharing and improvement, and supports the development and performance of others.
- Demonstrates adaptability and sound judgement when working across multiple countries and in changing operational environments.
- Promotes a working environment free from discrimination, harassment, retaliation, sexual exploitation and abuse, and upholds HAMAP-Humanitaire’s safeguarding and PSEA principles.
- Promotes inclusion and equal participation and considers gender and diversity perspectives in the performance of responsibilities.

**Technical**

- Good understanding of basic accounting principles, financial procedures, and bookkeeping practices.
- Ability to prepare and maintain accurate cashbooks, bankbooks, reconciliations, and financial records.
- Ability to review invoices, receipts, and supporting documentation for accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
- Familiarity with donor financial requirements, expenditure eligibility, and internal controls.
- Ability to review partner supporting documents and identify discrepancies.
- Good proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
- Familiarity with accounting software and financial reporting tools would be an asset.

## Languages

- Fluency in Arabic, both written and spoken, is required.
- Good working knowledge of English, both written and spoken, is required.
- Knowledge of French would be an asset.

## Personal Profile

HAMAP-Humanitaire is looking for a reliable, organised, and detail-oriented Finance Assistant with a strong sense of accountability and commitment to accurate financial recordkeeping.

The successful candidate should be able to carry out routine financial tasks independently within established procedures, meet reporting deadlines, communicate effectively with colleagues and local partners, and contribute to maintaining transparent and compliant financial operations in Syria.

## Rules of conduct

While working for HAMAP-Humanitaire, carrying out entrusted tasks, or representing themselves as working for the NGO, all employees are expected to:

- Systematically report their activities to their line manager and seek approval before undertaking any unplanned activity.
- Act appropriately and in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s values in all interactions. This excludes any discrimination based on nationality, ethnicity, religion, class, gender, sexual orientation, or any other legal right.
- Respect local customs and practices, as well as the laws and regulations of the country, in order to preserve HAMAP-Humanitaire’s reputation.
- Maintain strict confidentiality regarding HAMAP-Humanitaire documents, projects (ongoing and future), development prospects, stakeholders, and service providers.
- Refrain from using their position within HAMAP-Humanitaire for personal purposes.

**To be a source of proposals and individual initiatives are welcomed, nonetheless any action undertaken in the name or as an employee of HAMAP-Humanitaire must, first, be approved by the Coordinator for Middle East.**

## Conditions

Conditions will be determined in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s salary and benefits framework, selected duty station, and applicable national contractual status.

**Technical reporting line:** Regional Support Services Manager for Middle East

**Coordinates with**: Regional Finance Officer, programme and technical teams, Regional Security Coordinator, HQ support departments, local implementing partners, suppliers, and service providers.
