jobs.title: WASH Field Engineer
jobs.company: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
**Department:** Program

**Position:** WASH Field Engineer

**Direct Manager:** WASH Program Manager

**Contract duration:** 8 Months (with the possibility of renewal).

**Duty Location:** Idleb, Lattakia, Hama, Deir Ez zor, Aleppo

## **About AMAL Organization for Relief & Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war torned.

Amal Organization is a relief and development organization, was established in early 2013 in the northern countryside of the city of Homs on 6/6/2014 and the organization was licensed and registered in Turkey – Gaziantep

**POSITION PROFILE:**

The WASH Engineer will work within the project areas and in its host communities with possible travel to needed areas. The main responsibilities will include working to design and improve the technical engineering implementation aspects of Amal’s WASH program and sanitation technology including designing, quantifying, specifying boreholes, preparing contractual documents and managing them, managing geophysical studies, submersible and hand pump installation and repairs, submersible, and hand pump repair and maintenance training, designing and constructing water distribution systems, pump testing, water quality testing, hand-dug well construction, and/or paving road. The WASH Engineer will also be responsible in coordinating and leading any emergency relief situations involving WASH efforts, creating and drafting technical designs, and submitting regular reports on the work being completed.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

1. **Assess needs for WASH interventions (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene facilities) at the community level including public schools and Health facilities.**
2. **Ensure the project will satisfy the needs of the beneficiaries and provide oversight of water source construction and sanitation projects to ensure quality:**

- Preparation of drawings (AutoCAD), BoQ/Cost Estimates and Tender documents for all WASH infrastructures
- Ensuring the training staff of water station in technical areas including water quality testing, and building and maintaining quality water point structures;
- Help design and revise the construction/rehabilitation works component of the project work-plan, and monitor that the implementation of the construction/ rehabilitation activities respects the time-table milestones and deadlines
- Conduct trainings regarding operation and maintenance of water supply and sanitation facilities for beneficiaries and Water management committees
- Develop and maintain good relationships and lines of communication with relevant local authorities and communities, prior to intervention explaining Amal’s role as an NGO and liaising with them during all phases of the project.
- Regular monitoring of ongoing construction activities to ensure that all the activities are executing as per design, specifications and work schedule
- Extend all possible technical support to other team members and contractors when and where required
- Keep close coordination with contractors through regular meetings
- Preparation of weekly, monthly work plans and construction progress reports
- Preparation of feasibility studies/ reports, borehole pumping tests analysis & reporting and completion certificates
- Verify the work done at the site and recommend for the payments to contractor(s)/casual labors etc
- Working in harmony with all other project staff and field team for the effective and efficient day-to-day management of the WASH project.
- Coordinate with other stakeholders on the ground for smooth, efficient and effective implementation of the activities.

1. **When need be, Represent Amal in coordination meetings such as WASH cluster and other cluster meetings.**

**QUALIFICATIONS / EXPERIENCE:**

- Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical, civil, topographic or related field.
- At least five years’ work experience in WASH and a similar role.
- Proficient in Auto CAD, Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
- Good written and spoken English.
- Able to be diplomatic in communications with all NGO, governmental, and community partners.
- Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability in an ever-changing environment.
- Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
- Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
- Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal is dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so maintaining equal opportunities and nondiscrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. jobs.description:
**A. About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific and Africa. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience. The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Philippines. In the Philippines, ADPC will work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to provide technical support for capacity-strengthening activities, including contextualization of LEARN materials, training facilitation, organizational capacity strengthening, remote coaching and technical assistance to participating L/NNGOs. To support this work, ADPC seeks to engage a **Capacity Building Expert (Public Health) – Philippines**. The consultant will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point, working closely with the ADPC project team, the Health Emergency Management (HEM) Specialist, the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating L/NNGOs and relevant stakeholders to plan, deliver and follow up practical technical support within the agreed country implementation arrangements.

A key focus of the assignment will be to ensure that LEARN's capacity-strengthening approaches and resources are appropriately contextualized to the Philippine public health, humanitarian, disaster risk, and institutional context, and that participating L/NNGOs receive practical technical support to strengthen their readiness and capacity to respond to infectious disease outbreaks.

**Note:** *It is not the intent of the ToR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**D. Duties and Responsibilities**

Under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Emergency Preparedness and Response/LEARN Program Lead of ADPC, the Capacity Building Expert will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point for LEARN activities in the Philippines. The consultant will work closely with participating L/NNGOs, relevant stakeholders, the ADPC project team and the IMC Philippines Country Team on day-to-day planning, implementation coordination, organizational engagement and follow-up, and translation of LEARN technical approaches into practical, context-appropriate support responsive to identified organizational and operational needs. The consultant will undertake the following key responsibilities:

**1. Technical and Capacity-Building Support**

- Provide technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and response to support ADPC's technical contribution to LEARN implementation in the Philippines.
- Jointly plan capacity-strengthening activities with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and undertake agreed technical preparation, contextualization, facilitation and follow-up of training, exercises and other capacity-development interventions for participating L/NNGOs and local first responders, in accordance with the approved workplan and country implementation arrangements.
- Adapt relevant LEARN training materials, tools and technical resources in consultation with the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating organizations and relevant stakeholders to reflect organizational capacities, priorities and Philippine realities; submit substantive technical products to the ADPC LEARN team for technical review and quality assurance before use, and incorporate agreed feedback.
- Support the review of English-to-Filipino/Tagalog and relevant local-language translations of LEARN training materials, tools and guidance for accuracy, clarity, consistency of public health terminology and suitability for participating organizations. Work with the IMC Philippines Country Team and qualified translators or language reviewers, drawing on the Consultant’s language competencies, and coordinate with project team to resolve technical ambiguities before use.
- Provide technical facilitation and resource support for agreed LEARN training and capacity-development activities, coordinating participant engagement, schedules, field access, event arrangements and logistical requirements with the IMC Philippines Country Team and ADPC according to their agreed responsibilities.
- Apply appropriate adult-learning, participatory and practical training methodologies to strengthen the application of knowledge and skills by participating organizations.
- Provide practical technical support according to assessed needs on infectious disease preparedness and response, including Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) or equivalent response mechanisms, health emergency management (HEM) systems, activation and escalation arrangements, emergency operations/incident coordination, community-based surveillance and reporting, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), referral pathways and multisectoral coordination.
- Apply the 7-1-7 framework as an additional ADPC technical framework, rather than an existing LEARN contractual requirement, with participating L/NNGOs and local first responders as appropriate to their roles and Philippine public health systems: detect a suspected infectious disease outbreak within seven days of emergence, notify the appropriate public health authority within one day of detection, and complete priority early response actions within seven days of notification.
- Integrate relevant 7-1-7 concepts into assessments, training, coaching and exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team to identify bottlenecks and enabling factors in detection, notification and early response, and strengthen reporting, activation and coordination pathways. Organizational support will contribute to wider system performance within each organization’s mandate; the Consultant will not be responsible for measuring national 7-1-7 performance.

**2. Organizational Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance**

- Work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to plan and conduct the agreed technical components of organizational and readiness assessments using agreed tools; document baseline capacities, strengths and gaps, validate findings with participating L/NNGOs, and submit findings to project team for technical review to inform capacity-strengthening support.
- Translate validated assessment findings into organization-specific capacity-strengthening action plans with participating L/NNGOs and the IMC Philippines Country Team, identifying priorities, responsible persons, timelines, training and coaching requirements, and evidence of progress. Align implementation with the Program’s approved workplan, country implementation arrangements and available resources.
- Provide ongoing technical assistance, mentoring, practical exercises and remote or in-person just-in-time coaching, as appropriate and authorized, to participating organizations to implement agreed capacity-strengthening priorities and apply learning in their preparedness and response arrangements, coordinating support and follow-up with the IMC Philippines Country Team.
- Support L/NNGOs in developing, testing and updating organizational preparedness arrangements and community response plans, including roles and responsibilities, activation triggers, reporting and referral pathways, coordination and resource needs, based on assessed priorities.
- Monitor progress against organization-specific action plans through documented follow-up, evidence of practical application and reassessment where appropriate; identify additional coaching needs, support problem-solving, and escalate unresolved technical issues and operational constraints to the Program Lead and IMC Philippines focal point, as appropriate.
- Promote approaches that build on existing national and local systems, structures and capacities and support locally led preparedness and response.

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Field Coordination**

- Coordinate regular technical engagement with participating L/NNGOs, local first responder networks, public health and humanitarian actors, community-based organizations and other relevant stakeholders in close collaboration with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, following agreed country engagement and communication arrangements.
- Jointly conduct participatory stakeholder mapping exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team, building on existing country mapping, and periodically update the mapping of L/NNGOs, local first responders, community-based organizations, public health authorities, health facilities, surveillance and laboratory actors, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and technical partners relevant to approved project locations.
- Analyze stakeholder roles, capacities, geographic and population coverage, coordination relationships, referral and reporting pathways, and gaps or duplication to inform organizational screening, selection and onboarding recommendations and capacity-strengthening priorities.
- Support participating organizations in establishing or strengthening linkages with relevant national and subnational public health preparedness and response mechanisms, as appropriate
- Maintain an updated stakeholder map/database in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team, applying appropriate data protection procedures and sharing relevant information with ADPC.
- Maintain regular technical communication with participating organizations to identify emerging capacity needs and provide appropriate follow-up support.
- Contribute to consultations, technical discussions, workshops and other LEARN engagements as required.
- Provide contextual and technical updates to the ADPC LEARN team on public health emergency preparedness, disaster-health risks and other developments affecting capacity strengthening and project implementation in the Philippines.
- Facilitate peer learning among participating organizations in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and participate in cross-site technical exchanges with the Thailand–Myanmar Border Capacity Building Expert, HEM Specialist and relevant LEARN partners to share tools, lessons and practical solutions while maintaining context-specific implementation.
- Contribute Philippine experience and lessons to the refinement of LEARN capacity-strengthening resources and approaches.

**4. Outbreak Readiness and Response Support**

- Maintain awareness of emerging infectious disease events and public health threats relevant to participating organizations and project locations through coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and appropriate public health information sources, and communicate significant developments and potential support needs to ADPC.
- Where an outbreak or other public health emergency creates a need for additional LEARN support, provide agreed technical and coordination assistance to participating L/NNGOs in close collaboration with the IMC Philippines Country Team, subject to ADPC/LEARN authorization, available resources, security considerations and defined project scope. Support will be coordinated with responsible public health authorities and relevant response mechanisms and remain within Consultant’s competencies and authorized role.
- Support rapid identification of organizational operational needs, capacities and gaps with IMC Philippines and participating organizations, and translate findings into priority actions. As authorized and appropriate, assist activation of RRTs or equivalent mechanisms, coordination, information management and reporting, community engagement, referral pathways, IPC/WASH and response planning; provide remote or field-based just-in-time coaching.
- Document operational bottlenecks, enabling factors and lessons from response support with IMC Philippines, applying 7-1-7 or Early Action Review principles where appropriate, and integrate agreed learning into organizational action plans, community response plans and subsequent preparedness activities.

**5. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting**

- Monitor capacity-strengthening activities and organizational progress against agreed workplan milestones, action plans and LEARN indicators in coordination with the ADPC project team and IMC Philippines Country Team, using agreed country monitoring systems and reporting schedules.
- Maintain training attendance and participant profiles, learning assessments, exercise findings, mentoring/coaching logs, stakeholder mapping records, organizational action trackers, technical review records and evidence of follow-up, using agreed formats and safe data-management procedures. Coordinate record collection and consolidation with the IMC Philippines Country Team to avoid duplication and disaggregate participation data by sex, age and disability where feasible, appropriate and safe.
- Provide regular technical and implementation updates to ADPC and share relevant updates with the IMC Philippines Country Team through agreed reporting arrangements, including achievements, action-plan progress, challenges, emerging needs, agreed corrective actions and responsibilities for follow-up.
- Contribute technical inputs and supporting information to ADPC's periodic LEARN progress reports, monitoring requirements and other project documentation.
- Document feedback, lessons learned, capacity-development results, good practices and emerging technical needs from participating organizations and field implementation.
- Propose improvements to technical tools, learning resources and guidance based on assessment findings, implementation experience and feedback from participating organizations and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and submit substantive technical revisions to the HEM Specialist for review and quality assurance.
- Support continuous improvement of LEARN capacity-strengthening approaches and contribute Philippine experiences and lessons to cross-country learning and refinement of technical resources.

**6. Cross-Cutting Responsibilities**

- Integrate Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout stakeholder engagement, organizational assessments, training, coaching, community response planning and monitoring.
- Facilitate safe, inclusive and accessible participation, taking into account language, disability-related needs, displacement-related barriers and other relevant contextual considerations.
- Protect confidential organizational and community information, apply appropriate data protection and information-sharing procedures, and report safeguarding concerns through established ADPC and partner mechanisms.
- Undertake other related technical and capacity-strengthening responsibilities as may be reasonably required to support effective implementation of LEARN in the Philippines.

**E. Working Principles**

In performing the duties and responsibilities outlined above, the Consultant will report directly to the LEARN Program Lead, who will provide overall programmatic, contractual and management oversight, including workplan and budget management, coordination with IMC, and approval of major implementation decisions. For country-level implementation, the Consultant will work in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team on activity planning, organizational engagement, implementation arrangements, technical delivery and follow-up, in accordance with agreed partner responsibilities and coordination mechanisms.

**F. Required Qualifications**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

**Education:**

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree preferred) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Emergency/Disaster Management, Community Health, International Development, or another relevant field.
- A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline combined with substantial relevant professional experience may be considered.

**Professional Experience:**

- At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in public health, humanitarian health, infectious disease preparedness and response, health emergency management, community health, disaster preparedness or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated experience in capacity strengthening, training facilitation, mentoring and/or coaching of local organizations, health workers or community-based responders.
- Practical experience in infectious disease outbreak preparedness and/or response, public health emergency management or related programming.
- Proven experience working with government/public health institutions, health emergency coordination mechanisms, local government structures, NGOs and technical partners in the Philippines.
- Demonstrated experience working with local and national NGOs, civil society organizations and/or community-based organizations.
- Experience conducting or supporting organizational/capacity assessments and translating identified gaps into capacity-development interventions.
- Experience facilitating participatory, competency-based and/or scenario-based training is highly desirable.
- Experience with Rapid Response Teams (RRTs), emergency operations, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement, IPC/WASH, community response planning or related technical areas would be an advantage.
- Knowledge of contemporary outbreak readiness and response frameworks, including 7-1-7, is highly desirable. Experience supporting real-time outbreak response, RRTs, emergency operations/incident coordination, Early Action Reviews, after-action reviews or comparable operational learning processes would be an advantage.
- Experience working across the disaster–health nexus, including preparedness and response in areas affected by natural hazards and concurrent public health emergencies, would be an advantage.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of the Philippine public health emergency preparedness and response context, including national and/or subnational systems, is strongly preferred.
- Experience working with organizations or stakeholders in Luzon/NCR and/or Mindanao/BARMM would be an advantage.

**Language**

- Excellent written and spoken English is required.
- Professional proficiency in Filipino/Tagalog is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of relevant local languages in project implementation areas would be an advantage.

**G. Performance Competency**

**Core competencies**

- **Integrity:** Demonstrates the highest level of commitment and demonstrates respect for persons of concern to ADPC, partners, and colleagues in all aspects of work. Ensures that personal and professional behavior is of the highest standard.
- **Diversity Awareness:** Able to embrace the uniqueness of all individuals along several dimensions such as race, religious beliefs, ethnicity, age, gender, physical abilities, political beliefs, socioeconomic status, disability, political conviction, or any other distinguishing features.
- **Equality Awareness:** Understands that each individual has an equal opportunity to make decisions, participate in social activities, perform any work at the organization, and make the most of her/ his life and talents.
- **Teamwork and Collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.

**H. Preparedness and Climate Action Department Functional Competencies:**

- **Teamwork and collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.
- **Results Orientation:** Focuses on delivering agreed-upon results through effectively managing internal and external resources to achieve results. Demonstrates a commitment to both personal and organizational excellence, with an emphasis on results.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Skills:** Displays analytical thinking by identifying, defining, and analyzing information, situations, and problems. Arrives at viable solutions through a variety of approaches. Demonstrates critical thoughts, methodical review of implications, intuition, and rational conclusions.
- **Adaptability:** Demonstrates flexibility, both intellectually and behaviorally, to adapt to and work effectively in various situations, often under demanding conditions, and to cope with the unforeseen or unexpected. Looks for opportunities presented by change and is not "paralyzed" by new and unusual scenarios. Creates opportunities to improve how they work.

**I. Duty Station**

Manila, Philippines. Technical support will cover participating L/NNGOs and approved LEARN project locations in the Philippines. Specific locations, remote support and field missions will be agreed through the approved workplan in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team; travel requires ADPC authorization, available resources, appropriate access and security arrangements, and alignment with project scope.

**J. Duration**

November 2026 – September 2027 (11 months)

**K. Itinerary**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC financial policy.

**L. Condition of payment**

The Consultant will receive a monthly payment upon submission of completed timesheets. In addition, the Consultant is eligible for reimbursement of any program-related expenses incurred in the implementation of project activities, subject to the prior approval of the Program Lead.

jobs.title: Strategy, Program Quality & Impact Director
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Strategy, Program Quality & Impact Director**, you will provide strategic and technical leadership to a multidisciplinary team of technical and sector specialists, including the Design, Monitoring and Evaluation (DME) team. You will ensure high-quality technical guidance, effective application of approved project models and approaches, and compliance with organisational standards and best practices to strengthen programme quality and maximise sustainable impact for children, families and communities.

You will design and institutionalise a comprehensive Strategy Performance Monitoring Framework covering Ministry Impact, Ministry Funding, Operational Excellence, and People, Learning & Growth. You will monitor and report performance against agreed targets, provide regular updates to leadership and stakeholders, lead the annual Strategy Review with SMT and SST, and oversee the implementation of at least one strategic initiative assigned by your supervisor.

**KEY PERFORMANCE AREA:**

**Integrated Programme Framework (IPF) Implementation, Monitoring and Learning**

***Programme Framework Implementation***

You will lead staff orientation and capacity building on IPF and Most Simplified Solution (MSS) requirements, integrate Sponsorship Minimum Programme Requirements (MVPs), guarantees and Future Ready Sponsorship (FRS) into implementation, and ensure that ADP plans are evidence-based and contextually relevant.

***Monitoring and Performance Measurement***

You will lead project and programme monitoring and performance measurement, including the annual impact measurement process across 22 APs. You will strengthen data collection, analysis, quality assurance and use, standardise monitoring tools and practices, and ensure findings inform programme adaptation and improvement.

***Learning, Documentation and Reporting***

You will ensure timely submission of high-quality quarterly reports, strengthen evidence-based learning, documentation and knowledge management, and promote the use of evidence to improve programme quality, impact and innovation.

***Knowledge Management, Learning, Research and External Engagement***

You will lead the development and implementation of a Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) framework that promotes continuous learning, innovation and evidence-based decision-making. You will oversee research, evaluations, learning reviews and case studies; ensure programme impact is measured and communicated; strengthen knowledge-sharing and communities of practice; and share evidence and best practices with partners, donors, government stakeholders and the wider World Vision Partnership to support influence, visibility and resource mobilisation.

***Leadership, Line Management and Coordination with Sectors***

You will provide overall leadership and management of the SPQI function, ensuring effective planning, prioritisation, resource allocation and delivery of objectives. You will foster collaboration and accountability across technical, programme, operations, grants and support teams; coordinate cross-sector planning and implementation; support technical teams in delivering quality programmes; and facilitate regular reviews to address challenges and monitor progress. You will also strengthen coordination between the National Office, Area Programmes, Regional Office and Global Centre.

***Organisational Culture, Staff Supervision and Staff Development***

You will provide strategic direction and oversight to the PQI/DME teams, building a collaborative, accountable and high-performing culture. You will lead staff capacity development on programme quality, DMEAL and good development practices; promote continuous learning and professional development; and ensure technical staff provide appropriate guidance and support across operational areas. You will also develop individual development plans, coach and mentor direct reports, and lead talent management and succession planning to strengthen staff capabilities and organisational continuity.

**Requirements include:**

- Minimum of 10 years in managerial and leadership positions, demonstrating increasing levels of responsibility.
- Advanced/graduate degree with an additional post-graduate in a relevant field, potentially including public health, development, M&E, statistics, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated expertise in development of user-friendly tools and resources for MEAL and utilization of learning platforms for helping others learn.
- Qualitative and/or quantitative research and evaluation skills, including but not limited to study design, survey instrument design and use, establishing and measuring outcome and process indicators, sampling, data analysis plans, data cleaning, and statistical analysis.
- Demonstrated experience in business strategy development, monitoring and reporting.
- Experience and competencies data analysis using appropriate software tools (e.g. SPSS, SAS, ABTAB).
- Experience in synthesizing new learnings and developing approaches for change within the organization.
- Strong experience in developing capacity building materials and rolling out new approaches across the organization.
- Knowledge of the monitoring and evaluation requirements of key institutional donors (UN Donors, EU, USAID, etc.).
- Consistently demonstrates high-level influence and strategic engagement skills and tactical savvy in delivery of technical assistance.
- Comfort and confidence working in a diverse and inclusive team environment.
- Ability to think broadly and look at the macro, strategic issues to inform strategy choices and management process
- Portuguese is not mandatory, but it will be an added advantage. Fluency in both spoken and written English is essential.

jobs.company: Medecins du Monde - Turkey / Dunya Doktorlari Dernegi
jobs.description:
**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Status**:Fixed-term contract

**Expected Starting Date:** ASAP

**1. Position Purpose**

The HR/Administration Manager is responsible for the effective day-to-day management of DDD's human resources and general administrative operations in Syria, ensuring reliable personnel administration, compliance with applicable legal and organisational requirements, and adequate administrative support to field operations.

The position contributes to the progressive establishment of DDD's HR and administrative management capacities in Damascus, including the transfer of selected responsibilities currently performed by Istanbul HQ or supported through external service providers.

The HR/Administration Manager is expected to combine operational HR and administrative management with the development of practical procedures, tools, records and internal coordination mechanisms adapted to the evolving operational structure of DDD in Syria.

**2. Main Responsibilities**

**A. Human Resources Administration and Personnel Management**

· Coordinate day-to-day HR administration for DDD personnel across Syria.

· Ensure the preparation, administration and proper filing of employment contracts, amendments and other personnel documentation.

· Maintain accurate and up-to-date personnel records, including employment status, contractual conditions, leave, attendance and other relevant information.

· Coordinate payroll preparation, including verification of attendance, contractual entitlements, deductions and other payroll-related information.

· Monitor contract expiry dates, renewals and other administrative deadlines.

· Support recruitment processes, including vacancy publication, candidate coordination, interview arrangements, contracting and onboarding.

· Coordinate staff departures, contract terminations and related administrative formalities.

· Ensure consistent application of DDD's HR policies and procedures, in coordination with Istanbul HQ.

**B. Employment Compliance and Institutional Administrative Liaison**

· Monitor and coordinate compliance with applicable Syrian employment and personnel administration requirements.

· Follow up on employee registration, social insurance, payroll-related declarations and other statutory obligations, as applicable.

· Maintain regular working relationships with relevant public administrations and competent authorities concerning HR and administrative matters.

· Coordinate with external legal advisers and administrative service providers when required.

· Prepare and maintain documentation supporting DDD's institutional registrations, authorisations and administrative obligations in Syria.

· Monitor regulatory developments affecting employment and administrative operations, and inform country management and HQ of relevant implications.

· Ensure appropriate follow-up of official correspondence, submissions, renewals and administrative deadlines.

· Maintain clear records of completed, ongoing and pending regulatory and administrative actions.

**C. General Administration and Office Management**

· Coordinate the administrative functioning of the Damascus office and support administrative arrangements in other Syria field locations.

· Oversee office management activities, including premises administration, utilities, supplies, service contracts and routine administrative requirements.

· Coordinate travel arrangements, accommodation, official visits and administrative support to staff movements when required.

· Maintain administrative records, registers, contractual documentation and official correspondence.

· Coordinate administrative aspects of office establishment, relocation or expansion.

· Support the administration of facilities, equipment and assets in coordination with the relevant logistics and IT functions.

· Ensure that administrative expenditures and commitments follow established authorisation and documentation procedures.

· Identify administrative bottlenecks and propose practical solutions to maintain operational continuity.

**D. HR Reporting, Records and HQ Coordination**

· Establish and maintain reliable HR information and personnel monitoring tools, using appropriate systems or structured Excel-based records where necessary.

· Prepare periodic HR reports covering staffing, contracts, recruitment, leave, attendance and other relevant personnel information.

· Ensure the accuracy, completeness and confidentiality of personnel records and HR-related documentation.

· Coordinate with Istanbul HQ on HR reporting requirements, contractual matters, policy interpretation and administrative compliance.

· Provide relevant personnel information for budgeting, workforce planning, donor reporting and internal management purposes.

· Support internal reviews, audits and compliance verifications by preparing the required HR and administrative documentation.

· Maintain regular communication with the HQ General Services Department, particularly concerning HR administration, organisational procedures and administrative obligations.

Istanbul HQ retains institutional HR policy oversight, methodological guidance and the validation responsibilities established under DDD's delegation of authority.

**E. HR/Administrative Organisation and Capacity Development**

· Contribute to the progressive transfer of operational HR and administrative responsibilities from Istanbul to Damascus.

· Assess existing personnel administration practices, records, tools and workflows across Syria operations.

· Establish practical HR calendars, personnel tracking tools, administrative checklists and standard documentation.

· Clarify responsibilities and information flows between Damascus, other field locations, country management and HQ.

· Supervise and support HR and administrative personnel assigned to Syria operations.

· Identify training and capacity development needs among HR and administrative staff.

· Propose improvements that strengthen administrative reliability, legal compliance and operational efficiency without unnecessarily complicating existing processes.

**3. Working Relationships and Responsibilities**

The HR/Administration Manager operates within the Syria Country Mission's management structure, under the direct managerial and operational authority of the Country Director.

The position maintains functional working relationships with the HQ General Services Department, particularly concerning HR policies, personnel administration, employment compliance, organisational procedures and administrative reporting.

The HR/Administration Manager works closely with the Finance Manager on payroll preparation, personnel cost monitoring and employment-related financial obligations, and with operational and field managers on staffing and administrative support requirements.

The position also coordinates, as necessary, with legal advisers, public administrations and external service providers, ensuring that institutional commitments and administrative decisions remain within established delegations of authority.

**4. Required Qualifications and Experience**

· Relevant university qualification in human resources, business administration, management, law or a related field.

· Demonstrated experience in HR administration and general administrative management within an NGO, international organisation or comparable multi-site operational environment.

jobs.title: Access and Security officer - Raqqa
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Access and Security Officer will support World Vision’s safety and security risk management efforts in North East of Syria ensuring alignment with WV security policies and standards, She or he will support Syria Security Coordinator by keeping all Core Security Requirements are updated and implemented in line with local context and in accordance with WVSR Security management approach

Based in Ar Raqqa office ,the Access and Security Officer will support NES Area Manager directly with Liaison and Access by maintaining safe, principled and sustained humanitarian access for WVSR operations in North East of Syria by engaging with local authorities, governmental bodies, local stakeholders ,community interlocuter and coordination platforms to ensure smooth operational access and compliance as well as maintain a professional coordination with related Syrian Government agencies and facilitate approvals of WVSR projects in North East Syria.

The Access and Security Officer will report directly to the Security Coordinator with matrix reporting to the NES Area Manager.

**Major Responsibilities:**

1. **Security: Organization and Planning 25%**

- Ensure alignment with WV security policies and standards, thus ensuring that operational priorities are appropriately supported.
- Support Syria Security Coordinator with Security Risk Assessments and Context risk rating for North East of Syria
- Ensure adequate and contextually appropriate Planning, including: Safety and Security Management Plan, Contingency Plans, and Emergency Plan.
- Support Syria Security Coordinator to review and keep up-to-date Safety and Security Management SOPs.
- Work closely with Syria Security Coordinator, NES Area Manager, and relevant WV staff and selected Partner staff for NES operation area as appropriate to carry out Security Risk Assessments.
- Technically, supervise security guards in WV Raqqa office /warehouse /guesthouse

1. **Safety &Security: Monitoring and implementation 25%**

- Support the Security Coordinator by ensuring Core Security Requirements are implemented in line with local context and in accordance with WVSR Security Management
- Maintain daily situation awareness, as it relates to safety and security threats in the area as well as WV staff, assets, and Programs in NES.
- Ensure that all security incidents are reported in accordance with WV Security Policy.
- Support in enhancing a culture of security awareness and monitor compliance among NES staff.
- Provide security-related advice, in written and oral form, to the Area Manager, Security Coordinator and other staff.
- Support the Security Coordinator by conducting rehearsals and practical exercises to ensure that NES staff are familiar with contingency plans and can implement them confidently.
- Facilitate security briefings and awareness sessions for WVSR NES staff
- Monthly safety inspection for WVSR premises in NES
2. **Access, Liaison and External Engagement.**
- In Support of the NES Area Manager will establish and maintain professional working relationships with relevant local authorities, administrative bodies, security actors, community leaders, tribal representatives, civil society actors and other stakeholders relevant to humanitarian access.
- Work with local authorities and ICD offices in NES to secure all required authorizations and permissions for WVSR local staff movement and distributions, for project implementation
- Support with all access and security-related liaison matters at NES / Raqqa level
- Coordinate with Area Manager, Security and operations teams to facilitate safe and authorized staff movements and field missions.
- Coordinate with concerned Syrian Government agencies and facilitate approvals of new projects for WVSR in NES.
- Support in developing and maintaining an updated access map and stakeholder overview for areas of operation in NES
- Monitor political, security, social, economic and community developments that may affect humanitarian access in NES.
- Support WVSR's efforts to strengthen community acceptance.
- Develop and maintain contact networks relevant to humanitarian access
- Ensure all correspondence with authorities adheres to WVSR policies and is documented, retained, and filed in an organized and secure manner.
- Ensure engagement with stakeholders and governmental bodies remains consistent with WVSR's humanitarian principles, neutrality, impartiality and independency.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**
- Bachelor’s Degree in a field related to humanitarian work, Access and risk management, such as security management, regional studies, International relationships, business administration or similar.
- A detailed understanding of security, local governance and community structures North East Syria.
- Good experience in humanitarian access facilitation and negotiation
- Computer competency with email and MS Office.
2. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**
- At least 3 years’ work experience in Humanitarian Access, Liaison and Security, preferably - in an international organization.
- Undergraduate degree in relevant field would be an asset.
- Professional qualifications would be an asset (e.g. ToT ,CSMP )
3. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- Requires regular travel in Syria

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

- Very good command in English (written and spoken) is a must.
- Fluency in Arabic is also mandatory.

jobs.title: Consultancy for Multimedia Artist for the Production Digital Safety Resources
jobs.description:
*November 2026 – February 2027*

**Organisational context**

ECPAT International is a global network of civil society organisations dedicated to ending the sexual exploitation of children in all its manifestations. This includes the exploitation of children in prostitution, in the context of digital environments, in the context of trafficking of children for sexual purposes, the sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism and some forms of child, early and forced marriage.

ECPAT has a network with a membership of 141 civil society organisations in 113 countries. The ECPAT International Secretariat coordinates the global work of the organisation and is based in Bangkok, Thailand. The Secretariat designs and implements global and regional level programmes and undertakes programming, campaigning, advocacy and research to facilitate a range of network initiatives.

**Background**

ECPAT International actively works to strengthen child safety and shift gender norms in the online gaming space. Since 2022, we have been directly engaging the gaming industry, communities, trade associations, and adjacent sectors, to enhance knowledge on child protection issues and gender-related dynamics in online gaming environments—with the goal of developing concrete solutions at different scales, in-game or within the ecosystem, that promote safe gaming and positive behaviors among children.

ECPAT is embarking on a new collaboration with Roblox that aims to produce an online interactive safety resource designed to equip Roblox Creators. With this, ECPAT is seeking to engage a Multimedia Artist (Individual or Team) to support in the creation of multimedia assets including short animated videos, digital flash cards, project poster, and a consolidated illustrated PDF, which will complement the written component of each module under the umbrella theme of gender and child safety in online gaming. The Multimedia Artist will work in strict collaboration with the teams at ECPAT and Roblox for onboarding, inputs and finalisation of the work.

**Scope of assignment**

1. **Proposal of design studies**

- Propose 2-3 design studies to provide a visual direction for all materials, harmonising the look and feel across different outputs and applying the necessary co-branding guidelines.

**2. Production of multimedia assets**

- **Module assets.** Produce the visual aids needed for maximum 5 learning modules (in batches), based on the written text or outline provided by ECPAT.

*Each written module may include a combination of:*

- *1-3 short animated videos (~10-15 seconds)*
- *2-6 digital flash cards (static photos, portrait, back-to-back)*
- **Cover poster.** Create a Canva-ready poster to be used to promote the collaboration resources on social media and newsletters.
- **Illustrated PDF.** Consolidate the modules into a single illustrated PDF that will serve as the alternate, website library-ready resource summarizing the topics learned (written text provided by ECPAT).

**3. Support for integration into final hosting site**

- Once the final hosting site is identified by ECPAT and Roblox, provide support to adjust (e.g., sizing) and optimise the digital outputs to ensure seamless integration.

**4. Turnover of all final materials**

- Provide ECPAT with a copy of all final resources in a shared Google Drive or compressed file.

**Ideal qualifications**

The Individual/Team should have:

- Proven skills in video animation, graphic design, and layout.
- Prior experience in producing similar outputs, particularly educational materials, child safety toolkits, and other similar informational resources.
- Strong information design skills with great attention to detail and accessibility for learning.
- Familiarity with online gaming, Trust & Safety practices, and child safety and gender dynamics in the digital environment is a strong plus.
- Experience within the children’s rights, gender equity, and/or gender-based violence sectors would be an asset.
- Ability to take initiative and work independently and within the established deadlines.
- Understanding of and commitment to ECPAT International mission and values, including ethical and bias-free design practices.

Please visit our website for further information; [https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026-11-RfP-Roblox-Safety-Resources.pdf](https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026-11-RfP-Roblox-Safety-Resources.pdf)

**Duration and modality of the assignment**

- This consultancy will run from November 27, 2026, to February 26, 2027.
- This is a remote, home-based, opportunity. The consultant must provide their own equipment for use in this assignment, including digital licenses (if any). The consultant should be available to attend meetings within the Southeast Asia or Central Europe time zone.

**Term of payment**

Budget indication: USD 10,000

**Our Commitments**

As ECPAT’s International Secretariat we recognise that our strength lies in the diversity of the people who make up our global network, staff, volunteers and consultants. We are committed to being an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds and cultures can strive and be themselves. This means we will challenge ourselves to do better and to continue learning, to create and maintain a working environment steeped in respect, tolerance, safety, and where all parties are valued equally.

As a child-focused organisation, ECPAT has a strong commitment to child safeguarding and rigorous procedures, and the successful candidate will be required to sign our 2 codes of conduct.

jobs.title: Country Director, Rwanda
jobs.description:

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.**About the Role:**
As Country Director at CBM Rwanda, you will manage the organisation’s operations, leading a country programme with an operational scope typically ranging between USD 3–10 million. You will ensure quality delivery across all stages of programme development and implementation, with a focus on strategic programming opportunities that strengthen CBM’s relevance and reach. You will also strengthen CBM’s presence in Rwanda and represent the organisation to donors, government authorities, partners, the media, and local communities to maintain a strong and credible organisational profile. This includes coordinating the Board and the Annual General Assembly (where applicable) in line with Rwanda’s regulatory and governance requirements and CBM’s internal policies.

## **You Will:**

- Fulfil the role of Country Director to deliver CBM’s Disability and Inclusive Development work in the country.
- Lead the development and effective implementation of CBM’s Country Plan and its operational requirements, ensuring high-quality performance and alignment with CBM’s Federation strategy.
- Ensure strong financial discipline within the Country Office and work with partners to meet all operational and financial reporting requirements.
- Identify programme opportunities and areas where the organisation can demonstrate its value and relevance.

Significant experience in organisational development, change management, and capacity building.

- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
