jobs.title: Chief of Party II, Honduras
jobs.description:
**NOTE: This recruitment is contingent upon donor approval.**

CRS seeks Chief of Party II candidates for the anticipated USDA Non-Emergency Food for Peace projects. These multi‑year, development-focused projects seek to combat chronic and acute malnutrition especially in children and mothers, strengthen early recovery and resilience, and support communities.

The Chief of Party II will provide vision, leadership and overall management of these large and complex projects to serve the poor and vulnerable. The incumbent’s strategic leadership, management and technical knowledge will ensure the delivery of high-quality programming and advance the position of CRS as a leading agency in the respective field. As a senior leader, the Chief of Party II will proactively manage security and mitigate security risks.

Honduras is a Central American country with Caribbean Sea coastlines to the north and the Pacific Ocean to the south. In Honduras, CRS promotes sustainable economic growth, youth empowerment, more peaceful and just societies, and help communities protect the environment while preparing for and responding to natural disasters.

CRS Honduras leads and implements programs in education, water-smart agriculture, emergency response, disaster risk resilience, youth development, peacebuilding, local partner capacity strengthening, and water. In 2024, CRS´ programs benefited more than 500,000 vulnerable individuals in Honduras in 16 departments. CRS partners with the USDA, BHA, FAO, foundations, private sector, the Government of Honduras and 12 local organizations to create transformational and lasting change in the lives of Honduras´ most vulnerable families.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Lead all aspects of the development, implementation and consolidation of the assigned project, including sharing how the project contributes to the thought leadership of the industry. Serve as the primary point of contact with the donor as well as public, private and non-government stakeholders.
- Ensure the project is designed and implemented to meet donor expectations in terms of timely and quality results and budget, including strategies for phase out and sustainability. Lead coordination efforts between program and operations leads to ensure CRS program quality standards are adhered to.
- Effectively lead senior programming and operations talent. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching and mentoring. Strategically tailor individual development plans and complete performance assessments for direct reports. Oversee the development of staffing plans and the recruitment process of senior staff.
- Proactively manage and mitigate risk by monitoring national and regional issues that may impact staff and programming. Ensure all CRS staff safety and security policies and plans are regularly updated and all staff understand and adhere to these policies.
- Promote, uphold and model a commitment to the efficient use of agency and donor resources.
- Ensure compliance with donor grants, including financial tracking and oversight of partner budgets, finance, administration and donor reporting. Approve program expenditures, budget adjustments, and cost modification requests to donors.
- Represent CRS programming in international circles, highlighting innovative work. Publish program results and deliver presentations. Oversee the development of communication strategies and materials, complying with donor and CRS’ branding and marketing requirements and procedures.
- Manage relationships with consortium partner organizations, including organization of review/planning workshops. Coordinate the roles and activities of staff from other consortium member organizations to ensure implementation is in line with CRS partnership principles.
- Create and maintain proper conditions for learning. Establish a safe environment to share ideas, solutions, and difficulties. Build the internal capacity to detect, analyze and respond quickly to deficiencies.
- Identify performance gaps and training opportunities for CRS and partner staff and ensure the design and delivery of high-quality training and technical assistance.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, International Relations or a relevant technical area.
- Minimum of 8 years of relevant management and technical experience.
- Minimum of 7 years’ experience managing donor funds, including multi country grants. Excellent knowledge and experience in budget management.
- Minimum of 5 years of staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Experience coaching and mentoring senior program staff.
- Demonstrated experience of successful program management, including management of complex, high-value, multi-activity projects, with complicated logistics.
- Established leader in sector as demonstrated by peer reviewed publications, conference presentations etc.

**Preferred Qualifications**
- Master’s degree in a related field.
- Experience engaging partners and strengthening partnerships. Knowledge of CRS partnership strategy.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
- Ability to represent and present at high levels.
- Excellent knowledge of MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems.
- Excellent strategic, analytical, systems thinking, andproblem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big pictureand ability to make sound judgment and decisions.
- Excellent relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Ability to strategically approach each relationship.
- Team leadership abilities with diverse and multi-disciplinary teams. Coaching/mentoring skills.
- Strong communication and presentation skills. Ability to develop tailored and persuasive messaging for varied audiences.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented mindset.
- **Required Languages:** Fluency in English and Spanish is required.
- **Travel:** Must be willing and able to travel up to 35%.
- **Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.

jobs.description:
Announcement Date: 06/11/2026

Employer: Syrian Center for Media and Freedom of Expression (SCM)

Vacancy code: 05/Vdc2026

Application deadline: 15/11/2026

Program/ Project / Department: VDC Project –Reports to the Field Coordinator

Job title: Field Documentation Officer

Number of positions available: 4

Workstation: Syria

Expected starting date: 01 December 2026

Type and duration of contract: Temporary contract 8 months, renewable With a renewable three-month probationary period

**Roles and responsibilities**

- Conduct field-based documentation of human rights violations within the assigned geographical area, including identifying and documenting incidents and collecting information from victims, witnesses and other credible sources in accordance with SCM’s methodologies and documentation standards.
- Conduct interviews with victims, survivors, witnesses,family members and other relevant sources, ensuring informed consent, confidentiality, sensitivity and adherence to SCM’s protection and do-no-harm principles.
- Collect, verify and document testimonies and other relevant information and materials, including documents, photographs, videos and other available evidence, and ensure their proper entry and archiving in SCM’s documentation system.
- Maintain regular field presence and follow developments within the assigned geographical area, identifying incidents and documentation needs and reporting relevant developments to the Field Documentation Coordinator.
- Build and maintain a reliable network of local contacts and sources, including victims and affected communities, local actors and other relevant stakeholders, to support access to information and effective documentation.
- Coordinate with the Field Documentation Coordinator and other members of the documentation team, including OSINT investigators, to support verification, corroboration and follow-up of documented incidents.
- Undertake field missions and travel within the assigned geographical area as required for interviews, documentation and follow-up activities, taking into account relevant security and protection procedures.
- Ensure the confidentiality, security and protection of victims, witnesses, sources and information throughout the documentation process.
- Undertake other documentation-related tasks assigned by the direct supervisor in line with the objectives and methodologies of the project.

**Required skills and qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in law, human rights, social sciences or another relevant field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Previous experience in documenting human rights violations, field research, or related work is strongly preferred.
- Experience conducting interviews with victims, survivors, witnesses or other sources, including the ability to conduct sensitive interviews professionally and ethically.
- Good understanding of human rights documentation principles and methodologies.
- Ability and willingness to conduct regular fieldwork and travel within the assigned geographical area, including to locations required for documentation and interviews.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to build trust and engage respectfully with victims, witnesses and affected communities.
- Ability to assess information critically, identify inconsistencies and documentation gaps, and conduct appropriate follow-up with sources.
- Ability to use digital tools and documentation/database systems and to learn new technical tools required for the position.
- Ability to work independently in the field while maintaining effective coordination with the documentation team and coordinator.
- Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple documentation tasks and priorities.
- Commitment to confidentiality, professionalism, impartiality and human rights principles.
- Knowledge of International Human Rights Law and International Humanitarian Law is an asset.
- Experience with open-source research and verification is an asset.
- Fluency in Arabic
- Good command of English is an asset.

رمز الوظيفة: 05/Vdc2026

مهلة تقديم الطلبات: 15/11/2026

القسم/ البرنامج/ المشروع (التبعية الإدارية): مشروع توثيق الانتهاكات– يتبع للمنسق الميداني

اسم الوظيفة: موثق ميداني

عدد الشواغر المعلن عنها: 4

مكان العمل: سوريا

تاريخ المباشرة المتوقع: 01 ديسمبر 2026

نوع العقد وفترة التعاقد: عقد مؤقت
8 أشهر قابلة للتجديد مع فترة تجريبية 3 أشهر

**الدور والمسؤوليات**

- إجراء عمليات توثيق ميدانية لانتهاكات حقوق الإنسان ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، بما يشمل رصد الحوادث وتحديدها وتوثيقها، وجمع المعلومات من الضحايا والشهود وغيرهم من المصادر الموثوقة، وذلك وفقاً لمنهجيات المركز السوري للإعلام وحرية التعبير (SCM) ومعايير التوثيق المعتمدة لديه.
- إجراء مقابلات مع الضحايا والناجين والشهود وأفراد أسرهم وغيرهم من المصادر ذات الصلة، مع ضمان الحصول على الموافقة المستنيرة، والحفاظ على السرية، ومراعاة الحساسية في التعامل، والالتزام بمبادئ الحماية ومبدأ عدم إلحاق الضرر المعتمدة لدى المركز.
- جمع الإفادات والمعلومات والمواد ذات الصلة والتحقق منها وتوثيقها، بما في ذلك الوثائق والصور ومقاطع الفيديو وغيرها من الأدلة المتاحة، وضمان إدخالها وأرشفتها بشكل سليم في نظام التوثيق المعتمد لدى المركز.
- الحفاظ على حضور ميداني منتظم ومتابعة التطورات ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، ورصد الحوادث واحتياجات التوثيق، وإبلاغ منسق التوثيق الميداني بالتطورات ذات الصلة.
- بناء شبكة موثوقة من جهات الاتصال والمصادر المحلية والحفاظ عليها، بما يشمل الضحايا والمجتمعات المتضررة والجهات الفاعلة المحلية وأصحاب المصلحة المعنيين، بما يسهم في تسهيل الوصول إلى المعلومات وتعزيز فعالية عمليات التوثيق.
- التنسيق مع منسق التوثيق الميداني وأعضاء فريق التوثيق الآخرين، بمن فيهم المحققون المختصون بالاستقصاء مفتوح المصدر (OSINT)، لدعم عمليات التحقق من الحوادث الموثقة ومطابقة المعلومات والأدلة وتعزيزها ومتابعتها.
- تنفيذ المهام والزيارات الميدانية والتنقل ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، حسب الحاجة، لإجراء المقابلات وعمليات التوثيق وأنشطة المتابعة، مع مراعاة إجراءات الأمن والسلامة والحماية ذات الصلة.
- ضمان سرية وأمن وحماية الضحايا والشهود والمصادر والمعلومات طوال مراحل عملية التوثيق.
- تنفيذ أي مهام أخرى ذات صلة بالتوثيق، بما يتماشى مع أهداف المشروع ومنهجيات العمل المعتمدة.

**الشهادات والكفاءات المطلوبة**

- شهادة جامعية في القانون أو حقوق الإنسان أو العلوم الاجتماعية أو أي مجال ذي صلة، أو خبرة مهنية عملية معادلة في مجال ذي صلة.
- تُفضّل الخبرة السابقة في توثيق انتهاكات حقوق الإنسان أو إجراء البحوث الميدانية أو العمل في مجالات ذات صلة.
- خبرة في إجراء المقابلات مع الضحايا والناجين والشهود أو غيرهم من المصادر، بما في ذلك القدرة على إجراء المقابلات الحساسة بمهنية وأخلاقيات عالية.
- فهم جيد لمبادئ ومنهجيات توثيق انتهاكات حقوق الإنسان.
- القدرة والاستعداد للعمل الميداني بشكل منتظم والتنقل ضمن النطاق الجغرافي المحدد، بما في ذلك الوصول إلى المواقع اللازمة لأغراض التوثيق وإجراء المقابلات.
- امتلاك مهارات تواصل وتفاعل شخصية قوية، بما في ذلك القدرة على بناء الثقة والتعامل باحترام مع الضحايا والشهود والمجتمعات المتضررة.
- القدرة على تقييم المعلومات بشكل نقدي، وتحديد أوجه التناقض والثغرات في التوثيق، وإجراء المتابعة المناسبة مع المصادر.
- القدرة على استخدام الأدوات الرقمية وأنظمة التوثيق وقواعد البيانات، والاستعداد لتعلّم الأدوات التقنية الجديدة اللازمة لأداء مهام الوظيفة.
- القدرة على العمل بشكل مستقل في الميدان، مع الحفاظ على التنسيق الفعّال مع فريق التوثيق والمنسق المسؤول.
- امتلاك مهارات تنظيمية قوية والقدرة على إدارة مهام وأولويات متعددة متعلقة بالتوثيق.
- الالتزام بمبادئ السرية والمهنية والحياد ومبادئ حقوق الإنسان.
- تُعد المعرفة بالقانون الدولي لحقوق الإنسان والقانون الدولي الإنساني ميزة إضافية.
- تُعد الخبرة في البحث والتحقق باستخدام المصادر المفتوحة (OSINT) ميزة إضافية.
- إجادة اللغة العربية.
- يُعد امتلاك مستوى جيد في اللغة الإنجليزية ميزة إضافية.

jobs.title: Research Manager
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUND ON REACH**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to lead our research team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 1 year, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027.

## **Country profile**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea.

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community in Somalia. Data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to directly inform humanitarian response planning, as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Key areas of focus include:

**Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA):** REACH conducts the annual MSNA, whose findings feed into the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) workshop and, through it, the annual Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

**Food Security and Nutrition:** REACH conducts food security and nutrition assessments that feed into Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition analyses.

**Cash and Markets:** REACH provides research and analytical support to the Somali Cash Consortium and conducts market monitoring analysis as part of a harmonised approach, led by the Cash Working Group.

**Ad-hoc Research:** REACH conducts ad-hoc assessments as needs arise, including rapid needs assessments following sudden-onset shocks such as flooding, drought and conflict-induced displacement.

To ensure that research findings meaningfully inform humanitarian response planning, REACH shares data through formal coordination platforms, including the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), needs analysis and planning processes, the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, among others. Partner feedback is actively integrated to validate and triangulate findings, as well as to guide research design and geographic targeting.

## **FUNCTIONS**

REACH is seeking an experienced candidate who has previously managed teams and implemented projects in a complex humanitarian setting. Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, and in close coordination with the Country Representative and HQ, the Research Manager will be responsible for overseeing the implementation, development, and strategy of the research portfolio of the REACH Somalia mission. This includes managing the teams responsible for the MSNA, food security and nutrition assessments, the Somali Cash Consortium, market monitoring, and ad-hoc assessments such as rapid needs assessments.

The candidate should be comfortable representing REACH with donors and be able to coordinate and liaise with a range of senior external partners, including OCHA, cluster coordinators, UN agencies and NGOs. This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, humanitarian cluster, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager’s responsibilities include the following:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Direct management of international and national research staff across the MSNA, food security and nutrition, cash and markets, and ad-hoc assessment workstreams, including recruitment, appraisals, and capacity building;
- Day-to-day management of the research team, including the development of work plans and performance indicators, and development and implementation of capacity training plans to improve efficiency and performance;
- Conduct regular check-ins with staff within the unit, and promote team building, productivity and staff welfare as the main pastoral focal point for research staff;
- Provide regular support and technical backstopping;
- Take on additional work streams and management responsibilities as well as advise in strategic mission decision-making as a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), as required.

***RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant project and programme objectives, and REACH’s research cycle guidelines;
- Ensure that all (Senior) Research Officers are comprehensively briefed on objectives and expected outputs of research cycles, and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood;
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation for an assessment;
- For each research cycle, review ToRs before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that ToRs are validated before data collection begins;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning, data collection, and management;
- Monitor data collection, ensuring correct implementation in line with agreed ToRs, and keep track of progress and delays of all assessments throughout the research cycle;
- Work closely with the Field Manager and Ops teams to ensure logistics, finance, administration, security and HR processes directly related to REACH are appropriately implemented, alongside the relevant Acted departments.

***PORTFOLIO OVERSIGHT***

- Oversee the timely delivery of the annual MSNA, ensuring that findings are available in time to feed into the JIAF workshop and the HNRP, and support the team in preparing for and participating in the JIAF process;
- Oversee food security and nutrition assessments, ensuring that methodologies, timelines and outputs are aligned with IPC requirements and that data is made available to IPC analyses as planned;
- Oversee REACH’s research support to the Somali Cash Consortium, ensuring that deliverables meet consortium and donor requirements and timelines;
- Oversee market monitoring analysis, ensuring consistent, timely outputs that are used by Cash Working Group partners;
- Lead the planning and rapid deployment of ad-hoc assessments, such as rapid needs assessments, in response to emerging crises and partner information needs, in coordination with OCHA and the clusters.

***ANALYSIS AND DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure research staff maintain regular communication with HQ on progress and deadlines for written products;
- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs (i.e. reports, factsheets, briefs, presentations, etc.), complying with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Review all research products before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- Under supervision of HQ, ensure that research products are uploaded to relevant data portals, as specified in research ToRs;
- Under the direction of the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, engage in the dissemination of research products, including emails, presentations to coordination bodies, and bilateral meetings, such as with donors;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in conducting monitoring and evaluation as specified in the research ToRs and in line with REACH guidelines.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- With the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, identify information gaps in line with humanitarian priorities in Somalia, and identify advocacy and dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of REACH’s work;
- Lead on formalising synergies with other assessment and knowledge management actors, as well as strategic partnerships with key humanitarian stakeholders and decision makers;
- As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Somalia country strategy.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Represent REACH at the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG) and in other inter-agency coordination forums, and act as a key REACH focal point for OCHA on needs analysis and humanitarian programme cycle processes;
- Represent REACH in cluster and multi-sector meetings and technical working groups, including the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, and follow up on technical issues identified in these forums;
- In coordination with the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, present research findings to relevant partners to enhance their use and impact;
- Ensure that external communications with partners and key stakeholders, including UN agencies, local and national authorities, and NGOs, are conducted and documented as appropriate;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in external engagement on REACH strategy and, when requested, in fundraising and grants management.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs, and will ensure that the research team does the same. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

The Research Manager is also responsible for ensuring that all interactions with crisis-affected populations are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner, and that communities are adequately consulted and informed about REACH programme objectives, activities and methodologies.

## **REQUIREMEnTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international relations, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, social research, or similar).
- **Years of work experience** At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis.

- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high-level presentations and briefings to senior external audiences.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to manage multiple research cycles in parallel with tight deadlines in a complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the Horn of Africa region is desirable, or in any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’660 **CHF** and 3’720 **CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 **USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.

- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)

- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees

jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our team in Somalia.**

**Department**:REACH

**Position**:Senior Research Officer

**Contract duration**:4 months, with high likelihood of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu

**Starting Date**: 7 September 2026

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Research Manager, the Senior Research Officer is responsible for the implementation of IMPACT’s MSNA research cycle in Somalia, including the preparation, data collection, analysis, drafting, dissemination, and evaluation stages. Throughout the MSNA, the Senior Research Officer engages with partners and stakeholders to promote their participation and maximize their impact. They also ensure an efficient and transparent use of resources required for project implementation.

This position requires strong research skills (particularly in quantitative and mixed methodology sampling), willingness to work in hardship location, an analytical mind, creativity, independence, and an interest in the national and regional context. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings, as well as engage with external stakeholders in the design and dissemination of the research cycle. The position will regularly require interpreting data, highlighting relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research.

BACKGROUND OF MULTI SECTORAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT

IMPACT HQ in Geneva support the work of Multi-Sector Needs Assessments (MSNAs) in more than 20 countries. As a result of the World Humanitarian Summit and the Grand Bargain, a commitment was made to “impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context sensitive, timely and up to date” joint needs assessments that can serve as “a sound evidence base for humanitarian response plans”. These exercises have been informing consolidated humanitarian appeals since 2016. Since 2016, the number of MSNAs supported by REACH has more than quadrupled; MSNA data continues to influence flagship humanitarian response processes such as Humanitarian Needs and Response Plans (HNRPs). This indicates that evidence-based decision making is increasingly becoming a cornerstone of effective humanitarian action.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Research Officer is responsibilities include:

***Research CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Anticipate knowledge gaps prior to the execution of a Research Cycle through strong understanding of the Somali context.
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation of an assessment.
- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant research and project objectives and with IMPACT’s research cycle and other relevant guidelines.
- Design research approaches and methodologies according to IMPACT’s requirements and principles as well as partners’ information needs.
- Compose and construct, in close coordination with GIS and data teams, qualitative and quantitative data collection tool.
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in research design and planning.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING***

- Line manage the MSNA Research Officer directly and lead the MSNA team throughout the research cycle
- In close liaison with the Field Manager and Ops teams (field officer and logistics team), manage assessment logistics, including with partner organizations, identifying assessment areas, facilitating design workshops, managing joint data collection processes, and facilitating joint analysis workshops.
- In close liaison the Ops teams, ensure logistics, financial, administration, security and HR processes directly related to ongoing and upcoming assessments are appropriately planned, implemented and coordinated with the relevant Acted departments.
- In close liaison with data colleagues, provide quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data analysis on primary and/or secondary data as per ToRs, ensuring that meaningful techniques are used to analyze the data collected.
- Promoting capacity building across the IMPACT Somalia mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience)
- Providing day-to-day direct and indirect management of the research team within their unit/workstream, and field team during data collection.

***Internal Coordination***
- Interacting autonomously with HQ departments and serve as mission focal point for HQ’s corresponding unit and specialists in particular themes or technical areas.
- Engage in the development and implementation of IMPACT’s strategy in Somalia
- Conduct regular meetings with relevant national and international assessment staff members to assess progress in relevant research cycles and to review work plan.
- For all activities, ensure that all assessment and field teams are comprehensively briefed on objectives, expected outputs and that the overall implementation strategy is clearly understood.
- Ensure that project/field staff are given required training and resources to achieve their tasks in line with IMPACT and project requirements. Support to the line managers and specialists in the development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Be available to provide regular support and technical backstopping; regularly debrief team members to receive feedback on the progress of an activity.
- In coordination with line manager, contribute to conduct induction for new staff members, including training in basic technical competencies for research design, implementation and analysis.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs that consolidate the analyses from each research cycle into relevant products such as factsheets, reports, briefs, presentations, etc which comply with IMPACT’s guidelines and quality standards.
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact in line with their intended use for the relevant audiences.
- Follow the designated timeline of reports to be submitted to project partners and donors. Ensure that delays or identified challenges for specific assessments are reported in writing and orally in a timely manner.
- Maintain regular communication with country Management and IMPACT HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ before external release.

***External Engagement***

- Ensure that relevant partners are consulted and involved at all stages of research cycle: assessment preparation; data collection; data analysis; review of research products; product dissemination; and lessons learnt.
- After validation by the line manager, represent IMPACT in relevant external meetings/ working groups.
- Follow up on issues identified by partners or during meetings / working groups.
- Promote an active use of datasets and research findings by partners and the broader humanitarian community for their decision making.
- After validation by line manager, disseminate research findings to relevant third parties in order to enhance their use and impact.
- Ensure that all partner engagement and all external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues.
- More generally, contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of IMPACT’s mandate, ethics, values and stand-point with regard to other actors.

***Data Confidentiality and Protection***

- The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOPs. He/she will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis, etc.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience required. Ability to adapt, implement and interpret methodology, sampling and analysis to a high standard
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA type of research and humanitarian assessments is an asset. Prior experience working with components of FSL/public health is highly desirable
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills for effective and accurate reporting required
- **Academic** **qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Master’s degree in relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, etc)
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Advanced skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage; Experience with InDesign an asset.
- **Level of independence** Proven ability to work independently.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the HoA region is desirable; or any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between **3’000 CHF** and **3’120 CHF** monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of **300 USD**
- NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. IMPACT is hosted by Acted in this country \[to be adjusted depending on the country\]
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as an HQ Procurement Officer!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

This role ensures the effective management of procurement and purchasing activities for both country programmes and HQ departments, securing timely, compliant and cost-effective acquisition of goods and services while supporting operational continuity and organisational efficiency.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Manage international procurement for country program to ensure the availability of goods and equipment required for field operations.
- Manage transport and import/export compliance activities to ensure the efficient, secure delivery of goods to country programs.
- Manage the HQ ordering process, in collaboration with relevant departments, to ensure traceability and efficient procurement.
- Manage HQ stock to ensure the continuity of operational support to country programs and departments.
- Support HQ and country teams with their purchasing and procurement needs (sourcing, contracting, purchasing, delivering and invoicing) to enhance supply chain performance and operational continuity.
- Implement procurement strategies with stakeholders to ensure efficient and sustainable procurement.
- Manage supplier relationships and coordinate with key stakeholders to ensure a reliable supply, meet operational needs and reduce risks.
- Assess purchasing and procurement performance to identify optimisation opportunities, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen supply chain resilience.
- Ensure procurement and purchasing activities comply with organisational policies, standards and applicable regulations.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Procurement or related field.
- CIPS Level 3 or equivalent, an asset.

*Experience*

- Significant experience in humanitarian supply chain and procurement.
- Previous MSF field experience.
- Experience with transport, customs and import/export activities.
- Desired : Familiarity with MSF ERP systems and supply chain digital tools &/or HQ procurement or purchasing experience.

*Languages*

- English C1/2
- French C1/2
- Desired: German B1.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Sector-specific knowledge: procurement, purchasing, stock management and Transport & Customs regulations.
- Software & Tools: UniField, MSF Log Portal, Dynamics, Microsoft Office Suite
- Global knowledge: MSF's various logistics technical fields, Solid grasp of MSF’s operational environment.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Cross-Cultural Sensitivity
- Stakeholder Partnership
- Planning and Prioritisation
- Analytical Thinking
- Continuous Improvement
- Adaptability in Complex Environments
- Communicative and collaborative mindset

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: February 8th, 2027
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 87’372.- to CHF 100’608.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Field Support Officer – Cameroon (national applicants only)
jobs.description:
**Organization Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organisation (INSO) is an international non-governmental organisation that helps humanitarian NGOs operate safely and effectively in some of the world’s most challenging environments. We provide free, independent safety and security services that enable aid organizations to stay operational and continue delivering assistance to people in need.

INSO works in more than 20 of the world’s most insecure countries and is headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands.

**INSO Cameroon**

INSO Cameroon began operations in 2017 as one of the INSO offices for the Lake Chad Basin and was launched as an autonomous Mission in late 2021. Today, the program has a regional office in Bamenda and an antenna in Maroua. The national office is located in Yaounde, the capital. Armed group fragmentation, intercommunal violence, climate-related disasters and weak socio-economic infrastructure have generated significant humanitarian needs in one of the world’s most neglected crises, where access and safety risks for NGOs remain high and where INSO’s field-based data, crisis support, alerts, coordination and contextual analysis are essential to informing high-quality humanitarian programming. As part of INSO in Cameroon, you will support around 100 local and international NGOs to provide vital aid more safely and efficiently in the two crisis-affected regions of Cameroon: the North West, South West, and the Far North.

**Job Summary**

As a Field Support Officer, you will play a central role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day operations of the field office. You will be the go-to person supporting colleagues across finance, HR, logistics, administration, and procurement, helping teams operate efficiently and enabling the successful delivery of INSO’s mission. Working closely with field and country office teams, you will contribute to creating a well-organized, compliant, and supportive working environment in a dynamic operational setting.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

*Finance*

- Manage petty cash, banking transactions, cash advances, and reconciliations.
- Monitor and close outstanding advances and maintain accurate financial records.
- Support monthly financial reporting, accounting documentation, and audit compliance.
- Forecast cash requirements and coordinate timely fund transfers.
- Serve as a focal point for finance-related questions and provide support to colleagues.

*Human Resources & Administration*

- Support international and national staff with visas, residency permits, accommodation, and administrative matters.
- Maintain leave, attendance, and personnel records.
- Ensure staff are familiar with INSO policies, procedures, and required documentation.
- Coordinate with health insurance providers and support payroll-related processes.

*Logistics, Procurement & Operations*

- Coordinate procurement processes in line with INSO procedures and compliance standards.
- Identify vendors, obtain quotations, conduct bid analyses, and issue purchase orders.
- Organize logistics for trainings, workshops, meetings, and operational activities.
- Manage office assets, inventories, facilities, equipment, and vehicle records.
- Oversee office maintenance, supplier contracts, and stock levels of essential supplies.
- Support the efficient functioning of the field office through strong operational coordination.

*Other Responsibilities*

- Undertake additional duties as reasonably assigned by your supervisor in support of operational priorities.

**Requirements**

*Essential:*

- At least 2 years of relevant work experience in similar roles with NGOs
- Working proficiency in Microsoft Office
- Good English language skills, both written and verbal
- Ability to process large amounts of data
- Close attention to detail and time management skills
- A professional certificate in finance, accounting, logistics, HR or another relevant field

**Core Competencies**

- Integrity – Maintains confidentiality, acts ethically, and manages sensitive information with professionalism.
- Organization – Plans, prioritises, and coordinates multiple tasks while maintaining accuracy and efficiency.
- Collaboration – Builds positive working relationships and works effectively across multicultural teams.
- Communicative – Communicates clearly and professionally with colleagues, partners, and external stakeholders.
- Initiative– Proactively identifies needs, takes ownership, and suggests practical improvements.
- Resilient – Remains flexible and performs effectively in changing, demanding, or high-pressure environments.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to the safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers, and we will ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policy throughout the recruitment process.

**Warning Clause**

This job description is not an exhaustive list of skills, efforts, duties, and responsibilities related to the position.
