- Fluent in English, with professional proficiency in Spanish and/or Portuguese.

***Other information***

- Status: Part time – Consultancy

jobs.title: Request for Proposal Rika Phase Two UX and Engineering Services AASHA
jobs.description:
## Request for Proposal Rika Phase Two UX and Engineering Services AASHA

**Kenya**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Rika Phase Two UX and Engineering Services

Procurement Method Open competitive bid

Supplier Type Digital product, UX and software-engineering agency or consortium

Primary Market Kenya

Platforms Rika web platform, chatbot and programme data dashboard

Contract Period December

Proposal Deadline 20th November 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

## **Who We Are**

[Girl Effect](https://girleffect.org/) is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust, and need. From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content helps adolescent girls in Africa and Asia make life choices and changes.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, and relationships, empowering girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible “for a girl.”

Our reach is 50 million and counting. And we’re using technology to reach girls at scale so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning, and her livelihood.

Because when a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

In Kenya, Girl Effect’s programs, like WAZZII Chatbot, WAZZII Dadas, and Tukisonga, have reached over 62 million youth worldwide, connecting them to vital health, education, and livelihood opportunities.

## **Background**

AASHA, the Age-Appropriate Sexual Health Approach, is a government-led initiative co-designed with adolescents and young people. It aims to provide age-specific sexual and reproductive health information for audiences aged 10–14, 15–17 and 18–24 through government-led digital platforms and complementary communication channels.

Girl Effect is supporting Kenya’s Ministry of Health to strengthen Rika, a government-led digital platform for age-appropriate information.

Phase One delivered a web-based minimum viable product with an embedded chatbot. Phase Two will use research and testing with users in Kwale, Narok and Migori to:

- Improve the user journey;
- Design and build priority features;
- Strengthen data and approved AI capabilities;
- Improve platform accessibility, security and performance; and
- Deploy a secure and maintainable MVP2.

## **Objective**

Girl Effect seeks a qualified digital product, UX, and software engineering agency or consortium to research, design, build, test, deploy, and hand over Rika Phase Two.

The supplier will work with the Ministry of Health, Girl Effect, and young people to deliver an accessible, mobile-first, and secure web platform, chatbot, and data dashboard that can be sustainably owned and operated by the Ministry of Health.

**Government -Led Digital Platform**

The Government of Kenya has developed guidelines on messaging adolescents but does not have a single platform that provides youth in Kenya with age-appropriate sexual health information tailored to meet the unique demands of AGYW and ABYM. Through the AASHA program, Girl Effect will support the Ministry of Health in creating a centralized repository of all age-appropriate SRH information.

**The Rika - AYP platform**

To deliver the digital platform, Girl Effect has identified the Rika - AYP digital platform, launched as MVP 1 by the Ministry of Health, as a potential foundational platform that could be improved with additional features developed to achieve our goals (See the link to the live site [here](https://rika.go.ke/)).

The Rika -AYP platform has been co-designed by the Ministry of Health RMCAH department and the digital health department, in partnership with a cohort of youth identified by the Ministry of Health working under the Entity Lomogan Solutions.

Girl Effect is providing technical advice to the Ministry of Health and the young developers, borrowing from Girl Effect’s tech development process to improve the Rika -AYP platform.

This is being done in two phases:

**Rika Phase One:** The goal of the first phase was to build on the ongoing government-led platform development process and deliver a simple web-based MVP prototype with an embedded chat function.

Working in collaboration with MOH and tech youth creators supported by MOH, we have designed and launched Rika ([https://rika.go.ke/explore](https://rika.go.ke/explore) ), a web version of the digital platform with a chatbot embedded.

**Rika Phase Two:**

With the first version of Rika developed, we want to offer MOH technical support to:

- Conduct additional comprehensive needs analysis among TA to test usability of the Rika website and chatbot and identify additional needs for features and channels
- Refine the consumer journey while factoring in insights from the needs assessment exercise
- Design additional features on Rika
- Build additional features on Rika
- Test additional features on Rika
- Deploy an updated version of Rika - MVP2

## **What You will do**

Girl Effect seeks to engage the services of an agency to design and develop the second phase of the Rika platform (Web and chatbot). The scope of work will include UX design and engineering support.

Working alongside the Ministry of Health, Digital Health team, Girl Effect tech UX design and HCD experts, you will conduct a comprehensive needs assessment exercise across Migori, Narok and Kwale counties to identify additional features for MVP 2. You will design a comprehensive updated consumer journey, develop a comprehensive requirements document, design wireframes for new features, build and test all additional MVP 2 (web and chatbot)features to meet the needs of our target audience, and work alongside the GE data team.

Needs assessment:

- You will define the approach for conducting an additional needs assessment for Rika Tech, working alongside the MOH, the GE HCD and UX teams.
- You will develop tools to conduct a needs assessment to ensure relevant insights to advise on tech considerations are obtained from the exercise.
- You will co-facilitate the needs assessment session in Kwale, Narok, and Migori counties alongside MOH, UX designer, GE, and HCD consultant with a focus on generating tech-related insights
- You will conduct user testing of the MVP1 during needs assessment workshops to obtain feedback
- You will work alongside the GE UX design team and MOH team to package tech-related insights from the needs assessment into a Rika version two requirements document for the Rika website and Chatbot.
- You will work alongside the GE UX design team to support the design of updated consumer journeys and wireframes to be handed over to the engineering team for build
- You will lead the development of additional features for the Rika Web and Chatbot while working alongside the Girl Effect engineering team. This will include creation of chatbot and website copy and any AI-related features
- After the build of Rika version two, you will conduct user acceptance testing and usability testing of all new features
- You will also develop a data dashboard

NB: This scope of work covers design for the Rika web platform and the Rika chatbot.

**Activity Output**

Support planning for needs assessment exercise UX research tools

Participate in needs assessment workshops

and facilitate MVP1 user testing Document and synthesize MVP1 insights

Consolidate tech-related outputs from workshops UX research report and recommendations

Design wireframes for additional features Updated user journey and Wireframes

Develop additional features Additional features built, tested, and deployed on Rika web and chatbot, including AI and Data features.

Support UAT Document Tools and Insights document

Deployed all MVP 2 tech updates Updated version of Rika fully deployed

Weekly check-in meetings (1 -2 hours per week) throughout the duration of implementation

Budget Consumption: All work performed, including time reserved for recurring meetings, will be tracked against the agreed budget. Duration and Working Arrangements

The supplier will report to the designated Girl Effect Programme Manager and work closely with relevant Girl Effect, Ministry of Health and Rika representatives.

## **Who You Are**

Bidders should demonstrate:

- At least five years of relevant experience delivering user-centred web platforms, chatbots and data products.
- Experience in health, youth or public-sector digital products.
- Demonstrated capability in:
- Product discovery;
- UX research and design;
- Accessible and mobile-first design;
- Software architecture;
- Front-end and back-end engineering;
- Chatbot or conversational design;
- Data analytics and dashboards;
- Secure engineering;
- Quality assurance;
- DevOps and deployment; and
- Technical documentation and handover.
- Experience working with government stakeholders and multi-partner approval structures in Kenya, which is highly desirable.
- A strong relevant portfolio.
- At least three recent client references.
- Evidence of successfully taking over, assessing, and improving an existing codebase.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening
- Technical evaluation
- Financial evaluation.

Evaluation Criterion

- Understanding of the assignment and proposed product approach:15%
- UX research, design and accessibility methodology: 10%
- Engineering architecture, security, data and quality-assurance approach: 20%
- Relevant experience, portfolio and government or health-sector delivery: 10%
- Team capability, workplan, handover and support model: 15%
- Financial proposal and value for money: 20%

Girl Effect may request:

- Written clarifications;
- Technical presentations;
- Product demonstrations;
- Interviews;
- Reference checks;
- Code, architecture or security evidence;
- Due diligence information; or
- Best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **Proposal Submission**

Invited agencies must submit separate technical and financial proposals.

The technical proposal should not exceed 10 pages, including CVs, references, company documents, and supporting evidence.

**Technical Proposal**

The technical proposal should include:

- Understanding of Rika, AASHA, the target users, and the Phase Two objectives.
- Identification of key delivery risks, assumptions and dependencies.
- Proposed discovery and research methodology.
- UX design and accessibility approach.
- Software-engineering and architecture approach.
- Data and analytics approach.
- Chatbot and approved AI-safety approach.
- Quality-assurance and testing methodology.
- Security, privacy and safeguarding approach.
- Deployment, monitoring and rollback methodology.
- Documentation, handover and training approach.
- Proposed warranty and support model.
- Proposed approach to assessing and working with the existing technology stack.
- Measures for minimising vendor lock-in.
- Detailed workplan showing phases, milestones, dependencies, review points and delivery dates.
- Proposed team, roles, availability and CVs
- Three comparable case studies.
- Relevant work samples.
- Three recent client references.
- All proposed third-party tools, licences, hosting services and recurring costs.
- Assumptions, exclusions and client responsibilities.

**Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal should include:

- Detailed pricing in **Kenyan shillings.**
- Costs broken down by phase and deliverable.
- Proposed roles, rates and estimated level of effort.
- Applicable taxes shown separately.
- Reimbursable expenses shown separately.
- A rate card for approved additional work.
- Confirmation that the proposal will remain valid for 90 days.
- All pricing assumptions and exclusions.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 6th November, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 20th November 2026

**General and Commercial Terms**

- Contracting and Payment: The successful supplier will sign Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones and receipt of a correct invoice.
- Pricing and Scope: Prices must be quoted in Kenyan shillings and include all costs except clearly identified exclusions. No change to the approved scope, asset quantity, format, language, schedule or budget may proceed without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. Supplier errors and the agreed review rounds will not be treated as chargeable changes.
- Taxes and Expenses: Applicable taxes, licences, talent fees and reimbursable costs must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by law. Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable.
- Intellectual Property and Rights: Subject to the final agreement, Girl Effect will own the approved outputs and commissioned project materials paid for under the engagement. The supplier must secure and document all talent, music, stock, location and third-party rights required for government, campaign, web, social-media and digital use.
- Confidentiality and Data Protection: The supplier must protect all confidential, personal and sensitive information accessed or created during the assignment.
- Safeguarding and Conduct: The supplier and all personnel, contributors and subcontractors must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical, anti-fraud, data-protection, information-security and supplier-conduct requirements.
- Conflicts of Interest: Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- Equal Opportunity: Girl Effect welcomes proposals from qualified organisations and consortiums with diverse professional, cultural and geographic backgrounds.
- Right to Award: Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for costs incurred in preparing a proposal.
- Proposal Validity: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Diaspora as Anticipatory Actors in Conflict-Induced Displacement Consultancy
jobs.description:
Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

## Purpose of the consultancy

Under the project Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD), the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and DEMAC are commissioning a consultancy to consolidate lessons and findings on the role of diaspora in anticipatory action under the project. The consultancy focuses on two levels:

**(1) Context monitoring, community sensing and early warning:** examining whether diaspora and local partner specific signals, including remittance patterns and community sensing indicators, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement; and,

**(2) Response and activation:** the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, including how they mobilise resources quickly and exploring other innovative modalities for channelling support.

## Background

AHEAD — Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement — is a global project led by the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) that aims to strengthen humanitarian responses by improving the ability to act before displacement occurs. Implemented in eight countries (Yemen, Myanmar, Somalia, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Uganda, South Sudan), it combines in-country implementation with cross-context learning to build an evidence base for anticipatory action (AA) in conflict settings — an area far less developed than AA for climatic shocks. A key component of the project is to strengthen the inclusion of diaspora and local actors in designing AA frameworks and supporting their engagement in preparedness, early warning dissemination, and rolling out AA responses.

Diaspora, often outside formal humanitarian structures, play an essential role in conflict-prone contexts. Sitting at the intersection of a layered, real-time information ecosystem, they occupy a unique position of trust and access that formal systems cannot replicate, receiving real-time community intelligence — often within hours — and disseminating warnings through channels, communities actually listen to in areas hard to reach. The same trusted channels that receive community intelligence also serve as the fastest available mechanism for mobilising and transferring resources. Across crises, they share unique capacities to mobilise and transfer resources swiftly, rapidly and innovatively, serving as often overlooked yet critical lifelines that are sustained beyond the lifespan of a crisis. This dual function of sensing and acting is what makes diaspora actors uniquely positioned in the AA ecosystem, and what distinguishes them from other formal early warning actors.

Yet while diaspora actors are increasingly recognised as informal humanitarian actors and vital responders in the aftermath of crisis, their capacity to mobilise existing knowledge, networks and resources in the critical window *before* displacement peaks remains largely under-conceptualised and under-examined. This gap extends across both dimensions of diaspora engagement: the signals they detect and the modalities through which they mobilise support. Remittances are illustrative. As a signal, shifts in remittance behaviour may point to deteriorating conditions in real time — when communities begin planning their displacement journey — yet their reliability and specificity as an early warning indicator remain untested. And while Somali remittances exceed USD 2 billion annually, outpacing official development assistance and humanitarian aid combined, these flows are inherently kinship-based and solidarity-driven, mediated by relations of trust and reciprocity, and mobilised almost exclusively in reaction to crises that have already hit. Accordingly, this raises broader questions about whether their support can be relied upon proactively, and/or sustained across recurrent shocks without exhausting the networks they depend on. Across both the predictive and the financing dimensions, it remains unexamined whether diaspora signals and resources — remittances among them — can be oriented towards anticipatory ends. This is the conceptual and empirical gap the consultancy sets out to explore and address.

This consultancy is anchored in the AHEAD Somalia context - a context that combines recurrent, overlapping conflict- and climate-driven displacement with an exceptionally strong, densely connected diaspora. As AHEAD is implemented in Somalia, DRC and its partners generate evidence on two questions: whether the signals diaspora detect are reliable enough to act on, and how their engagement affects outcomes once a response is triggered. The consultancy's role is to consolidate this evidence and package it into a structured account of diaspora as anticipatory actors. In doing so, the consultancy seeks to position diaspora as a missing piece in AA systems, with the Somalia experience presenting an emerging, largely unexplored frontier whose lessons could strengthen how anticipatory action is designed, funded and activated across other contexts.

Because this work concerns anticipation, its object is inherently uncertain — whether a predicted crisis will take place, and when or how often partners activate, cannot be known in advance; the consultancy is therefore designed to follow the implementation as it unfolds and adapt to what it surfaces, rather than evaluate predetermined events.

## Objective of the consultancy

The consultant will consolidate and package the evidence generated under the project by DRC across four learning areas. The guiding questions under each set out what the consolidated learning should answer.

Across these areas, the consultant will be required to:

1. **Context monitoring, community sensing and early warning:** Examine and consolidate findings on whether signals reported by diaspora and local partners, namely shifts in remittance patterns and community sensing data gathered under the AHEAD project, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

Sub-questions:

1. *Can changes in remittance patterns — spikes or drops in transfer volumes, frequency, and requests — serve as a reliable early warning indicator for conflict-induced displacement, and/or as an earlier precursor of crisis?*
1. *Can social signals related to community sensing, including social media monitoring and social pattern detection serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement, and/or as earlier precursors of crisis?*
2. **Activation – Response:** Examine and consolidate lessons on the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, and how their engagement affects outcomes (assessed against indicators such as access, speed and trust). This includes capturing lessons from innovative modalities for support emerging from AHEAD’s implementation in Somalia. Among these, DRC is currently exploring trigger-based payments that connect early warning triggers to diaspora transfers ahead of a predicted crisis; should this be taken forward, it would form part of this learning.

Sub-questions:

1. *How does diaspora engagement in AA implementation affect outcomes for affected communities — e.g. reach to hard-to-reach groups, trust, acceptance, complementarity with the formal response, and associated risks?*
2. *How do the speed and modality of diaspora financial support affect AA outcomes?*
3. *What innovative modalities for channelling diaspora support emerge through AHEAD's implementation in Somalia, such as trigger-based payments, and what conditions, infrastructure and partnerships are needed for them to work as anticipatory funding ahead of a predicted crisis?*
4. **Linking Informal to Formal EW/AA Structures:** Examine and consolidate lessons on the conditions, benefits and risks of connecting diaspora and community-based early warning (EW) structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism across both the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle.

Sub-questions:

1. *What conditions proved necessary for diaspora and community-based EW structures to connect effectively to the AHEAD AA response mechanism across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle?*
1. *What benefits and risks did this surface for the actors involved — including effects on community ownership, diaspora–local partner trust, and responsiveness to warnings?*
2. **Cross-Cutting - Learning & Advocacy**: Package the consolidated learning into case studies for external publication and a synthesis report to inform AHEAD and broader diaspora programming, drawing out implications for scaling to other contexts.

## Scope of work and Methodology

The consultant will prepare a **methodology and work plan** setting out how the evidence generated in-house will be consolidated and packaged against the objectives above, and the support required from DRC and DEMAC.

**Division of roles:** All primary data collection, triangulation and assessment is carried out in-house. DRC's AHEAD team and partners collect early warning and monitoring data, including bi-weekly reporting from diaspora–local partner pairs; DRC's MEAL and data teams triangulate and assess this data, together with activation and outcome data. The consultant complements this with targeted qualitative fieldwork on remittance flows and community sensing (objective 1) and on the diaspora contribution in activation (objective 2), and consolidates the evidence and findings generated in-house and package them into the outputs set out below. Accordingly, the consultancy will work in a very coordinated manner with the data and MEAL team to avoid potential duplications.

**Indicative scope:** the evidence covers diaspora–local partner pairs across four or five locations in Gedo (Luuq and Beled Xawo) and Hiraan (BeledWeyne, Jalalaqsi, and Buulo Burte (TBC)), including bi-weekly monitoring data from all (up to five) and activation in up to three locations (AHEAD target locations; eg. Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi). The number and timing of activations cannot be known in advance.

The learning notes produced under **areas 1–3 serve as interim outputs**, feeding into the final synthesis report and policy brief.

All deliverables are to be submitted in English. Fieldwork will be conducted in Somali

The main tasks related to achieving the above-mentioned objectives are described in detail below:

**Scope**

**Deliverables**

**Suggested Activities**

**Community context monitoring (objective 1)** Examine and consolidate findings on whether signals reported by diaspora and local partners, namely shifts in remittance patterns and community sensing data gathered under the AHEAD project, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

1 learning note on whether diaspora and community sensing signals are reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

Consolidate DRC in-house context monitoring data (which will cross-compare and triangulate indicators received from diaspora and local partners with DRC community context monitoring) an carry out complementary qualitative fieldwork examining how remittance flows (including mobile money transfers) and community sensing signals shift ahead of displacement.

n each of the four to five target locations, this includes around 5 (five) key informant interviews (with mobile money agents or remittance providers, local partners, community leaders and local authorities) and 1 (one) focus group discussion with recipient households. In addition, around 8 (eight) remote interviews with diaspora senders.

Findings feed into the assessment of reliability, timeliness, accuracy, bias and conflict sensitivity.

**Activation – Response (objective 2)** Examine and consolidate lessons on the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, and how their engagement affects outcomes (assessed against indicators such as access, speed and trust). This includes capturing lessons from innovative modalities for support emerging from AHEAD’s implementation in Somalia.

1 learning report on the diaspora contribution in activation, including resource mobilisation and innovative modalities (which could include trigger-based payments)

Complement in-house activation and outcome data with qualitative fieldwork to assess the quality, relevance and acceptance of diaspora and local partner assistance across partial and full activation, including the speed and modalities of resource mobilisation. In each location where activation takes place (up to three), this includes around five key informant interviews (with local partners, community leaders, local authorities and other responders) and two to three focus group discussions with affected communities.

Capture lessons from innovative modalities for support, including trigger-based payments if taken forward.

Quantitative impact data on needs mitigation following AA assistance will be provided by in-house MEAL Specialist. Measurable outcome analysis is provided in-house by MEAL Specialist.

**Linking Informal to Formal EW/AA Structures (objective 3):** Through after-action review, assess the conditions, benefits and risks of connecting diaspora and community-based early warning (EW) structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism, across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle.

1 assessment of connecting informal diaspora and community EW structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism.

Consolidate lessons and support AHEAD team in conducting after-action review, examining the connection at each stage of the cycle — monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation — drawing on the evidence from areas 1 and 2.

**Cross-Cutting – Learning & Advocacy (objective 4):** Generate case studies for external publication and a synthesis report to inform AHEAD and broader diaspora programming, and assess implications for scaling to other contexts.

3 Case studies for external publication; a final synthesis report and policy brief.

Document case studies from AHEAD's implementation in Somalia; produce interim learning notes; present findings at AHEAD convenings; deliver the final synthesis report and policy brief with recommendations on diaspora inclusion in AA and implications for scaling.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will submit the following deliverables as mentioned below:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description of tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Phase 1 — Inception & baseline**

1 Inception report with approved methodology and work plan

Kick-off meeting; agree methodology and work plan with DRC

5 working days (4 lead / 1 field team) over period Q4 2026

**Phase 2 — Context monitoring**

1 Learning note on the reliability of diaspora and community-sensing signals as early warning

Consolidate in-house monitoring data and analysis; carry out fieldwork across the four to five target locations (ie. Luuq and Beled Xawo (Gedo), and BeledWeyne, Jalalaqsi and Buulo Burte TBC) (Hiraan) (key informant interviews and focus group discussions) and remote interviews with diaspora senders.

35 working days (15 lead / 20 field team). over period Q1-Q2 2027

**Phase 3 — Activation & response**

1 Learning report on the diaspora contribution in activation, including resource mobilisation and the feasibility of trigger-based payments

Consolidate in-house activation and outcome data; Qualitatively examine diaspora engagement across partial and full activation (up to three locations); capture lessons from innovative modalities for support, including trigger-based payments if taken forward.

40 working days (18 lead / 22 field team) over period Q1–Q3 2027, following activation as it occurs

**Phase 4 — Linking informal to formal**

1 After-action review assessment of connecting diaspora and community EW structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism

After-action review across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle, drawing on the evidence from Phases 2 and 3

10 working days (8 lead / 2 field team) over period of Q2–Q3 2027

**Phase 5 — Cross-cutting & synthesis**

3 case studies for external publication; 1 final synthesis report and 1 policy brief

Produce case studies to present findings at AHEAD convenings; deliver the final synthesis report and 1 policy brief with recommendations and implications for scaling across contexts.

20 total working days (18 field team / 2 local).(Case studies run alongside Phases 2–4 (Q1–Q3 2027); final report and policy brief by 1st September 2027.

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The assignment involves up **to 110 working days** spread over a contract period of up to 10 months, from December 2026 to 30 September 2027. **Payment is linked to approved deliverables, not to days worked.**

- **Instalment 1:** Inception report, data collection tools and fieldwork plan (Phase 1) – 30%
- **Instalment 2:** Learning note on context monitoring and early warning & Activations (Phase 2 & 3) – 20%
- **Instalment 3:** Learning note on linking informal to formal structures & Case studies, final synthesis report and policy brief (Phase 4 & 5) – 50%

The consultant shall be prepared to complete the assignment no later than **30 September 2027.**

The level of effort is **expected to vary throughout the assignment**. Periods of higher intensity are anticipated during the inception phase, including the development of the methodology and workplan, and during the final synthesis and evaluation phase, including analysis, reporting, and dissemination of findings. Additional periods of increased effort may arise in connection with activation events and response monitoring; however, the timing and frequency of such activations cannot be determined in advance and will depend on contextual developments.

Should fewer activations occur than anticipated, days allocated to Phase 3 may be reallocated to other deliverables, as agreed with DRC.

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

**Eligibility**

- The bidder is a research or consultancy firm registered as a legal entity in its country of incorporation; individual consultants are not eligible.
- The firm proposes a named team leader and a field research team meeting the profiles below.

**Experience**

**Firm:**

- At least 2 years since registration
- Proven track record delivering qualitative research or evaluations, ideally in humanitarian or conflict settings
- At least three research, evaluation or review assignments for international organisations, research institutes or development agencies, preferably in the Horn of Africa[\[SO6\]](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_6)
- Record of producing publishable outputs (reports, policy briefs, case studies)
- Ability to access and work safely in the target locations in Gedo and Hiraan

Desirable: established presence or research network in Somalia; familiarity with anticipatory action and community-based early warning

**Proposed Composition of Team**

**Team leader**

- Master's degree or PhD in social sciences, development studies, peace and conflict studies or a related field; a PhD is an asset
- At least 5 years' post-graduate research experience in humanitarian, displacement or conflict settings in the Horn of Africa
- Demonstrated research on the Somali diaspora, diaspora humanitarianism or remittances, evidenced by at least two publications or research projects
- Strong research design, qualitative analysis and after-action review skills
- Demonstrated ability to synthesise and package findings into high-quality, publishable outputs (reports, briefs, case studies)
- Experience overseeing qualitative fieldwork (FGDs, KIIs) in Somalia, including in hard-to-reach areas, and coordinating in-country researchers
- Established access to, and trust with, relevant diaspora and local actors (desirable)
- Excellent written and spoken English required, fluency in Somali is an asset.

**Field research team:**

- At least 3 years of field-research experience in Somalia; research experience in Gedo or Hiraan is an asset
- Somali-speaking field researchers able to conduct key informant interviews and focus group discussions in target locations
- Deep knowledge of Somalia and its context — clan and community structures, conflict and displacement dynamics
- Established access to, and trust with relevant local actors and communities in the target areas

## Technical supervision

### The selected consultant will work under the supervision of: ***DRC Diaspora AA lead***

*In close coordination with the DRC AHEAD team, including DRC AA Lead/PM at country office and regional level (EAGL) and DRC data team.*

## Location and support

Remote or based in East Africa.

The Firm will provide her/his own computer and mobile telephone.

## Travel

The assignment is expected to be mainly remote for the team leader. The financial bid should include all travel and fieldwork costs( travel, accommodation, meals etc), based on a minimum of:

- One field round in each of the four confirmed target locations during Phase 2 (Luuq, Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi), plus Buulo Burte if confirmed
- One field round in each location where activation takes place during Phase 3 (up to three, expected to be Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi)

jobs.title: Manager Safeguarding & Enquêtes
jobs.description:
**Rattachement hiérarchique :** Directeur·rice Pays

**Conditions :** *Contrat à durée déterminée de 6 mois, renouvelable sous réserve de la disponibilité de financements futurs*

**Grade :** GB5 (42 136 € – 46 818 €)

**Exigences du poste :** *Le poste est basé à Goma, avec plusieurs missions à l’intérieur du pays*

[GB4-6 Unaccompanied International Staff T&Cs](https://concern.icims.com/icims2/servlet/icims2?module=AppInert&action=download&id=299&hashed=-877963960)

**Responsibilities**

*Gestion des enquêtes sur les fautes de conduite*

- Mener des enquêtes en matière de Safeguarding et de fraude conformément au manuel d’enquête de Concern, sous la supervision technique du/de la Responsable des enquêtes au siège
- Être responsable de la mise en œuvre de l’évaluation des risques et du plan de Safeguarding tout au long des enquêtes, et assurer la liaison avec l’équipe Safeguarding du siège, si nécessaire, afin de garantir un soutien solide aux survivants et l’application des principes de Safeguarding
- Rédiger des rapports d’enquête
- Tenir un registre précis des détails et des conclusions de chaque enquête, en veillant au respect des normes de confidentialité et de protection des données
- Veiller à ce que la cartographie des services pour chaque base et zone d’intervention soit complète et à jour
- Orienter les participants, victimes et survivants concernés par les enquêtes et les incidents de faute de conduite vers les services appropriés
- Former et encadrer d’autres enquêteur·rice·s en matière de fautes de conduite
- Préparer les notifications aux bailleurs, sous la supervision de l’équipe Enquêtes internes et Audit du siège, en veillant au respect des étapes d’approbation prévues.

*Prévention : sensibilisation et formation du personnel, des partenaires et des fournisseurs*

- Dispenser des formations techniques aux partenaires et fournisseurs de Concern, ainsi que des formations plus approfondies sur le Safeguarding et la fraude au personnel de Concern, le cas échéant
- Appuyer les points focaux Safeguarding (DSFP) dans l’élaboration et la coordination des supports d’IEC, de sensibilisation et de formation
- Élaborer, en collaboration avec les DSFP, un calendrier de formation en Safeguarding pour le personnel, les partenaires et les fournisseurs
- Travailler avec l’équipe du Mécanisme de feedback, plaintes et réponses (FCRM) à l’élaboration et à la coordination des supports d’IEC, de sensibilisation et de formation
- Former les responsables hiérarchiques, les points focaux RH et les points focaux des organisations partenaires à la réception et au traitement des signalements liés au Safeguarding, y compris les approches centrées sur les survivants, la confidentialité, les exigences de documentation, les circuits de référencement et les obligations de signalement
- Animer des formations et fournir un appui technique continu sur la conduite d’enquêtes relatives aux fautes de conduite
- Organiser des formations de sensibilisation au Safeguarding et à la fraude
- Assurer le suivi des mesures correctives et des recommandations issues des cas de Safeguarding et veiller à leur mise en œuvre

*Amélioration de la qualité / suivi des recommandations*

- Assurer le suivi des recommandations issues des enquêtes sur les fautes de conduite et des évaluations des risques, en tenant à jour une liste des actions convenues et de leurs responsables
- Accompagner les points focaux Safeguarding dans l’élaboration et la mise à jour de leurs plans d’action nationaux
- En étroite collaboration avec le/la Directeur Pays, le/la Directeur des Systèmes, le/la Directeur des Programmes, le/la PDQC et le/la Conseiller Enquêtes et Conduite, veiller à ce que les procédures et les politiques soient adaptées pour intégrer la prévention des problèmes de Safeguarding (processus d’apprentissage)
- Représenter Concern dans les forums et groupes de travail pertinents, et participer au groupe de travail PSEA et aux autres instances de coordination associées
- Veiller à ce que les valeurs et les engagements politiques de l’organisation, notamment en matière de redevabilité et d’égalité, se reflètent dans les responsabilités confiées.
- Veiller à ce que tous les dossiers soient protégés, gardés confidentiels et traités conformément à l’ensemble des politiques et procédures applicables
- Participer activement à toute réponse d’urgence, si nécessaire.

**Role Holder Requirements**

*Critères essentiels*

- Maîtrise courante du français
- Licence dans un domaine pertinent (travail social, sociologie, droit, etc.)
- Expérience dans la conduite d’enquêtes sur des fautes de conduite, qu’elles soient sexuelles ou financières (fraude)
- 3 ans d’expérience après l’obtention du diplôme dans un environnement dynamique, avec une exposition aux questions de protection et/ou de fraude
- Expérience dans l’organisation de programmes de formation en RDC
- Excellentes capacités de rédaction de rapports
- Capacité à traiter des informations hautement sensibles et confidentielles
- Capacité à apporter un soutien psychosocial et/ou des premiers secours psychologiques
- Capacité avérée à rédiger des rapports concis, logiques et analytiques pour transmettre des messages complexes
- Capacité à travailler en équipe
- Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques et de la suite Office

*Critères souhaités*

- Expérience des enquêtes sur la fraude et la corruption
- Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire dans l’Est de la RDC
- Expérience préalable au sein d’organisations non gouvernementales
- Expérience dans des projets de protection, de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre et/ou de soutien psychosocial
- Maîtrise courante de l’anglais
- Maîtrise courante du swahili

*Compétences requises*

- Gestion de soi
- Leadership individuel
- Communication et travail d’équipe
- Atteinte des résultats
- Planification et prise de décision
- Créativité et innovation
- Influence, plaidoyer et réseautage

jobs.title: Request for Proposal RikaWeb Content Development AASHA
jobs.description:
## Request for Proposal RikaWeb Content Development AASHA

**Kenya**

### **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title RikaWeb Content Development

Supplier Type Content production agency or qualified consortium

Primary Market Kenya, with cultural relevance to Kwale, Narok and Migori

Target Audiences Adolescents and young people aged 10–14, 15–17 and 18–24

Indicative Outputs 54 videos and five illustrated web articles

Contract Period December

Proposal Deadline 20th November 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

### **Who We Are**

[Girl Effect](https://girleffect.org/) is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust, and need. From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content helps adolescent girls in Africa and Asia make life choices and changes.

We create safe spaces for girls to share facts and ask questions about health, nutrition, education, and relationships, empowering them with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible “for a girl.”

Our reach is 50 million and counting. And we’re using technology to reach girls at scale so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning, and her livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do the same. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

### **Background**

AASHA, the Age-Appropriate Sexual Health Approach, is a government-led initiative co-designed with adolescents and young people. It aims to provide age-specific sexual and reproductive health information for audiences aged 10–14, 15–17 and 18–24 through government-led digital platforms and complementary communication channels.

Girl Effect is supporting Kenya’s Ministry of Health, through the Directorate of Family Health and the Division of Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health, to strengthen and roll out AASHA.

Rika has been identified as a government-led digital platform that can be scaled as a trusted source of age-appropriate information. The initial web platform is live, and a substantial package of youth-friendly content is now required.

### **Objective**

Girl Effect seeks an experienced content production agency to co-create, develop and deliver accurate, engaging, age-appropriate and platform-ready video and article content for RikaWeb.

The supplier will work with Girl Effect, the Ministry of Health, technical experts and young creators to translate approved briefs into content that is safe, culturally relevant and suitable for national digital use.

### **Content Package**

Audience Video Outputs Illustrated Articles

Ages 10–14 Four videos covering bodily changes for boys,

bodily changes for girls, menstruation,

and abstinence as a healthy and valid choice Two articles covering abstinence, curiosity, and peer pressure; and understanding menstrual health

Ages 15–17 Eight videos covering GBV awareness, abstinence,

mental health, and five videos on teenage pregnancy

and related SRH issues Three articles covering GBV; abstinence and self-control; and abstinence and personal goals

Ages 18–24 Forty-two videos covering SGBV awareness,

mental health, 15 contraception videos,

15 maternal-health videos, and 10 HIV and STI videos None currently specified

The indicative total is 54 videos and five illustrated articles.

Bidders must validate the quantities against the supplied creative briefs and identify any discrepancy before submitting their financial proposal. Final quantities and briefs will be confirmed during inception. No asset may enter production without written brief approval.

### **What You will do**

#### **Inception and Content Planning**

The supplier will:

- Review the AASHA strategy, Ministry of Health messaging guidance, approved topic matrix, Rika platform requirements and supplied creative briefs.
- Validate the asset register, intended audience, objective, key message, format, duration, language and approval route for every asset.
- Submit a detailed production plan covering co-creation, scripting, filming, article development, review rounds, testing, post-production and final handover.
- Maintain a live asset tracker showing status, dependencies, feedback, approvals, risks and delivery dates.

#### **Co-Creation and Creative Development**

The supplier will:

- Plan and facilitate safe co-creation sessions with adolescents and young people, including participants from the relevant counties and age groups.
- Refine each creative brief using audience insights while preserving approved health information and policy requirements.
- Develop the creative concepts, treatments, scripts, storyboards or shot lists, article outlines and illustration direction.
- Submit all concepts, scripts and outlines for approval before production begins.
- Use age-appropriate, non-judgemental and inclusive language.
- Avoid stigma, fear-based messaging, harmful stereotypes and unsupported health claims.

#### **Video Production**

The supplier will:

- Manage all pre-production activities, including casting, locations, permits, contributor agreements, scheduling, equipment, crew and production logistics.
- Produce each approved three-to-five-minute video in a format appropriate to the target audience and creative brief.
- Use presenter-led, documentary, animation, live action, drama or mixed formats where approved.
- Provide professional editing, colour correction, sound mixing, music, graphics, animation and quality control.
- Deliver captioned and non-captioned masters, thumbnails and transcripts.
- Deliver agreed social cut-downs or platform adaptations where included in the approved asset register.
- Provide final upload-ready files and editable project and source files in the agreed technical formats.

#### **Article and Illustration Development**

The supplier will:

- Research and draft web articles based on approved briefs and verified Ministry of Health sources.
- Develop original, age-appropriate illustrations and imagery.
- Include captions, alternative text and source information where relevant.
- Structure articles for mobile-first reading using clear headings, short sections, practical actions and appropriate referral or help-seeking information.
- Deliver final copy, editable source files and web-ready images in the agreed formats and dimensions.

#### **Technical Review, Audience Testing and Approval**

The supplier will:

- Coordinate technical review with Girl Effect, the Ministry of Health and designated subject-matter experts.
- Conduct proportionate audience testing with the relevant age group.
- Document findings on comprehension, relevance, safety, accessibility and usability.
- Maintain a feedback and version-control log.
- Incorporate consolidated feedback within agreed turnaround times.
- Allow for at least two consolidated review rounds at the concept or script stage and two consolidated review rounds at the rough-cut or draft stage.
- Correct supplier errors at no additional cost.
- Obtain written Girl Effect and Ministry of Health approval before finalisation and publication.

Any additional changes outside the approved brief or agreed review rounds will require a written change request and approval before implementation.

### **Technical and Quality Requirements**

- Final technical specifications, including resolution, aspect ratio, file size, codecs, image dimensions and content-management requirements, will be agreed during inception and recorded in the asset register.
- All content must be mobile-first, accessible, factually accurate, age-appropriate and compatible with the Rika platform.
- English and Kiswahili requirements, and any local-language versions, must be confirmed for each asset.
- Translations must be completed or reviewed by qualified language specialists and checked for meaning rather than translated literally.
- Captions, transcripts, readable on-screen text, alternative text and suitable visual contrast must be included where applicable.
- All facts, claims and referral information must be traceable to approved sources and current Ministry of Health guidance.
- Videos must have clear sound, balanced levels, legible graphics and consistent visual and technical quality.
- Articles must be clear, concise, youth-friendly and suitable for mobile reading.
- The supplier must conduct technical, editorial, language, safeguarding and factual quality checks before every submission.

### **Deliverables**

- Inception package, including validated asset register, methodology, workplan, team, risk register, approval matrix and production schedule
- Co-creation plan, tools and consent process
- Co-creation findings report
- Creative treatments, scripts, storyboards and article outlines
- Video rough cuts and draft articles and illustrations
- Audience-testing report and response-to-feedback tracker
- Final approved videos and illustrated articles
- Handover archive

A deliverable will be accepted only after written approval by Girl Effect and completion of the required Ministry of Health review.

The supplier must correct factual, technical, safeguarding, formatting or production errors attributable to its work at no additional cost.

### **Duration and Working Arrangements**

The supplier will report to the designated Girl Effect Programme Manager and work closely with relevant Girl Effect, Ministry of Health and Rika representatives.

Girl Effect will:

- Provide the available creative briefs, programme guidance and approved reference materials.
- Coordinate consolidated organisational feedback through the designated focal person.
- Support access to relevant Ministry of Health reviewers and technical experts.
- Approve deliverables or provide consolidated feedback within agreed review periods.

The supplier will:

- Manage its personnel, subcontractors, production resources and schedule.
- Maintain the production and approval tracker.
- Flag delays, dependencies, safeguarding concerns and decisions promptly.
- Avoid proceeding with unapproved content, costs or changes.

### **Who You Are**

Skills and expertise:

- Project Management: Ability to effectively manage projects, coordinate diverse teams, develop strategies, and ensure successful execution within timelines.
- Depth in production capacity: Demonstrate clear capacity in developing creative, compelling content targeting young people in Kenya. With qualified team members to support all components of production. (Portfolio and CVs to be attached)
- Demonstrated experience in developing social behavioural change content briefs and campaign strategies and managing the ideation and approval process with the Ministry of Health in Kenya.
- Local Market Knowledge: Strong understanding of local trends, media landscape, and cultural nuances, especially in Kwale, Narok, and Migori counties. Social media and radio experience are a bonus.
- Time and Budget Management: Proficiency in delivering projects on schedule and within budgetary constraints, ensuring efficient resource allocation.
- Creative Ideation & Short-Form Fiction Content: Skill to generate innovative and unique ideas, specifically for short-form fiction content, aligned with objectives and target audience (AGYW and ABYM), with a proven ability to translate subject matter expertise into appropriate content.
- Strategic Thinking: Ability to analyze client goals, target audience preferences, and market trends to develop strategic approaches for effective creative solutions.
- Multi-platform Expertise: Proficiency in creating content for diverse platforms such as digital, social media, print, TV, radio, and emerging media channels (chatbots). Experience in health-related content/behavior change content production in Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights is a significant bonus.
- Branding and Storytelling: Capability to craft compelling brand narratives and storytelling techniques that effectively communicate the Girl Effect message, create emotional connections, and build brand loyalty.
- Visual and Design Skills: Strong aesthetic sense and knowledge of design principles encompassing graphic design, photography, videography, and visual effects for visually appealing and impactful creative assets.
- Technical Proficiency: Familiarity with the latest creative production tools, software, and technologies, including design software, video editing tools, and content management systems.
- Collaboration and Teamwork & Influencer Management: Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with clients, creative teams, copywriters, designers, and stakeholders, including identifying, recommending, briefing, and coordinating with online influencers for collaborative posts and managing ideation and production workflows.
- Language: Effective communicator and writer in English and Kiswahili, with the ability to synthesize, communicate, and simplify complex language concepts for girls and young women.
- Safeguarding: Experience working with young adults and understanding of policies involved when working with minors.

Attitudes we are looking for:

- Comfortable with complex organizational and government structures and multiple stakeholders
- Comfortable with shared decision-making
- A ‘do-er thinker’
- Enthusiastic about talking to and interacting with people across cultures and geographies - this role will require extensive conversations, presentations, documentation, and fire-fighting
- Highly empathetic and context-sensitive - able to balance conflicting needs and priorities decisively
- Mission-driven and cares about making a difference in the lives of young people and vulnerable sections of society.

### **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening
- Technical evaluation
- Financial evaluation.

Evaluation Criterion

- Understanding of the assignment and strength of the creative approach: 20%
- Relevant youth, health and social and behaviour change content portfolio and references: 20%
- Methodology for co-creation, production, audience testing and quality assurance: 20%
- Team capability, government engagement and delivery capacity: 20%
- Financial proposal and value for money: 20%

Girl Effect may request clarifications, creative presentations, interviews, reference checks or best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

### **Proposal Submission**

Invited agencies must submit separate technical and financial proposals.

The technical proposal should not exceed 10 pages, including CVs, references, company documents, and supporting evidence.

**Technical Proposal**

The technical proposal should include:

- Understanding of AASHA, RikaWeb, the target audiences, and the assignment.
- Proposed creative and production approach.
- Co-creation and youth-participation methodology.
- Audience-testing and quality-assurance methodology.
- Workplan showing production batches, approval gates, dependencies, resourcing and delivery dates.
- Proposed team, roles, availability, CVs and relevant experience.
- Three comparable assignments and relevant work samples.
- Three client references, including contact details.
- Approach to managing changes, delays and stakeholder approvals.

#### **Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal should include:

- Detailed pricing in Kenya shillings by asset type and production stage.
- Separate costs for co-creation, scripting, filming, talent, travel, post-production, animation, illustration, testing and final handover.
- Unit rates for each video and article category.
- A consolidated total for the complete validated asset package.
- Applicable taxes shown separately.
- Reimbursable expenses shown separately and supported by clear assumptions.
- A proposed milestone-based payment schedule.
- Confirmation that prices will remain valid for 90 days from the proposal deadline.

### **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 6th November, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 20th November 2026

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- Contracting and Payment: The successful supplier will sign Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones and receipt of a correct invoice.
- Pricing and Scope: Prices must be quoted in Kenyan shillings and include all costs except clearly identified exclusions. No change to the approved scope, asset quantity, format, language, schedule or budget may proceed without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. Supplier errors and the agreed review rounds will not be treated as chargeable changes.
- Taxes and Expenses: Applicable taxes, licences, talent fees and reimbursable costs must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by law. Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable.
- Intellectual Property and Rights: Subject to the final agreement, Girl Effect will own the approved outputs and commissioned project materials paid for under the engagement. The supplier must secure and document all talent, music, stock, location and third-party rights required for government, campaign, web, social-media and digital use.
- Confidentiality and Data Protection: The supplier must protect all confidential, personal and sensitive information accessed or created during the assignment.
- Safeguarding and Conduct: The supplier and all personnel, contributors and subcontractors must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical, anti-fraud, data-protection, information-security and supplier-conduct requirements.
- Conflicts of Interest: Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- Equal Opportunity: Girl Effect welcomes proposals from qualified organisations and consortiums with diverse professional, cultural and geographic backgrounds.
- Right to Award: Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for costs incurred in preparing a proposal.
- Proposal Validity: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Request for Proposal Production and Digital Manager (Individual Consultant)
jobs.description:
## Request for Proposal Production and Digital Manager (Individual Consultant)

**Tanzania**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Individual Consultant Production and Digital Manager – Maternity Cover

Procurement Method Open competitive tender

Eligible Applicants Qualified individual consultants legally able to work in Tanzania

Location Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, with in-person attendance and travel as required

Contract Type Full-time individual consultancy

Contract Period Six months

Level of Effort Full-time, approximately 40 hours per week

Expected Start December 2026, subject to contracting

Proposal Deadline 19 November 2026

Submission Email supplier@girleffect.org

### **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust and need.

From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content is reaching millions of girls in Africa and Asia to make choices and changes in their lives. Igniting their confidence to act differently at a time that can define their future.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, and so much more. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, her community, her country. That’s the Girl Effect.

### **Background and Objective**

Girl Effect Tanzania is seeking an experienced production professional to cover the Digital and Production Manager role during the post holder’s maternity leave. The role manages all content production for Tujibebe, Girl Effect’s youth brand in Tanzania, including its community radios, social media, IEC materials, etc.

The main purpose of this cover is to keep production running without interruption: projects delivered on time, on budget and to brand standard; the right people found and contracted for each project; schedules kept accurate; and every part of each production completed. The post holder will also maintain Tujibebe’s digital and social channels using existing plans and processes, so that reach and audience interaction are kept up during the cover period.

This is a full-time individual consultancy and does not create an employment relationship. The consultant must personally deliver the assignment and may not substitute another person or hold another conflicting full-time engagement during the contract period.

### **What You will do**

***Production management (approximately 70% of time)***

- Lead end-to-end production of Tujibebe’s audio products and community radio content: planning, scripting support, recording, post-production, quality assurance and delivery to broadcast partners.
- Manage production coordination for Tujibebe and Girl Effect Tanzania, including shoots, events and workshops: scoping, scheduling, locations, logistics, call sheets, safeguarding and consent processes, and wrap.
- Find, brief, contract and manage creative crew, freelancers and agencies, including producers, presenters, scriptwriters, photographers, videographers, graphic designers, illustrators and animators, so that all work is aligned with brand objectives and direction.
- Build and maintain an accurate production calendar so that every part of each production is completed on time, and flag risks to delivery early.
- Own production budgets: prepare cost estimates, raise purchase orders and supplier contracts, track spend, and complete reconciliations at the close of each project.
- Hold the quality bar for all content, checking it against brand guidelines, editorial standards and Girl Effect’s safeguarding and content policies before release.
- Make sure audience feedback and insights from the talk show and channels are acted on in the next round of production.
- Look for ways to make creative and production processes more efficient and effective, and record them for the returning post holder.

***Digital platform maintenance (approximately 20% of time)***

- Maintain Tujibebe’s digital platforms (IVR and social) following the existing content plan, so that reach and interaction are kept up.
- Write and sign off copy for social media posts, Tujibebe website articles and SMS blasts, working with freelancers and influencers where needed.
- Support ad-hoc and campaign activity, including product and brand re-launch communications, as directed by the Senior Brand and Content Lead and the global team.
- Track and report on basic channel performance alongside production delivery.

***Handover, coordination and reporting (approximately 10% of time)***

- Complete a structured handover with the post holder at the start of the cover and with the returning post holder at the end.
- Work across Girl Effect’s matrix structure with local and global teams, including brand, insights, safeguarding, finance and partnerships.
- Contribute to strategic initiatives or planning when asked. This is occasional and not a routine accountability of the cover role.

### **Management Arrangements**

The consultant will:

- Report to the Creative Director, Girl Effect Tanzania.
- Work day to day with the Tujibebe Create team and relevant local and global functions.
- Participate in weekly production-status meetings and other essential project meetings.
- Manage external creative suppliers only within delegated authority and approved budgets.
- Maintain availability during agreed Tanzania working hours.
- Promptly escalate urgent delivery, safeguarding, financial or reputational risks.
- Work full time, approximately 40 hours per week, primarily Monday to Friday, with reasonable flexibility for approved production schedules.
- Obtain prior approval for planned absences and provide an appropriate handover for urgent matters.

### **Who You Are**

**Qualifications and experience**

***Essential***

- Around 3–5 years’ experience in content production, with a track record of delivering audio, video or broadcast content to schedule and budget.
- Hands-on experience of every stage of a creative production: scoping, budgeting, pre-production, production, post-production, quality assurance, reconciliation and retrospectives.
- Experience of directly managing production partners, agencies, crew and consultants to produce high-quality creative work.
- Experience of working with creatives across a range of disciplines, including creative directors, producers, scriptwriters, copywriters, designers, illustrators and crew.
- Strong production planning, scheduling and budget management skills, including supplier contracting and financial reconciliation.
- Multiplatform or integrated production experience.
- Experience of working in cross-functional teams and complex matrix reporting structures.
- Fluency in Kiswahili and English, written and spoken.

***Desirable***

- Experience producing content for young people, particularly girls, or on health and social topics, including safeguarding and informed consent practice.

**Working style**

- Highly organised and delivery-focused; able to step into live projects quickly and keep them moving.
- Able to move between big-picture planning and the detail of an individual production.
- Brings structure and order to processes, and leaves clear records so work can be handed back smoothly.
- Engaging and communicative, balancing humility and authority; an excellent communicator in person and in writing.
- A solutions-focused problem solver who shows energy and resilience and avoids unnecessary bureaucracy.
- Adaptable to situations and people, and respectful of and sensitive to multiple cultural contexts.

### **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Applicants must submit separate technical and financial proposals.

**Technical Proposal**

The technical proposal should not exceed 5 pages. It should include:

- Current CV/Profile;
- A short cover letter explaining suitability for the assignment;
- Two relevant case studies, with links or work samples;
- Three contactable client references;
- Confirmation of full-time availability, ability to work in Tanzania and earliest available start date.

**Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in Tanzanian shillings and include:

- Proposed fixed monthly consultancy fee;
- Total fee for the six-month assignment;
- Applicable taxes shown separately;

### **Evaluation**

Proposals will be assessed in the following order:

1. Pre-screening;
2. Technical evaluation;
3. Financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion**

- Relevant production and digital management experience: 50%
- Consultant qualifications, technical skills, interview and personal capability:20%
- Experience in content creation for youth:10%
- Technical Total 70%
- Financial proposal and overall value for money 30%

Total 100%

Girl Effect may request clarifications, interviews, presentations, reference checks, due diligence or a best-and-final offer.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

### **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: **6 November 2026**
- Deadline for proposal submission: **19th November 2026**

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The selected consultant will sign Girl Effect’s standard services agreement. Payment will be linked to satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed monthly outputs.
- **Pricing:** The accepted consultancy fee will be fixed in **Tanzanian shillings** for the approved scope. No increase will apply without an authorised written change order.
- **Expenses:** Only expenses expressly included in the contract or approved in writing before they are incurred will be reimbursable. Required receipts and supporting documents must be provided.
- **Taxes:** Applicable taxes must be shown separately. Girl Effect will deduct withholding tax and other statutory deductions where required by law.
- **Personal Performance:** The consultant must personally perform the assignment. Delegation, substitution or subcontracting is not permitted without Girl Effect’s prior written approval.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The consultant must protect Girl Effect’s confidential, personal and sensitive information and comply with applicable data-protection requirements.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference and safeguarding checks. The consultant must comply with Girl Effect’s policies and codes of conduct.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing or presenting a proposal.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the process; reject any or all proposals; award all or part of the scope; or make no award.
- **No Commitment:** Publication of this RFP does not commit Girl Effect to enter into a contract.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

## **We unlock power with coastal communities.**

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities, restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

## **Summary Job Description**

This is a fixed-term maternity cover within Blue Ventures’ central Programme Performance team, covering the Senior Manager – Programme Evaluation.
