jobs.title: Assessment Grader - Human Rights
jobs.description: Result of Service Accurate, consistent and timely assessment results support fair, merit-based decisions on the inclusion of qualified candidates in rosters endorsed by the Central Review Bodies for Professional-level vacancies across the United Nations Secretariat. Work Location This opportunity is home-based. Expected duration 1-2 months Duties and Responsibilities The Department of Operational Support (DOS) was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, offices away from headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. The Human Resources Services Division (HRSD) provides dedicated services in support of human resources requirements of client entities, from process development through service delivery. The Division establishes and manages rosters across all job families, organizes testing and examinations, provides operational support and other advisory service for clients for the full spectrum of their delegated authorities, and supports managers and business partners in the use of non-staff personnel. The Global Rostering Section (GRS) is responsible for managing a variety of UN Secretariat staff selection rosters which provide pre-cleared and assessed candidates for rapid selection, including through Generic Job Openings, the Young Professionals Programme, and competitive examinations for language positions. This position is located in the Human Resources Services Division (HRSD) within the Operational Support Office (OSO) of the Department of Operational Support (DOS). The Individual Contractor (Assessment Grader) will report to the Chief of the Global Rostering Section. The incumbent will be responsible for the following duties and responsibilities: 1. Technical Assessment Evaluation and Scoring - Grade and evaluate candidates’ technical assessment responses submitted in English or French for Professional-level positions at the P-3, P-4 and P-5 levels. - Assess candidate submissions against established scoring criteria, competency frameworks and technical requirements. - Review written responses for technical knowledge, analytical ability, judgment, communication skills and relevance to the position. - Provide clear scoring rationales and maintain accurate assessment records, as required. 2. Quality Assurance and Review - Ensure consistency, accuracy, objectivity and fairness in the application of grading standards. - Participate in calibration and quality-assurance exercises to ensure uniform grading across assessors. - Review and resolve scoring discrepancies with co-graders, escalating unresolved cases as required. - Conduct first- or second-level reviews of assessment results, as assigned. - Identify and flag irregularities or assessment-related concerns for further review. 3. Confidentiality and Compliance - Maintain strict confidentiality of examination materials, candidate information, scores and selection processes. 4. Service Delivery and Performance - Complete assigned grading volumes within established deadlines while maintaining high-quality grading standards. 5. Feedback and Process Improvement - Provide feedback on assessment methodology, grading rubrics and potential process improvements. - Prepare summary feedback, reports and grading statistics, as required by the Global Rostering Section. Qualifications/special skills Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in human rights, law, political science, international relations, social sciences, economics, public policy, sustainable development, humanitarian affairs or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Experience in human rights or a related area is required, as follows: a minimum of five years for grading P-3 assessments, seven years for grading P-4 assessments and ten years for grading P-5 assessments. Relevant experience may include political affairs, public affairs, international relations, law, social sciences, economics, development or humanitarian affairs. Candidates should demonstrate knowledge of international human rights law, norms, standards and mechanisms; application of a human rights-based approach, including gender equality, women’s empowerment and leaving no one behind; and strong analytical and drafting skills. For P-4 and P-5 assessments, experience in programme management, stakeholder engagement, partnership-building or people management is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, either English or French is required. Additional Information Not available. jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The position is located within the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH). Pursuant to Security Council resolution 2793 (2025), UNSOH has been mandated to provide support; primarily to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), the Haitian National Police (HNP), and the Haitian Armed Forces in the context of any joint operations with the GSF. Additionally, UNSOH is tasked with delivering technical assistance to the Organization of American States (OAS). The Human Rights Officer supports coordination in the implementation of the Human Rights Due-Diligence Policy on UN support to non-UN forces, including by contributing risk assessments and conducting relevant human rights monitoring to gather relevant information and advice on follow-up initiatives to implement the HRDDP Policy. He/She supports integration of human rights in UNSOH HRDDP framework through briefings, exchange analysis, and coordinate responses to human rights concerns, including and provide advice to non-United Nations security forces as recipients of United Nations support during the conduct of their operations. He/she advises internal teams on the human rights implications of operational decisions and contributes to identifying courses of action to prevent escalation or address tensions. He/she formulates recommendations and suggests strategies to better promote and protect human rights in the mission area especially ensuring compliance with HRDDP; The Human Rights Officer also establishes external relationships with government officials, civil society organizations, community representatives, parties to conflict, academia, media outlets, and the diplomatic community to coordinate joint activities, gather detailed information on alleged violations, advocate for protective measures, and promote understanding of human rights. He/she organizes and implements capacity-building activities and designs targeted support measures in collaboration with external partners. He/she leads coordination at the working level and serves as a recognized technical resource within the office. The position is located in Port-au-Prince and the incumbent will report to the section chief of designate official. Responsibilities Within limits of delegated authority, the Human Rights Officer, P-3 will be responsible for the following duties: - Conduct substantive monitoring of the implementation of human rights and international humanitarian law and follow up on recommendations from human rights mechanisms, including treaty bodies, the UPR and special procedures, as well as investigative findings, to ensure compliance with human rights and advance accountability. - Collect, document and analyse evidence-based information on civil, cultural, economic, social and/or political rights, including the right to development, to enable analysis, early warning and response, accountability and informed decision-making, identifying gaps and contribute to ensuring human rights data is discoverable, interoperable and appropriately shared, including from gender and leave no one behind perspectives. - Conduct human rights monitoring and field verification missions, including assessments and early-warning exercises, in accordance with UN methodology, gender indicators and victim/witness protection standards, and draft comprehensive reports on findings and recommendations. - Conduct fact-finding or investigative missions to document violations of international human rights and humanitarian law, ensuring adherence to victim and witness protection standards and facilitating cross-component collaboration as necessary. - Draft, review and disseminate human rights reports, briefings and other communications, with legal analysis as appropriate, and prepare analytical papers to inform strategies, policies, programmes, crisis management, guidance and decision-making processes, with attention to gender integration and leave-no-one-behind perspectives. - Collect, verify and analyse multi-source information relevant to the human rights thematic and/or country-specific situation, ensuring data quality and methodological compliance, including from a gender perspective and leaving no one behind. - Undertake analysis and prepare analytical papers, including on lessons learned, to inform human rights strategies, crisis management, prevention and response policies, programmes and other decision-making processes. - Advise or support national counterparts to draft technical inputs for constitutions, legislation and security-sector reforms that meet international human rights norms and standards. - Provide human-rights-based technical assistance on administration of justice and security-sector issues, including trial and detention monitoring, transitional justice support and/or vetting of security actors as relevant. - Provide substantive advisory support to civil society on the integration of human rights into protection, rule of law, the human rights economy, transitional justice and accountability exercising professional judgment under the guidance of senior staff. - Participate in advising UN partners on the implementation of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy on United Nations Support to non-United Nations Security Forces (HRDDP). - Contribute substantively to the development of strategies on protection of civilians, conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) and child protection, translating early warning into coordinated responses. - Promote transitional justice processes, including truth‑seeking, prosecutions and reparations, through substantive advocacy, analysis and engagement aimed at supporting efforts to address impunity, under the guidance of senior staff. - Engage in the promotion of Human Rights through advocacy and impactful outreach activities. - Engage substantively in the Office’s partnership‑building activities, including supporting the identification, development and maintenance of partnerships, under the guidance of senior staff. - Implement effective communication activities to amplify human rights messaging and outreach contributing substantive content, coordination and outreach under the guidance of senior staff. - Maintain confidentiality and integrity and handle sensitive information with discretion, ensuring compliance with the UN data privacy, security requirements, and standards. - Deliver training programmes and workshops using various platforms for different audiences to enhance the capacity of UN staff and partners. - Prepare and contribute to the review of training materials for practitioners in collaboration and consultation with relevant UN Agencies and other partners. - Provide guidance to team members to promote professional development and a positive team culture. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; Solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; Is willing to learn from others; Places team agenda before personal agenda; Supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; Shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Accountability: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honors commitments; Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. A first-level degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Experience with the United Nations, national governments or other relevant organizations, particularly in providing substantive support on peacebuilding, the rule of law and security institutions, including in the context of mission transitions, is required. The position is based in Port-au-Prince within the Mission Support Centre. The Military Liaison Officer, P-4, reports to the Chief, Mission Support Centre (P-5), or their designate. Established in 1965, UNDP plays a pivotal role in supporting nations in their efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and advance socio-economic development. With a focus on inclusive and equitable growth, UNDP provides technical expertise, mobilizes financial resources, and delivers policy and other services to support the formulation and implementation of effective development strategies and solutions that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates in over 170 countries and territories, collaborating with local partners, governments, and other stakeholders to build resilient communities and foster sustainable development.

UNDP's initiatives span a wide range of areas, including climate change, gender equality, governance, and crisis response, embodying its commitment to creating a better and more sustainable future for people across the globe.

The Office of Human Resources (OHR) is part of the UNDP Bureau for Management Services (BMS) of UNDP. It is the anchor of the global HR function for UNDP, providing strategy and policy setting, guidance and oversight. In addition, BMS/OHR provides a broad range of HR advisory and talent management services enabling UNDP to deliver fully integrated development solutions to enable its workforce to deliver more and better results. BMS/OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by developing high quality and innovative human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

With its People for 2030 strategy, OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by strengthening and innovating its human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

Within this innovative, ambitious and dynamic context, BMS/OHR is seeking high calibre HR professionals with a strong HR background, and the capacity, commitment, and attitude needed to drive a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, transformative results, as well as inclusion, respect and trust.

People Programmes and Partnership team (PPP) works to enable a diverse pipeline of people programmes, hereunder Early Talent initiatives and outreach with a vision to nurture the rejuvenation of UNDPs workforce, as well as manifesting itself as a Centre for Excellence in providing solutions and services on Early Talent programmes and Management across UN system agency clients, member states as well as other potential partners.

These programmes include the Junior Professional Officer, Specialist for Development, Graduate Programme as well as Internship and Fellowship Programmes. PPP also manages the Technical Expert Secondment Programme, and it equally engages in designing and developing new people programmes meeting strategic organizational objectives of both UNDP and Partners

Position Purpose

PPP provides end-to-end HR Services to Donors, UN Agencies and staff members hired under these programmes. Hereunder, services on recruitment, assessment and selection, HR services, advisory, learning and career development, partner relations and reporting, and financial oversight.

Under the strategic leadership of the Chief, People Programme and Partnerships (PPP), the HR Specialist will contribute to the development and roll out of the Early Professionals for Impact and Change strategy (EPIC), as well as provides oversight in management of People Programmes (JPO/SDP, Fellowship, Secondment Programmes, and oversight of HR services ensuring their transparency and integrity. The HR Specialist acts as team lead of HR Associates providing HR services to young professionals in both UNDP and 14 partner agencies, and government secondment programmes as well as leads a part-time Learning analyst to deliver learning and development offerings to early professionals. The HR Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and promotes the maintenance of high staff morale and engagement.

The HR Specialist works with a wide range of strategic partners and clients including staff, donor governments, UN partner organizations as well as UNDP offices. The HR Specialist works closely with the OHR HR Business Partners, Talent Development Unit, Talent Acquisition, Deployment and Succession team, People Analytics Unit, GSSU-HR and UNDP hiring offices in delivering client-oriented services in People Programme management, HR service delivery and design of talent acquisition strategies.

UNDP has adopted a portfolio approach to effectively respond to changing business needs and leverage relevant synergies and linkages to achieve its strategic goals. This is in recognition of the interconnected nature of development challenges that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, all UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Effective Oversight of People Programmes.

- Coordinate service innovation on enhanced HR service delivery on people programmes, as well as leveraging emerging business opportunities.

- Contribute to the design and development of new People Programmes.

- Manage, oversee and further refine the implementation of People Programmes (JPO, and others) incorporating partner feedback into programme design and HR service delivery.

- Promote and nurture partnerships across UN Agencies and partner countries as well as other stakeholders engaged in the delivery and development of People Programmes.

- Support and contribute to the finalization, launch and implementation of the Early Professionals for Impact and Change strategy, EPIC.

2. Ensure the delivery of client-oriented HR services for People Programmes to UNDP and partner agencies and facilitate knowledge management.

- Oversee and coordinate HR service delivery and development in HR administration for improved services to PPP/JPOSC Partner countries and UN Agencies.

- Analyse corporate HR strategies and policies, facilitating their implementation and alignment for People Programmes.

- Ensure compliance of HR benefits and entitlements determinations with UNDP rules and regulations, strategies and policies/procedures.

- Advise and guide partner UN Agencies, Stakeholders and HR team on interpretation and application on policies on non-routine cases.

- Provide advisory services and HR Solutions to relevant stakeholders on facilitating complex cases for placements under the People programmes.

- Within delegated authority and in consultation with the Chief/PPP present exceptional considerations and recommendations for approval.

jobs.title: Communications Clerk (NPSA-3) [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The UNDP Serbia Digital Innovation Portfolio is at the forefront of driving digital transformation across the country. The portfolio designs and implements key initiatives in digital governance, cyber resilience, e-services, digital literacy, and future-ready skills. Operating in a dynamic and fast-paced environment, the portfolio helps build robust policies, ecosystems, and public services that leverage digital solutions to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

To amplify the impact of these initiatives, the Digital Innovations Portfolio requires dedicated communications support. The Communications Clerk will work within the Digital Innovations Portfolio team to help streamline public relations, simplify complex technical topics for public channels, and support portfolio events and promotion of achievements, in close coordination with the UNDP Serbia Communications Unit.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Serbia Digital Innovations Portfolio Manager, and in coordination with the UNDP Serbia Communications Unit, the Communications Clerk will provide operational support for communications activities, digital content preparation and portfolio events. All communications materials will be prepared in accordance with UNDP communication guidelines and submitted for review and clearance, as appropriate.

Communications Clerk will undertake the following tasks:

Event Communications & Logistics Support:

- Support the preparation and coordination for portfolio workshops, hackathons, tech talks, and high-level bilateral digital exchanges.

- Drafting event agendas, basic moderation scripts, brief talking points, and logistics-related communication materials and providing moderation support during portfolio events, workshops, conferences, and other relevant activities, as required.

- Providing active on-site communications support during events (including photography, social media coverage, and coordinator/guest facilitation).

Support in Content Creation & Digital Storytelling:

- Simplifying complex technical topics (e.g., cyber resilience, data privacy, and e-government platforms) into engaging content for a general audience.

- Provide support in drafting articles, blog posts, press releases, and success stories highlighting the portfolio's project milestones.

- Support the preparation of inputs for monthly/quarterly newsletters or updates targeted at government partners, tech sectors, and international digital agencies.

Support in Coordination & Channel Alignment:

- Supporting communication and coordination between the Digital Innovations Portfolio and the central UNDP Serbia Communications Team.

- Ensuring all drafted digital content, graphics, and messaging align with UNDP corporate communication guidelines and are ready for dissemination via official UNDP Serbia channels.

Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing relevant to the project:

- Participate in training on internal procedures for the project staff and provide support to the organization of training and other capacity building activities as needed.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Maintain organized records of project data, field activities, case studies, human-interest stories, photographs, and other relevant documents that can be drawn upon in support of knowledge sharing and advocacy.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Communications Clerk will work under the overall guidance and supervision of the Digital Innovations Portfolio Manager.

Competencies

- Core Competencies: Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional and Technical Competencies:

- Business Management - Monitoring and evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively. Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Business Management - Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Digital - Social Media Knowledge of social media and ability to advise the use of social media for development outcomes.

- Digital - Story telling Ability to empathize with people's perceptions, motivations, feelings and mental models and craft narratives to build an emotive argument for change accordingly. Ability to present data, insights or information in compelling ways to mobilize resources, talent or action. Ability to choose media and channels that is fit for purpose to reach specific target audiences.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Completion of secondary education is required.

Experience:

- Minimum 3 years of relevant work experience in communications, digital media, digital marketing, public relations, or other related fields.

Desired skills:

- Experience in drafting and editing communication materials, such as articles, press releases, newsletters, success stories, or social media content.

- Experience in supporting the creation of digital and multimedia content, including graphics, photographs, or short videos, using digital design and editing tools.

- Experience in supporting the organization and communication coverage of events, workshops, conferences, or similar activities.

- Experience in contributing to social media channels and digital communication campaigns.

- Previous experience working with international organizations, development agencies, or public sector institutions is an asset.

- Experience with digital transformation topics (e.g., e-governance, cyber resilience, e-services, digital skills) and the ability to easily grasp technical project concepts.

- Experience translating complex or technical project updates into inputs for highly engaging, simple, and public-friendly stories, articles, or social media posts.

- Experience drafting, editing, and verbal communication in both Serbian and English.

- Experience with user-friendly design and editing platforms (such as Canva, mobile video editors, or basic photo-editing software) to quickly draft visual assets.

- Experience with basic event photography, live social media posting/coverage, and helping facilitate speakers or guests on-site.

- Experience acting as a smooth communication bridge between a highly technical portfolio team and the central UNDP communications unit.

Languages:

- Fluency in Serbian and English is required.

Important Information

The online application form must be fully completed. Applicants are required to carefully complete their online application form and reflect all of their work experience history in the application.

Only attaching a CV is not sufficient for applicants to be considered for positions. All applicants have to complete the Experience, Education, Language, and Nationality & Permanent Residence fields fully.

Managers may ask (ad hoc) for any other materials relevant to pre-assessing the relevance of their experience, such as reports, presentations, publications, campaigns or other materials.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Asistente en Ing. Electromecánica (1 Chiriquí / 1 Panama)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Antecedentes /Descripción de la oficina / Unidad / Proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Desde hace 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

El proyecto 1005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el desarrollo”, busca contribuir al posicionamiento del INADEH como rector de la formación profesional, al fortalecimiento institucional, a la mejora de la calidad de la oferta educativa de hoy y del futuro, y a la mejora de la gestión operativa.

De esta manera, la acción del PNUD se centra en apoyar en la generación de una visión del sistema de formación técnica profesional con alternativas diferenciadas que sirvan a las personas, a la economía y a la sociedad. Organizar la gobernanza de la formación técnica y profesional, la vinculación educación – empleo, superar la sexta frontera, y poner el talento y capacidad de las y los panameños en reactivar nuestra economía y desarrollar la estrategia del cambio del proyecto definida como “Formación profesional como instrumento para fortalecer competencias, asegurar medios de vida y hacer una economía competitiva”.

La Oficina de Proyectos del INADEH es la instancia principal de comunicación y gestión de proyectos que ejecuta el INADEH con diversos organismos e instituciones, por lo que su rol principal es brindar estrecho seguimiento a la ejecución de los proyectos que se ejecutan como aquellos que se proyectan ejecutar en la institución, tanto en el corto como en el mediano plazo.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asistente en Ingeniería Electromecánica brindará apoyo técnico a la Oficina de Proyectos de Transformación y Mejora Integral del INADEH, contribuyendo a la planificación, diseño, supervisión, seguimiento y control técnico de las obras y proyectos que ejecuta la institución, en el ámbito de su especialidad y de conformidad con los requerimientos técnicos, contractuales y la normativa aplicable.

Apoyo en levantamientos, planos y presupuestos

- Participar en los levantamientos de requerimientos y en las visitas de campo, apoyando la verificación y rectificación de medidas, condiciones existentes y demás información técnica necesaria para el diseño y ejecución de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de especificaciones técnicas para la contratación y ejecución de obras, suministros e instalaciones electromecánicas, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad.

- Apoyar la elaboración y revisión de planos de instalaciones y sistemas electromecánicos, con base en los levantamientos, requerimientos y especificaciones técnicas de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de presupuestos, cómputos métricos y cálculos de materiales, equipos y componentes correspondientes a los sistemas electromecánicos de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la revisión del cumplimiento de la normativa legal y técnica vigente aplicable a los diseños de los sistemas eléctricos, de aire acondicionado y refrigeración, gas, plomería, protección contra incendios y sistemas especiales, según corresponda a su ámbito de competencia, e informar al profesional responsable sobre las observaciones identificadas.

Apoyo en la inspección y seguimiento técnico de obras

- Participar en visitas de campo e inspecciones técnicas y apoyar el seguimiento de las obras y proyectos del INADEH, de acuerdo con la ubicación asignada y las necesidades del Proyecto.

- Apoyar el seguimiento del cronograma y la ejecución de las obras, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad, verificando, bajo la orientación del profesional responsable, su correspondencia con los planos, especificaciones técnicas, términos de referencia y condiciones contractuales.

- Apoyar la revisión de los materiales, equipos, acabados y sistemas electromecánicos propuestos para las obras y preparar los insumos técnicos requeridos para su evaluación por parte del profesional responsable.

- Apoyar la revisión de los planes de calidad y seguridad presentados por las empresas contratistas en los aspectos relacionados con su especialidad, así como identificar y documentar desviaciones, deficiencias o posibles incumplimientos técnicos durante la ejecución de las obras, para consideración y gestión del profesional responsable.

- Apoyar las acciones orientadas a promover la calidad de las obras, el uso eficiente de los materiales y recursos y la incorporación de soluciones sostenibles y amigables con el medioambiente.

Apoyo en la gestión contractual, documental y financiera de las obras

- Apoyar la revisión y verificación de la documentación técnica presentada por las empresas contratistas, identificando posibles inconsistencias con los requerimientos establecidos y las condiciones contractuales para consideración del profesional responsable.

- Recopilar y preparar los insumos técnicos necesarios para el análisis de cuentas, reclamos, órdenes de cambio, obras adicionales y demás solicitudes relacionadas con la ejecución de las obras, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad.

- Apoyar la preparación del detalle y la documentación técnica requerida para la tramitación de cuentas ante la Contraloría General de la República de Panamá, de acuerdo con el avance de las obras.

- Apoyar la preparación de las certificaciones de satisfacción correspondientes a las obras asignadas, mediante la recopilación y verificación preliminar de la información relacionada con el cumplimiento de los cronogramas, planos, especificaciones técnicas y condiciones contractuales.

Informes, seguimiento y apoyo a la gestión del Proyecto

- Apoyar la preparación de informes técnicos semanales y periódicos sobre las actividades realizadas y el avance de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de registros e informes preliminares sobre las incidencias, deficiencias o posibles incumplimientos identificados durante las visitas de campo.

- Recopilar y preparar información técnica sobre las obras asignadas para apoyar el seguimiento y la toma de decisiones del Proyecto.

- Brindar asistencia técnica, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad, a las actividades e iniciativas desarrolladas en el marco del Proyecto y del Programa País del PNUD, bajo la orientación del profesional responsable.

Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos relacionados con el proyecto.

- Participar en la capacitación del personal del proyecto sobre procedimientos internos y brindar apoyo en la organización de actividades de formación y fortalecimiento de capacidades, según sea necesario.

- Realizar aportes valiosos a las redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica.

- Mantener registros organizados de datos del proyecto, actividades de campo, estudios de caso, historias de interés humano, fotografías y otros documentos relevantes que puedan utilizarse para apoyar el intercambio de conocimientos y las actividades de incidencia.

El/la titular desempeñará otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Proyecto, la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

- Supervisión: El/la Asistente en Ingeniería Electromecánica trabajará bajo la supervisión general del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto y del/de la Director/a del Proyecto. Sus servicios se prestarán en el marco del Proyecto 01005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el Desarrollo”. La relación contractual se establecerá directamente con la Oficina de País del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), en coordinación con el equipo del Proyecto, el Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental y el Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH).

- Lugar de trabajo: Se contemplan dos (2) posiciones, con las siguientes ubicaciones y áreas de cobertura: Una (1) posición con sede en la provincia de Chiriquí, con disponibilidad para movilizarse a los proyectos, centros y sedes regionales del INADEH ubicados en las provincias de Chiriquí, Veraguas y Bocas del Toro. Una (1) posición con sede en la sede principal del INADEH, ubicada en Vía Tocumen, con disponibilidad para movilizarse a los proyectos, centros y sedes regionales ubicados en las provincias de Darién, Panamá, Panamá Oeste, Coclé, Veraguas, Herrera y Los Santos.

- Horario : El/la profesional deberá laborar en horario regular de lunes a viernes. Cuando las necesidades del Proyecto lo requieran, deberá tener disponibilidad para laborar en horario extendido.

- Movilización: Los gastos de movilización, alojamiento y alimentación derivados de misiones oficiales o actividades previamente autorizadas, conforme a los requerimientos del Proyecto, serán cubiertos por este, de acuerdo con las normas y procedimientos aplicables.

Competencias

Competencias Básicas

1. Logro de Resultados

Nivel 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega un trabajo de calidad antes de la fecha límite.

2. Piensa de manera innovadora

Nivel 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático solucionador de problemas, hace mejoras.

3. Aprende contínuamente

Nivel 1: De mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación

4. Se adapta con agilidad

Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja constructivamente la ambiguedad/incertidumbre, es flexible.

5. Actúa con determinación

Nivel 1: Muestra impulso y motivación, capaz de rendir con calma frente a la adversidad confiado.

6. Compromiso y Asociación

Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión, comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

7. Diversidad e Inclusión

Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, confronta la discriminación

Competencias Transversales

Area Temática

Nombre

Definición

Capacidad para reunir a diversos grupos de personas, datos, información, ideas y tecnología para resolver problemas y diseñar soluciones o servicios.

Conocimiento y comprensión de los principios, la metodología, el diseño y las prácticas de la inteligencia colectiva.

Capacidad para planificar, organizar, priorizar y controlar recursos, procedimientos y protocolos para alcanzar objetivos específicos.

Competencias Técnicas

Administración y Operaciones

Gestión de espacios en edificios, instalaciones y oficinas

Conocimiento y capacidad para facilitar la renovación y mejora de oficinas, incluyendo la revisión de planos complejos de ingeniería y arquitectura; negociar acuerdos técnicos para garantizar la plena operatividad de la infraestructura y los servicios del edificio; diseñar políticas y procedimientos (POPP) para los locales y las instalaciones, entre los que se incluyen las normas de espacio; gestionar las instalaciones y los espacios; y validar las notas de los estados financieros sobre datos de arrendamientos.

Entorno Digital

Metodologías y prácticas ágiles

Capacidad para gestionar proyectos y procesos mediante la iteración, el aprendizaje y la mejora continuos. Capacidad para gestionar equipos multifuncionales autoorganizados y fomentar una cultura de curiosidad y aprendizaje dentro del equipo. Aptitud para actuar con agilidad, improvisar y adaptarse rápidamente a eventos imprevistos o cambios en las condiciones o el contexto.

Requisitos mínimos de educación

- Educación secundaria completa es requerida.

- Estudios universitarios (a nivel de licenciatura completa) en Licenciatura en Ingeniería Electromecánica se dará debida consideración, pero no son un requisito

Años de Experiencia mínima relevante

- Mínimo cinco (5) años de experiencia (con educación secundaria completa) o dos (2) años (con título universitario de licenciatura) en actividades relacionadas con el levantamiento, diseño, instalación, mantenimiento, supervisión, gestión o seguimiento de obras o proyectos de sistemas electromecánicos, incluyendo sistemas de aire acondicionado, refrigeración, instalaciones eléctricas de baja y media tensión y sistemas especiales.

Habilidades Requeridas

- Experiencia en el manejo de programas computacionales de Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Teams y Power Point), Zoom, plataformas de formación, otras.

- Experiencia en el levantamiento de requerimientos y elaboración de especificaciones técnicas para instalaciones electromecánicas en obras de construcción.

- Experiencia en la elaboración de cálculo de materiales y presupuestos de sistemas electromecánicos.

Investments and Debt Finance Specialist, Africa [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development. SFH work is delivered through three interconnected portfolios: 1) Public Finance for the SDGs; 2) Private Finance for the SDGs; and 3) Global & Country Financing Policy Frameworks.

The European Commission (EC), together with EU Member States, development agencies, EU financial institutions and UN organizations, have embarked on coordinating their offer of EU expertise and resources for low- and middle-income countries in the area of sustainable finance, inspired by EU experience, through the EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, of which UNDP is an implementing partner, focusing on supporting countries on sustainable finance taxonomy development, disclosure frameworks and thematic/green bond framework development.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Debt and Investments and with a cross-reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Africa, the Investment and Debt Finance Specialist will primarily be responsible for the delivery of activities under the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub implemented by UNDP. The role is hosted within the SFH Private Finance Portfolio, under the Investments and Debt unit.

Working closely with colleagues across the SFH portfolios and the Global Policy Network in Africa, the Specialist will provide technical and analytical support to partner governments, financial institutions, and issuers on sustainable finance instruments, with a focus on green and sustainability bond issuance. This includes pre- and post-issuance support, knowledge generation on fixed-income markets and other debt instruments, identification and assessment of green investment opportunities, and design of monitoring and reporting frameworks for environmental and climate impacts. The role will also contribute to building in-house capacity and institutional knowledge on debt and investment finance, ensuring effective translation of these skills into the design and implementation of innovative financing instruments at the country level, in line with the objectives of the Global Green Bond Initiative and the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub both being linked to Global Gateway.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Investments and Debt Finance Specialist will play a central role in advancing UNDP’s Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) agenda in Africa, while also contributing to global workstreams. Based in UNDP Sustainable Finance Hub for Africa, the incumbent will be responsible for the following functions and duties:

1. Provision of thematic debt instruments and country support

- Advise and support the development and implementation of UNDP’s thematic debt offering and lead the design and piloting of innovative development bond frameworks in selected countries across the Africa region, in close coordination with SFH portfolios, UNDP Country Offices and SFH Regional Advisors;

- Provide tailored technical advice to governments and partners to address country-specific financing needs with a particular focus on green bonds with the European Commission under the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub.

2. Strategic alignment with European commission initiatives

- Ensure key focus and coherence with the European Commission’s Global Green Bond Initiative;

- Contribute to joint EC-UNDP workplans and reporting, promoting alignment with EU sustainable finance frameworks and global standards;

- Provide technical inputs as an implementing partner of EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, in coordination with SFH portfolios;

- Prepare donor reports, and contribute to monitoring frameworks, ensuring consistency with regional priorities and global strategies and UNDP/SFH systems.

3. Ensure partnerships and scaling of sustainable finance solutions

- Contribute to UNDP’s broader financing and investment agenda by leveraging networks, fostering partnerships, and identifying opportunities to scale sustainable finance solutions at global and country-levels with a focus on blended finance structures.

4. Provision of methodological guidance and flagship initiatives

- Contribute to the development of methodological tools and guidance related to thematic bonds and debt instruments

- Provide support to SFH Portfolios, enhancing their application and impact in - countries in Africa.

5. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia;

- Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application;

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on development and project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area;

- Promote advocacy for UNDP’s work and opportunities for collaboration in address in development trends in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Investment and Debt Finance Specialist will carry out relevant duties under the guidance and direct supervision of the Head of Debt and Investments and with a cross-reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Africa, the Investment and Debt Finance Senior Specialist.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

Business Direction & Strategy

Strategy

- Negotiation and Influence: Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Development

Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively. Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Required Skills and Experience

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of experience in sustainable finance, thematic bond issuance or related areas, is required.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing thematic bond frameworks, including impact measurement, evaluation, and reporting.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia for its current Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

- Human Development

- Nature, Decarbonisation and Resilience

- Economic and Digital Transformation

The Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) portfolio supports governance institutions and development actors to strengthen public-sector effectiveness, local governance and capacity building, promoting transparency and accountability, and building resilience towards climate change and other development risks. The portfolio promotes collaboration across levels of government and locally driven solutions that translate national priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals into measurable results for communities.

The Local Governance Analysist provides substantive technical, analytical and programmatic support across the HDRG portfolio, with emphasis on local governance, local economic development, sub-national institutional capacity building, municipal planning and budgeting, and quality public service delivery, inclusive participation, development financing, evidence and data, partnerships, quality assurance, and knowledge management.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.Local governance policy and technical advisory support

- Lead the local governance pillar for UNDP Indonesia by providing applied policy and technical advice on decentralization, multi-level governance, local public administration, digitalised public service delivery and innovations, and national and sub-national institutional capacity.

- Assess and translate national policy directions and sub-national priorities into practical programme options, technical recommendations, implementation pathways and scalable solutions.

- Conduct political-economy, institutional, stakeholder, capacity and policy analyses, combining quantitative and qualitative evidence and clearly identifying implementation constraints, incentives, risks and opportunities.

- Integrate human rights, gender equality, disability inclusion, Leaving No One Behind, conflict sensitivity, social and environmental standards, and digital and data considerations into technical analysis and advice.

- Prepare high-quality technical briefs, policy notes, issue papers, talking points and presentations for engagement with government at national and subnational levels, as well as development partners to strengthen local governance and local development .

2. Programme and project design

- Lead or substantively contribute to concept notes, project documents, theories of change, result frameworks, workplans, budgets, risk registers, monitoring frameworks, implementation arrangements and sustainability strategies.

- Develop options for piloting, testing, adapting and scaling local governance interventions, including digital or data-enabled approaches where suitable and responsible.

- Apply results-based management principles and ensure clear causal logic, measurable indicators, baselines, targets, assumptions, evidence sources and learning mechanisms.

- Ensure alignment of local governance and local development opporunities with UNDP strategic priorities, the Country Programme, national and sub-national development plans and priorty works streams of UNDP Indonesia across the three clusters

- Ensure programme designs are operationally feasible, risk-informed and supported by credible stakeholder ownership and institutional arrangements.

3 Partnerships and multi-stakeholder engagement

- Establish strong partnerships with public sector actors who have a role in enabling strong local governance and local development by engaging with regional governments, Ministry of Home Affairs, Bappenas, Ministry of Finance, sectoral ministries and agencies, provincial and district/municipal governments, universities, think tanks, civil society, private-sector actors and development partners.

- Design and facilitate inclusive policy dialogues, consultations, technical working groups, missions, workshops and peer-learning processes involving stakeholders with different interests and levels of technical expertise.

- Identify opportunities for diversified partnerships to unlock public financing to strengthen local development and local governance with clear entry points for UNDP

- Identify opportunities for joint programming, knowledge exchange, and capacity development while promoting complementarity with government and partner initiatives.

4 Resource mobilization and development finance

- Identify and assess funding and co-financing opportunities linked to local governance and sustainable human development, including public finance, private-sector participation, philanthropy and development-partner funding.

- Prepare donor intelligence, funding maps, partnership pipelines, investment cases, pitch materials, proposal narratives and substantive inputs to financing strategies.

- Develop technically credible options for blended finance, public-private collaboration, pooled or catalytic funding and other financing approaches, with explicit attention to feasibility, additionality, safeguards and risk.

- Coordinate substantive follow-up on partnership and funding opportunities, maintaining clear ownership, decision points, documentation and next steps.

- Support due diligence and risk analysis for proposed partnerships and financing arrangements in coordination with relevant UNDP functions.

5. Knowledge management and capacity development

- Generate and curate knowledge from programme implementation, field engagement, peer exchange and research, including lessons, good practices, innovations and evidence of results and convert learning into recommendations for programme adjustments and scale

- Produce or coordinate policy briefs, case studies, guidance notes, analytical products, presentations, learning materials and data-informed narratives for policy and programme audiences.

- Design and facilitate communities of practice, peer exchanges and capacity-development activities for national and sub-national stakeholders.

- Ensure knowledge products are technically accurate, accessible, inclusive, appropriately sourced and responsive to the needs of intended users.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: N/A

Institutional Arrangement

The Local Governance Analyst (LGA) will work under the overall supervision of the Team Leader HDRG, providing policy, analytical and technical advisory support on local governance, decentralization and sub-national development. The incumbent will work closely with HDRG programme and other units to translate policy priorities, institutional analysis and evidence into practical programme solutions, technical recommendations, partnership opportunities and knowledge products. The LGA will also provide substantive inputs to programme and project design, stakeholder engagement, resource mobilization and capacity development, and may coordinate technical contributors supporting relevant workstreams.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
