Background /Project Description

The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria was created to significantly increase resources to fight three of the world’s most devastating diseases, and to direct those resources to areas of greatest need. The Global Fund attracts, manages and disburses resources in a public-private partnership that makes a sustainable and significant contribution to the reduction of mortality and morbidity caused by the three diseases and to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

UNDP is a key partner to the Global Fund to Fight HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM) and is the UN agency assuming the role of Principal Recipient of GFATM grants in South Sudan for TB and HIV/AIDS. In its role as Principal Recipient, UNDP ensures quality financial management, timely procurement of supplies, and efficient monitoring and delivery service. UNDP’s management role consists of implementing grants, ensuring financial accountability, and training of national and international counterparts on programme management, financial accountability and timely programmatic reporting to the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) and Global Fund (GF) Secretariat.

Position Purpose

The Monitoring and Evaluation Analyst will report to the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist and will work within the Programme & M&E unit to support the Finance & QA unit, the PSM & Procurement unit and the Warehouse/Supply Chain Management team. Under the guidance of the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist, the Analyst will liaise with the Local Fund Agent (LFA), the CCM, the SSAC, the MOH, the technical working groups responsible for HIV and TB, and U. S. Department of State Implementing Partners, Sub Recipients, various other partners and stakeholders. The incumbent will be required to travel to service delivery sites for the purpose of monitoring and supporting project activities including integration of HIV/TB services into primary health care, a key deliverable for the GC8 grant.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist (Global Fund), the Monitoring and Evaluation Analyst will be responsible for the following key tasks:

Support the GC8 monitoring and evaluation framework and plans:

- Support the development and updating of M&E frameworks and plans for the HIV, TB and RSSH portfolio in coordination with MOH, national programmes, SSAC and partners.

- Support regular analysis of grant performance against GC8 targets, identify implementation gaps and emerging risks, and recommend concrete corrective actions in coordination with programme teams and sub-recipients.

- Work with MOH, Service Delivery SR, SSAC, and NEPWU to develop quarterly joint field supportive supervision including service delivery and community interventions.

- Develop quarterly supportive supervision reports, including issues, remedial actions, timelines and responsible parties.

- Manage the tracking tool for issues identified from quarterly supportive supervision visits, providing monthly updates and presenting the issues during internal team meetings and as well as SR review meetings.

- Prepare data Power BI analytics for presentations during meetings with the Global Fund, LFA, CCM, MOH, partners and stakeholders.

- Support the develop M&E tools, indicator reference sheets and training materials for the PMU, SRs and implementing partners.

- Support SRs to strengthen their M&E systems for timely and accurate reporting.

- Supervise and monitor the work of assigned M&E consultants assigned to support the team.

- Conduct M&E capacity assessments of SRs and national partners and implement a capacity development plan.

- Review progress reports against targets and propose remedial actions for under-performing indicators.

- Monitor implementation bottlenecks and provide analytical inputs to programme decision-making.

- Support the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to develop quarterly Management Letters to Sub Recipients following review of quarterly combined programme and financial reports, summarising feedback on performance and recommendations.

- Develop an individual workplan

Deliver grant performance reporting to the Global Fund:

- Support the preparation of Programme Updates and Disbursement Requests (PUDRs), bi-annual and annual updates to the Global Fund.

- Consolidate quarterly programmatic information and ensure timely submission through corporate systems and the Global Fund transparency portal.

- Organize and document programme review meetings, including preparation of background data, presentations and follow-up action points.

Ensure Data quality assurance for the HIV, TB and RSSH portfolios:

- Review data from HMIS/DHIS2 and programme sources for completeness, accuracy and consistency.

- Plan and conduct routine data quality assessments (RDQA/DQA) and support sub-recipient site quality assurance (RSQA).

- Mentor and support the sub-recipient M&E Focal Points (TB/HIV, RSSH).

- Support the strengthening the use of routine programme data, including DHIS2 and community-level reporting, to identify service delivery gaps, monitor coverage among key and vulnerable populations, and inform programme adjustments.

Manage surveys, evaluations and learning

- Support the coordination of baseline, mid-term and end-line surveys and evaluations, including drafting Terms of Reference and providing technical direction.

- Support the dissemination of evaluation findings and the preparation of management responses.

- Support the documentation of lessons learned and promote their use in programme design and grant revisions.

Build M&E capacity and support nationalization:

- Deliver M&E and health information systems (HIS) training to SSAC, MOH, National Programmes staff and SRs, including NEPWU, SSNEP+ and NASOSS.

- Support the Country Dialogue Transition Plan (CDTP) and capacity transfer for progressive nationalization of the PR role.

- Support the development and monitoring of measurable milestones for transferring M&E responsibilities to national institutions, including strengthened national ownership of data quality assurance, analysis and Global Fund reporting.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the PMU, Country Office and the Organization.

The key impact of the post will be high-quality, timely monitoring, evaluation and reporting of the GC8

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Proyecto en Programas de Manejo de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas
jobs.description:
Descripción del Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos de la CONANP para fortificar la gestión jurídica y técnica vinculada con el manejo, la conservación y el establecimiento de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas, contribuyendo a la solidez de los procesos institucionales, la coordinación entre las áreas involucradas y la toma de decisiones de la Comisión.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

Realizar estudios y acciones necesarias para el seguimiento y manejo de áreas protegidas.

Elaborar documentos jurídicos, informes, oficios y proyectos relacionados con los asuntos competencia del área.

Formulación y revisión de estrategias de manejo y conservación.

Dar seguimiento a los procesos de opinión requeridos para los nuevos decretos de ANP de las regiones definidas por la CONANP.

Integrar información y elaborar reportes técnicos-jurídicos para apoyar la toma de decisiones.

Coordinar acciones y brindar apoyo jurídico a las unidades administrativas y autoridades involucradas en la atención de los asuntos.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Derecho o áreas afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Exeriencia Relevante:

- Para candidatos(as) con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 3 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

jobs.title: AI Innovation Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Unit of Information and Technology Management (ITM) in New York are the enablers supporting UNDP Country Offices around the world with technological solutions that empower the projects we deliver. Our Unit offers a stimulating and versatile internship in an international environment with contact to various partners from some 166 countries with UNDP presence. We are a team who work in a dynamic and informal atmosphere, and we expect our interns to become vital members of the team.

UNDP is committed to leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative tool to advance sustainable development objectives. The AI, Data and Engineering Team works across divisions to design and implement cutting-edge AI solutions tailored to the unique challenges faced by global communities. This dynamic role facilitates innovation and AI-based insights that help achieve the organization’s strategic goals.

The AI Innovation Analyst is responsible for contributing to the development and implementation of AI-based solutions, fostering a culture of technological innovation, and ensuring adherence to ethical AI principles within UNDP’s global operations.

Duties and Responsibilities

1- Contribute to the AI Solutions Development:

- Support in designing AI tools and platforms that address corporate operation challenges.

- Contribute to the deployment of AI systems to optimize operational efficiency and business processes.

2- Contribute to the Strategic Innovation:

- Collaborate with business counterparts to identify new AI opportunities.

- Contribute to building frameworks for AI-driven decision-making processes.

3- Ensure Ethical Compliance:

- Ensure all AI initiatives align with international ethical standards and UNDP policies.

- Monitor AI implementations for potential risks and mitigate concerns proactively.

4- Facilitate Capacity Building and knowledge sharing

- Facilitate knowledge-sharing activities and conduct training workshops for stakeholders to understand AI applications.

- Work with partners to scale emerging AI innovations and foster collaboration and support capacity building

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

On a day-to-day basis, the AI Innovation Specialist will be working with and directly reporting to the Chief of AI, Data and Engineering.

Competencies

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Information Management & Technology - User Experience and business analyst: Capacity to translate efficiently users’ needs in IT requirements around human-centred design principles. Knowledge of ServiceNow, Oracle Cloud, Salesforce, and Microsoft 365 an asset.

Digital - Digital business analysis: Ability to support digital business processes across a range of digital projects, programmes, and activities

as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to

jobs.title: Regional Hub Security Associate [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP’s Istanbul Regional Hub is UNDP’s advisory hub for the Europe and the CIS region tasked with the responsibility to provide policy and programmatic support to UNDP’s development activities in the region. Throughout UNDP’s focus areas, it works towards increasing the impact of UNDP’s activities in the region by assisting Country Offices in development of country-level initiatives through advisory services and technical support and by implementing regional-level projects in partnership with a wide range of partners supported to a global network of expertise. Under the leadership of the Manager, the RBEC Regional Hub employs will a multi-disciplinary team of specialists and advisors, project managers, operations and programme support staff.

IRH is a common premises/services with other UN Agencies, including IFAD, UNDCO, UNICEF, UNDSS, and UN Women. Under the immediate supervision of the IRH Operations Advisor, the Regional Hub Security Associate (IRH SA) will provide assistance in the implementation of the security plan and all matters relating to safety and security operations and management. The Regional Hub Security Associate will report to the Regional Security Advisor (RSA) for functional security matters.

Overall, it is important to note that the IRH SA is a local national with vocational experience in security and assists in the implementation of security operations and all matters relating to the management of safety and security for Istanbul Regional Hub personnel

IRH success in its delivery of UNDP programmes is dependent on ensuring an adequate security framework is in place. The Host Government has primary responsibility for the security and protection of personnel employed by United Nations Security Management System organizations, their eligible family members, and property. The IRH security team, in collaboration with UNDP Security Office and regional security staff, reinforces and supplements the capacity of the Host Government where needed to enable ongoing delivery of UNDP programmes, particularly in insecure and unstable environments. Specifically, the IRH SA ensures the integration and mainstreaming of security risk management into IRH Office operations, including incorporation of security considerations into the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all IRH projects and programmes.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Hub Manager and Operations Advisor, the Regional Hub Security Associate implement the establishment of security measures and sound security management at the IRH. Assists in providing security management support to the protection of and minimization of risk to UNDP personnel, property and operations while at the same time enabling UNDP programme delivery throughout the country and/or established project areas. The IRH SA supports the region's country offices when required, including with surge deployment and safety and security training.

The IRH SA may supervise the IRH Office GS security staff and interacts with UN Department of Security and Safety (UNDSS), security partners in other UN agencies, national and local security counterparts, counterparts in Diplomatic missions, NGOs, municipal/civic/religious and traditional leaders to exchange information and implement security programs.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Assist in providing security management support and provide guidance on relevant security policies and regulations to the IRH management through the IRH Operations Advisor to enable effective programme delivery and activities of IRH while protecting and minimizing those risks to UNDP personnel and operations

- Contribute to and conduct security risk management for UN Security Management System (SMS) and UNDP Programmes in designated areas. Assist in mainstreaming security and its costs into all levels of programme design, implementation and delivery by monitoring assigned projects and programmes, under guidance of more senior security staff in the country or region.

- Working closely with more senior security staff in country or region, review the impact of security factors on UNDP Programme design and delivery as well as the potential impact that programmes might have on stability and security. Make recommendations regarding possible security needs and improvements.

- Working in close coordination with more senior staff in the country or region, in conducting of UNDP security risk assessments, and advise the IRH management on security measures for UNDP offices and projects in all locations to address security risks and support their implementation.

- Support the implementation of person-centered security risk management approaches to address specific threats or vulnerabilities in alignment with security assessment results and procedures.

- Provide inputs for UNDSS in preparing country security documents covering areas where UNDP staff, dependents and equipment are present

2.) Support the IRH in implementing the IRH Security Plan, Contingency Plans, Business Continuity Management, and the UN Security Framework

- Coordinate with UNDSS to provide guidance to the IRH security team to ensure availability of updated and adequate procedures for dealing with emergencies involving UNDP staff and operations, in consultation with or guidance from senior security staff in country or region.

- Ensure coordination with the HR Unit in the maintenance and ongoing provision of updated Staff Lists to UNDSS to ensure that all UNDP personnel are covered by relevant Security Plans.

- Formulate and test UNDP specific security and contingency plans of the Istanbul Regional Hub, as needed, and including IRH Business Continuity Plan.

- Conduct / organize , SSAFE, IFAK, Road Safety, fire safety, first aid, and security communications training for the appropriate staff members in coordination with UNDSS or other relevant agencies and provide security orientation training to newly assigned personnel and dependents.

- In coordination with HR, monitor UNDP staff security training compliance

- Provide advice on selection and procurement of appropriate security equipment, and monitor their deployment and functionality

3.) Monitor the security compliance of UNDP IRH premises and international staff residences.

- Provide input to the implementation of physical security and security risk management measures for UNDP IRH premises.

- Conduct periodic appropriate security assessments of UNDP premises and equipment and provide advice on shortfalls in security preparedness with recommended improvements and solutions.

- Represent UNDP security interests, when delegated, in any common premises that UNDP occupies in the country ensuring that staff safety and security are primary considerations

4.) Provide timely and accurate information and briefings to UNDP Management and advice to staff on security procedures, processes and requirements; and maintain contact with security counterparts internally and externally to facilitate the flow of information on important security matters affecting UNDP programmes, the IRH and its personnel.

- Produce and provide substantive input in the preparation of security reports as required by the IRH and the Security Office in a timely and efficient manner.

- For all security and safety related incidents involving UNDP staff and eligible dependents, provide support in coordination with UNDSS and immediately report such incidents to UNDSS in the country as well as to the most senior security staff in the duty station or the UNDP Security Office.

- Maintain, test and implement UNDP IRH security communication systems and processes to ensure integration with UN Security Communication System.

- Coordinate with partner organizations and counterparts to ensure the safety and security of UNDP staff as the highest priority in planning and carrying out missions.

- Represent UNDP at Security Cell and other security meetings as required.

- Contribute to knowledge networks and professional communities

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: May supervise IRH GS security staff

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management competencies:

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Management

- Communication Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Customer Satisfaction/Client Management Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the Organization beyond processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

Security Services

- Security advice, planning and coordination Ability to provide with authoritative advice and guidance on security management, plan and coordinate security activities

- Security information management Analytical capabilities to process diverse security information and develop recommendations

- Security risk management Ability to assess threats and risks, identify and oversee implementation of mitigation measures, including ability to design and test security plans

- Physical/premises security design, implementation and management Ability to conduct accurate premises assessments on UN facilities to ensure appropriate mitigation measures are in place. Ability to design, support the implementation and test physical security systems for UNDP premises

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary Education is required.

- University degree (bachelor’s or master’s equivalent) in Political Science, Military Studies, Security Management, Management or a relevant field will be given due consideration, but is not a requirement

- Applicable security, police and/or military training is desirable

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with high school diploma) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant progressively responsible experience in security, preferably in the military or police context or related field of work. Prior experience with the UN system or an international NGO is desirable.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP.

- Experience in the use of radio communications systems and knowledge of Country security codes is desirable.

- Valid driver’s license is required.

- Having a trainer title in safety and security-related areas such as personal safety, road safety and first aid is desirable.

- Experience in diplomatic security, protection, counter terrorism and intelligence is considered an asset.

- Knowledge of UN regulations, rules, and procedures is an asset.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and Turkish is required.

- Knowledge of another UN language is desirable.

jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde el año 2013, la historia del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) está ligada al establecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, contribuyendo a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17 “Revitalizar la alianza mundial para el Desarrollo Sostenible”, con el propósito de apoyar los esfuerzos de la AMEXCID para transitar hacia un modelo eficaz, que refleje las particularidades de un Cooperante Dual, oferente y receptor de cooperación en sus diversas modalidades, y País de Renta Media Alta, de acuerdo con sus propias prioridades y visión, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible.

En su Tercera Etapa (2019-2025), el Programa de Cooperación promueve que la Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (CID) sea un instrumento para alcanzar las prioridades de desarrollo incluidas en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2019-2024, alineado particularmente al compromiso de “Conducir la política exterior en apego a los principios constitucionales y articulada con las prioridades de la política interna”, siendo la CID uno de los siete principios de la política exterior de México.

Específicamente, se apoyarán los esfuerzos que realiza la AMEXCID para consolidarse institucionalmente, encaminados a desarrollar sus capacidades nacionales, fortalecer su política de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta, así como establecer alianzas estratégicas con otros actores relevantes (como el sector privado, la academia y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, otras agencias de cooperación multilaterales y bilaterales presentes en México que realizan esfuerzos de naturaleza complementaria), por medio de esquemas innovadores de cooperación al desarrollo. Además, se apoyará la contribución de la Agencia a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Lo anterior está orientado a potenciar los 6 ejes de acción de la AMEXCID (diplomacia deportiva; diplomacia en ciudadanía, diplomacia científica y tecnológica; diplomacia económica empresarial; diplomacia educativa; y diplomacia humanitaria), su nueva estructura (coordinación de la política de cooperación internacional; análisis y evaluación de proyectos; implementación de proyectos), así como las prioridades de México como país receptor y país oferente de CID.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1.Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2.Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3.Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4.Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1.Apoyar la coordinación y el seguimiento de procesos administrativos y operativos vinculados con los proyectos e iniciativas de cooperación de la AMEXCID, organizando actividades, responsables, plazos y compromisos de las áreas involucradas.

2.Dar seguimiento a la programación y ejecución de planes de trabajo institucionales, mediante la recopilación de información de avances, identificación de necesidades administrativas y preparación de reportes que faciliten la toma de decisiones.

3.Colaborar en la integración, revisión y organización de expedientes administrativos, oficios, minutas, acuerdos, registros y documentación de respaldo de las actividades y proyectos de la Agencia, conforme a los procedimientos aplicables.

4.Facilitar la coordinación operativa entre las áreas de la AMEXCID y las instituciones públicas participantes en iniciativas de cooperación, apoyando la organización de reuniones, mesas de trabajo y el seguimiento de los acuerdos adoptados.

5.Contribuir a la planeación y organización de recursos, servicios y apoyos logísticos para actividades institucionales y proyectos de cooperación, en coordinación con las unidades responsables y conforme a las disposiciones vigentes.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El/la Asociado/a en Gestión Administrativa y Coordinación de Proyectos de Cooperación formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID o de la dirección general en la que se asigne, responsable de autorizar, coordinar y supervisar los programas, proyectos y acciones que realicen las unidades administrativas y órganos administrativos desconcentrados de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, en temas de cooperación científica, educativa, tecnológica, deportiva, económica y empresarial, en ciudadanía y cultural, de asistencia humanitaria y de ayuda internacional, conforme a las políticas que dicte el Secretario y en concordancia con la Ley de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo y el Programa de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diveraidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos:

- Certificado de preparatoria (Bachillerato), es requisito.

- Estudios universitarios a nivel licenciatura en Administración, Administración Pública, Economía, Contaduría, Ciencias Políticas o áreas afines, no son requisito, pero se les dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con bachillerato: 7 años de experiencia en gestión administrativa, coordinación operativa o servicios institucionales en organizaciones públicas o proyectos.

- Para candidatos/as con título de licenciatura: 4 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en gestión y seguimiento de procesos administrativos, servicios institucionales o actividades operativas de unidades, dependencias o proyectos.

- Experiencia en coordinación entre áreas de trabajo, seguimiento de planes y compromisos, y elaboración de reportes o documentos administrativos.

- Conocimiento de procedimientos y normatividad de la administración pública mexicana aplicables a la gestión institucional y manejo de documentación.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en administración o coordinación operativa de instituciones públicas de los ámbitos federal, estatal o municipal, incluyendo organismos educativos u otras entidades públicas.

- Conocimientos o experiencia en finanzas gubernamentales, control interno, auditoría, solventación de observaciones o procesos de entrega-recepción administrativa.

- Experiencia en organización de equipos, coordinación de personal o seguimiento de actividades institucionales con diversas dependencias y autoridades públicas.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar.

jobs.title: Asociado/a de Género y Finanzas para el Desarrollo
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

La promoción de la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento de las mujeres constituye una dimensión central del mandato del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD). El Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2029 orienta el trabajo de la organización hacia cuatro objetivos estratégicos —prosperidad para todas las personas, gobernanza eficaz, resiliencia ante las crisis y un planeta sano—, impulsados por tres aceleradores del desarrollo humano: la transformación digital y la inteligencia artificial, la igualdad de género y la financiación sostenible. Esta posición se sitúa particularmente en la intersección entre los aceleradores de igualdad de género y financiación sostenible, buscando que las decisiones económicas y financieras contribuyan de manera más explícita a resultados de igualdad.

La Estrategia de Igualdad de Género del PNUD 2026-2029 reconoce que las desigualdades se reproducen también a través de las instituciones, las políticas y las decisiones de financiación. En el marco del acelerador de financiación sostenible, el PNUD plantea apoyar a los países para alinear recursos públicos y privados con la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento económico de las mujeres; movilizar inversión privada hacia empresas lideradas por mujeres y mercados inclusivos; fortalecer las finanzas públicas para generar resultados de igualdad; y promover enfoques integrales vinculados con los Marcos Nacionales Integrados de Financiamiento (INFF), la cartera de Finanzas Públicas para los ODS y otras iniciativas corporativas como Equanomics.

En Ecuador, esta agenda abre oportunidades para fortalecer la incorporación de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, el análisis económico, las finanzas públicas, la inclusión financiera, el financiamiento sostenible y los instrumentos de financiación para el desarrollo. Asimismo, permite ampliar el uso de datos y evidencia económica para comprender las brechas que enfrentan las mujeres en materia de ingresos, empleo, cuidados, pobreza, acceso a activos y servicios financieros, emprendimiento, participación económica y acceso a oportunidades productivas, y traducir esos hallazgos en mejores políticas, programas e instrumentos.

Una prioridad inicial de la posición será apoyar el proyecto “Advancing Fiscal Policy Coherence for Climate, Nature and Inclusive Development in Ecuador”, que busca fortalecer la inteligencia fiscal, la coherencia de políticas y las capacidades institucionales para mejorar la calidad del gasto público y orientar futuras reformas. Tras la reorganización institucional del Ejecutivo, el trabajo se articulará principalmente con el Viceministerio de Economía y Finanzas del Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo, así como con otras instituciones y actores vinculados con la gestión fiscal y financiera desde una perspectiva de género.

El componente de igualdad de género del proyecto busca evitar que el gasto relacionado con clima y naturaleza sea considerado neutral al género. Entre sus prioridades se encuentran la incorporación de criterios sensibles al género en el Clasificador Verde; el desarrollo de una metodología e indicadores para analizar el gasto climático y de naturaleza desde la igualdad de género; el fortalecimiento de esta dimensión en la Coherencia de la Política Fiscal y los procesos vinculados al INFF; y la construcción de una ruta institucional para el Sello de Igualdad de Género o un mecanismo equivalente de fortalecimiento y rendición de cuentas. La hoja de ruta técnica identifica además oportunidades para avanzar en análisis de incidencia fiscal, evaluación ex ante y ex post de medidas fiscales y una mayor utilización de datos desagregados para la toma de decisiones.

De manera complementaria, PNUD Ecuador busca consolidar un portafolio más amplio de género y finanzas para el desarrollo. Esto incluye el acompañamiento a instituciones financieras públicas y privadas para fortalecer productos, servicios, carteras e instrumentos con perspectiva de género; el trabajo con mecanismos de regulación y supervisión financiera; la integración de género en iniciativas de financiamiento de biodiversidad y sostenibilidad, incluido BIOFIN; el fortalecimiento de la inclusión financiera de las mujeres; y la exploración de soluciones como seguros, microseguros, seguros paramétricos, garantías, mecanismos de distribución de riesgos, financiamiento combinado y mercados de capitales. Estos esfuerzos podrán articularse con procesos del Sello de Igualdad de Género para Instituciones Financieras y para el Sello para el Sector Privado, complementando el acompañamiento institucional con una mirada especializada sobre resultados financieros y económicos.

En este contexto, PNUD Ecuador requiere incorporar un/a Asociado/a en Género y Finanzas para el Desarrollo que brinde apoyo técnico especializado al Analista de Género y contribuya, en articulación con el/la Analista de Programa-Economista de la Oficina País, a conectar la igualdad de género con las agendas económicas, fiscales y financieras. La posición tendrá un carácter de análisis aplicado, ejecución técnica, acompañamiento programático y seguimiento, con capacidad para trabajar con datos, indicadores, herramientas cuantitativas y evidencia económica, así como para apoyar el desarrollo de nuevas alianzas e iniciativas en este ámbito.

Acuerdo institucional

La persona contratada estará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Género de PNUD Ecuador. Además, el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto efectuará co-supervisión de esta posición, y la persona contratada trabajará en coordinación técnica con el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de la Oficina País. Asimismo, coordinará con las áreas programáticas y operativas, los equipos de proyecto, las contrapartes nacionales, instituciones financieras, socios, consultores/as y equipos regionales o globales pertinentes. La posición no tendrá responsabilidades de supervisión de personal.

Duties and Responsibilities

Bajo la orientación y supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Género, y en coordinación técnica con el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de PNUD Ecuador, la persona contratada brindará apoyo especializado para fortalecer la integración de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, el análisis económico, las finanzas públicas, el sector financiero y las soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo. Su prioridad será la implementación del componente de género del proyecto de Coherencia de la Política Fiscal, sin perjuicio de apoyar otras iniciativas y oportunidades de la Oficina País relacionadas con género, empoderamiento económico y finanzas. Sus principales funciones y responsabilidades serán las siguientes:

- Apoyar la integración de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, las finanzas públicas y los instrumentos de planificación financiera: Apoyar la incorporación de criterios sensibles al género en los Clasificadores de Gasto del Gobierno Nacional y en las orientaciones, herramientas, reportes y procesos presupuestarios asociados, de manera que el gasto público pueda analizarse también por su contribución a la igualdad de género y al empoderamiento de las mujeres. Contribuir al desarrollo y aplicación de metodologías, indicadores y campos de información para el análisis fiscal sensible al género, incluyendo ejercicios piloto sobre gasto climático, de naturaleza u otras áreas de política pública. Apoyar la integración de la perspectiva de género en los análisis de Coherencia de la Política Fiscal, los procesos del INFF y otros ejercicios de política fiscal, incluyendo análisis de incidencia, impactos diferenciados y opciones de reforma cuando corresponda. Apoyar la construcción e implementación de una ruta institucional con el Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo para fortalecer la gestión fiscal sensible al género, incluyendo el Sello de Igualdad de Género para Instituciones Públicas o un mecanismo alternativo de institucionalización, capacidades y rendición de cuentas. Preparar y dar seguimiento a insumos técnicos, matrices, reportes, reuniones y productos del componente de género del proyecto, en coordinación con el Analista de Género, los equipos responsables, las contrapartes y el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de la CO.

- Desarrollar análisis económicos y cuantitativos para la igualdad de género, el empoderamiento y la inclusión económica de las mujeres: Recopilar, depurar y analizar información económica, social, fiscal y financiera proveniente de encuestas, registros administrativos, bases de datos y otras fuentes, incorporando desagregaciones relevantes para identificar brechas y resultados diferenciados. Apoyar el desarrollo y aplicación de indicadores, métricas, modelos, simulaciones y ejercicios de análisis distributivo o de incidencia que permitan comprender los efectos de políticas, programas e instrumentos económicos y financieros sobre mujeres y hombres. Contribuir a análisis sobre de las mujeres, incluyendo pobreza y pobreza multidimensional, empleo e ingresos, cuidados, acceso a activos, emprendimiento, mercados, crédito y servicios financieros, de acuerdo con las prioridades de la Oficina País. Preparar notas técnicas, visualizaciones, tableros, resúmenes ejecutivos y recomendaciones de política basadas en evidencia, y apoyar iniciativas corporativas o nacionales que vinculen economía e igualdad de género, incluyendo enfoques como Equanomics cuando corresponda.

- Fortalecer la integración de género en el sector financiero y en las soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo: Brindar apoyo técnico a iniciativas con instituciones financieras públicas y privadas, entidades de regulación o supervisión, cooperativas y otros actores del sistema financiero para identificar y reducir brechas de género en productos, servicios, carteras, datos, gobernanza e inclusión financiera. Apoyar los componentes económicos y financieros de procesos del Sello de Igualdad de Género para instituciones públicas o para el sector privado vinculados con entidades financieras, en articulación con los equipos responsables de dichos procesos. Contribuir al diseño o adaptación de instrumentos y soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo con perspectiva de género, incluyendo crédito, garantías, seguros y microseguros, instrumentos paramétricos, mecanismos de distribución de riesgos, financiamiento combinado u otras soluciones pertinentes. Apoyar iniciativas de financiamiento sostenible, biodiversidad y naturaleza, mercados de capitales y otras agendas relacionadas con BIOFIN, banca de desarrollo, bolsas de valores u otros socios, identificando oportunidades para ampliar el acceso de las mujeres a recursos, inversiones y beneficios.

- Apoyar el desarrollo del portafolio, las alianzas y nuevas iniciativas de género y finanzas para el desarrollo: Identificar y sistematizar oportunidades de programación, cooperación y movilización de recursos en la intersección entre igualdad de género, economía y finanzas, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento del pipeline de la Oficina País. Preparar insumos para notas conceptuales, propuestas, términos de referencia, análisis, presentaciones y otros documentos relacionados con nuevas iniciativas de género y finanzas para el desarrollo. Apoyar la articulación técnica con instituciones públicas, entidades financieras, organismos reguladores, sector privado, academia, sociedad civil, organismos internacionales, donantes y otros actores relevantes para desarrollar alianzas y oportunidades de colaboración. Brindar apoyo, cuando sea requerido, a otras áreas y proyectos de la Oficina País en asuntos relacionados con análisis económico, empoderamiento económico, inclusión financiera, política fiscal y financiación para la igualdad de género, dentro del nivel de responsabilidad de la posición.

- Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes: Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos. Brindar apoyo a otras actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción. Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas. Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas.

El/la titular desempeñará otras actividades dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y de la Organización.

Competencies

Competencias organizacionales

Lograr resultados

Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea su trabajo, presta atención a los detalles y entrega un trabajo de calidad dentro del plazo establecido.

Pensar de forma innovadora

Nivel 1: Apertura a ideas creativas; soluciona problemas de forma pragmática y promueve la mejora continua.

Aprender continuamente

Nivel 1: Mentalidad abierta y curiosa; comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores y solicita retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con agilidad

Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja constructivamente la ambigüedad y la incertidumbre y demuestra flexibilidad.

Actuar con determinación

Nivel 1: Muestra interés y motivación; se desempeña con calma en situaciones bajo presión y demuestra confianza en sí mismo/a.

Hacer alianzas y colaborar

Nivel 1: Demuestra empatía y comprensión, trabaja de manera colaborativa y construye relaciones positivas

Propiciar la diversidad y la inclusión

Nivel 1: Valora y respeta las diferencias, reconoce los prejuicios inconscientes y confronta la discriminación.

Competencias multidisciplinarias y técnicas

Área temática: Gestión institucional

Nombre: Trabajar con datos y pruebas

Definición: Capacidad para examinar, depurar, transformar y modelar datos con el objetivo de descubrir información valiosa, orientar conclusiones y fundamentar la toma de decisiones.

Área temática: Agenda 2030: Personas

Nombre: Género

Definición: Datos e investigación sobre igualdad de género.

Área temática: Agenda 2030: Personas

Nombre: Género

Definición: Financiación para la igualdad de género.

Área temática: Agenda 2030: Personas

Nombre: Género

Definición: Economías inclusivas y empoderamiento económico de las mujeres

Área temática: Agenda 2030: Personas

Nombre: Género

Definición: Presupuestos con perspectiva de género

Área temática: Agenda 2030: Asociaciones

Nombre: Financiación de los ODS

Definición: Presupuestos para los ODS.

Área temática: Finanzas

Nombre: Experiencia en financiación del desarrollo

Definición: Capacidad para desarrollar y trabajar con mecanismos e instrumentos de financiación innovadores, como bonos de impacto social o de desarrollo, garantías, financiación climática, etc.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Requisitos mínimos de educación: Título de Bachiller (Educación Secundaria) es requerido. Título universitario de Tercer Nivel (Licenciatura/Ingeniería) en Economía, Finanzas, Estadística, Econometría, Ciencia Políticas, Administración Pública, Desarrollo, Ciencias Sociales será considerado una ventaja, pero no es requisito.

Experience:

Años mínimos de experiencia laboral relevante: Se requieren mínimo seis (6) años (con Educación Secundaria) o tres (3) años (con Título Universitario de Tercer Nivel) de experiencia relevante en análisis económico, financiero, fiscal o cuantitativo con énfasis en género o grupos vulnerables; política pública con énfasis en políticas públicas sociales y/o de género; financiación para el desarrollo e igualdad de género; inclusión financiera para mujeres o grupos vulnerables; o investigación aplicada sociales y/o de género.

Habilidades requeridas (otros conocimientos y capacidades):

- Experiencia en la elaboración de análisis, reportes, notas técnicas o recomendaciones de política en temas económicos, financieros, fiscales o de desarrollo.

- Experiencia en la incorporación de consideraciones de igualdad de género en análisis, políticas, programas, proyectos o investigaciones.

- Experiencia en el manejo avanzado de Microsoft Excel y experiencia con al menos una herramienta de análisis estadístico, programación o visualización de datos, como R, Stata, Python, SPSS, Power BI o equivalente.

- Experiencia en redacción técnica y de presentación de información cuantitativa a audiencias técnicas y no técnicas.

Experiencia y/o habilidades deseables:

- Experiencia en finanzas públicas, presupuestación, política fiscal, análisis de incidencia fiscal, evaluación de impactos de gastos, impuestos y subsidios;

- Experiencia en análisis económico y social con enfoque de género, incluyendo presupuestos sensibles al género, empoderamiento económico de las mujeres, pobreza, mercado laboral, economía del cuidado o desigualdades con perspectiva de género;

- Experiencia en banca de desarrollo, sector financiero, seguros, cooperativas, mercados de capitales, financiamiento sostenible, climático o de biodiversidad;

- Experiencia en diseño o evaluación de instrumentos financieros, simulaciones, modelos económicos o análisis distributivos;

- Experiencia en instituciones públicas, organismos multilaterales, Sistema de Naciones Unidas, entidades financieras.

Disponibilidad para viajar

La persona deberá estar disponible para realizar desplazamientos dentro del territorio nacional cuando las actividades de análisis, coordinación, fortalecimiento de capacidades, trabajo con instituciones financieras o contrapartes y seguimiento técnico lo requieran.

Nota: El salario neto mensual de esta posición es USD 1,867.38 más 8,33% (contribución Seguridad Social).

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

1- Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet.

In Pakistan, UNDP is working with the Government of Pakistan, civil society, national partners, and the people of Pakistan to help find solutions to persistent development challenges. Its work derives from and contributes to four outcome areas of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2023-2027) which include: governance; sustainable, inclusive and green economic transformation; climate change resilience and environment; and gender equality and women’s empowerment. Supported by enablers, UNDP uses a portfolio approach in Pakistan, triangulating structural transformation, leaving no one behind, and building resilience.

UNDP's country programme document for Pakistan envisions that all Pakistani people are educated and healthy, their well-being promoted and protected through economic opportunities, jobs and a climate-resilient future in a country where women and girls are safe and able to exercise their rights and to put their trust in and benefit from improved governance.

UNDP Pakistan works with the Government and communities to develop and implement local solutions to development challenges. In an evolving development context, UNDP supports the efforts of Government of Pakistan to build a more equitable, prosperous, peaceful, and resilient society, and to achieve its SDGs and COP25 targets.

Resilience, Environment and Climate Change Unit (RECCU) is supporting projects across the country to respond to the growing threat of climate change, to mainstream environmental concerns into national development planning processes, and to expand access to environmental and energy services for the poor. In particular, UNDP has sought to ensure that the poor have stronger capacities to manage, adapt, and monitor climate change. Climate Change is a huge development challenge as well as a huge environmental challenge. It is a growing problem and is now hitting the poorest and the most vulnerable first and hardest.

The 2022 floods in Pakistan have affected 33 million people, resulted in the loss of more than 1,700 lives, displaced around 9 million men, women, and children, and inundated almost one-third of productive agricultural land in Pakistan. These downstream challenges are compounded with institutional issues whereby the Government of Pakistan requires support for developing overarching frameworks to structure its flood response activities and technical expertise to set up and develop bankable projects, establish standardized mechanisms for monitoring and evaluation, and enhance strategic communications for public

outreach. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP.

UNDP has responded to the challenge by developing and launching a flagship Flood Recovery Programme (FRP) to support the Government of Pakistan’s flood recovery and rehabilitation efforts. The Programme has four key objectives dealing with the following thematic areas:

- Restoration of housing and access to/revival of essential community services.

- Restoration of livelihoods and income-generating capacities.

- Restoration of governance and service delivery.

- Accelerated environmental clean-up with strengthened capacities for Disaster Risk Management.

2- Scope of Work

The Procurement Officer will report to CO Procurement Specialist with a matrix reporting line to the FRP Operations Specialist and will work in close collaboration with the Programme Unit and project teams for resolving complex Procurement- related issues.

- Provide support to projects in developing TORs and specifications focusing on following results: Provide continuous coaching and support to staff on developing TORs for consultancies, research work and technical services Perform research and market analysis to provide support to requesting units and projects in preparing specifications for goods and assets that are required to be procured. Review and perform quality assurance of TORs and specifications developed by the requesting unit and projects before initiation of procurement process. Build the capacities of staff to develop succinct, crisp and clear TORs for required services and specifications of goods giving details of deliverables, time period, qualification and experience requirements

- Ensure administration and implementation of the operational strategies focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance with procurement activities with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and strategies; implementation of effective internal control, proper functioning of a client- oriented procurement management system Elaboration of proposals and implementation of cost saving and reduction strategies in consultation with office management. Provision of researched information for formulation and implementation of contract strategy and strategic procurement in the CO including tendering processes and evaluation, managing the contract and contractor, legal considerations and payment conditions, sourcing strategy, supplier selection and evaluation, quality management, e-procurement implementation.

3- Organize procurement processes assigned to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support project team in preparation of procurement plan for the project and its implementation and monitoring.

- Organization of procurement processes including preparation and conducting RFQs, ITBs or RFPs, receipt of quotations, bids or proposals, their evaluation, negotiation of certain conditions of contracts in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations.

- Preparation of purchase orders and contracts in and outside Quantum/UNAll, preparation of Recurring purchase orders for contracting of services, vendors’ creation in Quantum/UNAll. Buyers profile in Quantum/UNAll. Review of procurement processes conducted by the project; submissions to the Contract, Asset and Procurement Committee (CAP) and Advisory Committee on Procurement (ACP). Implementation of the internal control system which ensures that purchase orders are duly prepared and dispatched. Timely corrective actions on POs with budget check errors and other problems. Presentation of researched information on procurement in the project. Preparation of cost-recovery bills for the procurement services provided by UNDP to projects. Keep Record and responsible for proper achieving of completed cases at Procurement Unit Database.

4- Ensure implementation of sourcing strategy and e-procurement tools focusing on achievement of the following results

- Development and update of the rosters of suppliers, implementation of supplier selection and evaluation.

- Conduct formal market research through Expression of Interest (EOI), Pre-Qualifications, Request for Information (RFI) and Open Announcements.

- Ensure effective contract management and risk assessment

- Establish contract management group and convene monthly meetings of group.

- Develop automated system alerting contract managers on critical contract dates and milestones and process the contract amendments/extensions/variations when and where required.

- Provide support and guidance to project personnel in contract management and resolving issues and disputes with the contractors/service providers/vendors.

- Manage the contract performance of different vendors and escalate to Head of Procurement regarding occurrences of non-performance by the vendors.

- Manage financial instruments such as bid securities, performance bank guarantees and performance bonds.

- Conduct risk assessment of complex and high value procurement actions for programme and project and devise risk mitigation measures.

- Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Organize and deliver various training/coaching sessions on different Procurement Topics to Project and other operations personnel.

- Organize learning sessions to create awareness about procurement rules and regulations.

- Develop flow charts of procurement methods to demonstrate steps involved and roles and responsibilities of staff.

- Synthesis of lessons learnt and best practices in Procurement.

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

3- Institutional Arrangement

The Procurement Officer will perform her/his duties under a matrix management arrangement. He/she will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP CO Procurement Specialist, with a secondary reporting line to the FRP Operations Specialist.

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is a global organization that is part of the broader United Nations System, dedicated to promoting sustainable development. Established in 1965, UNDP plays a pivotal role in supporting nations in their efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and advance socio-economic development. With a focus on inclusive and equitable growth, UNDP provides technical expertise, mobilizes financial resources, and delivers policy and other services to support the formulation and implementation of effective development strategies and solutions that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates in over 170 countries and territories, collaborating with local partners, governments, and other stakeholders to build resilient communities and foster sustainable development. UNDP's initiatives span a wide range of areas, including climate change, gender equality, governance, and crisis response, embodying its commitment to creating a better and more sustainable future for people across the globe.

The Office of Human Resources (OHR) is part of the UNDP Bureau for Management Services (BMS) of UNDP. It is the anchor of the global HR function for UNDP, providing strategy and policy setting, guidance and oversight. In addition, BMS/OHR provides a broad range of HR advisory and talent management services enabling UNDP to deliver fully integrated development solutions to enable its workforce to deliver more and better results. BMS/OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by developing high quality and innovative human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

With its People for 2030 strategy, OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by strengthening and innovating its human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

Within this innovative, ambitious and dynamic context, BMS/OHR is seeking high calibre HR professionals with a strong HR background, and the capacity, commitment, and attitude needed to drive a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, transformative results, as well as inclusion, respect and trust.

People Programmes and Partnership team (PPP) works to enable a diverse pipeline of people programmes, hereunder Early Talent initiatives and outreach with a vision to nurture the rejuvenation of UNDPs workforce, as well as manifesting itself as a Centre for Excellence in providing solutions and services on Early Talent programmes and Management across UN system agency clients, member states as well as other potential partners.

These programmes include the Junior Professional Officer, Specialist for Development, Graduate Programme as well as Internship and Fellowship Programmes. PPP also manages the Technical Expert Secondment Programme, and it equally engages in designing and developing new people programmes meeting strategic organizational objectives of both UNDP and Partners

Position Purpose

PPP provides end-to-end HR Services to Donors, UN Agencies and staff members hired under these programmes. Hereunder, services on recruitment, assessment and selection, HR services, advisory, learning and career development, partner relations and reporting, and financial oversight.

Under the strategic leadership of the Chief, People Programme and Partnerships (PPP), the HR Specialist will contribute to the development and roll out of the Early Professionals for Impact and Change strategy (EPIC), as well as provides oversight in management of People Programmes (JPO/SDP, Fellowship, Secondment Programmes, and oversight of HR services ensuring their transparency and integrity. The HR Specialist acts as team lead of HR Associates providing HR services to young professionals in both UNDP and 14 partner agencies, and government secondment programmes as well as leads a part-time Learning analyst to deliver learning and development offerings to early professionals. The HR Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and promotes the maintenance of high staff morale and engagement.

The HR Specialist works with a wide range of strategic partners and clients including staff, donor governments, UN partner organizations as well as UNDP offices. The HR Specialist works closely with the OHR HR Business Partners, Talent Development Unit, Talent Acquisition, Deployment and Succession team, People Analytics Unit, GSSU-HR and UNDP hiring offices in delivering client-oriented services in People Programme management, HR service delivery and design of talent acquisition strategies.

UNDP has adopted a portfolio approach to effectively respond to changing business needs and leverage relevant synergies and linkages to achieve its strategic goals. This is in recognition of the interconnected nature of development challenges that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, all UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Effective Oversight of People Programmes.

- Coordinate service innovation on enhanced HR service delivery on people programmes, as well as leveraging emerging business opportunities.

- Contribute to the design and development of new People Programmes.

- Manage, oversee and further refine the implementation of People Programmes (JPO, and others) incorporating partner feedback into programme design and HR service delivery.

- Promote and nurture partnerships across UN Agencies and partner countries as well as other stakeholders engaged in the delivery and development of People Programmes.

- Support and contribute to the finalization, launch and implementation of the Early Professionals for Impact and Change strategy, EPIC.

2. Ensure the delivery of client-oriented HR services for People Programmes to UNDP and partner agencies and facilitate knowledge management.

- Oversee and coordinate HR service delivery and development in HR administration for improved services to PPP/JPOSC Partner countries and UN Agencies.

- Analyse corporate HR strategies and policies, facilitating their implementation and alignment for People Programmes.

- Ensure compliance of HR benefits and entitlements determinations with UNDP rules and regulations, strategies and policies/procedures.

- Advise and guide partner UN Agencies, Stakeholders and HR team on interpretation and application on policies on non-routine cases.

- Provide advisory services and HR Solutions to relevant stakeholders on facilitating complex cases for placements under the People programmes.

- Within delegated authority and in consultation with the Chief/PPP present exceptional considerations and recommendations for approval.

- Coordinate, manage and continue HR business processes review and improvements and ensure development/updated Standard Operating procedures in HR management.

- Actively liaise with relevant UN and UNDP entities to seek policy clarifications and/or aligned procedures ex. GSSC and UN Secretariat.

- Act as approver for benefits and entitlements payments, and discretionary decisions under appliable DOA when required.

- In collaboration with the OHR/PPP Strategic Partnerships and Outreach Specialist, design and implement satisfaction surveys targeting People Programme participants and its main stakeholders.

- Liaise with Payroll and Finance Unit on complicated cases and identify resolutions.

- Identify lessons learned and good practices, ensuring their dissemination across UNDP and integration into programme design and delivery.

3. Coordinate and manage recruitment and career services for People Programmes to UNDP and Partner Agencies.

- Oversee and coordinate the overall recruitment service provision from PPP/JPOSC in partnership with Partner countries and receiving agencies, and UNDP Units.

- Ensure timely, transparent and competitive recruitment and selection processes for all placements under People Programmes

- Ensure alignment of People Programme placements with corporate procedures under UNDPs assessment and selection framework and governing special measures.

- Coordination, planning and oversight of the HR team recruitment activities across partner agencies, UNDP as well as in partnership with sponsoring partner countries.

- Develop and coordinate the HR service provision on end-to-end learning, career and development services under the Formation Journey to early professionals under People Programmes in partnership with Learning Analyst and TDU.

4. Ensure Excellence in the Performance of the People Programmes HR Team and the Learning Analyst.

- Act as Team lead of the People Programmes HR Team ensuring excellence in performance and delivery of end-to-end HR services and HR solutions.

- Supervise the Learning & Development Analyst ensuring excellence in performance and delivery of learning and development activities.

- Motivate team members by creating an engaging work environment, fostering innovation, enable feedback loops and encourage knowledge sharing and professional growth.

- Monitor and assesses the performance of teams responsible in compliance with the UNDP performance management framework.

- Plan, coordinate and oversee workload facilitate redistribution and ideal work-resource balance with the team.

- Promote the building of capabilities in emerging technologies and corporate tools, hereunder how to leverage Generative AI and tools such as UN All, Power BI, etc.
