Background

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP supports sustainable human development in Cuba by focusing on economic, social, and environmental progress. Working alongside the country, UNDP helps implement the National Economic and Social Development Plan through 2030, as well as the objectives of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The organization encourages a dynamic economy, protects social achievements and equity, and promotes practices that ensure the sustainable use of natural resources. This includes advancing renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, and building resilience to climate change and natural disasters.

Guided by national priorities and strategies set with the Cuban government in the Country Programme Document (CPD) and aligned with the United Nations Cooperation Framework, UNDP’s work in Cuba centers on four main areas: Local Human Development, Disaster and Risk, Nature, Climate and Energy, and HIV/AIDS prevention and control. Gender equality is integrated into all these areas. UNDP also promotes decentralized, bilateral, multilateral, and South-South cooperation.

Within the Nature, Climate and Energy (NCE) area, UNDP develops initiatives that align with Cuba’s goals to enhance the conservation and resilience of both natural and built environments. These projects integrate environmental concerns into development plans and economic activities, support environmental finance, and address climate change adaptation and mitigation. Attention to gender and social equity is included throughout these efforts.

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

In Cuba, the SGP began activities in 2005 to support local initiatives in the focal areas of biodiversity, land degradation, and climate change, while generating sustainable livelihoods in communities. Since then, it has provided support to 177 community projects across the country. Project grants have benefited more than 100 Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs).

To ensure the desired environmental, economic, and social quality and impact, the national coordination of the SGP has developed a strong strategic alliance with scientific and academic institutions throughout the country. This has allowed projects to be innovative, characterized by the transfer of technology and knowledge that guarantees environmental sustainability, while also contributing to the fulfillment of national policies and the country’s international commitments.

During the period 2005–2024, projects have addressed three key environmental areas: land degradation, biodiversity conservation and Climate Change. The emphasis of the projects has been focused on:

- The gradual recovery of productive capacity on degraded lands through the implementation of sustainable land management principles, agroecological practices, and the establishment of agroforestry and silvopastoral systems.

- The efficient use of water resources and the conservation of water resources, including the reduction of pollution in watersheds.

- The conservation of terrestrial and marine landscapes, with an emphasis on areas of high value for biological diversity; including the conservation and sustainable use of threatened or high-value species.

- Support for the energy transition in communities and agricultural cooperatives.

- The diversification of livelihoods and subsistence means in rural communities.

Currently, the SGP has two sources of funding to support the implementation of projects in Cuba: the GEF (which is the traditional source that finances the program) and the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (which was recently incorporated).

Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the NCE Programme Officer, the SGP National Coordinator will report to the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist., the SGP National Coordinator will be responsible for the implementation of the overall work of SGP, the SGP Programme Associate/ Assistant, and the National Steering Committee at the country level.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNOPS rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations ( CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

jobs.title: Communications and Partnership Specialist (Open to internal and external applicants)
Strategic Communications, Advocacy and Partnerships Specialist [Open to Internal & External applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

Based in UNDP, the Better Than Cash Alliance (BTCA) is a partnership of over 80 governments, companies and international organizations that accelerates the transition from cash to digital payments in order to reduce poverty and drive inclusive growth by:

- Advocating for the transition from cash to responsible digital payments in a way that advances financial inclusion and promotes responsible digital finance.

- Catalyzing the development of inclusive digital payments ecosystems in member countries to reduce costs, increase transparency, advance financial inclusion-- particularly for women-- and drive inclusive growth; and

- Conducting action research and sharing the knowledge and experiences of our members to inform strategies for making the transition.

Billions of dollars in cash payments and transfers are made daily in emerging and developing economies, including payment of salaries, social welfare and relief, payments to suppliers, remittances, etc. The problems with these cash payments include a lack of transparency, accountability and security, as well as inefficiency. Individuals who receive cash payments are often part of the 1.7 billion excluded from the formal financial sector. This means they are excluded from access to a range of appropriate and affordable financial services to help them save safely take advantage of economic opportunities and reduce their vulnerability to risk.

Shifting these payments from cash to digital has the potential to improve the lives of low-income people, particularly women, while giving governments, the development community and the private sector a more transparent, time and cost efficient, and often-safer means of disbursing payments.

From a corporate perspective, payments completed in the value chain of businesses represent some of the most significant payment flows of national economies. To highlight this impact, the Alliance published a report on “The Future of Supply Chains: Why Companies are Digitizing Payments" showcasing how companies in different business sectors have benefited from digital payments in their supply chains and play an important role in building an inclusive digital payment ecosystem. Thus, the Better Than Cash Alliance is committed to supporting digitization of companies' payment flows in different business sectors across the corporate payment grid (B2B, B2P, B2G, and P2B).

The Better Than Cash Alliance Team’s Core Values are the following:

- Achieving together

- Striving for excellence

- Service oriented

- Results oriented

Through its Strategy 2030, the Alliance seeks to ensure that 100 million more women, young people, micro and small businesses, and displaced and marginalized communities have the choice to use responsible digital payments that improve livelihoods, strengthen resilience and expand economic opportunities. Achieving this ambition requires strong strategic communications, advocacy and partnerships to position responsible digital payments as a development priority, strengthen collaboration with governments, development partners, Alliance members and UNDP Country Offices, and translate evidence into policy dialogue and action.

Under the overall supervision of the Global Advocacy and Communications Specialist, and in close collaboration with programme, partnerships and communications colleagues, the Strategic Communications, Advocacy and Partnerships Specialist will lead strategic communications, advocacy and partnership engagement across the Alliance's priority programmes in Africa, with a primary focus on East and West Africa, while providing strategic communications support to initiatives in Arabic-speaking countries, particularly Jordan and Sudan.

The Specialist will strengthen the Alliance's visibility and influence, foster strategic collaboration with Alliance members, governments, central banks, UNDP Country Offices and development partners, and translate programme evidence into strategic communications, advocacy and policy engagement at country, regional and global levels.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Specialist will drive the implementation of the strategic communications, advocacy and partnership priorities of the Better Than Cash Alliance Strategy 2030, with a primary focus on East and West Africa and strategic communications support to programmes in Arabic-speaking countries, particularly Jordan and Sudan.

The assignment will contribute to:

- Strategic communications, thought leadership and executive positioning;

- Advocacy and policy engagement to advance responsible digital payments;

- Strategic partnerships and stakeholder engagement;

- Country and regional communications support across Africa and the Arab States.

Coordinate the strategic communications, thought leadership and executive positioning.

- Actively contribute to the implementation of the Alliance's strategic communications priorities in alignment with Strategy 2030;

- Develop executive communications, including speeches, talking points, opinion pieces and strategic messaging for senior leadership;

- Coordinate to the development and dissemination of flagship publications, knowledge products and multimedia content across digital and traditional platforms and partner networks to communicate and bring greater visibility to programme results and institutional priorities;

- Collaborate closely with Alliance members, UNDP Country Offices, Regional Bureaux and strategic partners to amplify communications efforts.

Advance advocacy and policy engagement to ensure usage of responsible digital payments.

- Coordinate the implementation of advocacy initiatives that translate implementation evidence into policy dialogue and strategic engagement;

- Coordinate in cooperation with the Head of Communications and Advocacy the Alliance's participation in global and regional policy platforms and initiatives, including the G20, the G7 Partnership, Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and Africa CDC;

- Develop policy briefs, executive briefings, advocacy materials and key messages for high-level engagement;

- Coordinate the planning and delivery of policy dialogues, high-level events and advocacy campaigns;

- Promote the integration of implementation evidence into policy and regulatory discussions.

Strengthen strategic partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

- Collaborate with the Partnerships Specialist to strengthen engagement with Alliance resource members and strategic partners;

- Coordinate joint communications and advocacy initiatives with global and regional partners, including development finance institutions, philanthropies and private sector actors;

- Facilitate collaboration across partners to strengthen programme coherence and collective impact.

Deliver country and regional communications, advocacy and knowledge exchange.

- Coordinate strategic communications and advocacy for priority country programmes, with a focus on East and West Africa and Arabic-speaking countries, particularly Jordan and Sudan;

- Capture, package and translate implementation evidence, country experiences and lessons learned into strategic communications, advocacy and knowledge products;

- Facilitate knowledge exchange across Alliance members to support policy dialogue, peer learnings and internal organizational learning.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Institutional Arrangements

The Strategic Communications, Advocacy and Partnerships Specialist will be recruited by the Better Than Cash Alliance and will report to the Global Advocacy and Communications Specialist.

The Specialist will work in close collaboration with programme, partnerships and communications colleagues across the Alliance Secretariat, UNDP Regional Bureaux, UNDP Country Offices, Alliance members and strategic partners.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively identify opportunities, mitigate risks and develop innovative solutions to complex challenges.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand knowledge and promote continuous learning.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Champion change and respond effectively in evolving environments.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate barriers and achieve strategic results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Demonstrate political acumen, cultivate strategic relationships and foster collaboration across institutions and sectors.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Champion inclusive approaches and promote diversity.

Cross Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction and Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

External Relations & Advocacy – Communications

- Advocacy strategy and implementation Ability to create and implement advocacy strategies which lead to impactful change.

Communications

- Media Relations Ability to develop media relations across all aspects of media work including relationships with media and preparing media materials such as messages.

- Campaign management Ability to produce and implement communications and advocacy campaigns which lead to impactful change.

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

- Strategic Engagement Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Communications, Journalism, International Relations, Public Policy, Development Studies, Political Science or another relevant field. OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the above fields, combined with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 5 years (with a Master's degree) or 7 years (with a Bachelor's degree) of progressively responsible experience in strategic communications, advocacy, partnerships or stakeholder engagement.

Required Skills

- Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing strategic communications and advocacy initiatives in the field of international development is required;

- Experience building and managing partnerships with governments, development partners, donors and international organizations is required;

- Experience in supporting high-level stakeholder engagement, policy dialogue and institutional positioning is required.

Desired Skills

- Experience in developing communications products for resource mobilization, partnership development and institutional positioning is highly desirable.

- Experience working with Africa and/or the Arab States region is highly desirable

- Experience working with UNDP, UN agencies or multilateral organizations, including collaboration with Country Offices or regional bureaux, is desirable.

- Experience in communicating on digital financial inclusion, responsible digital payments, digital public infrastructure, women's economic empowerment or digital transformation is desirable;

- Experience designing and delivering strategic communications campaigns, high-level events and knowledge products for international audiences is an asset.

Languages

Professional Certificates

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background and Organizational Context

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC) is part of UNV's Management Services, supporting ever growing number (over 15,000 in 2025) and providing timely and high-quality delivery of services on volunteer HR pre-assignment activities, contract administration, payroll, and evacuation UN Volunteers assigned to agencies, funds, and programs, and UN missions throughout the UN system.

With a presence in nine locations globally, VSC ensures timely and high-quality delivery of services in volunteer HR pre-assignment activities, contract administration, payroll, and evacuation support.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS) and other relevant sections at Headquarters, Regional Offices, Field Units, and the UNDP Global Shared Service Centre (GSSC) to deliver seamless, consolidated services in accordance with UN Volunteers Conditions of Service, regulations, policies, and best practices. In delivering its functions, VSC also liaises with UNDP Country Offices, other UN Agencies, Service Centers and operations counterparts.

Position Purpose

Reporting to the Deputy Chief, VSC, the Operations Analyst manages day-to-day activities of the integrated volunteer management pillar, with a focus on timely and quality delivery of volunteer deployment and lifecycle management services. S/he oversees the work of regional teams outposted to multiple locations, monitors service risks and supports consistent application of agreed workflows, validation points and escalation arrangements. The incumbent works in close collaboration with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders contributing to the provision of operational services to candidates, UN Volunteers and their host entities. The Operations Analyst promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and supports the maintenance of high-quality service delivery and client satisfaction.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

Oversight of volunteer deployment

- Coordinate and monitor the timely provision of volunteer deployment services as per business objectives and key performance indicators (KPIs);

- Monitor deployment speed across regional portfolios; identify bottlenecks and propose improvement measures for consistent application;

- Support consistent implementation of agreed workflows and validation points related to UN Volunteer deployment globally.

Oversight of volunteer lifecycle management

- Coordinate and monitor the quality and timeliness of volunteer lifecycle administration, including hiring, contract management and separation as per corporate policies, procedures and key performance indicators (KPIs);

- Ensure timely follow-up on open items and complex cases; Identify operational hurdles, queue and backlog patterns and recurring issues, and propose improvements to workflows and controls;

- Support consistent implementation of agreed workflows and validation points related to volunteer lifecycle management globally.

Coordination of payroll impacting lifecycle actions

- Coordinate with VSC Payroll Team to support timely and accurate handover of lifecycle actions with payroll impact, including effective dates, extensions, separations, funding updates and retroactive changes;

- Support first-line validation of lifecycle data before payroll-impacting actions are triggered, in line with agreed workflows and escalation arrangements;

- Ensure timely follow-up on open items and operational cases, escalating complex, sensitive or policy-related matters to the Deputy Chief, as required;

- Monitor open items originating from lifecycle administration and ensure timely follow-up or escalation through agreed coordination channels;

- Coordinate with the VSC Payroll Team on communications and process interfaces lifecycle actions impacting payroll, without assuming functional ownership of payroll processing, validation, reconciliation or controls.

Ensure Performance monitoring and operational analysis

- Monitor and analyze volunteer lifecycle performance data, including deployment pipeline, queue ageing, transaction volumes, backlogs, service timeliness, exceptions and regional trends;

- Support first-line monitoring of compliance with agreed workflows, validation points, SOPs and escalation protocols across volunteer lifecycle processes.

- Identify operational bottlenecks, recurring issues, workload imbalances and service risks across lifecycle stages, and propose practical corrective actions to improve timelines, quality and consistency;

- Manage planned and ad hoc reporting inputs related to volunteer lifecycle management, in coordination with relevant VSC teams and technical counterparts;

- Produce timely and accurate inputs to section-level reporting, corporate monitoring and audit requirements, as they relate to volunteer deployment and contract administration and post EOD lifecycle actions;

- Contribute to improving reporting requirements, dashboards, data quality and workflow monitoring to strengthen visibility, accountability and evidence-based operational management

- Provide inputs on policies, processes, workflow streamlining, system enhancements, optimization and automation in coordination with relevant subject matter experts;

- Keep abreast of relevant trends and benchmarks in areas related to deployment, contracting and administration of personnel and use these insights to support continuous improvement of VSC service delivery;

- Contribute to the analysis of the integrated volunteer management services results by region and portfolio, report on trends and propose operational adjustments to improve workload distribution, service quality and delivery timelines.

Facilitate knowledge building and knowledge sharing

- Lead knowledge management efforts for volunteer lifecycle management, including capturing lessons learned, compiling and updating internal guidance materials, and overseeing; maintenance of the content of the internal knowledge management platform, in coordination with relevant VSC teams;

- Co-create and facilitate local onboarding process of new personnel, leveraging corporate tools, in close consultation and coordination with direct supervisors;

- Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in personnel management;

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Direct supervision of 3 GS staff (Team Leads) with indirect oversight of about 40 GS staff at multiple locations. Responsible for creating an empowering work environment, performance management, and capacity development, as well as establishing and monitoring the implementation of annual work plans for the teams.

Education

- Advance University degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Human Resources, Finance or related field is required. or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in human resources operations, personnel administration, service delivery or related operational areas in a multilateral organization at the global, regional or national level is required;

- Experience in coordinating operational workflows and transaction processing in a high-volume service environment is required;

- At least 2 years recent supervisory responsibility in a diverse environment is required;

- Experience in the usage of office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and cloud-based ERP systems is required; working knowledge of Salesforce Service Cloud or a similar service management system would be an asset.

- Familiarity with HR policies, contractual modalities, conditions of service or administration of non-staff contract modalities within the UN system is desirable;

- Work experience in a shared service centre or geographically dispersed operational environment is desirable.

Achieve Results:

Think Innovatively:

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Justiça 4.0 é um dos maiores programas do mundo de transformação digital do Poder Judiciário. Iniciado em 2020, fruto de um acordo de cooperação firmado entre o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD/ONU), o projeto visa desenvolver e aprimorar soluções tecnológicas para tornar os serviços oferecidos pela Justiça brasileira mais eficientes, eficazes e acessíveis à população, além de otimizar a gestão processual para magistrados(as), servidores(as), advogados(as) e demais atores do sistema de Justiça. A iniciativa também dialoga com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e com a Agenda 2030 da ONU.

Para mais informações sobre o programa, acesse o site do Justiça 4.0.

Duties and Responsibilities

O(A) profissional atuará no projeto Inteligência de Dados no âmbito do Programa Justiça 4.0. O foco do trabalho é a estruturação de dados processuais, incluindo a implantação e o fomento ao uso do DataJud e do Codex, além da produção de diagnósticos e painéis de transparência. A atuação será em estreita articulação com as equipes do CNJ e do PNUD, visando o saneamento e a qualificação da Base Nacional de Dados do Poder Judiciário (DataJud), instituída pela Resolução CNJ nº 331/2020.

As atividades previstas para este posto incluem:

- Engenharia e tratamento de dados: a. Extrair, limpar e tratar grandes volumes de dados de diversas fontes utilizadas pelo CNJ. b. Estruturar e organizar as diferentes fontes de dados para garantir consistência entre eles.

- Diagnóstico e qualidade de dados: a. Identificar ativamente inconsistências, anomalias e falhas nas bases de dados. b. Desenvolver e implementar soluções técnicas e rotinas para corrigir as inconsistências encontradas. c. Projetar soluções escaláveis para correção contínua e enriquecimento das bases de dados, elevando o padrão de qualidade da informação.

- Análise de dados e geração de relatórios: a. Produzir relatórios, painéis e dashboards com estatísticas descritivas. b. Utilizar visualizações de dados como gráficos, tabelas e mapas para comunicar resultados de forma eficaz.

- Modelagem estatística e preditiva: a. Elaborar e aplicar modelos preditivos e/ou de classificação para extrair insights e apoiar a tomada de decisão. b. Contribuir tecnicamente para a elaboração de diagnósticos complexos e estudos estatísticos do CNJ.

- Suporte técnico e transferência de conhecimento: a. Articular-se com os pontos focais do CNJ e do PNUD, prestando suporte técnico na implementação do projeto. b. Sistematizar novas metodologias para facilitar a transferência de tecnologia e conhecimento ao CNJ. c. Homologar ferramentas e sistemas para validar as entregas do projeto.

O titular desempenhará outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

A pessoa contratada será supervisionada pela Gerência de Projetos e pela Coordenação Técnica de Projetos.

Pensamento Inovador: NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, é pragmático para resolver problemas, faz melhorias

Aprendizagem Contínua: NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar com Agilidade: NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se à mudança, lida de forma construtiva com a ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Atuar com determinação: NÍVEL 1: Mostra determinação e motivação, capaz de entregar com calma diante da adversidade, confiante

Engajar-se e ser Parceiro: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão para com os outros, forma relacionamentos positivos

Promover Diversidade e Inclusão: NÍVEL 1: Apreciar/respeitar as diferenças, consciente do preconceito inconsciente, confrontar a discriminação

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios | Pensamento Estratégico

Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e Estratégia de Negócio | Perspicácia Empresarial

Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização.

Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de Negócios | Gestão de projetos

Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Capacidade de inspecionar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, informando conclusões e apoiando a tomada de decisão.

Office/Unit/Project Description

At country level, the UNV Field Unit (FU) and/or designated UNV personnel are responsible for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes in the areas of peace, development and humanitarian assistance.  UNV Field Units/designated UNV personnel represent and position UNV in the respective countries with a focus on the UN Country Team, bringing UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners within a client service approach and collaborating with other stakeholders from government, civil society and private sector. As UNDP represents UNV at country level, UNV personnel are usually hosted within a UNDP Office and are accountable to the Supervisor and UNV Executive Coordinator for compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations

Scope of Work

- Assist in mobilizing volunteers and developing and maintaining partnerships

- Support in the management of key accounts of assigned partnerships.

- Support and maintain relationships with assigned UN partner/s in the country/countries to ensure an understanding of UNV’s mandate, key offers and the added value that UN Volunteer assignments bring in support to the achievement of their respective mandates.

- Support in the identification of volunteer placement opportunities based on UN agency strategies and plans and present UNV value proposition and volunteer modalities with the objective of maximizing the relevance of volunteerism for impact.

- Support in the preparation of descriptions of assignment, with a focus on the assigned partners.

- Support in the development of offers and initiatives that respond to the evolving needs of partners for volunteer solutions.

- Contribute to the organization of advocacy campaigns, key events and other external communication efforts that raise awareness and foster engagement.

- Ensure knowledge is documented, systematized and fed back into volunteer mobilization, using UNV's Client Relationship Management (CRM) to track interactions and updates.

- In consultation with the Online Volunteering (OV) Programme Associate in the respective Regional Office, act as a focal point for online volunteers and accreditation of OV service organizations, focusing on supporting host entities with developing OV opportunities through advocacy engagements and promoting the concept of OV.

2. Contribute to business intelligence in support of strategic and sustained mobilization

- Support partnerships development by collecting and analyzing data of UN Cooperation Frameworks and agency programming frameworks to identify volunteer engagement areas.Record volunteer mobilization opportunities and business intelligence in CRM.

- Support in the engagement with potential partners by preparing presentations, mapping etc. on opportunities for volunteerism for internal use by UNV.

- Support the identification of opportunities for communicating on positive volunteer stories and strengthening visibility of the Agency partnership and the impact of volunteerism.

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

- Assist in gathering feedback from volunteers through surveys or informal check-ins and help compile and share insights to inform improvements in volunteer management practices.

- Support the organization of appreciation initiatives and local events to acknowledge volunteer contributions and foster a sense of belonging.

- Support the Country Coordinator in ensuring volunteers’ satisfaction with their assignment.

- Backstop other functions in the Field Unit/at country level during peak periods or personnel absences, ensuring continuity of service and contributing to a seamless and positive volunteer experience.

4. Support duty of care of UN Volunteers serving in the assigned area

- Liaise with the respective entities’ security focal points or heads of office, as applicable, and provide support to ensure a detailed and precise understanding among UN Volunteers on all security-related issues, including e.g. assistance with headcounts in emergency situations.

- Provide timely and accurate support to UN Volunteers undergoing medical evacuation, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV, while maintaining compliance with established procedures.

- Provide tailored support to UN Volunteers who do not speak the UN official language, to facilitate their understanding and providing key information, and navigate their assignment environment effectively throughout the volunteer management cycle.

- Provide host entities with comprehensive information on the enabling instruments available through UNV that support the health and wellbeing of UN Volunteers, such as insurance and related benefits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the general guidance of the Regional Manager, with day-to-day reporting to the Country Coordinator, the Client Engagement Assistant supports the identification, development, and cultivation of select partnerships with UN Agencies / Host Entities at country level. This includes managing the relationship with priority partners, gathering and sharing data and information that influence mobilization opportunities, ensuring client satisfaction with volunteer services, and bridging the delivery of services from centralized functions of the volunteer management cycle. The critical purpose of this role is the sustained mobilization of volunteers to the designated partners (clients) and support to the duty of care for serving volunteers.

The role involves regular contact and liaison with counterpart UN personnel at all levels, including senior level staff. Within UNV, all personnel are expected to work across multiple units, functions, and teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP provides support to the Solomon Islands Country Coordinating Mechanism (SICCM) to enable it to effectively fulfil its governance, oversight and coordination responsibilities for Global Fund investments.

The SICCM brings together government, civil society, communities affected by HIV, tuberculosis and malaria, technical partners and other stakeholders to guide and oversee the country’s coordinated engagement in the response to the HIV, TB and Malaria, supported by the Global Fund. The CCM Secretariat plays a central role in ensuring that the SICCM operates effectively, transparently and inclusively and that its decisions are implemented and followed up in a timely manner.

The Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM[1]) is a national committee of voluntary members that submits funding applications to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, oversees the grants on behalf of their country and ensures alignment with the national response. The Secretariat of a CCM facilitates the mandate and supports the CCM in both the execution of its decisions and coordination of its activities. The roles and responsibilities of the CCM Secretariat shall be to assist the CCM to execute its core functions in the areas of Oversight, Engagement, Positioning and Operations.[2]. The Country Coordination Mechanism (CCM) agreement was launched in August 2016 with Global Fund to provide Secretarial Support to Solomon Islands Country Coordination Mechanism.

The Executive Officer will work under the contractual and administrative supervision of the UNDP Country Manager or designated UNDP supervisor. The incumbent will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the SICCM Chair, in consultation with the Vice-Chair and Executive Committee, and will support the SICCM General Assembly in implementing its approved decisions. The annual performance assessment will be completed by the designated UNDP supervisor, informed by documented feedback from the SICCM Chair.

Under direct supervision of designated UNDP supervisor in Solomon Country Office, and programmatic reporting to UNDP Effective Governance Team Lead and in consultation with the SICCM Executive headed by the CCM Chair and other responsible parties, the Executive Officer will be responsible for supporting the CCM in the overall implementation of its mandate. The Executive Officer leads as CCM Secretariat and is accountable to the CCM. Through the coordination of various donor and partner resources the CCM Secretariat supports the CCM to effectively implement a national disease strategy that pursues the goal of ending the diseases as pandemics by 2030. The CCM Secretariat facilitates the work of the CCM by enabling an effective governance mechanism using highly proficient political and technical skills. They maintain a repository of CCM documents, mediate in areas of dispute amongst members and act as an advisor for the CCM in-country. They also serve as a bridge between national stakeholders and the Global Fund Secretariat.

The Executive Officer is expected to provide strong and proactive support to the CCM members, exercise sound judgment, anticipate and address operational and governance challenges, and ensure timely follow-up on CCM decisions and commitments. The role requires a high degree of initiative, diplomacy and political awareness, as well as the ability to build trust and work effectively with senior government officials, civil society and community representatives, Principal Recipients, development partners and the Global Fund.

[1] For purposes of this paper, CCMs includes Regional Coordinating Mechanisms (RCMs) as further defined in the CCM Policy.

[2] Definitions of the four core areas can be found here https://www.theglobalfund.org/en/country-coordinating-mechanism/evolution/

Duties and Responsibilities

The Executive Officer receives strategic and day-to-day functional guidance from the SICCM Leadership Chair/Vice Chair and supports the implementation of decisions of the CCM General Assembly. Administrative supervision, performance assessment, leave approval, and contractual oversight are the responsibility of the designated UNDP supervisor. In addition the SICCM Secretariat/Executive Officer serves the SICCM as well as its appointed committees. The Secretariat is under the direct supervision of the Chair of the SICCM

Scope of Work – Key areas of Responsibilities

- Operations – Serve as the CCM Secretariat and support the operational structures of the CCM.

- Oversight - Enhance efficiency of oversight procedures as per Global Fund processes

- Positioning - Facilitate political discussions and strengthen sustainability efforts

- Engagement – Foster meaningful, inclusive and active participation of key stakeholders

Operations: Contribute to the effective functioning of the SICCM

- Plan, coordinate and document SICCM General Assembly, Executive Committee and other standing or ad hoc committee meetings, including preparation of agendas and papers, logistical arrangements, minutes, decision records and follow-up actions.

- Respond to the operational needs of the CCM particularly supporting CCM leadership, including ensuring all members are knowledgeable about Global Fund strategic and technical directives and guidelines, and enabling member engagement as required (coordinating logistics, facilitating participation and circulating minutes).

- Serve as the Secretariat in supporting CCM members and fulfilling its obligations to the Global Fund such as financial reporting on CCM funding and adherence to CCM eligibility requirements.

- Proactively identify operational, governance and coordination issues that may affect the effective functioning of the CCM; propose practical solutions to CCM leadership; and ensure that agreed actions and decisions are followed through in a timely manner. S

- Support CCM committees: those that are permanent (e.g., executive, oversight, governance) and temporary (e.g., elections).

- On a continuous basis, document information regarding CCM operations and ensure robust management of key documents.

- Provide support to the Global Fund Country Team and other stakeholders from the Global Fund, for example, Board members and parliamentarians from donor countries, working towards the common goal of ending the three diseases as pandemics by 2030.

Oversight: Support effective grant oversight and access to funding

- Under the CCM leadership, support all relevant aspects of the Global Fund access to funding processes - national strategic plan, gap analysis, request for funding design stages through the final signature of Global Fund grants by Principal Recipients (PRs) - and ensure that all processes are documented, led and informed by appropriate data-based decision-making.

- Support the oversight committee in its mandate of gathering and analyzing grant and national data and developing recommendations to CCM leadership to resolve bottlenecks or suggest solutions such as technical cooperation needs. In transitioning contexts, support the oversight committee in overseeing transition workplans and implementation of transition readiness assessment recommendations.

- Accompany the CCM through the process to access Global Fund support, including coordinating the country dialogue and PR selection process. The funding request will be aligned to the country context and global goals to end the pandemics.

- After the grant-making process, in partnership with the Global Fund Country Team and with the relevant resources from the CCM Secretariat team, oversee a “knowing your grant” orientation of the CCM.

- Advocate on behalf of national stakeholders and CCM members on areas of Global Fund-related requirements linked to accessing the country’s full Global Fund grant allocation. This includes the country adhering to co-financing commitments and/or PRs improving grant performance.

Positioning: Ensure coordination, sustainability and transition

- Develop proposals for the CCM leadership and the Global Fund on the appropriate positioning of the CCM and document the necessary linkages between the CCM and all other significant coordinating platforms in the country. The main purpose being to support harmonization and strengthened efficiency (both in terms of governance bodies and in the fight against the three diseases). In countries where a disease component/s is preparing for or transitioning from Global Fund financing, focus on documenting links to other platforms that are relevant to transition preparedness, planning and implementation.

- Attend and support other national health platforms to help convey the views of the CCM and also to identify synergies in the coordination of health and donor investment.

- Facilitate the CCM’s role in sustainability and transition planning and implementation, including ensuring strong inclusion of civil society and participating in efforts to strengthen sustainability of Global Fund investments.

Engagement: Facilitate inclusive and informed stakeholder participation and knowledge management

- Work with the Global Fund Country Team, PRs and CCM to discuss Global Fund communications, and guide the CCM on their implications for actions and relevant adjustments.

- Engage with senior government officials to promote the role of the CCM in the national health landscape. • Ensure that credible and verified community input on the CCM is brought to high-level government discussions in order to drive a more informed response to the three diseases.

- CCM decisions and agreed actions are systematically tracked and followed up, with delays, bottlenecks and issues requiring leadership attention identified and escalated in a timely manner.

- Carry out additional tasks under all the above-mentioned functional areas as requested by the CCM, according to its context and threshold level.

Background/ Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end poverty, inequality and climate change, working in more than 170 countries.

The Regional Bureau for Africa (RBA) provides strategic direction, quality assurance and oversight across UNDP's 46 Country Offices in sub-Saharan Africa. Its Regional Programme Document (RPD) 2026–2029, anchored in the African Union's Agenda 2063 and the Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan — the "decade of acceleration" — pursues four outcomes: Prosperity, Governance, Crisis Prevention and Resilience, and Planet. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) — digital identity, payments and data exchange — is a foundational enabler across all four. It provides the digital rails for AfCFTA implementation and for SME and youth access to markets and credit; underpins RPD Output 2.4 on digital and AI policy for safe, secure public service delivery; enables risk-informed social protection and digital health; and strengthens natural resource governance and just energy transitions.

The Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub is UNDP's global centre of excellence for digital transformation, providing technical advisory, capacity building and programmatic support to Regional Centres and Country Offices. Within it, the DPI Safeguards Team ensures Africa's foundational digital rails are built with protection and equity at their core, so that scaling DPI does not deepen inequality or compromise human rights.

The position sits within the DPI Safeguards Team and is the operational bridge between the DAI Hub and RBA. It translates the RPD's digital ambition into country-level delivery — embedding safeguarding-by-design across the regional DPI portfolio, supporting country readiness assessments and national implementation roadmaps, and mobilizing partnerships and financing for the Africa DPI Accelerator.

Delivery spans 46 diverse country contexts — Anglophone, Francophone, Lusophone and Arabic-speaking, several fragile or crisis-affected — with uneven digital maturity, politically sensitive data governance environments, and multiple sovereign and continental stakeholders. The role is home-based and requires remote engagement across time zones.

Duties and Responsibilities

Lead strategic design and alignment of the regional DPI portfolio

- Align the Africa DPI Accelerator with the RPD 2026–2029, embedding digital ID, payments and data exchange in the Prosperity and Governance outcomes through a use-case-led approach across health, financial inclusion, livelihoods, agriculture, climate and digital trade. Contributes to: RPD Outcomes 1 and 2; AU Digital Transformation Strategy and Agenda 2063 Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan.

Lead country readiness and national implementation roadmaps

- With the DAI Hub readiness assessment lead, programme-manage DPI readiness assessments in priority countries, identify programmatic entry points to close the digital divide, and support national implementation roadmaps.

- Contributes to: Country Office programming across 46 offices; national digital transformation strategies; SDG acceleration.

Safeguarding-by-design across the DPI lifecycle

- Integrate universal DPI safeguards — data privacy, digital rights, inclusive governance — into country implementation plans from design through maintenance, and standardize repeatable protocols across Country Offices.

- Contributes to: RPD Outcome 2 (Governance) and Output 2.4; UNDP Universal DPI Safeguards Framework and the global DPI Safeguards agenda; UNDP Social and Environmental Standards.

Provide high -level technical advisory and regional intelligence

- Advise RBA leadership and Country Offices on responsible DPI and AI deployment, generate evidence on how DPI accelerates sectoral results, and track global and regional DPI trends, innovations and emerging risks.

- Contributes to: RPD target of 15 regional and national institutions strengthened by 2029; RBA knowledge leadership and UNDP's global DPI positioning.

Build strategic partnerships, knowledge management and sustainable financing

- Build alliances with the AU, RECs and Smart Africa to harmonize cross-border digital policy and interoperability standards; mobilize resources through concept notes, proposals and blended finance; and leverage timbuktoo to connect startups and tech hubs to national DPI projects and capital. Advise on knowledge building and sharing.

- Contributes to: AfCFTA implementation; RPD resource mobilization targets; timbuktoo and the Digital Public Goods Alliance, Co-Develop, GovStack and 50-in-5 communities; South-South and triangular cooperation.

Ensure Institutionalization and sustainability

- Curate regional DPI intelligence for the "State of DPI in Africa" agenda, convene a regional community of practice, and design the roadmap for transitioning the DPI Accelerator from a catalytic programme into a permanent regional facility.

- Contributes to: sustainability of the Africa DPI Accelerator beyond 2028; integration of DPI safeguards into UNDP's core service offer.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Digital Public Infrastructure Advisor – Africa reports directly to the Director, Regional Programme for Africa (RBA) and to the Director, AI Hub and Head of Digital and AI Programmes.

As an RBA-anchored position, the Director, Regional Programme for Africa is the primary supervisor, responsible for setting priorities, approving workplans and conducting performance assessment. The Director, AI Hub and Head of Digital and AI Programmes provides second-level reporting, ensuring technical coherence with UNDP's global digital, AI and DPI safeguards standards. The incumbent maintains regular coordination and information sharing with the DAI Hub, including the DPI Safeguards Team, so that regional delivery remains aligned with global methodologies and the Hub's work benefits from regional evidence.

The incumbent works in close collaboration with RBA regional programme teams and the 46 Country Offices in sub-Saharan Africa, DAI Hub technical teams, and relevant continental and regional partners. The position carries no supervisory responsibilities but is expected to lead joint RBA–DAI workstreams and task teams on a matrix basis.

The position is home-based.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

- Human Development

- Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

- Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrates its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities

INSIGHT

To translate Indonesia’s ambitious climate and digital transition priorities into concrete action, UNDP Indonesia partners with national institutions to build robust, scalable financing enablers. A cornerstone of this effort is the Institutional Strengthening for Indonesian Environment Fund Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT) Project, which bridges high-level policy advice with practical, localized execution.

The Institutional Strengthening for Indonesian Environment Fund Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT) Project is implemented by UNDP in partnership with IEF/BPDLH, with financial support from the Government of Norway. The project runs through 31 August 2028 and seeks to strengthen IEF/BPDLH as a trusted, accountable and internationally credible climate and environmental financing institution capable of mobilizing, managing and governing increasingly diverse sources of finance.

The Indonesian Environment Fund, or Badan Pengelola Dana Lingkungan Hidup (IEF/BPDLH), is Indonesia’s national environmental financing institution and a Public Service Agency under the Ministry of Finance. I IEF/BPDLH mobilizes, manages, invests and channels domestic and international finance for climate action, environmental protection and sustainable development. Its role supports Indonesia’s RPJMN 2025–2029 priorities, Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution and FOLU Net Sink 2030 agenda. As the scale and complexity of its portfolio grows, IEF/BPDLH is expected to maintain governance, fiduciary, environmental and social safeguards, transparency, data, monitoring, reporting and accountability systems that are consistent with evolving national and international standards. It manages grants, revolving funds, Results-Based Contributions, and other financing arrangements serving national programmes and community-level initiatives. Its institutional credibility therefore depends on the consistent application of appraisal, financial management, safeguards, data governance, portfolio management, and public accountability arrangements across a diverse portfolio.

INSIGHT addresses institutional transformation at three interconnected levels: the enabling environment, including policies, regulations, mandates and inter-institutional relationships; organizational capacity, including governance, systems, processes, structures, resources and accountability mechanisms; and individual capacity, including leadership, technical competencies, skills, knowledge and organizational behavior. The project emphasizes practical application, institutional ownership, and sustainability rather than stand-alone policies, systems, or training products.

The INSIGHT project is implemented by UNDP. and housed under the Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) Unit. Day to day management is carried out by a Project Management Unit (PMU) led by a National Project Manager, who reports to the Head of the HDRG Unit or delegated authority and is supported by technical and operational staff to ensure effective delivery, compliance, and coordination across project activities.

Scope of Work

The INSIGHT project is implemented by UNDP and housed under the Human Development and Responsive Governance HDRG) Unit, Day to day management is carried out by a Project Management Unit (PMU) led by a National Project Manager, who reports to the Head of the HDRG Unit or delegated authority and is supported by technical and operational staff to ensure effective delivery, compliance, and coordination across project activities.

The Chief Technical Advisor reports to the Deputy Resident Representative and matrix manager to the Head of Unit of the and works closely with IEF/BPDLH counterparts, relevant government institutions, UNDP technical and operations units, project personnel, consultants and institutional service providers. The position may coordinate technical contributors assigned to the relevant workstreams but does not hold overall project accountability; approve financing, accreditation, procurement or institutional decisions; certify expenditure; or acceptcontractual deliverables outside delegated authority.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative and matrix manager to Team Leader/Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) and close coordination with National Project Manager, the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) will perform the following five key functions:

Provide senior technical and strategic advice on climate and environmental finance

- Advise UNDP and IEF/BPDLH on climate and environmental finance priorities, institutional financing architecture and strategic linkages with national and international initiatives.

- Coordinate technical work on programme and project appraisal, including fiduciary, environmental and social safeguards, gender, results, sustainability and conflict-of-interest requirements.

- Coordinate accreditation-readiness planning, gap tracking, cross-directorate evidence generation and quality review without performing independent accreditation assessments or replacing specialist reviewers.

- Support readiness reviews and decision-gate documentation for priority financing mechanisms or windows, including applicable legal, fiduciary, safeguards, gender, monitoring, grievance, operational and financing conditions.

- Advise on qualified investment-pipeline development, eligibility and appraisal standards, risk considerations, institutionalization and potential funding sources.

- Contribute technical specifications and terms of reference and support technical review of deliverables within assigned authority and UNDP procedures.

Lead strategic stakeholder engagement and ecosystem coordination

- Maintain a strategic stakeholder, and partnership plan linked to financing, institutional strengthening, accountability and resource mobilization.

- Coordinate inter-institutional processes involving IEF/BPDLH, and other key actors such as the Coordinating Ministry of Food Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, and Ministry of National Development Planning/Bappenas, Plan and facilitate senior-level consultations, policy and technical dialogues, inclusive finance forums to identify readiness constraints, financing barriers and options for institutional or ecosystem-level resolution.

- Document material stakeholder inputs, responsible follow-up and responses, and how relevant inputs informed recommendations, tools or decisions.

- Build working relationships with development partners, climate and environmental funds, financial institutions, private-sector actors, civil society, academia and other relevant stakeholders.

Support resource mobilization, financing partner engagement, impact reporting and institutional positioning

- Lead opportunities with potential financing partners, including those from public and private sectors, both national and international.

- Provide substantive inputs to financing strategies, partner-engagement plans, partnership proposals, donor briefs, concept notes, presentations and management communications;

Lead and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area(s) and UNDP

Ensure appropriate training and other relevant capacity building activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia. Tiered Approach
