Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the United Nations’ lead agency for international development. It works with countries and partners to address interconnected development challenges, strengthen institutions and resilience, and advance sustainable development. UNDP operates through a global network of headquarters, regional and country offices, and delivers programmes across development, humanitarian, crisis and post-crisis contexts.

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is one of the key UNDP corporate Bureaus that provides the corporate management architecture, policies, systems, advisory support and operational services that enable UNDP to deliver results with accountability and effective stewardship of resources.

Within BMS, the Office of Human Resources (OHR) is responsible for UNDP’s people management function, with a focus on enabling UNDP to have the right capacity and organizational culture to deliver on its mandate and enable people who work for the organization to perform at their best in the environment of inclusion and respect.

UNDP is currently operating in a period of significant institutional transformation, requiring OHR to strengthen strategic people leadership, modernize HR service delivery and enable the organization to adapt with agility while sustaining performance and accountability. In this context, OHR is seeking a high-caliber leader with a strong HR management background and the capacity, commitment and mindset to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship and transformative results in the role of Chief, HR Services.

Duties and Responsibilities

As a member of OHR’s leadership team, working under the direct supervision of the Director, OHR and in close partnership with the Deputy Director, OHR and Director, BMS/Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC), the Chief, HR Services, provides strategic leadership for the design and delivery of integrated, client-focused HR services to UNDP offices, teams and personnel globally, including policy advice, business partnering, HR (re-)alignment, career transition, people analytics, special people and early-career programmes and insurance services.

The Chief, HR Services fosters innovation across the strategic HR services portfolio by using workforce data, artificial intelligence, automation and other digital solutions responsibly to improve decision quality, user experience, operational efficiency and organizational agility.

The Chief, HR Services champions organizational excellence and professionalism and models inclusive and supportive people leadership and management by fostering accountability, collaboration, innovation and high performance and creating an environment in which personnel can perform, develop and thrive.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks and crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1. Provide Leadership to Strategic Business Partnering

- Provide strategic leadership and technical oversight of HR business partnering, ensuring high-quality advisory support, capacity building and effective backstopping to headquarters units, regional bureaux and country offices.

- Spearhead the redesign and implementation of an integrated HR Business Partnering model to strengthen organizational effectiveness and enable the delivery of UNDP’s strategic priorities.

- Provide HR advice to ensure people decisions are consistent, fair, transparent and compliant with the UN Staff Regulations and Rules, applicable legal frameworks and UNDP policies, while effectively managing institutional and people-related risks.

- Work with the Management Consulting Team and other relevant partners in the design and implementation of Organizational Unit Restructuring Plans (OURP), establishing effective governance, monitoring progress and organizational impact, managing workforce and institutional risks, and ensuring consistent application and alignment with UNDP’s strategic priorities.

- Foster cross-functional collaboration across OHR and maintain strategic engagement with BMS/Office of Legal Services and Global Shared Services Centre to ensure coordinated, consistent and effective delivery of people-management initiatives and services across UNDP.

- Make a strategic contribution to the development of a solid HR policy portfolio, ensuring HR policies are responsive to evolving organizational needs and informed by operational experience, workforce data, legal considerations and consultations with key stakeholders.

- Foster collaboration with the global UNDP HR community to ensure effective capacity building and support.

2. Provide Strategic Leadership for Partner Personnel Service Agreement (PPSA) Services and Other Agency Services

- Provide strategic leadership and executive oversight of the development and delivery of a comprehensive portfolio of OHR services to UNDP business units and external partners; ensure effective service delivery models and financial sustainability.

- Strengthen client relationship management to ensure responsive, high-quality delivery.

- Lead the identification and implementation of technology solutions supporting effective service delivery.

- Oversee the delivery of Partner Personnel Service Agreement services to partner agencies, ensuring effective governance, responsible financial management, appropriate risk controls, service quality, and compliance with UNDP policies and partnership agreements.

- Provide strategic leadership to and effective management of the insurance portfolio.

3. Oversee Career Transition and Separation Services

- Provide strategic oversight of HR programmes supporting career transitions, including terminations, separations and inter-agency mobility, ensuring consistent, timely and people-centered delivery.

- Strengthen strategic partnerships with UN entities and other stakeholders to facilitate seamless inter-agency mobility and coordinated transition support.

- Ensure that career transition services are governed by robust standards and delivered in compliance with applicable legal, regulatory and UNDP policy frameworks, while proactively managing institutional and people-related risks.

4. Provide Strategic Leadership and Oversight of People Analytics

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the people analytics function, ensuring the delivery of timely, high-quality workforce and talent insights that inform executive decision-making, strategic workforce planning and organizational priorities.

- Champion the enterprise-wide use of workforce data, predictive analytics and responsible artificial intelligence to anticipate workforce trends, strengthen evidence-based people strategies and drive organizational performance and continuous improvement.

- Strengthen the governance, quality and accessibility of workforce data and analytics, ensuring appropriate standards, safeguards and capabilities are in place to support reliable and responsible organizational decision-making.

5. Oversee Special People Programmes, e.g. JPOSC and Medical Insurance Services

- Undertake senior-level engagement with UN entities, donor governments, and external partners to strengthen strategic partnerships, mobilize resources, and enhance UNDP's position as an employer of choice.

- Oversee pipeline programmes for early career talent, including Junior Professional Officers, Young Professionals, and Internships/fellowships;

- Exercise oversight and monitoring of the medical insurance portfolio managed by UNDP, including annual meetings, complaint handling, and regular reporting.

- Provide expert advice to senior management and stakeholders on medical insurance-related issues, medevac, and liaise with third-party administrators and providers

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent directly oversees three HR Advisors (P5) and two HR Specialists (P4).

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: ​​LEVEL 4: Prioritize team workflow, mobilize resources, drive scalable results/strategic impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 4: Easily navigate complexity, encourage/enable radical innovation, has foresight

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 4: Create systems and processes that enable learning and development for all

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 4: Proactively initiate/lead organizational change, champion new systems/processes

- Act with Determination: ​​LEVEL 4: Able to make difficult decisions in challenging situations, inspire confidence

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 4: Construct strategic multi-partner alliances in high stake situations, foster co-creation

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 4: Create ethical culture, identify/address barriers to inclusion ​

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical:

- Business Direction and Strategy - Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management Change Management: Initiate, design and ensure successful implementation of organizational change; prepare and support individuals and teams in implementing change Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

- HR People Strategy & Planning - People Analytics: Ability to generate and align people data with business intelligence data to inform strategic decision-making; knowledge of databases, their architecture, integration and landscape; ability to create and use data models; knowledge of visualization techniques. Gathering and using data and information to provide insights into people issues and guide decision-making Business Partnering: Strategic thinking and development of long-term plans for the organization’s human resources needs while analyzing the current environment and developing strategies to achieve long-term objectives

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or other relevant field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 15 years (with master’s degree) or 17 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in human resources management or related fields at senior levels is required.

- At least five (5) years of experience managing teams in a diverse workplace in private or public international organizations is required.

- Professional certification in human resources management is desired.

- Experience working in the UN system or other international organizations is desired.

- Experience working across headquarters, shared service centres and/or field office environments is desired.

- Experience delivering HR business partnering and/or designing HR business partnering models is an advantage.

- Experience providing authoritative advice on complex, sensitive or high-risk HR matters to senior executives is an advantage.

- Experience leading organizational restructuring, workforce realignment or change-management initiatives is desired.

- Experience interpreting and implementing HR policies and ensuring consistent application across multiple organizational entities is desired.

- Experience leveraging workforce analytics, predictive analytics or business intelligence to support executive decision-making is desired.

- Experience developing and managing services, cost-recovery mechanisms or service delivery funding models is desired.

- Experience establishing and managing strategic partnerships with UN entities, governments, international organizations or other external stakeholders is desired.

- Experience supporting inter-agency mobility, career transition, or workforce transition programmes is desired.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Intern (Procurement & Supply Chain / Pharmacy)
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Como agencia líder de las Naciones Unidas en desarrollo, el PNUD trabaja en 170 países y territorios para erradicar la pobreza y reducir la desigualdad. Ayudamos a los países a desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo, habilidades de asociación, capacidades institucionales y a desarrollar resiliencia para lograr los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS). Nuestro trabajo se concentra en tres áreas de enfoque; desarrollo sostenible, gobernanza democrática y consolidación de la paz, y resiliencia climática y ante desastres.

El mandato global del PNUD es poner fin a la pobreza, construir una gobernanza democrática, un estado de derecho e instituciones inclusivas. Abogamos por el cambio y conectamos a los países con el conocimiento, la experiencia y los recursos para ayudar a las personas a construir una vida mejor.

Sobre la base de ese mandato global, las funciones del PNUD en Venezuela se focalizan en apoyar al país para acelerar el logro de los ODS, contribuyendo a la construcción de una sociedad resiliente, justa y equitativa, con una vida digna, mediante la promoción de un desarrollo económico socialmente inclusivo y sostenible desde el punto de vista ambiental, que contribuya al desarrollo humano integral.

Para ello, el PNUD promueve políticas sociales centradas en la reducción de la pobreza, la optimización de los sistemas de servicios sociales esenciales, la mitigación de los efectos del cambio climático y la adaptación a ellos y la gestión integral del riesgo de desastres, junto con la aplicación de medidas para la conservación de la biodiversidad y la mejora de la gestión ambiental urbana y rural con un enfoque territorial, con el fin de reducir la vulnerabilidad de la población a fenómenos socioeconómicos y socioambientales.

El PNUD en Venezuela es el Receptor Principal (RP) de la subvención aprobada por el Fondo Global de Lucha contra el VIH, la Tuberculosis y la Malaria (FG) para ejecutar la implementación de esta iniciativa, siguiendo los lineamientos establecidos en la propuesta formulada por los Programas Nacionales del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS), en conjunto con la Organización Panamericana de la Salud/ Organización Mundial de la Salud (OPS/OMS), Organizaciones No Gubernamentales (ONG) nacionales e internacionales y demás Organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil.

El PNUD adopta un enfoque de cartera para dar cabida a las cambiantes necesidades de negocio y aprovechar los vínculos entre las intervenciones para lograr sus objetivos estratégicos. Por lo tanto, se espera que el personal del PNUD trabaje a través de unidades, funciones, equipos y proyectos en equipos multidisciplinarios con el fin de mejorar y permitir la colaboración horizontal, y con los lineamientos generales de la subvención aprobada por el Fondo Global de Lucha contra el VIH, la Tuberculosis y la Malaria, para apoyar las acciones en el país, con el acompañamiento permanente del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud.

En línea con la política corporativa en la materia, el objetivo del programa de pasantía es proporcionar a estudiantes y recién licenciados de diversas formaciones académicas una exposición a las cuestiones de desarrollo y una experiencia de primera mano con el entorno de trabajo cotidiano del PNUD, ya sea en persona o a distancia.

Se prevé dos (2) puestos de pasantías, para integrarse al equipo de PSM (Procurement and Supply Management) de la unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela:

- Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro , donde el/la pasante trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de la Analista de PSM, e interactuará de forma cotidiana con el Equipo de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela (Gerencia de la Unidad, finanzas, Programas, Monitoreo y Evaluación).

- Farmacia, donde el/la pasante trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de la Analista de PSM, e interactuará de forma cotidiana con el Equipo de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela (Gerencia de la Unidad, finanzas, Programas, Monitoreo y Evaluación).

Duties and Responsibilities

Los/as pasantes deberán realizar las siguientes actividades con fines de aprendizaje y fortalecimiento de capacidades, bajo la orientación y supervisión del equipo de PSM de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo:

Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro:

- Apoyar la organización y seguimiento administrativo de procesos de adquisiciones, colaborando en la recopilación, registro y archivo de información y documentación relacionada con compras, contrataciones y gestión de proveedores.

- Brindar apoyo en el seguimiento de embarques nacionales e internacionales, procesos de importación, trámites documentales, recepción y distribución de suministros de salud, con fines de aprendizaje sobre los procesos logísticos y de cadena de suministro.

- Colaborar en actividades de monitoreo de inventarios y almacenamiento, participando en la actualización de registros, inventarios físicos y revisión de información relacionada con existencias, vencimientos y movimientos de productos.

- Apoyar la consolidación y organización de datos e información relacionada con adquisiciones, logística e inventarios, contribuyendo a la elaboración de herramientas de seguimiento y análisis bajo supervisión.

- Colaborar en la preparación de informes, presentaciones, bases de datos, minutas y otros documentos de apoyo relacionados con las actividades de la cadena de suministro.

- Participar en reuniones, sesiones de trabajo y actividades de capacitación que contribuyan al fortalecimiento de sus conocimientos en adquisiciones, logística, abastecimiento y gestión de la cadena de suministro.

- Apoyar la redacción, actualización y organización de correspondencia, comunicaciones y documentos informativos de la Unidad.

- Colaborar en la preparación y edición de presentaciones, materiales visuales, informes y otros productos documentales requeridos por la Unidad.

- Brindar apoyo en otras actividades formativas y de apoyo operativo que contribuyan a su desarrollo profesional y al fortalecimiento de las iniciativas de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo.

Farmacia:

- Apoyar la revisión y organización de información técnica y documental relacionada con medicamentos, insumos de salud y actividades de aseguramiento de la calidad, fortaleciendo sus conocimientos sobre normativas y estándares aplicables.

- Colaborar en el seguimiento administrativo y documental de procesos relacionados con adquisiciones, logística, recepción y distribución de productos de salud, con fines de aprendizaje sobre la gestión de la cadena de suministro farmacéutica.

- Participar en actividades de monitoreo de inventarios y almacenamiento, apoyando la actualización de registros y la recopilación de información relacionada con existencias y fechas de vencimiento.

- Apoyar la consolidación y organización de información utilizada en ejercicios de cuantificación, abastecimiento, consumo e indicadores de gestión, contribuyendo a la elaboración de herramientas de seguimiento bajo supervisión.

- Colaborar en la organización de expedientes técnicos, documentación regulatoria, permisos y archivos relacionados con la gestión farmacéutica y los programas de salud.

- Participar en reuniones técnicas, actividades de monitoreo, capacitaciones y otras iniciativas orientadas al fortalecimiento de conocimientos en gestión farmacéutica, calidad y cadena de suministro.

- Apoyar en la elaboración y actualización de reportes, bases de datos, presentaciones, materiales visuales, informes y demás documentos relacionados con los procesos de abastecimiento, inventarios, distribución y otras actividades de apoyo a los programas de salud.

- Apoyar la redacción, actualización y organización de correspondencia, comunicaciones y documentos informativos de la Unidad.

- Brindar apoyo en otras actividades formativas y de apoyo operativo que contribuyan a su desarrollo profesional y al fortalecimiento de las iniciativas de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo.

Competencies

Gestión y liderazgo:

• Enfoque de gestión orientado a resultados.

• Condiciones para establecer buenas relaciones interpersonales y transmitir lineamientos institucionales.

• Respeto por la diversidad y género.

• Altos niveles de responsabilidad, ética y transparencia.

• Alta capacidad de aprendizaje e iniciativa, sensibilidad humana, responsabilidad y ética.

• Planificación y organización.

• Habilidad y vocación de servicio para trabajar con poblaciones en heterogeneidad social y situación de vulnerabilidad.

• Responsabilidad y creatividad.

• Iniciativa para la solución de problemas.

Trabajo en equipo y coordinación:

• Capacidad para trabajar en equipo y bajo presión.

• Capacidad y facilidad para adaptarse a ambientes de trabajo multiculturales.

Capacidad Técnica y Gestión de Conocimiento:

Pasante de Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro

• Conocimiento básico de adquisiciones, logística, comercio internacional, administración, cadena de suministro o áreas afines.

• Comprensión básica de procesos de abastecimiento, compras, inventarios, almacenamiento y distribución.

• Interés en la gestión de productos de salud, logística humanitaria y fortalecimiento de sistemas de salud.

• Capacidad para recopilar, analizar e interpretar información relacionada con adquisiciones, inventarios, consumos y desempeño logístico, no limitativo.

• Manejo de Microsoft Office, especialmente Excel, Word y PowerPoint.

• Capacidad para trabajar con bases de datos, herramientas de seguimiento y análisis de información, no limitativo.

• Habilidad para elaborar informes, presentaciones y documentos técnicos, no limitativo.

• Capacidad para organizar información, gestionar múltiples actividades simultáneamente y cumplir plazos establecidos.

• Capacidad para aprender y aplicar procedimientos, normativas y herramientas de gestión del PNUD y organismos internacionales.

• Excelente redacción y ortografía.

• Buen conocimiento y manejo de nuevas tecnologías.

• Pensamiento analítico.

• Creatividad y proactividad.

Pasante de Farmacia

• Conocimiento básico de gestión farmacéutica, medicamentos, insumos médicos, reactivos entre otros

• Conocimiento básico de aseguramiento de la calidad y documentación técnica de productos farmacéuticos.

• Interés en las áreas de cadena de suministro, logística, adquisiciones y gestión de productos de salud.

• Capacidad para recopilar, organizar, analizar e interpretar datos relacionados con inventarios, consumos, abastecimiento y desempeño de la cadena de suministro, no limitativo.

• Buen manejo de herramientas informáticas, especialmente Microsoft Office (Excel, Word y PowerPoint), así como capacidad para trabajar con bases de datos y herramientas de reporte.

• Habilidad para redactar informes técnicos, minutas, presentaciones y documentos de apoyo para la toma de decisiones, no limitativo.

• Capacidad para aprender y aplicar procedimientos, normas y lineamientos institucionales del PNUD, Fondo Mundial y autoridades sanitarias nacionales.

• Capacidad para gestionar múltiples tareas, organizar información y cumplir plazos establecidos.

• Excelente redacción y ortografía.

• Buen conocimiento y manejo de nuevas tecnologías.

• Pensamiento analítico.

• Creatividad y proactividad.

Comunicación:

• Capacidad de comunicación efectiva, oral y escrita, en particular para redactar documentos.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

La/El Pasante deberá estar matriculada/o en el último año universitario o ser recién egresada/o de las carreras de Farmacia, Comercio Internacional, Comercio exterior, Administración de Aduanas o carreras afines, que cumplan con alguno de los siguientes requisitos.

• Estar cursando el último año de la carrera de grado universitario;

• Estar cursando un programa de prácticas profesionales de diplomado o haberlo hecho en el pasado

• Estar recién egresados de las carreras

Experience:

• No se requiere experiencia laboral previa

Idiomas:

• Español (requerido)

• Inglés (deseable)

Otros requerimientos

• Excelente manejo de programas de Office (Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, Excel).

• Buen conocimiento y manejo nuevas tecnologías.

• Deseable manejo de herramientas de diseño (Canva, Adobe, etc)

Condiciones:

• Disponibilidad de tiempo conforme los requerimientos establecidos.

• Contar con propio equipamiento informático y espacio de oficina para desarrollar la pasantía.

• Capacidad de trabajo en equipo.

• Responsabilidad y compromiso.

Está pasantía está sujeta a la política del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), que estipula un estipendio mensual fijo.

Además, requiere que el/la pasante cuente con seguro médico, que deberá ser debidamente presentado. Al final del período, el/la pasante deberá entregar un informe aprobado por el supervisor al PNUD y recibirá el certificado de pasantía.

Disclaimer

We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, OHR [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the United Nations’ lead agency for international development. It works with countries and partners to address interconnected development challenges, strengthen institutions and resilience, and advance sustainable development. UNDP operates through a global network of headquarters, regional and country offices and delivers programmes across development, humanitarian, crisis and post-crisis contexts.

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is one of the key UNDP corporate Bureaus that provides the corporate management architecture, policies, systems, advisory support and operational services that enable UNDP to deliver results with accountability and effective stewardship of resources.

Within BMS, the Office of Human Resources (OHR) is responsible for UNDP’s people management function, with a focus on enabling UNDP to have the right capacity and organizational culture to deliver on its mandate and enable people who work for the organization to perform at their best in the environment of inclusion and respect.

UNDP is currently operating in a period of significant institutional transformation, requiring OHR to strengthen strategic people leadership, modernize HR service delivery and enable the organization to adapt with agility while sustaining performance and accountability. In this context, OHR is seeking a high-caliber leader with a strong HR management background and the capacity, commitment and mindset to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship and transformative results in the role of Deputy Director, OHR.

Duties and Responsibilities

As a member of OHR’s leadership team, working under the direct supervision of the Director, OHR and in close partnership with the Chief, HR Services, the Deputy Director, OHR provides substantive leadership for the continued development and implementation of an integrated talent management system that connects strategic workforce planning, organizational and job design, talent acquisition and deployment, succession management, career and leadership development, performance management, workplace experience, organizational culture, health and wellbeing. The Deputy Director fosters innovation across this system by using workforce data, artificial intelligence, automation and other digital solutions responsibly to improve decision quality, user experience, operational efficiency and organizational agility.

The Deputy Director ensures that integrated talent management strategies, policies, capabilities and service delivery arrangements are aligned with UNDP’s strategy and priorities and evolving business, operating and funding models. This includes shaping talent solutions that respond to changing programme and operational requirements, resource trends and the needs of different organizational contexts, while safeguarding fairness, inclusion, accountability and the effective management of institutional risk. The Deputy Director is accountable for strategic coherence and operational excellence across the talent lifecycle and for enabling a high-performing, adaptable and healthy workforce capable of delivering sustainable development results.

The Deputy Director serves as the Director’s principal strategic partner and deputizes for the Director, including representing OHR in senior management and inter-agency and staff-management forums.

The Deputy Director champions organizational excellence and professionalism and models inclusive and supportive people leadership by promoting accountability, collaboration, innovation and high performance and creating an environment in which personnel can perform, develop and thrive.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks and crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to strengthen horizontal collaboration.

1. Provide Strategic Leadership, Portfolio Oversight and Deputy Direction for OHR

- Provide strategic direction and oversight for the teams in the Deputy Director’s portfolio, ensuring integrated, client-focused delivery aligned with UNDP’s People Strategy and organizational priorities.

- Build and sustain strategic partnerships with UN entities, Member States, donors and external institutions, and mobilize resources to advance UNDP’s people priorities, programmes and services.

- Lead the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies across the portfolio to improve decision-making, service quality and operational efficiency.

- Ensure the quality, coherence and consistent delivery of corporate integrated talent management programmes across headquarters, regional and country offices.

- Represent OHR and deputize for the Director as assigned, including supporting the Director and UNDP in negotiations with staff representatives.

- As required, represent UNDP in senior-level HR forums, inter-agency bodies and strategic working groups, shaping system-wide dialogue, policies and practices.

2. Oversee Strategic Workforce Planning and Workforce Architecture

- Shape and lead the corporate workforce planning function, ensuring alignment with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, People Strategy, business and funding models and evolving business priorities.

- Lead the governance and continued evolution of UNDP’s workforce architecture, including job design, ensuring coherent job families, role profiles, position titles, career pathways and job design standards across the organization.

- Provide advice on complex workforce and organizational design matters, including reorganization, workforce optimization, as well as functional and HR alignment processes.

3. Provide Leadership to Talent Acquisition and Deployment

- Provide strategic oversight of UNDP’s talent acquisition and recruitment strategies, ensuring timely, transparent and effective outcomes of related processes.

- Ensure development and continuous improvement of talent acquisition, recruitment and deployment policies, procedures and practices across UNDP, and compliance with these across UNDP.

- Oversee senior-level recruitment and selection processes, ensuring sound governance, institutional rigor and the identification of high-caliber and diverse leadership talent.

- Provide strategic direction for talent deployment and mobility, including the Internal Talent Marketplace.

- Engage relevant stakeholders to anticipate talent needs and continuously improve talent acquisition and deployment strategies, policies and practices.

- Ensure UNDP leverages workforce analytics, digital platforms and innovative sourcing approaches to strengthen talent pipelines.

4. Oversee Succession Management and Talent Development

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the succession management function, ensuring leadership continuity, robust pipelines for critical and senior-level roles, and effective management of succession risks.

- Oversee the design and implementation of people and leadership development strategies that build a skilled, diverse and adaptable workforce aligned with UNDP’s evolving priorities.

- Ensure succession and talent development strategies are integrated with strategic workforce planning, career development, mobility, performance management and other functions in the integrated talent management cycle.

5. Oversee Performance Management, Workplace Experience and Culture

- Provide strategic leadership for UNDP’s organizational culture, ensuring that organizational values, leadership practices, people systems and ways of working reinforce inclusion, collaboration, accountability and high performance.

- Shape UNDP’s performance management, workplace experience and employee engagement approach.

- Lead organizational efforts to promote gender parity, diversity, equity and inclusion and to sustain a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, sexual harassment and abuse of authority, in coordination with relevant policy, ethics, oversight and support functions.

- Ensure that evidence from employee engagement, workplace experience and performance management informs leadership action, workforce planning, talent development, succession management, recognition and the continuous improvement of people policies and programmes.

- Oversee organizational approaches to mental health, psychosocial support, wellbeing and workforce resilience.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development. SFH work is delivered through three interconnected portfolios: 1) Public Finance for the SDGs; 2) Private Finance for the SDGs; and 3) Global & Country Financing Policy Frameworks.

The European Commission (EC), together with EU Member States, development agencies, EU financial institutions and UN organizations, have embarked on coordinating their offer of EU expertise and resources for low-and middle-income countries in the area of sustainable finance, inspired by EU experience, through the EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, of which UNDP is an implementing partner, focusing on supporting countries on sustainable finance taxonomy development, disclosure frameworks and thematic/green bond framework development.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Debt and Investments and with a cross-reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Asia and Pacific, the Investment and Debt Finance Specialist will primarily be responsible for the delivery of activities under the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub implemented by UNDP. The role is hosted within SFH Private Finance Portfolio under the Investments and Debt unit.

Working closely with colleagues across SFH portfolios and the Global Policy Network in Asia and the Pacific, the Specialist will provide technical and analytical support to partner governments, financial institutions, and issuers on sustainable finance instruments, with a focus on green and sustainability bond issuance. This includes pre- and post-issuance support, knowledge generation on fixed-income markets and other debt instruments, identification and assessment of green investment opportunities, and design of monitoring and reporting frameworks for environmental and climate impacts. The role will also contribute to building in-house capacity and institutional knowledge on debt and investment finance, ensuring effective translation of these skills into the design and implementation of innovative financing instruments at the country level, in line with the objectives of the Global Green Bond Initiative and the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub both being linked to Global Gateway.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Duties and Responsibilities

The Investments and Debt Finance Specialist will play a central role in advancing UNDP’s Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) agenda in Asia and the Pacific, while also contributing to global workstreams. The incumbent will be responsible for the following functions and duties:

Advice on Thematic Debt Instruments and Country Support

- Support the development and implementation of UNDP’s thematic debt offering and lead the design and piloting of innovative development bond frameworks in selected countries across the Asia-Pacific region, in close coordination with SFH portfolios, UNDP Country Offices and SFH Regional Advisors;

- Provide tailored technical advice to governments and partners to address country-specific financing needs, with a particular focus on green bonds in collaboration with the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub.

Ensure Strategic alignment with European Commission initiatives

- Ensure key focus and coherence with the European Commission’s Global Green Bond Initiative;

- Contribute to joint EC-UNDP workplans and reporting, promoting alignment with EU sustainable finance frameworks and global standards;

- Provide technical inputs as an implementing partner of EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, coordination with SFH portfolios;

- Prepare donor reports, and contribute to monitoring frameworks, ensuring consistency with regional priorities and global strategies, and UNDP/SFH systems.

Build Strategic Partnerships and Scaling Sustainable Finance Solutions

- Contribute to UNDP’s broader financing and investment agenda by leveraging networks, fostering partnerships, and identifying opportunities to scale sustainable finance solutions at global and country-levels with a focus on blended finance structures.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

- Human Development

- Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

- Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities

Indonesia is one of the world's largest producers of agricultural commodities such as palm oil and cocoa, which are vital to both the national economy and the livelihoods of millions of smallholders. However, unsustainable production practices present challenges related to deforestation, biodiversity loss, and climate change. In response, the Government of Indonesia (GoI) is implementing systemic reforms to transition toward a green economy, promoting agricultural sustainability, landscape restoration, and enhanced smallholder welfare. To support these goals, UNDP Indonesia’s Nature and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) unit manages a growing, interconnected portfolio of sustainable landscape and commodity initiatives, including:

- The Forest Agriculture and Sustainable Trade (FAST) Project: The project aims to strengthen sustainable agricultural commodity governance, with a particular focus on palm oil and cocoa, by supporting policy and regulatory improvements, institutional capacity development, sustainability standards and certification systems, and market and trade-related cooperation. Key interventions include strengthening the implementation of Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO), supporting the National Action Plan for Sustainable Palm Oil (NAP-SPO), advancing sustainable cocoa policy frameworks, and facilitating policy dialogue and collaboration among government, industry and other stakeholders.

- The Food Systems, Land Use and Restoration (FOLUR) Impact Program: The project promotes sustainable commodity production, responsible land use, landscape restoration and biodiversity conservation through an integrated landscape approach. Focusing on key commodities, including palm oil, cocoa, coffee and rice, the project aims to strengthen sustainable value chains, reduce deforestation, enhance multi-stakeholder collaboration and improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and local communities. Policy support under FOLUR focuses on strengthening enabling conditions, institutional coordination and policy coherence for sustainable food systems and landscape management.

- The Sustainable Landscape Programme Indonesia (SLPI): The project aims to advance sustainable landscape management, responsible commodity production, forest conservation and inclusive rural development by strengthening landscape governance, promoting sustainable land-use practices and fostering collaboration among government institutions, private sector actors and local communities. Its policy-related interventions support the alignment of national and subnational policies, institutional frameworks and development planning processes to advance sustainable landscape and commodity governance.

The three projects share complementary objectives in strengthening sustainable commodity governance, improving policy and regulatory frameworks, enhancing institutional coordination and promoting sustainable and inclusive agricultural value chains. Their combined interventions provide opportunities to improve policy coherence, facilitate knowledge exchange and strengthen linkages between national policy development and implementation at subnational and landscape levels.

To support these complementary initiatives, and the overall strategic priority of UNDP on nature-based development, UNDP seeks to recruit a Sustainable Commodity Policy Analyst (Sustainable Commodity Policy), NPSA-9, who will provide substantive technical leadership and analytical support across FOLUR, SLPI Phase II and FAST, and be a thematic resource for the Country Office as a whole. The Sustainable Commodity Policy Analyst will contribute to policy analysis and formulation, review regulatory and institutional frameworks, preparation of evidence-based policy recommendations, facilitation of policy dialogue, and coordination with relevant government institutions and stakeholders. Working closely with the respective UNDP teams, government counterparts, the Sustainable Commodity Policy Analyst will support the alignment of sustainable commodity policies and their implementation across national and subnational levels, while contributing to knowledge sharing, capacity development and the achievement of project-specific results.

The Sustainable Commodity Policy Technical Analyst will deliver high-quality technical advisory, strengthen government partnerships, and drive policy coherence across UNDP's sustainable commodities portfolio. The scope of work covers the following key functional areas:

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Head of the Nature and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) Unit / Program Manager, the Technical Analyst on Sustainable Commodity Policy will operate on a day-to-day basis in close coordination with the National Project Managers and Project Management Units (PMUs) of the FAST, FOLUR, and SLPI projects.

In executing these functions, the incumbent will maintain continuous technical liaison and build robust strategic partnerships with key government counterparts—including the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, Coordinating Ministry of Food, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Environment and Forestry, and relevant subnational authorities—while engaging closely with smallholder networks, private sector coalitions and international donors.

Sustainable Commodity Policy Analysis and Advisory

- Provide high-level policy analysis, technical advisory, and strategic recommendations to strengthen national sustainable commodity governance, certification schemes (e.g., I SPO, RSPO, cocoa standards), and land-use regulatory frameworks;

- Lead the drafting of policy briefs, diagnostic reports, and technical guidance to align agricultural policies with national commitments (e.g., RAN-KSB 2025–2029, Green Growth priorities);

- Analyze emerging global and regional commodity trade requirements and supply chain regulations, advising UNDP and partners on strategic responses.

Government Engagement and Policy Interface

- Act as a key technical liaison and build robust relationships with primary government counterparts, including the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, the Coordinating Ministry of Food, the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry of Environment and Forestry, and relevant sub-national authorities;

- Participate in high-level policy dialogues, technical working groups, public-private partnerships, and multi-stakeholder forums (e.g., FoKSBI , Cocoa Sustainability Partnership);

- Facilitate consensus-building among diverse stakeholders, including ministries, private sector leaders, CSOs, and smallholder cooperatives—to advance regulatory and institutional reforms.

Policy Coherence Across the Sustainable Commodities Portfolio

- Proactively identify synergies, eliminate overlaps, and align policy-related activities across FAST, FOLUR, and SLPI, ensuring a unified approach to sustainable commodity value chains to strengthen UNDP Indonesia’s position on the issue;

- Ensure that subnational interventions (such as jurisdictional land-use plans under SLPI) are structured to support and feed back into national policy targets (such as FAST's output 1 deliverables);

- Collaborate on inter-agency regulatory efforts, data interoperability, and digital information systems (e.g., SIPERIBUN integration to secure unified progress on commodity traceability.

Technical Quality Assurance and Knowledge Integration

- Provide robust technical quality assurance for policy studies, supply-chain research, digital development initiatives, and landscape-level interventions commissioned across the portfolio;

- Synthesize complex project datasets, evaluation findings, and landscape realities into high-quality, publishable knowledge products, technical briefs, and lessons-learned summaries;

- Deliver capacity-building support and technical guidance to project management units (PMUs), subnational implementation partners, and government staff on sustainable policy instruments.

Translate Project and Landscape Evidence into Policy and Institutional Results

- Develop and operationalize a systematic mechanism to capture field-level evidence (e.g., smallholder performance, certification hurdles, jurisdictional successes) and translate it into formal regulatory inputs;

- Formulate actionable roadmaps and institutionalization strategies to turn project successes into permanent, government-led administrative structures, funding streams, or legal frameworks;

- Monitor, trace, and evaluate how project deliverables influence policy enactment, assessing progress, risks, and institutional bottlenecks to recommend corrective strategic paths.

Avoid any kind of discriminatory behaviour including gender discrimination and ensure that:

- Human rights and gender equality are prioritized as an ethical principle within all actions;

- Activities are designed and implemented in accordance with “Social and Environmental Standards of UNDP”;

- Any kind of diversity based on ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, disability, religion, class, gender are respected within all implementations including data production;

- Differentiated needs of women and men are considered;

- Inclusive approach is reflected within all actions and implementations, in that sense an enabling and accessible setup in various senses such as disability gender language barrier is created;

- Necessary arrangements to provide gender parity within all committees, meetings, trainings etc. introduced.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Think Innovatively: Level 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: Level 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: Level 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: Level 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Cross-functional and technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Strategic Thinking : Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business Management

- Result Based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

jobs.title: Intern – Climate and Energy Project Support - Office based (Rome, Italy) / Home Based: Overview
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development. We support countries and communities as they work to eradicate poverty, implement the Paris Agreement on climate change and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. We advocate for transformative change, and we connect countries to the resources they need to help people build a better life.

Rome Centre for Climate Action and Energy Transition

The central purpose of the Rome Centre is to ensure the effective implementation and further development of the strategic partnership between UNDP and the government of Italy across the objectives of sustainable development and in doing so advancing the broader partnership between UNDP and G7 and G20 countries.

The Rome Centre focuses on the critical policy areas of youth engagement in climate action, energy for development and climate finance. These objectives are pursued through the effective implementation of three initial main programmes: the Technical Assistance and Investment Support Facility, the Italy-UNDP Energy Partnership and Youth4Climate.

- PISTA (Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance) aims to mobilise finance for climate, energy and environment. Specifically, the Facility aims to originate projects that contribute to the decarbonization efforts of developing economies and to their transition to climate-resilient economies, and it aims to catalyse international financial resources toward these initiatives. Matching impactful projects with investors and capital providers goes hand in hand with the engagement with financial institutions – both institutional and private – at Italian and global level.

- The Energy for Growth initiative aims to promote access to sustainable energy in developing countries, contributing to SDG7. The goal of the partnership is to assist partner countries in unlocking finance to scale up the diffusion of clean energy solutions, increase access to energy and boost the energy transition. Overall, the initiative aims to foster the mobilization of public and private capital toward projects aligned with the international policy agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. It does so by connecting UNDP's capacity and connections in emerging economies and developing countries with the public-private ecosystem of Italy and other G7-G20countries, in the crucial sector of energy.

- Youth4Climate promotes youth engagement in climate action, contributing to SDG13. Youth4Climate supports the implementation of youth-led and youth-inclusive solutions to environmental and climate challenges, both financially and through capacity development. It also gives young people around the world who are committed to fighting climate change a platform to engage with policymakers and global leaders.

- The Rome Centre also has a broader mandate to engage with the Italian ecosystem as a whole, which involves close collaboration with key actors in the public and private sector, with the aim to effectively mobilize financial resources for development objectives. To guarantee the effective implementation of the Rome Centre’s workplan, and indeed to ensure the strategic and long term impact of both its programmes, the Centre will develop broader strategic partnerships and reinforce the overall collaboration with Italy and other meaningful partners.

- The Rome Centre functions as the UNDP Office in Italy. As a result, it plays a key role in the strategic engagement of public stakeholders in advancing Italy’s international cooperation priorities within broader multilateral frameworks, including the G7 and G20, as well as supporting the development objectives of National Strategies such as the Mattei Plan for Africa. For instance, it supports initiatives such as: Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII), the G7 Adaptation Accelerator Hub, the Digital Flagship for Africa, the AI Hub for Sustainable Development, as well as crises and recovery programmes. Through these efforts, the Centre acts as a hub to channel Italian priorities into global and regional programmes, while mobilizing finance and partnerships that scale SDG-aligned impact in developing and crisis-affected countries.

Delivering on its programmes, the Rome Centre will provide support to the international cooperation efforts of Italy and it will support UNDP’s global policy initiatives. Recognizing that change will be disruptive, UNDP will work to ensure that such transitions are just, and that their impact on vulnerable people is understood and duly mitigated.

Duties and Responsibilities

The main objective of the assignment is to provide daily support to UNDP Rome Centre in day-to-day management of the climate and energy portfolio. The intern will work under the guidance and technical supervision of team leaders.

The main duties that the intern will be expected to carry out are:

Research and Analysis:

- Assist in researching climate and energy topics, including sustainable energy solutions, renewable energy systems, and climate change mitigation strategies.

- Compile and analyze data for reports and presentations.

Project Coordination Support:

- Aid in coordinating ongoing projects within the Climate and Energy portfolios, including support to project preparation and investment facilitation activities.

- Track project progress and deadlines, and support logistics for meetings and events.

Administrative Assistance:

- Prepare documents, meeting minutes, and correspondence for the Climate and Energy teams.

- Maintain organized digital and physical records of the portfolio's activities.

Communication and Outreach:

- Contribute to drafting communications materials, including social media posts, newsletters, and briefing notes.

- Support outreach efforts to partners and stakeholders.

Event Support:

- Help organize workshops, webinars, and events related to climate and energy.

- Assist with logistical and technical arrangements during events.

Ad hoc:

- Perform any other related duties as may be required to support the effective functioning of the relevant team and the Rome Centre as a whole.

Competencies

Corporate

- Demonstrates integrity by modelling the UN’s values and ethical standards;

- Promotes the vision, mission, and strategic goals of UNDP;

- Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability;

- Treats all people fairly without favoritism.

Professionalism

- Works toward creative solutions by analyzing problems carefully and logically;

- Has a dynamic, positive and adaptive attitude towards work-related challenges;

- Facilitates discussions and meetings effectively and efficiently;

- Resolves conflicts as they arise;

- Sets priorities, produces quality outputs, meets deadlines and manages time efficiently;

- Highly organized, detailed oriented.

Communication

- Writes and presents clearly and convincingly.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship program must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

- Be enrolled in a graduate school program (second university degree or equivalent, or higher - Preference for master level) in fields such as Public Policy, Political Sciences Studies Environmental Science, Energy Studies, Climate Policy, International Relations, Economics, Engineering, Marketing or a related field or any related field.

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree program (minimum bachelor’s level or equivalent) in field mentioned above.

- Have graduated with a university degree (as defined above), and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.

Experience:

- Strong research and analytical abilities;

- Proficiency in MS Office and familiarity with project management tools;

- Interest in sustainable development and climate change issues;

- Knowledge at the intersection of youth and climate is an asset;

- Excellent writing skills, as well as strong analytical aptitude and strong communication skills;

- Strong organizational skills; ability to work independently and meet tight deadlines;

- Familiarity with the UN system, and/or other international organizations, multi-lateral and other academic and international institutions;

- Commitment to UNDP's mission, vision and values;

- Strong willingness and ability to learn on the job.

Language requirements

- Excellent oral and written communication skills in English language is required.

- Working knowledge of another official UN language or Italian is an asset.

In case an applicant is successfully selected, s/he will be requested to provide electronic versions of:

- letter from his/her university confirming current enrollment and graduation date;

- if sponsored - letter from his/her university confirming their sponsorship for the internship;

- letter of recommendation from a professor;

- copy of his/her most recent school transcript;

- copy of passport;

- completed UNDP internship application form;

- signed UNDP Internship Agreement;

- Medical Certificate of Good Health;

- Proof of medical insurance.

Kindly note the above documentation is required within one week after selection.

Pls include the following with your application:

- Copy of passport.

- Applicants must identify their availability period

- Applicant must identify if the application is for Home Base or office base

- Applicant must identify his residency location (City, Country) during the internship period (in case his application is selected).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Institutional Arrangements

The intern will report to the thematic team leaders and operations lead and will work closely with technical experts.

Interns’ Expenses

Interns may be given a stipend under conditions prescribed in the section on stipends, below. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, passports, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of:

(a) The nominating institution, related institution or government, which may provide the required financial assistance to its students;

Stipend

Where an intern is not financially supported by any institution or programme, such as a university, government, foundation or scholarship programme, a stipend intended to help cover basic daily expenses related to the internship, such as meals and transportation at the duty station, will be paid by UNDP. The stipend will be paid on a monthly basis and part-time internship arrangements are prorated accordingly.

Where an intern is financially supported by an institution, government or third party, UNDP will, subject to the rules of such institution, government or third party, pay the intern the difference, if any, between the external financial support provided and the applicable UNDP stipend. No other payments of any kind will be made to an intern by the office in connection with an internship agreement.

Interns will accrue leave at the rate of 1.5 days per month. Any accrued leave days not used by the end of the internship will be forfeited. Any unjustified absences during the internship period exceeding a total of nine days, will be deducted from the monthly stipend.

Insurance

Interns are responsible for securing adequate medical insurance for the duration of their internship with UNDP. UNDP will not reimburse the medical insurance of the intern. Any costs arising from accidents and illness incurred during an internship assignment will be the responsibility of the intern. Applicants for internships must show proof of valid medical insurance for the duty station in which they will intern. For applicants who are neither nationals or residents of the duty station, the insurance must include adequate coverage in the event of an injury or illness during the internship duration which:

- Requires transportation to the home country or country of residence for further treatment;

- Results in death and requires preparation and return of the remains to the home country, or country of residence.

Subsequent Employment

There is no expectation of employment with UNDP following an internship. Interns cannot apply for, or be appointed to, any position during the period of their internship.

Third-party claims

UNDP is not responsible for any claims by any parties where the loss of or damage to their property, death or personal injury was caused by the actions or omission of action by the interns during their internship.

Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents ('Green Card' holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.
